chapters.title: Chapter 201: Under The Spire [X / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The audio crackled as a massive section of the corridor fifty yards away completely caved in, burying the staircase in tons of rubble.

"I have an exciting morning announcement for all remaining Lords!" the dead god declared cheerfully. "Given that we are approaching the final phase of our game, I have decided to increase the pacing! Right now, as you can feel beneath your feet, the entire Treasury Dungeon is actively undergoing a complete chain-reaction tectonic collapse onto itself!"
Harper grabbed Silas’s arm, her purple eyes wide with horror as another boulder smashed into the floor ten feet away.
"He’s destroying the entire labyrinth?!"

"Listen closely to the rules of morning cardio!" Ititus shouted happily over the global broadcast. "There is currently only one specific structural sector in this entire subterranean dungeon that is not collapsing... and that is the central caldera below where the real Apex Vault and the primary Dungeon Core are located! You have exactly ten or twenty minutes!"
The god’s voice dropped into a dark sneer that promised inescapable death.

"If you do not run at maximum speed and cross the threshold into the stable place within the next ten to twenty minutes..." Ititus whispered, "...millions of tons of collapsing bedrock will completely crush you into atomized paste, and you will all die alone in the dark! Run, little Lords! RUN!"
The broadcast clicked off, leaving the cavern drowning in the deafening roar of collapsing earth and splitting stone.
Silas and Harper stood frozen in the center of the violently shaking intersection, the floor actively fracturing into jagged spiderwebs beneath their boots as falling gravel pelted their shoulders.
They looked at each other through the thick swirling dust of the collapsing dungeon, their faces identical masks of exhausted bewilderment.
’Seriously?’ Silas and Harper both thought in unison, blinking their eyes in disbelief as a massive stone pillar collapsed behind them.
Did this broken sadistic dead god genuinely want them to play his twisted game that bad?!
KRA-KRA-CRASH!
The apocalyptic roar of the falling ceiling violently drowned out any remaining semblance of peace within the damp subterranean corridor.
Millions of tons of ancient bedrock, pulverized stone, and freezing moisture completely collapsed, plummeting downward with the terminal velocity of a meteor strike.
Silas didn’t even have a second to hesitate.
He violently grabbed Harper by the forearm with his Core igniting as he yanked the exhausted lightning mage completely out of the rapidly crumbling ice haven.
They burst into the open intersection just as the vaulted stone ceiling directly above their Safe Zone gave way entirely.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!

The massive boulders completely crushed the thick-walled ice tent they had been sleeping in just seconds prior, obliterating the intricate absolute-zero structure into a million glittering shards of useless blue frost.

The impact was so astronomically immense that a thick, suffocating cloud of grey dust aggressively blasted down the tunnel, choking the stagnant air and plunging the corridor into near-total darkness.
Silas coughed with his golden-ringed eyes watering as the entire floor beneath his heavy combat boots began to violently heave, roll, and aggressively buck.
"Move!" Silas roared over the deafening tectonic rumble, pulling Harper forward.
They sprinted down the corridor, but the destruction of the dead god’s twisted game was inescapable.

Deep fault lines violently tore through the damp stone floor directly in front of them, splitting the ancient bedrock wide open like the maw of a dying beast to reveal bottomless lightless chasms that reeked of sulfur and void.
Silas skidded to a violent halt with his boots carving deep grooves into the stone.
He aggressively grabbed Harper’s shoulder, physically jerking her backward to stop her from plummeting into a newly formed fissure that had just ripped open inches from her bare toes.
’What the fuck man...’
Silas whipped his head to his right, his eyes desperately scanning the architecture for an escape route.
The massive sweeping stone staircase they had ascended yesterday was completely gone too.
The entire architectural support structure of the stairs had violently buckled under the tectonic stress.

Before their very eyes, the massive stone steps aggressively collapsed, shearing away from the cavern wall and plummeting downward into a vertical drop into the Abyss, swallowed by the suffocating darkness below.

"The stairs are gone!" Harper screamed over the apocalyptic noise with her purple eyes wide with terror as she gripped the lapels of Silas’s oversized trench coat tightly around her shoulders. "How are we supposed to navigate to the Vault sector?! The whole place is shifting!"
Silas let out a deeply exhausted, frustrated sigh with his jaw clenching tight.

"We don’t need to navigate!" Silas shouted back, his voice cutting through the roar of the collapsing earth. "The entire labyrinth is actively collapsing right behind us! The only way left to go is straight forward! We just run completely past the destruction until we find stable ground!"
Silas turned to her with his sharp jawline going tight with adrenaline and focus.
He looked at her bare legs, her bruised skin, and the fact that she was wearing nothing but a coat.
"Can you keep up?!" Silas demanded.
"I can keep up!" Harper assured him frantically, aggressively nodding her head. "My core is mostly recovered! I can run!"
"Good," Silas said.
But as he looked at her trembling legs and the heavy trench coat dragging against the stone, he didn’t think so.
He didn’t trust her physical stamina one single bit. Nobles always overestimated their baseline endurance.
They both sprinted forward, leaping across a two-foot-wide crack in the floor, plunging deeper into the dark vibrating corridor.
Within exactly ten seconds, Silas’s suspicion was proven utterly correct.
Even while Silas was actively suppressing his Gold Core, merely maintaining a perfectly regular jogging pace to conserve his breath, Harper was already lagging terribly far behind.
Her bare feet were completely unsuited for the jagged bedrock.
The sharp stones sliced into her soles and her physique while magically potent enough to level a a lot of things completely lacked the raw cardiovascular endurance necessary to outrun a earthquake.
A massive chunk of the ceiling broke away, falling directly toward her trailing silhouette.
"Harper..." Silas barked.
He didn’t wait for her to dodge and he didn’t waste breath encouraging her.
Silas violently spun on his heel, aggressively reversing his forward momentum.
He closed the ten-yard gap in a terrifying blur of motion, sweeping his strong calloused arms directly underneath her bare knees and behind her back.
WHOOSH!

Silas effortlessly picked her up off the crumbling floor, pulling her into a secure, tight Princess carry just as the massive boulder smashed into the stone exactly where she had been standing a microsecond prior.
"Hang on!" Silas commanded.
Harper gasped with her hands instinctively flying up to wrap securely around his neck.
BOOOOOOM!
Silas compressed an explosive surge of Gold Core energy directly into his calves and violently shot forward down the collapsing corridor like a human cannonball!
The sudden acceleration was absolute.
The sheer G-force of a Gold Core sprint physically made Harper’s flawless face tremble with her cheeks vibrating from the wind resistance as Silas made the air tremble around him.
She gasped, burying her face deeply into his broad chest as the damp stone walls violently blurred past them in streaks of grey and black.
He was clearing massive amounts of distance in a single sustained blitz with his heavy combat boots effortlessly finding traction on the shifting earth.
But the dead god’s timer was ticking, and the ground behind them was beginning to crack even harder.
The deafening roar of the earth eating itself was following right on their heels and a tidal wave of destruction that refused to be outpaced.
Through the thick swirling dust, his golden-ringed eyes locked onto a massive, branching intersection up ahead.
"Another staircase!" Silas muttered.
Looming in the gloom was a secondary reinforced stone staircase leading sharply upward toward a higher cavern but it wasn’t safe.
The tectonic vibrations had already reached the architecture.
The ancient stone steps were violently cracking with jagged fissures tearing through the dead center of the ascent as the pillars holding it aloft began to buckle.
Silas didn’t slow down. He accelerated with his muscles bulging as he hit the base of the stairs at absolute full speed.
’If Ititius has no haters then I’m no longer alive!’
He bounded upward with his heavy boots flawlessly targeting the few remaining solid patches of stone.
He hopped cleanly over the points that were completely shattering beneath his weight, using the falling debris as temporary stepping stones to propel himself higher.
CRUMBLE! KRA-THOOM!
As he reached the midway point, the entire front half of the remaining staircase violently collapsed.
The stone steps simply fell away into the dark chasm below, leaving a massive twenty-foot horizontal gap between him and the upper landing.
Silas gritted his teeth.
He planted his boot on the very edge of the collapsing step, tightened his grip on Harper’s thighs, and leaped completely over the chasm.
WHOOSH!
Silas soared through the empty air, defying gravity for two agonizing seconds, before landing heavily but securely on the upper stone platform.
He hit the ground in a flawless roll, instantly bouncing back to his feet without losing an ounce of momentum, and continued sprinting down the upper corridor.
The escape only intensified from there.
The upper corridors were a nightmare as the labyrinth was aggressively collapsing right behind them with the darkness literally swallowing the stone a few yards behind his boots.
But it wasn’t just the architecture trying to kill them.
The violently shifting earth had disturbed the deepest darkest nests of the subterranean ecosystem.
SKREEEEEEE!
A horrific high-pitched ear-piercing screech echoed from a side tunnel up ahead.
Bursting out of the collapsing darkness, completely blocking their path forward, was a swarm of massive grotesque monsters.
They were towering, heavily armored tunnel-centipedes, their segmented bodies dripping with highly corrosive green acid that hissed and bubbled against the damp stone floor.
"Monsters!" Harper warned, her purple eyes wide as she desperately tried to summon a spark of lightning in her palm.
"I’ve got them!" Silas roared, his voice completely lacking any sort of fear.
He didn’t put her down.

While securely holding the entire weight of Harper in his strong left arm, Silas seamlessly reached over his shoulder and drew his mythril longsword with his right hand in a blinding flash of gold steel.
As he closed the distance, the first massive centipede reared up, its mandibles snapping violently as it lunged for his legs.
KRA-SLASH!
Silas swung his blade in a brutal blindingly fast upward arc, completely disregarding traditional swordsmanship in favor of brutality.
The mythril steel cleanly bisected the massive insect straight down the middle, splitting its armored head in two as thick, foul-smelling yellow ichor sprayed across the corridor.
The second centipede reared up, preparing to spit a highly pressurized stream of corrosive green acid directly at Harper’s exposed back.
Silas violently pivoted his torso, shielding her completely with his own body as he forcefully channeled his water mana into the steel of his blade.
"First Style!" Silas chanted rapidly.

He swung the sword horizontally, unleashing a hyper-pressurized crescent-shaped blade of cutting water that completely intercepted the acid stream, neutralizing it mid-air before cleanly decapitating the second monster.
Silas aggressively trampled directly over its ruined twitching carcass as he kept running, kicking the severed head into the Abyss.
The corridor opened up into a massive, wide-spanning underground bridge that overlooked a bottomless fiery pit and they were not the only ones running for their lives.
Sprinting desperately across the buckling stone bridge, his gold armor heavily dented and his face pale with unadulterated terror, was a familiar figure.
It was the Spear Lord!
The arrogant aristocratic man who had hunted them across the surface desert was currently screaming at the absolute top of his lungs.
He was desperately clutching his heavy iron spear with tears actively streaming down his soot-covered face as the bridge collapsed right on his heels, threatening to swallow him whole.
Silas didn’t engage as he simply accelerated, easily outpacing the exhausted terrified Lord and running right past him on the collapsing bridge like he was standing still.
As Silas blurred past, the Spear Lord’s desperate bloodshot eyes locked onto the Silas’s cargo.
He instantly recognized the purple-haired lightning mage being carried securely in Silas’s arms, wearing nothing but his black trench coat.

"You!" the Spear Lord roared, his intense fear momentarily overridden by a screaming wave of fury. "You lightning bitch! You killed my Siege Rhino! It cost me a Hero Summoning Card to summon that beast, you whore!"

chapters.title: Chapter 202: Under The Spire [XI / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The Spear Lord completely abandoned his survival sprint, violently pivoting his spear.
He aggressively charged at them at full speed with murderous intent, ready to drive his spear right through Harper’s back but Silas didn’t even bother raising his sword.
He simply maintained his wide gap, casually looking over his shoulder as he kept running.
"Watch your step, Noble." Silas said over the wind. "No seriously, watch your step..."
KRA-KRA-THOOM!
Before the Spear Lord could even throw his weapon, the structural integrity of the ancient stone bridge completely failed.
A massive chunk of the masonry directly where the Spear Lord had been standing just a second earlier violently crumbled away, plummeting downward into the fiery Abyss.
The Spear Lord looked back at the gaping chasm that had nearly swallowed him whole.
His murderous fury instantly evaporated, completely replaced by the primal horror of mortality.
"AAAAAAAAAHHHHHHH!"

He dropped his spear slightly, bursting into loud hysterical tears as he immediately turned around and began running significantly faster toward the far end of the cavern, abandoning his revenge in a desperate bid to survive.
Silas rolled his eyes, pushing his Gold Core to its limit as he hit the final stretch.
According to what his perception could see through the settling dust, after he ran up the final violently shaking flight of stairs, the collapsing corridor abruptly ended.
They burst out of the dark tunnels into a massive open expanse.
Floating entirely suspended in the dead center of the cavernous void, held aloft by ancient thrumming anti-gravity runes, was a massive and incredibly wide circular stone platform.
It was the stabilized sector.
That massive floating platform was the only part of the subterranean environment where the tectonic earthquake wasn’t touching.
The air around it was perfectly still, completely separated from the apocalyptic destruction of the labyrinth and currently standing safely on that floating platform were the other surviving Lords!
Silas could immediately see Aeliana, Valerius, and Mia clustered near the far edge, anxiously looking out into the collapsing darkness, scanning the crumbling tunnels for any sign of him.
The very second Aeliana’s glowing silver eyes locked onto Silas’s silhouette emerging from the dust of the final staircase, her pupils dilated into tiny pinpricks of overwhelming relief.
"Lord Sy!" Aeliana cried out, taking a step toward the edge of the platform.
Silas sprinted for the edge of the collapsing corridor, preparing to jump the forty-foot horizontal gap to the floating platform.
However, the dead god’s labyrinth had one final treacherous trick.
The earth directly below Silas’s right combat boot suddenly, violently collapsed into completely pulverized dust!
The Lord didn’t panic.
’You need to be faster than that to catch me off guard...’ Silas thought.

His momentum was already established and he had already pushed off the solid stone a microsecond before it broke, launching himself and Harper into the empty air, soaring directly over the bottomless void toward the safety of the floating arena.
But below them, tragedy struck.
The Spear Lord, who had been desperately running right behind them, wasn’t as fast, and he didn’t have as much momentum.
The edge of the corridor completely crumbled beneath his armored boots before he could jump.
"NOOOOOO!" the Spear Lord screamed in agony as he lost his footing, plummeting downward into the bottomless Abyss.
In a final frantic attempt to save his own life, the falling Spear Lord channeled his unique elemental affinity.
He violently thrust his hand upward, casting a specialized alteration spell.
"Polymer Extension!" he shrieked.
The heavy iron spear in his hand violently morphed.
The rigid metal instantly turned into an elastic and hyper-flexible rubber-like tether.
The Spear Lord whipped the rubberized weapon upward.
The hooked blade of the spear flew through the air, expertly wrapping securely around Silas’s left ankle mid-air!
SNAP!
The sudden, massive drag of a two-hundred-pound armored Lord violently yanking on his leg instantly killed Silas’s forward momentum.
The physics of the extra weight aggressively altered his trajectory as they were going to fall short of the platform and plummet into the Abyss.
Silas hung in the air, feeling the violent tug on his boot. He let out a suffering sigh.
"It’s always something with these people..." Silas muttered under his breath.
Silas didn’t try to kick the hook off as he utilized the physics of the situation.
While entirely suspended over the Abyss, Silas twisted his core, aggressively spinning his entire upper body like a horizontal centrifuge.
He used his own immense physical weight, the rotational power and the elastic tension of the Spear Lord’s spell to execute a flawless mid-air slingshot!
The violent rotational force whipped the Spear Lord completely up from the Abyss.
"WAAAAAAAAAH!" the Spear Lord screamed at the top of his lungs as he was violently launched up and over Silas’s head like a human cannonball.
The screaming noble soared across the massive gap, crashing heavily onto the solid stone of the floating platform and rolling to a bruised groaning halt.

A fraction of a second later, having expertly used the counter-rotational force to secure his own trajectory, Silas landed perfectly on both boots on the edge of the floating platform, completely unharmed.
The moment his boots stabilized on the safe ground, Silas was immediately forced to let go of Harper.
FWOOSH!
Aeliana blurred forward with terrifying speed.
She didn’t just offer a normal polite greeting hug as the usually composed disciplined Arcanist completely abandoned all decorum and professional boundaries.
Aeliana threw her pale arms around Silas’s neck and aggressively attached her entire body to his frame.
She leaped up, wrapping her slender, pale legs tightly around his waist, completely burying her face into his shoulder as she trembled with relief.
"Lord Sy, you’re a big fool!" Aeliana reprimanded him as she squeezed him tight enough to bruise his ribs. "Stop getting into completely suicidal dangerous situations without me covering your flank!"
Silas, caught off guard by the intensity of the embrace, instinctively wrapped his arms securely around her lower back to support her weight with a genuine smile touching his lips.
"I’m alright, Aeli," Silas murmured quietly into her white hair, patting her back. "I made it."
Standing awkwardly beside them, having been unceremoniously dropped to her own two feet, Harper slowly adjusted her head, rubbing her temple where she had bumped it during the landing.
"Ow," Harper muttered, completely disoriented.
She looked around the massive floating platform, taking in the surviving Lords as her confidence instantly evaporated into anxiety.
Standing a few yards away, glaring at her with cold intensity, were both Elora Verinda and Seraphina.
Harper visibly shrank back, instinctively sliding behind Silas’s broad back.
She wanted none of the smoke that inherently followed these two apocalyptic women.
She had already survived their three-way deathmatch once on the surface... Harper wasn’t eager to get vaporized by solar fire or impaled by ice in a confined space.
Across the platform, Maya and her mechanical-armed Archer were sitting heavily on the stone.
They were actively glaring at Harper with undisguised venom for her previous betrayal in the glass storm.
And sitting on the ground directly next to Elora’s boots, looking absolutely hollow, devastated, and deeply traumatized, was Jaxon.
The young Lord was tightly clutching a glowing, perfectly preserved Hero Summoning Card in his trembling hands, staring blankly at the stone floor.
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes flicked toward the card.
He really, really wanted to snag that high-tier item from the boy’s hands to bolster his own Territory’s military strength but as he analyzed the situation, he firmly decided against it.

Given the undeniable fact that Jaxon’s summoned Hero... the swordsman who had guarded his flank on the surface was no longer standing beside him on the platform, Silas could immediately deduce the grim reality.
The guy’s Hero had died for quite a while.
Silas actually felt a brief rare twinge of genuine pity for the kid so he wasn’t going to rob a grieving Lord on a safe platform.
Seraphina, however, was not dealing with grief.
She was dealing with a different and dangerously violent emotion.
The fiery noblewoman stood with her arms crossed tightly under her breasts, her crimson hair blowing wildly in the heavy wind generated by the collapsing labyrinth below them.

Her glowing red eyes darted aggressively between Silas, who was currently holding Aeliana by the thighs, and Harper, who was actively hiding behind his back wearing absolutely nothing but his oversized black trench coat.
’Why the hell did that stupid sadistic god mathematically match those two together in the dark?!’ Seraphina thought frantically with her jealousy spiking to maximum.
Her mind raced. She knew exactly what had happened during their three-way battle.
Harper’s leather armor had been completely destroyed by her solar fire.
If Harper was currently standing here, wearing Silas Graves’s trench coat, it meant she had been completely exposed to the elements.

’If this was the case...’ Seraphina realized with her face flushing a violent shade of red. ’...and considering the physical state she was in after our battle... did that mean Silas had seen her completely naked?!’
Seraphina scowled deeply, her teeth grinding together as she glared daggers at the dark-haired Lord.

’Not only did this fucker see me completely naked behind a sand dune on the very second day...’ Seraphina fumed internally with her hands sparking in white-hot uncontrollable fire. ’...but he also saw this manipulative, lightning-attuned harlot naked too?! In the dark?! Alone in the dungeon?! What an unrepentant shameless man!’
Aeliana, finally pulling herself back slightly from Silas’s neck to look at his face, immediately noticed the heavy black trench coat missing from his broad shoulders.
She slowly turned her head, her glowing green eyes locking directly onto Harper.
Aeliana’s expression went completely blank as the starlight in the cavern visibly dimmed around her.

"You," Aeliana demanded, her voice dropping to a frosty temperature that rivaled ice with her pointed elven ears standing straight up. "I highly request that you take off my Master’s trench coat immediately... It does not belong to you."
Harper blushed deeply, her pale face turning crimson as she clutched the lapels of the dark fabric much tighter around her chest.
She looked away, deeply embarrassed to confess her state in front of the entire Valoria elite.
"I... I can’t," Harper admitted softly, her voice barely a trembling whisper. "I am completely naked underneath."
Seraphina’s scowl deepened into fury.
Her Primordial Fire Spirit mark began to violently glow across the left side of her face, radiating intense heat.
She was about to completely crash out. She was ready to summon a devastating fireball and incinerate both the trench coat and the harlot right off the floating platform.
However, her bound spirit practically pulsed with soothing warmth.
’The Primordial Fire Spirit actively fed a calming rhythm directly into her core, forcibly cooling her raging jealousy down before she could commit mass murder in a Safe Zone.
’I-I’m not jealous... don’t get it wrong, I just don’t think he should be seeing women naked.’
Seraphina took a deep shuddering breath, aggressively crossing her arms and looking away.
Before the tension could escalate into physical violence, Valerius stepped forward, clapping his heavy iron gauntlets together with a loud sound.
"Well!" Valerius announced loudly, smoothly cutting through the lethal hostility.
He walked up to Silas, offering a genuine relieved smirk. "Good job for making it here in one piece, Graves. I thought for sure the sand was going to swallow you and your new... companion."
"I don’t die that easily," Silas replied, finally setting Aeliana securely back down onto her own feet.
Suddenly, the deafening roar of the collapsing labyrinth beneath them began to fade.
The massive floating circular platform violently shuddered as a deep thrum vibrating through the stone floor.
"Congratulations, my surviving little Lords!"
Ititus’s voice boomed directly from the center of the platform, vibrating with genuine finality.
The dead god sounded thrilled that his twisted game had reached its climax.
"You have successfully outrun the destruction and proven your worth!" the god announced. "Now, prepare yourselves for the final ascent!"
The massive stone platform slowly, steadily began moving upward.
It rapidly accelerated, acting as a massive anti-gravity elevator, carrying the surviving Lords straight up through the gaping dark vertical shaft of the labyrinth.
They ascended at terrifying speed with the damp stone walls blurring past them.
They were heading straight up, completely about to violently collide with the solid unbreakable bedrock ceiling of the Abyss!
"Brace yourselves!" Valerius shouted, raising his heavy mythril shield and bracing his boots.
Aeliana grabbed Silas’s arm with her eyes wide.
But there was no impact.

The exact second the platform touched the thick stone ceiling, the ancient magic activated flawlessly as the entire platform, and every single person standing on it, seamlessly phased completely through the solid rock as if it were nothing but an optical illusion.
FWOOSH!

sentences.text: The Spear Lord completely abandoned his survival sprint, violently pivoting his spear.
He aggressively charged at them at full speed with murderous intent, ready to drive his spear right through Harper’s back but Silas didn’t even bother raising his sword.
He simply maintained his wide gap, casually looking over his shoulder as he kept running.
"Watch your step, Noble." Silas said over the wind.
"No seriously, watch your step..."
KRA-KRA-THOOM!
Before the Spear Lord could even throw his weapon, the structural integrity of the ancient stone bridge completely failed.
A massive chunk of the masonry directly where the Spear Lord had been standing just a second earlier violently crumbled away, plummeting downward into the fiery Abyss.
The Spear Lord looked back at the gaping chasm that had nearly swallowed him whole.
His murderous fury instantly evaporated, completely replaced by the primal horror of mortality.
"AAAAAAAAAHHHHHHH!"

He dropped his spear slightly, bursting into loud hysterical tears as he immediately turned around and began running significantly faster toward the far end of the cavern, abandoning his revenge in a desperate bid to survive.
Silas rolled his eyes, pushing his Gold Core to its limit as he hit the final stretch.
According to what his perception could see through the settling dust, after he ran up the final violently shaking flight of stairs, the collapsing corridor abruptly ended.
They burst out of the dark tunnels into a massive open expanse.
Floating entirely suspended in the dead center of the cavernous void, held aloft by ancient thrumming anti-gravity runes, was a massive and incredibly wide circular stone platform.
It was the stabilized sector.
That massive floating platform was the only part of the subterranean environment where the tectonic earthquake wasn’t touching.
The air around it was perfectly still, completely separated from the apocalyptic destruction of the labyrinth and currently standing safely on that floating platform were the other surviving Lords!
Silas could immediately see Aeliana, Valerius, and Mia clustered near the far edge, anxiously looking out into the collapsing darkness, scanning the crumbling tunnels for any sign of him.
The very second Aeliana’s glowing silver eyes locked onto Silas’s silhouette emerging from the dust of the final staircase, her pupils dilated into tiny pinpricks of overwhelming relief.
"Lord Sy!" Aeliana cried out, taking a step toward the edge of the platform.
Silas sprinted for the edge of the collapsing corridor, preparing to jump the forty-foot horizontal gap to the floating platform.
However, the dead god’s labyrinth had one final treacherous trick.
The earth directly below Silas’s right combat boot suddenly, violently collapsed into completely pulverized dust!
The Lord didn’t panic.
’You need to be faster than that to catch me off guard...’ Silas thought.

His momentum was already established and he had already pushed off the solid stone a microsecond before it broke, launching himself and Harper into the empty air, soaring directly over the bottomless void toward the safety of the floating arena.
But below them, tragedy struck.
The Spear Lord, who had been desperately running right behind them, wasn’t as fast, and he didn’t have as much momentum.
The edge of the corridor completely crumbled beneath his armored boots before he could jump.
"NOOOOOO!" the Spear Lord screamed in agony as he lost his footing, plummeting downward into the bottomless Abyss.
In a final frantic attempt to save his own life, the falling Spear Lord channeled his unique elemental affinity.
He violently thrust his hand upward, casting a specialized alteration spell.
"Polymer Extension!" he shrieked.
The heavy iron spear in his hand violently morphed.
The rigid metal instantly turned into an elastic and hyper-flexible rubber-like tether.
The Spear Lord whipped the rubberized weapon upward.
The hooked blade of the spear flew through the air, expertly wrapping securely around Silas’s left ankle mid-air!
SNAP!
The sudden, massive drag of a two-hundred-pound armored Lord violently yanking on his leg instantly killed Silas’s forward momentum.
The physics of the extra weight aggressively altered his trajectory as they were going to fall short of the platform and plummet into the Abyss.
Silas hung in the air, feeling the violent tug on his boot.
He let out a suffering sigh.
"It’s always something with these people..." Silas muttered under his breath.
Silas didn’t try to kick the hook off as he utilized the physics of the situation.
While entirely suspended over the Abyss, Silas twisted his core, aggressively spinning his entire upper body like a horizontal centrifuge.
He used his own immense physical weight, the rotational power and the elastic tension of the Spear Lord’s spell to execute a flawless mid-air slingshot!
The violent rotational force whipped the Spear Lord completely up from the Abyss.
"WAAAAAAAAAH!" the Spear Lord screamed at the top of his lungs as he was violently launched up and over Silas’s head like a human cannonball.
The screaming noble soared across the massive gap, crashing heavily onto the solid stone of the floating platform and rolling to a bruised groaning halt.

A fraction of a second later, having expertly used the counter-rotational force to secure his own trajectory, Silas landed perfectly on both boots on the edge of the floating platform, completely unharmed.
The moment his boots stabilized on the safe ground, Silas was immediately forced to let go of Harper.
FWOOSH!
Aeliana blurred forward with terrifying speed.
She didn’t just offer a normal polite greeting hug as the usually composed disciplined Arcanist completely abandoned all decorum and professional boundaries.
Aeliana threw her pale arms around Silas’s neck and aggressively attached her entire body to his frame.
She leaped up, wrapping her slender, pale legs tightly around his waist, completely burying her face into his shoulder as she trembled with relief.
"Lord Sy, you’re a big fool!" Aeliana reprimanded him as she squeezed him tight enough to bruise his ribs.
"Stop getting into completely suicidal dangerous situations without me covering your flank!"
Silas, caught off guard by the intensity of the embrace, instinctively wrapped his arms securely around her lower back to support her weight with a genuine smile touching his lips.
"I’m alright, Aeli," Silas murmured quietly into her white hair, patting her back.
"I made it."
Standing awkwardly beside them, having been unceremoniously dropped to her own two feet, Harper slowly adjusted her head, rubbing her temple where she had bumped it during the landing.
"Ow," Harper muttered, completely disoriented.
She looked around the massive floating platform, taking in the surviving Lords as her confidence instantly evaporated into anxiety.
Standing a few yards away, glaring at her with cold intensity, were both Elora Verinda and Seraphina.
Harper visibly shrank back, instinctively sliding behind Silas’s broad back.
She wanted none of the smoke that inherently followed these two apocalyptic women.
She had already survived their three-way deathmatch once on the surface...
Harper wasn’t eager to get vaporized by solar fire or impaled by ice in a confined space.
Across the platform, Maya and her mechanical-armed Archer were sitting heavily on the stone.
They were actively glaring at Harper with undisguised venom for her previous betrayal in the glass storm.
And sitting on the ground directly next to Elora’s boots, looking absolutely hollow, devastated, and deeply traumatized, was Jaxon.
The young Lord was tightly clutching a glowing, perfectly preserved Hero Summoning Card in his trembling hands, staring blankly at the stone floor.
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes flicked toward the card.
He really, really wanted to snag that high-tier item from the boy’s hands to bolster his own Territory’s military strength but as he analyzed the situation, he firmly decided against it.

chapters.title: Chapter 203: Offending A God [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: They broke completely through the illusionary ceiling, instantly emerging into a different and breathtakingly immaculate environment.
The floating platform locked perfectly into place, forming the central floor of a massive and brightly illuminated subterranean chamber.
The walls were not damp stone, but polished flawless white marble lined with intricate, branching veins of pure gold.
Hanging from the high vaulted ceiling were dozens of massive, glowing crystal chandeliers that cast a warm radiant light over the room.
And resting perfectly dead center in the room, hovering securely above an ornate inscribed marble pedestal, was a massive glowing core entirely made of swirling, luminous golden sand.
This was the true Realm Core.
And this entire luxurious, immaculate chamber was meant to be the dead god’s ultimate Vault.

"Welcome to the Apex!" Ititus introduced the room, his voice echoing from the marble walls with deep divine pride and overwhelming arrogance. "This is my true Vault! The pinnacle of the Secret Realm! This is where my greatest, most priceless treasures were kept safe from the Ascension War!"
Silas stepped off the platform with his heavy boots clicking sharply against the polished marble floor.
He didn’t look impressed. After all, who would be? This place looked very suspicious.
Silas walked slowly around the glowing Realm Core with his golden-ringed eyes actively scanning every single corner of the massive empty room.
There were no heavy iron chests... There were no racks of glowing Mythril weapons... There were no skill tomes, no divine artifacts and no mountains of Gold.
"Right," Silas stated dryly with his voice echoing in the empty space. "So, what exactly is the treasure? Because all I see in this massive room is a giant ball of gold sand."
At the far end of the luxurious room, resting entirely alone upon a small, elevated velvet cushion, was a beautifully crafted and incredibly ornate glass jar.
Suddenly, the empty glass jar pulsed with a golden light as a voice spoke directly from the container.
"It is I," the voice echoed, filled with immense, unadulterated divine arrogance. "The God of Sand, Ititus! And I... am the only treasure that you will ever need."
The immaculate and brightly illuminated polished white marble walls of the Apex Vault fell into a profound silence.
The dozens of crystal chandeliers hanging from the vaulted ceiling cast a warm, radiant glow over the surviving Lords of the Secret Realm raid.
Every single Lord, Hero, and elemental entity standing on the floating platform was completely frozen in place.

Silas stood near the center of the room with his mythril longsword still resting loosely in his grip and his golden-ringed eyes staring blankly at the transparent ornate glass jar resting on the velvet cushion.
Did he just hear that correctly?
"I’m sorry," Valerius finally broke the agonizing silence, his voice echoing loudly across the massive empty chamber.
The blonde noble stepped forward, his heavy gauntlets clanking against his armored thighs as his face twisting into a mask of pure confusion. "Did you just say... you are the treasure?"
"Indeed!" the dead god Ititus proudly declared, his divine voice vibrating cheerfully from the glowing glass container.
Valerius blinked, looking around the massive completely barren room.
He looked at the giant, swirling ball of golden sand hovering over the pedestal, and then back at the jar.

"Okay, fantastic," Valerius said, his tone dripping with forced politeness and mounting irritation. "We love a good self-esteem moment. But where is the actual treasure this time? Where are the Mythic skill tomes? Where are the Tier 4 weapons? Where are the treasures you have amassed over your lifetime?!"
The glass jar pulsed with a slightly darker offended golden light.

"I just told you, mortal!" Ititus repeated, his voice losing a fraction of its cheerfulness and taking on a defensive tone. "There is no material ’ultimate prize’! I myself am the prize! I am the God of the Eternal Sands! My knowledge, my ancient wisdom, and my divine guidance are worth infinitely more than mere steel or gold! What kind of sane, ambitious person wouldn’t want to have a literal god formally contracted to their territory?!"
Once again, the massive Vault fell into deafening silence.
Aeliana, standing behind Silas, slowly blinked her green eyes with her flawless face completely deadpan.
Mia, perched casually on Aeliana’s shoulder, let out an audible snort of laughter and Elora Verinda crossed her arms with her icy blue eyes narrowing in disbelief.
’I can’t believe my ears...’
Seraphina’s jaw literally dropped open, her red eyes twitching with mounting fury.
Upon seeing everybody’s total, unenthusiastic silence, the sand god quickly attempted to justify his own divine worth.

"Do you simpletons not understand who you are looking at?!" Ititus demanded, his voice booming across the marble room as the golden sand core violently swirled in agitation. "I am a veteran of the Ascension War! I commanded armies of millions! I shaped the very deserts of the mortal realm!"
The god’s voice swelled with immense pride as he began rapidly listing half the things that he had achieved in his ancient life.

"I brought entire empires to their knees!" Ititus boasted loudly. "I constructed pocket dimensions that defied the laws of physics! I even personally took out a giant primordial crimson dragon that caused mass genocide across the western continents! I crushed her beneath a mountain of glass and sealed her away forever!"
Aeliana and Silas exchanged a brief glance.
They both knew exactly which crimson dragon the god was bragging about, considering that the daughter of the very same dragon was currently back in their territory.
However, the rest of the surviving Valoria coalition remained completely silent.
Nobody clapped, nobody bowed and nobody looked even remotely impressed.
The transparent jar pulsed rapidly. The sand god puffed its invisible chest out, his voice echoing with demand.
"Well?!" Ititus shouted. "Continue basking in my glory! Bow before your new divine patron!"
"Are you absolutely fucking kidding me?!"
The furious cracking voice didn’t come from Silas, Valerius, or Seraphina.
It came from the Spear Lord.
The battered, bruised, and traumatized noble violently pushed his way to the front of the group.

His gold armor was heavily dented, his face was covered in soot and dried tears from nearly falling into the Abyss, and his hands were trembling with outrage as he pointed his iron spear directly at the glowing glass jar.

"You made us do all of this... for absolutely no reason?!" the Spear Lord screamed, his voice echoing off the vaulted ceiling. "You forced us through a meat grinder! You dropped us into a death trap, made us fight your psychotic Sand Generals, and collapsed an entire labyrinth on our heads!"
The Spear Lord was hyperventilating.

"Not only did you not even have anything reasonable to offer us," the Spear Lord continued to rant, "but you have actively led to the gruesome deaths of a lot of elite Lords that came down here today! Entire people were wiped out! And for what?! For a jar of talking dirt?!"
"He has a point!" Seraphina suddenly chimed in, stepping forward with her hands igniting in red hot fire.
Her red eyes burned with killing intent as she glared at the jar.
"Secret realm, my ass! This is a complete scam! I could have gotten better higher-tier loot just by doing standard B-Rank subjugation quests at the Lord Association Buildings back in Teres City!"

"This is a farce," Elora Verinda agreed coldly, her blond hair whipping around her face as the temperature in the room plummeted. "You are an impoverishe washed-up deity attempting to trick Lords into carrying your shattered soul out of exile."

"You are really broke!" Valerius Sterling joined the roasting, pointing his heavy mythril sword at the pedestal. "You are poor! You are a destitute impoverished fragment of a forgotten era! Why did you even legally register a Secret Realm with the Sovereign System if all you had to offer was yourself?! We spent days eating things in this fucking miserable desert, losing our Heroes, and there was nothing at the end of it!"
The entire group began shouting at once, fiercely complaining and violently cursing the god for wasting their time, their resources, and their lives.
Throughout the entire, overwhelming barrage of insults, the glowing glass jar remained completely silent.
Silas stood back, his Gold Core slowly vibrating within his chest.
He let out a long sigh. He was incredibly pissed off too. He had fought a Tier 4 artifact, packs of Dire Wolves and monsters as well as an ancient Sand General for absolutely zero financial return.
But as the shouting continued, Silas’s paranoia aggressively flared.
He didn’t like how the usually cheerful, sadistic God had suddenly turned entirely silent under the insults.
"Valerius," Silas muttered, taking a slow step backward and raising his sword. "Shields up... Now."
Before Valerius could even ask why, the god finally spoke.
His voice didn’t boom with arrogance this time. It was a dark sinister whisper that bypassed their ears and resonated directly inside their skulls.
"I was being quite benevolent by offering you my contract," Ititus whispered. "But as of right now..."
KRA-SHATTER!
The ornate, transparent glass jar resting on the velvet cushion violently exploded into a million microscopic fragments!
"...I promise you that you will all die screaming!" the god roared.
The massive swirling core of golden sand hovering over the pedestal instantly destabilized.

Before anybody could even react, before Seraphina could throw a fireball or Valerius could raise his shield, the golden sand violently rushed upward and exploded outward in a catastrophic, omni-directional shockwave!
The golden sand slammed into every single Lord and Hero in the room, completely enveloping them in a suffocating unbreakable cocoon of hardened grit.
FWOOSH!
The physical laws of the Vault completely inverted. The ceiling of the marble chamber instantly dissolved into a massive vertical tunnel leading straight up toward the sky.
"AGGGGH!" Valerius screamed as he was violently ripped off his feet.
The Lords were popped up and launched toward the surface like high-velocity artillery rockets!
Silas felt the immense bone-crushing G-force slam into his chest as he was blasted upward through miles of bedrock, subterranean dirt, and sand at supersonic speed.
The golden sand cocoon protected his body from being shredded by the earth, but the velocity was completely paralyzing.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Like meteors breaking through the earth’s crust, the surviving members of the group violently erupted from the surface of the desert!
They soared hundreds of feet into the blindingly bright, sunlit amber sky before gravity finally caught them.
The golden sand cocoons instantly dissolved, and they each plummeted downward, landing heavily on the rolling sun-baked sand dunes of the surface world.
Silas hit the ground in a flawless roll, instantly bouncing to his feet with his mythril sword drawn and his golden-ringed eyes scanning the horizon.
He was back on the surface.
The sky was bright amber, the heat was baking, and the endless desert stretched out in every direction.

The other Lords... Seraphina, Valerius, Elora, Harper, the Spear Lord, and Maya as well as many others were scattered across the surrounding dunes, coughing and groaning as they picked themselves up from the brutal landing.
"Where is he?!" Seraphina screamed, her hands erupting in flames.
The golden sands that had launched them to the surface didn’t disperse into the wind.
Instead, the millions of grains rapidly coalesced in the dead center of the desert, violently spinning into a towering howling sandstorm.

"I assumed that something like this would happen," the god’s voice echoed from within the roaring vortex. "Mortals are inherently greedy, ungrateful parasites. Which is exactly why I rushed you to my Vault!"
The howling sandstorm began to aggressively compress.
The volume of the golden sand folded in on itself, solidifying and taking on a distinct physical shape.
"If you will not serve me," Ititus declared, "then you will die for me!"
As the dust completely cleared, Silas’s eyes widened in disbelief.
Standing in the center of the desert, formed entirely from luminous golden sand, was a towering, eight-foot-tall man.
The god possessed four massive, heavily muscled arms, his physique sculpted with impossible perfection.
He had long, flowing blond hair made of spun golden glass, and a face that looked like it had been carved by the heavens themselves.
He was a peerless incomprehensible beauty!

He looked at the giant, swirling ball of golden sand hovering over the pedestal, and then back at the jar.
"Okay, fantastic," Valerius said, his tone dripping with forced politeness and mounting irritation.
"We love a good self-esteem moment.
But where is the actual treasure this time?
Where are the Mythic skill tomes?
Where are the Tier 4 weapons?
Where are the treasures you have amassed over your lifetime?!"
The glass jar pulsed with a slightly darker offended golden light.
"I just told you, mortal!" Ititus repeated, his voice losing a fraction of its cheerfulness and taking on a defensive tone.
"There is no material ’ultimate prize’!
I myself am the prize!
I am the God of the Eternal Sands!
My knowledge, my ancient wisdom, and my divine guidance are worth infinitely more than mere steel or gold!
What kind of sane, ambitious person wouldn’t want to have a literal god formally contracted to their territory?!"
Once again, the massive Vault fell into deafening silence.
Aeliana, standing behind Silas, slowly blinked her green eyes with her flawless face completely deadpan.
Mia, perched casually on Aeliana’s shoulder, let out an audible snort of laughter and Elora Verinda crossed her arms with her icy blue eyes narrowing in disbelief.
’I can’t believe my ears...’
Seraphina’s jaw literally dropped open, her red eyes twitching with mounting fury.
Upon seeing everybody’s total, unenthusiastic silence, the sand god quickly attempted to justify his own divine worth.
"Do you simpletons not understand who you are looking at?!" Ititus demanded, his voice booming across the marble room as the golden sand core violently swirled in agitation.
"I am a veteran of the Ascension War!
I commanded armies of millions!
I shaped the very deserts of the mortal realm!"
The god’s voice swelled with immense pride as he began rapidly listing half the things that he had achieved in his ancient life.
"I brought entire empires to their knees!" Ititus boasted loudly.
"I constructed pocket dimensions that defied the laws of physics!
I even personally took out a giant primordial crimson dragon that caused mass genocide across the western continents!
I crushed her beneath a mountain of glass and sealed her away forever!"
Aeliana and Silas exchanged a brief glance.
They both knew exactly which crimson dragon the god was bragging about, considering that the daughter of the very same dragon was currently back in their territory.
However, the rest of the surviving Valoria coalition remained completely silent.
Nobody clapped, nobody bowed and nobody looked even remotely impressed.
The transparent jar pulsed rapidly.
The sand god puffed its invisible chest out, his voice echoing with demand.
"Well?!" Ititus shouted.
"Continue basking in my glory!
Bow before your new divine patron!"
"Are you absolutely fucking kidding me?!"
The furious cracking voice didn’t come from Silas, Valerius, or Seraphina.
It came from the Spear Lord.
The battered, bruised, and traumatized noble violently pushed his way to the front of the group.

His gold armor was heavily dented, his face was covered in soot and dried tears from nearly falling into the Abyss, and his hands were trembling with outrage as he pointed his iron spear directly at the glowing glass jar.
"You made us do all of this... for absolutely no reason?!" the Spear Lord screamed, his voice echoing off the vaulted ceiling.
"You forced us through a meat grinder!
You dropped us into a death trap, made us fight your psychotic Sand Generals, and collapsed an entire labyrinth on our heads!"
The Spear Lord was hyperventilating.

"Not only did you not even have anything reasonable to offer us," the Spear Lord continued to rant, "but you have actively led to the gruesome deaths of a lot of elite Lords that came down here today!
Entire people were wiped out!
And for what?!
For a jar of talking dirt?!"
"He has a point!" Seraphina suddenly chimed in, stepping forward with her hands igniting in red hot fire.
Her red eyes burned with killing intent as she glared at the jar.
"Secret realm, my ass!
This is a complete scam!
I could have gotten better higher-tier loot just by doing standard B-Rank subjugation quests at the Lord Association Buildings back in Teres City!"
"This is a farce," Elora Verinda agreed coldly, her blond hair whipping around her face as the temperature in the room plummeted.
"You are an impoverishe washed-up deity attempting to trick Lords into carrying your shattered soul out of exile."
"You are really broke!" Valerius Sterling joined the roasting, pointing his heavy mythril sword at the pedestal.
"You are poor!
You are a destitute impoverished fragment of a forgotten era!
Why did you even legally register a Secret Realm with the Sovereign System if all you had to offer was yourself?!
We spent days eating things in this fucking miserable desert, losing our Heroes, and there was nothing at the end of it!"
The entire group began shouting at once, fiercely complaining and violently cursing the god for wasting their time, their resources, and their lives.
Throughout the entire, overwhelming barrage of insults, the glowing glass jar remained completely silent.
Silas stood back, his Gold Core slowly vibrating within his chest.
He let out a long sigh.
He was incredibly pissed off too.
He had fought a Tier 4 artifact, packs of Dire Wolves and monsters as well as an ancient Sand General for absolutely zero financial return.
But as the shouting continued, Silas’s paranoia aggressively flared.
He didn’t like how the usually cheerful, sadistic God had suddenly turned entirely silent under the insults.
"Valerius," Silas muttered, taking a slow step backward and raising his sword.
"Shields up...
Now."
Before Valerius could even ask why, the god finally spoke.
His voice didn’t boom with arrogance this time.
It was a dark sinister whisper that bypassed their ears and resonated directly inside their skulls.
"I was being quite benevolent by offering you my contract," Ititus whispered.
"But as of right now..."
KRA-SHATTER!
The ornate, transparent glass jar resting on the velvet cushion violently exploded into a million microscopic fragments!
"...I promise you that you will all die screaming!" the god roared.
The massive swirling core of golden sand hovering over the pedestal instantly destabilized.

Before anybody could even react, before Seraphina could throw a fireball or Valerius could raise his shield, the golden sand violently rushed upward and exploded outward in a catastrophic, omni-directional shockwave!
The golden sand slammed into every single Lord and Hero in the room, completely enveloping them in a suffocating unbreakable cocoon of hardened grit.
FWOOSH!
The physical laws of the Vault completely inverted.
The ceiling of the marble chamber instantly dissolved into a massive vertical tunnel leading straight up toward the sky.
"AGGGGH!" Valerius screamed as he was violently ripped off his feet.
The Lords were popped up and launched toward the surface like high-velocity artillery rockets!
Silas felt the immense bone-crushing G-force slam into his chest as he was blasted upward through miles of bedrock, subterranean dirt, and sand at supersonic speed.
The golden sand cocoon protected his body from being shredded by the earth, but the velocity was completely paralyzing.
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
Like meteors breaking through the earth’s crust, the surviving members of the group violently erupted from the surface of the desert!
They soared hundreds of feet into the blindingly bright, sunlit amber sky before gravity finally caught them.
The golden sand cocoons instantly dissolved, and they each plummeted downward, landing heavily on the rolling sun-baked sand dunes of the surface world.
Silas hit the ground in a flawless roll, instantly bouncing to his feet with his mythril sword drawn and his golden-ringed eyes scanning the horizon.
He was back on the surface.
The sky was bright amber, the heat was baking, and the endless desert stretched out in every direction.
The other Lords...

Seraphina, Valerius, Elora, Harper, the Spear Lord, and Maya as well as many others were scattered across the surrounding dunes, coughing and groaning as they picked themselves up from the brutal landing.
"Where is he?!" Seraphina screamed, her hands erupting in flames.
The golden sands that had launched them to the surface didn’t disperse into the wind.
Instead, the millions of grains rapidly coalesced in the dead center of the desert, violently spinning into a towering howling sandstorm.
"I assumed that something like this would happen," the god’s voice echoed from within the roaring vortex.
"Mortals are inherently greedy, ungrateful parasites.
Which is exactly why I rushed you to my Vault!"
The howling sandstorm began to aggressively compress.
The volume of the golden sand folded in on itself, solidifying and taking on a distinct physical shape.
"If you will not serve me," Ititus declared, "then you will die for me!"
As the dust completely cleared, Silas’s eyes widened in disbelief.
Standing in the center of the desert, formed entirely from luminous golden sand, was a towering, eight-foot-tall man.
The god possessed four massive, heavily muscled arms, his physique sculpted with impossible perfection.
He had long, flowing blond hair made of spun golden glass, and a face that looked like it had been carved by the heavens themselves.
He was a peerless incomprehensible beauty!

chapters.title: Chapter 204: Against A God [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas stared at the god with his jaw clenching tight.
If Silas was considered one of the most handsome men on Earth as of right now, then the god was simply leagues above him.
The deity’s features were so flawless and so mathematically perfect, that it actively commanded the eye to stare.
And that realization pissed Silas off even more.
’Why is this guy so beautiful anyway?!’ Silas thought furiously, his ego taking a direct and completely unnecessary hit. ’He’s a literal pile of dirt! He has no right looking like a damn supermodel!’
The sandstorm around the god’s feet howled louder, whipping across the dunes.
"Come!" Ititus ordered them, extending all four of his perfect, golden arms in a gesture of absolute supremacy. "Face the wrath of the Sands!"
The surviving Valoria Lords, driven by survival instinct and burning outrage, didn’t hesitate.
"Kill him!" Valerius roared with his mythril sword glowing with violent green wind mana.
As the other Lords aggressively charged in his direction, Silas held his ground for a fraction of a second as he didn’t rush in blindly.
Silas wanted information before anything.

’System,’ Silas made a rapid inquiry through his interface. ’Is it mathematically possible for this coalition to defeat Ititus in open combat, even if it is just a fragmented soul left over from the Ascension War?’
A translucent blue tab instantly materialized in front of his retinas.
[System Inquiry Received.]
[Analyzing Combat Variables...]
[Result: Negative. It is quite impossible for your current coalition to defeat this entity in a war of attrition.]
Silas gritted his teeth.
He completely expected that answer. Even a shattered, weakened fragment of a true deity was still a deity.
There was a fundamental reason why gods were considered absolute freaks of nature in the Sovereign Realm.
Their mana capacity, physical density, and elemental absolute-control were completely beyond mortal parameters.
However, the System interface didn’t close. The text rapidly updated, displaying highly classified information.
[However, Entity ’Ititus’ has currently broken two administrative rules of the Sovereign Realm.]

[Rule Violation 1: When a Secret Realm is formally established and bound to the Sovereign Realm itself, the deity or owner of the Realm must be completely deceased. In Ititus’s case, he illegally left a living sentient part of his divine soul actively maintaining the core. The Council of Deities was initially willing to overlook this minor infraction.]

[Rule Violation 2: Entity ’Ititus’ is currently attempting to directly murder the participants inside his Secret Realm without the use of authorized trials, riddles, or monsters. Direct divine intervention against mortal challengers is a violation of the Sovereign Treaty.]
Silas’s eyes widened as he read the glowing blue text.

[The Council of Deities has formally registered this violation. They have instantly authorized and sent a nearby active Deity to completely destroy this Secret Realm and permanently execute Entity ’Ititus’.]
Silas’s heart hammered against his ribs. A true active deity was coming to wipe the floor with the sand god?
’System,’ Silas asked rapidly through his thoughts, ignoring the chaotic battle raging fifty yards away. ’What deity was it? Who is coming?’
There was a small, agonizing loading prompt on the screen.
[The Executioner dispatched by the Council is Thor, the Daughter of Odin. Estimated Time of Arrival: Within a few minutes.]
Upon confirming that name, Silas let out a long slow breath.
Thor.
The Daughter of Odin. If even a fraction of the Norse mythology he knew from Earth held true in this realm, Ititus was about to be turned into a glass parking lot.
Silas sighed, his golden-ringed eyes snapping away from the System tab and focusing dead ahead on the beautiful four-armed god currently batting away Valerius’s wind strikes like annoying flies.
A cold smirk slowly stretched across Silas’s face.
’A few minutes,’ Silas thought. ’However I really need to ensure that I get the absolute last hit on that guy even after Thor arrives.’
If he could legally get the killing blow on a literal god... even a weakened fragment of one... who knew what kind of astronomical UP he would receive?
It would be a monumental amount of power.
Aeliana appeared silently right next to him, her eyes glowing with fierce devotion as a condensed spear of starlight was already humming between her pale hands.
Silas looked at his Hero and they didn’t need to speak. They simply nodded at each other in perfect unison.
BOOOOOOM!
Silas and Aeliana violently pushed off the sand as they rushed forward to join the fray however they were behind and as a result, the Spear Guy arrived first.
"For my Rhino, you golden freak!" he screamed.
He aggressively thrust his hand forward, casting Polymer Extension.
His heavy iron spear violently stretched and whipped through the air like a lethal rubber band as the hooked blade wrapped securely around the god’s lower right arm, attempting to bind the limb.

"Pathetic," Ititus scoffed. The god didn’t even try to pull away as he merely flexed his golden bicep and the density of his sand body, instantly snapping the thick iron spear in half with a loud sound.
CRACK!
But the Spear Lord’s attack was just a distraction.
ZZZZZZZT!
Harper blurred into existence directly above the god’s head.
She had completely activated her blood magic as her pale skin was sparking violently and her purple eyes glowed like twin supernovas as she moved with speed faster than she had moved before.
"Fulgur Execution!" Harper roared.
She drove both of her hands downward, unleashing a catastrophic hyper-condensed pillar of purple lightning directly onto the god’s perfect blond head.
BOOOOOOOOOOOMMMMMM!
The electrical voltage was so intense that the air violently superheated with the ozone cracking like a whip.
Ititus raised his upper left arm, catching the lightning pillar directly in his bare golden palm.
The electrical current violently grounded itself through his body, turning the sand in his arm into glowing, superheated glass, but he didn’t even flinch.
FWOOSH!
While the god was distracted by the lightning, Seraphina arrived on his right flank.
The fiery noblewoman was smiling as her crimson hair had turned entirely silver with the intricate runic mark of her Great Spirit burning violently across her face.
She was begrudgingly forcing her Spirit to perform a combined attack with the rest of the coalition.
"Burn to ash!" Seraphina shrieked, her voice layered with the deep resonance of the Primordial Fire entity.
WHOOOOSH!
She unleashed a massive swirling torrent of pure white-hot solar flames directly at the god’s torso.
The power of the attack was astronomical, instantly flash-melting the sand dunes around them into bubbling pools of liquid glass.
On the completely opposite side of the battlefield, Elora and her summoned Frost Mage Hero were coordinating their assault.
"Glacial Confinement!" Elora commanded with her blond hair whipping around her face as she slammed her hands into the sand.

Her Frost Mage echoed the chant as a massive rapidly expanding wave of ultra-dense blue frost violently raced across the desert floor, completely freezing the sand and aggressively encasing Ititus’s legs in thick unbreakable pillars of ice, attempting to lock him in place while Seraphina roasted his upper body.
Valerius wasn’t idle either. He was hovering thirty feet in the air with his mythril sword glowing with terrifying green light.
"Tempest Severance!" Valerius roared, swinging his blade in a massive horizontal arc.
He unleashed a barrage of pressurized razor-sharp wind blades designed to slice through the god’s four arms.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
And then, Silas, Aeliana, and Mia arrived at the frontline.
Mia was perched securely on Silas’s shoulder.
She didn’t use a massive flashy area-of-effect spell as she pointed her tiny index finger directly at the god’s chest.
"Water Snipe." Mia whispered.
SHWK!
A condensed microscopic needle of heavy water shot from her fingertip at Mach 4.
It possessed the cutting power of a diamond saw. The water needle completely pierced the god’s golden chest, blowing a small, clean hole straight through his torso.
’I’m not too worried, a deity should be on their way by now.’ Silas thought
"Arcane Bombardment!" Aeliana said, hovering right beside Silas using the new spell her Grand Aunt taught her last night.
She drew heavily upon the near-limitless stamina of her Genesis Rune as she thrust her pale hands forward, unleashing a deafening continuous torrent of hyper-dense starlight spheres.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
The orbital bombardment slammed directly into the god’s face and chest, the concussive explosions tearing massive chunks of golden sand away from his flawless body.
And right in the center of the chaos, utilizing the openings created by the barrage, Silas was putting in work.
Silas blitzed into close-quarters combat.
He completely ignored the heat of Seraphina’s flames and the freezing cold of Elora’s ice as his Gold Core aura flared internally, making him much stronger.
His mythril longsword moving with terrifying precision.
KRA-SLASH! SHWK! CLANG!
Silas ducked under a massive golden fist with his blade entirely coated in cutting water mana.
He swung upward, cleanly slicing off the god’s lower left arm.
BAM!
He violently pivoted, driving his boot into the god’s knee joint to shatter the frozen ice, before executing a devastating horizontal cleave that tore deeply into Ititus’s abdomen.
SHHHH!
For the first sixty seconds of the chaotic multi-angled assault, everybody was pulling their best.
They were taking out sand clones the microsecond they formed, shattering glass constructs, and dealing massive, coordinated damage.
At first, it genuinely looked like they were dominating the deity. The god was missing an arm, his chest was riddled with holes, and his golden sand was actively melting into slag.
But then, Ititus sighed.
"You mortals are incredibly annoying," the god muttered, his divine voice completely devoid of pain or exertion.
The god decided to get serious. And when a deity gets serious, the laws of physics simply cease to exist.
KRA-THOOM!
Ititus casually stomped his golden foot against the desert floor.
A massive omni-directional tide of solid golden sand violently erupted outward from his body in a three-hundred-and-sixty-degree shockwave.
The force was astronomical and completely unblockable as the sand tide knocked aside a whole lot of the Lords like ragdolls.
Spear Guy was violently launched into a sand dune.
Valerius’s wind shield shattered instantly, sending the blonde noble spinning through the air.
Harper’s lightning was grounded, and she was blown backward across the glass.
Silas, Aeliana, and Mia were forced to violently disengage, skidding backward fifty yards just to avoid being crushed by the tidal wave of grit.
When the sand tide cleared, Ititus’s body had completely regenerated.
His severed arm was back, his chest was flawless, and his golden hair caught the sunlight.
Only one Lord refused to be blown away...
Seraphina.
The silver-haired proud World Council Magistrate’s daughter held her ground, her boots melting the sand beneath her.
She utilized the maximum output of her Primordial Fire Spirit, completely ignoring the sheer disparity in their power levels.
"I am not afraid of dirt!" Seraphina screamed, violently launching herself directly at the god.
Seraphina utilized her flames flawlessly with her fists moving in a flurry of white-hot strikes.
She drove a blazing right hook into the god’s jaw, following up with a spinning crescent kick that unleashed a wave of solar fire across his chest.
BOOM! CRASH! FWOOSH!
But Ititus was a four-armed god of war.
The Sand God effortlessly parried a white-hot punch with his upper right arm, completely ignoring the heat.
With his lower left arm, he drove a devastating fist directly into Seraphina’s stomach.
"Guh!" Seraphina coughed violently, her silver hair whipping forward as the wind was knocked from her lungs.
Before she could recover, Ititus stepped inside her guard. He used his upper left arm to violently swat her flaming dagger out of her hand, and then he struck.
With his massive flawless golden upper right hand, the god aggressively grabbed Seraphina directly by the throat.
SQUEEZE!
"Come on..."
He effortlessly lifted the struggling, kicking woman entirely off the ground, holding her up by the neck with a single hand.
Seraphina gasped for air with her hands desperately clawing at his golden wrist, her white-hot flames sputtering and dying out against the suffocating density of his divine grip.
Ititus held her suspended in the air, his impossibly beautiful face breaking into a dark and arrogant smirk.
Even gods were allowed to be lustful.
