Silas, Aeliana, and Mia were forced to violently disengage, skidding backward fifty yards just to avoid being crushed by the tidal wave of grit.
When the sand tide cleared, Ititus’s body had completely regenerated.
His severed arm was back, his chest was flawless, and his golden hair caught the sunlight.
Only one Lord refused to be blown away...
Seraphina.
The silver-haired proud World Council Magistrate’s daughter held her ground, her boots melting the sand beneath her.
She utilized the maximum output of her Primordial Fire Spirit, completely ignoring the sheer disparity in their power levels.
"I am not afraid of dirt!" Seraphina screamed, violently launching herself directly at the god.
Seraphina utilized her flames flawlessly with her fists moving in a flurry of white-hot strikes.
She drove a blazing right hook into the god’s jaw, following up with a spinning crescent kick that unleashed a wave of solar fire across his chest.
BOOM!
CRASH!
FWOOSH!
But Ititus was a four-armed god of war.
The Sand God effortlessly parried a white-hot punch with his upper right arm, completely ignoring the heat.
With his lower left arm, he drove a devastating fist directly into Seraphina’s stomach.
"Guh!" Seraphina coughed violently, her silver hair whipping forward as the wind was knocked from her lungs.
Before she could recover, Ititus stepped inside her guard.
He used his upper left arm to violently swat her flaming dagger out of her hand, and then he struck.
With his massive flawless golden upper right hand, the god aggressively grabbed Seraphina directly by the throat.
SQUEEZE!
"Come on..."
He effortlessly lifted the struggling, kicking woman entirely off the ground, holding her up by the neck with a single hand.
Seraphina gasped for air with her hands desperately clawing at his golden wrist, her white-hot flames sputtering and dying out against the suffocating density of his divine grip.
Ititus held her suspended in the air, his impossibly beautiful face breaking into a dark and arrogant smirk.
Even gods were allowed to be lustful.

chapters.title: Chapter 205: Thor, Daughter Of Odin [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: As Seraphina choked, the god’s glowing golden eyes slowly, deliberately trailed down her body.
He observed the way her ruined scorched armor clung to her curves, his gaze drinking in her thrashing form with blatant arrogant appreciation.
"What a fiery, beautiful little mortal," Ititus purred. "Perhaps, before I crush your throat, I should keep you as a concubine in my new—"
SWISH!
The god didn’t get to finish his disgusting sentence.
Silas intercepted instantly.
He simply produced a shockwave, utilizing a highly pressurized burst of water mana directly beneath his boots to slingshot himself horizontally across the battlefield.
Silas closed the distance instantly with his core roaring internally. He channeled every single drop of his water mana directly into the edge of his mythril blade.
"Sever!" Silas roared.
KRA-SLASH!
Silas swung his sword with monstrous physical strength.
The hyper-pressurized water blade sheared completely through the god’s golden bicep, cleanly cutting off the arm that was holding Seraphina by the throat!
The golden arm detached and Seraphina plummeted toward the glass floor, gasping for air.
Silas fluidly dropped his sword, stepping forward to perfectly save Seraphina.
He caught her securely in his strong left arm, pulling her coughing trembling body tightly against his chest.
’I’m only doing this so she forgives me...’ Silas thought, the last thing he wanted was for her to go complain to her Father.
Ititus roared in surprise with his remaining three arms reaching for them but Silas didn’t retreat.
He violently thrust his right palm directly forward, aiming point-blank at the god’s perfect face.
"Drown!" Silas commanded.
He blasted the god with a massive deluge of heavy water, firing gallons of pressurized liquid directly into Ititus’s eyes and mouth, completely soaking the golden sand.
"Ice Transformation!" Silas shouted, his voice echoing with lethal intent.
KRKKKKKKKKK!
The heavy water soaking the god’s head and torso violently flash-froze.
The temperature plummeted to absolute zero, completely encasing the upper half of the deity in an unbreakable block of solid blue ice, temporarily blinding and immobilizing him.
Silas didn’t stick around to admire his work.
Giving himself much-needed space, he kicked off the ground, carrying the coughing Seraphina thirty yards backward, landing securely next to Aeliana.
"Are you alright?" Silas asked, setting Seraphina on her feet.
Seraphina clutched her bruised throat, coughing violently.
Her silver hair slowly faded back to crimson as the Spirit retreated and she looked up at Silas as her red eyes went wide with a complex mixture of intense fury and undeniable gratitude.
"I had him," Seraphina rasped stubbornly, though she didn’t pull away from his grip.
Across the battlefield, a deep echoing laughter began to emanate from within the solid block of blue ice.
KRA-KRA-SHATTER!
The ice exploded outward into powder.
Ititus broke out of it effortlessly with the freezing magic completely unable to hold his divine physical density.
The god landed gracefully on the sand, instantly re-condensing his severed arm and reassuming his perfect flawless four-armed form.
He wasn’t smiling anymore as the arrogant lust was gone, replaced by divine wrath.
"I am done playing with you insects," Ititus declared, his voice shaking the very foundations of the Secret Realm.
The god raised all four of his arms high into the air.
The entire desert violently responded.
Millions of tons of golden sand began to rapidly gather, swirling aggressively into a massive tidal wave that eclipsed the sun.
He was about to completely consume all of them in a single, inescapable burst of crushing sand.
Silas tightened his grip on his sword, preparing to desperately try and steal the final hit before they were buried but he didn’t have to.
KRA-CRACK!
A deafening completely unnatural sound suddenly echoed across the heavens. It sounded exactly like a massive pane of thick glass violently snapping in half.
Everyone including the angry god stopped and looked up.
A massive literal crack went straight through the amber sky of the Secret Realm!
The very fabric of the spatial dimension was physically fracturing under an impossible outside pressure.
It was immediately followed by an explosion so massive and so completely astronomically immense, that it instantly destabilized the entire Secret Realm!
KRA-THOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The concussive shockwave ripped across the desert, instantly vaporizing the god’s apocalyptic sand tidal wave into harmless dust.
The environment of the realm violently failed as in a single fraction of a microsecond, the bright amber day turned to pitch-black night.
The stars didn’t appear as the sky was simply a void of crushing pressure.
Ititus’s flawless, arrogant face instantly went completely, bone-white pale.
The god lowered his four arms, his golden eyes widening in divine terror as he looked up at the shattered sky.
Someone was descending into the Secret Realm.

Through the massive crack in the sky, a blinding bolt of pure white-hot natural lightning violently struck the earth, impacting directly in the center of the battlefield between the Valoria coalition and the terrified sand god.
BOOOOOOM!
The sound of atmospheric thunder rolled across the dunes, so loud and heavy that it physically rattled the teeth in Silas’s skull.
The air instantly filled with the stench of static electricity.
As the light of the lightning strike slowly faded, a single silhouette stood in the center of the smoking vitrified glass crater.
The figure casually rolled her shoulders, dusting a speck of ash from her highly intricate runic-engraved silver armor.
She possessed long, braided blonde hair that crackled with residual static, and in her right hand, she casually held a short-handled war hammer that radiated a terrifying aura.
The woman stood up straight, completely ignoring the awestruck Lords surrounding her.
Then she cleared her throat politely with her voice carrying a calm tone that echoed flawlessly in the dead silence of the night.
"Hello," the woman introduced herself, offering a brief courteous nod to the group. "I am Thor. You may know me as the Daughter of Odin."
She hoisted her war hammer effortlessly, resting the heavy iron head casually against her silver-armored shoulder.
Her piercing electrical blue eyes slowly scanned the silent battlefield.
"Could any of you kindly direct me to the being known as Ititus, the Sand God?" Thor asked politely, an incredibly bright, deeply terrifying smile touching her lips. "I’m here to kill him."
WHOOSH!
The jagged fracture in the sky of the Secret Realm completely defied the fundamental laws of spatial reality.

It wasn’t a mere portal opening, nor was it a simple magical gateway... It was a literal physical tear in the cosmic fabric of the dimension, a violent wound leaking pure starlight into the pitch-black, destabilized void of the surface dungeon.
The sound of that sky ripping open once again was deafening.

It sounded like the screeching of tearing iron multiplied by a million, a frequency so agonizingly high that the remaining Lords and Heroes on the desert floor had to physically clamp their hands over their bleeding ears just to stop their eardrums from bursting.

Through that rippling violent tear in the heavens, a second figure floated down to join the heavily armored, blonde-haired woman who had just cheerfully introduced herself as Thor, the Daughter of Odin.
It was a Druid.
The woman descended gracefully through the freezing static-charged air, ignoring the apocalyptic destruction surrounding them.
She wore long flowing robes woven from living luminescent green vines and deep ancient brown bark that seemed to actively breathe with a heartbeat of its own.
Her eyes were a glowing, pupil-less white, lacking any sort of mortal emotion and she carried a polished wooden staff carved top-to-bottom with the rigid bureaucratic runes of the Council of Deities.
Her bare feet touched down lightly on the vitrified smoking glass of the crater directly beside Thor.

Wherever her toes made contact with the completely sterilized, superheated desert floor, tiny, impossible shoots of green grass instantly forced their way through the glass, aggressively rewriting the environmental laws of the dead god’s realm.
Her sudden silent appearance completely surprised everybody on the battlefield.
The surviving Lords... already paralyzed by the sheer, unadulterated terror of a divine executioner manifesting before them could only watch in breathless silence.
The Druid immediately raised her wooden staff, her glowing white eyes locking flawlessly onto the towering four-armed beautiful golden sand god standing fifty yards away in the center of the dunes.

"Executioner Thor," the Druid announced, her voice echoing with the dry monotone of a cosmic auditor who had clearly worked a double shift. "Target confirmed... That is the rogue entity known as Ititus."
She pointed a long, wooden finger directly at the Sand God.
Thor casually shifted her weight, resting the heavy iron head of her short-handled war hammer comfortably against her silver-plated shoulder.
Her piercing electrical blue eyes slowly dragged over the towering, luminous golden figure of Ititus.
Sensing the world-ending threat level radiating from the newly arrived Norse deity, Ititus’s paranoia should have violently flared.
He should have dropped to his knees, begged for Council amnesty, or immediately attempted to phase his core into the deepest bedrock of the planet to hide.
But his divine arrogance was a terminal incurable disease.
The Sand God actually puffed out his flawlessly sculpted golden chest.
He used one of his four massive hands to casually run his fingers through his shimmering, spun-glass blonde hair, ensuring he looked absolutely perfect for his impending confrontation.

"I am Ititus!" the Sand God proclaimed loudly, his voice vibrating with narcissistic pride that bordered on the psychotic. "The Sovereign of the Eternal Sands! And as you can clearly see with your own eyes, newcomer, I am undoubtedly one of the most handsom—"
"You look absolutely ridiculous," Thor interrupted him.
Her voice was deadpan, completely lacking any awe, respect, or even basic baseline politeness.
Ititus’s jaw literally dropped. The flowing golden sand of his pristine face froze in outrage at being cut off mid-sentence.

"You are literally just microscopic grains of dirt and sand magically melded together to form a shape," Thor stated bluntly, squinting her blue eyes critically at his glowing meticulously crafted physique as if examining a terribly painted portrait. "It isn’t even real flesh. You look incredibly fake. Honestly, it’s embarrassing... Even the fat, bald-headed men drinking cheap ale in the lowest, filthiest taverns of Asgard look significantly better than you."
Thor aggressively squeezed her flawless face into a deeply unimpressed disgusted grimace, her nose wrinkling in revulsion as if she were looking at a steaming pile of rotting goblin garbage.
The disrespect completely shattered Ititus’s fragile ego.
His flawless golden face violently contorted into a mask of pure, unbridled divine wrath.
The luminous sand making up his broad shoulders began to actively boil and hiss, his four hands clenching into massive fists that cracked the glass beneath his boots.
But before the Sand God could retaliate, before he could even draw a breath to formulate a curse, the true reality of Thor’s physical presence finally settled over the battlefield.
BZZZZZZZT...
The ambient atmospheric pressure in the vicinity violently multiplied.
It didn’t happen gradually. It was an instant, crushing weight that fell from the sky like a descending tectonic plate.
The other Lords and Heroes in the vicinity... Seraphina, Valerius, Elora, Harper, the Spear Lord, and other Lords were completely silent.
They were physically unable to move their bodies.
It wasn’t because they didn’t want to run as their survival instincts were screaming at maximum volume, begging them to sprint for the horizon.
It was strictly because of the suffocating gravitational pressure that was passively leaking out of Thor’s silver armor.
It felt like a ten-ton block of solid, cold iron had been violently dropped directly onto their spines.
The air was so incredibly thick with pure electrical mana that drawing a breath felt like trying to inhale liquid lead.
Harper, a Lightning Lord who had just spent the last hour throwing catastrophic bolts of purple electricity, felt her own Lord core completely shut down.
The purple static in her veins went dead.
She was utterly terrified into complete submission, her knees buckling against the sand as she realized she was standing in the presence of the predator of her own elemental affinity.
Seraphina’s white-hot solar flames died out completely, her Primordial Spirit retreating deep into her soul, refusing to even manifest a single spark in the presence of the Daughter of Odin.
Valerius dropped to his hands and knees with his mythril sword slipping from his numb fingers.
Only one single mortal on the entire battlefield managed to defy the total paralysis.
Silas Graves.

chapters.title: Chapter 206: Thor’s Power [I]
paragraphs: Silas’s Gold Core burned like a dying star inside his chest.
His willpower fought a brutal internal war against the divine gravity pressing down on his skull.

Silas’s heavy combat boots were planted firmly into the melted glass with his leg muscles bulging to the point of tearing, his veins pressing thick and blue against his neck as he forced his head to turn a fraction of an inch to look at the blonde executioner.
He could move but he found it incredibly hard to do so.
Every single millimeter of movement cost him an astronomical amount of physical stamina. His lungs burned and his vision swam with dark spots.
’This...’ Silas thought, his golden-ringed eyes trembling as he stared at Thor’s relaxed uncaring posture. ’This is the actual terrifying difference between a Lord and a true Deity.’
The Lord in that moment realized in that suffocating microsecond that they were leagues, oceans, entire galaxies apart.
It wasn’t a matter of training harder or finding better skill tomes...
The gap was so fundamentally immense that most people could not even comprehend matching Thor’s baseline passive power in a hundred lifetimes.
She wasn’t even flexing her aura... she was just standing there, and her mere existence was crushing Lords into the dirt.
If Silas ever wanted to reach that ultimate peak, his Mythic Gold Core wasn’t a trump card... it was merely the starting line.
Beside the terrifying thunder god, the bureaucratic Druid tapped her wooden staff against the glass crater with a sharp sound.

"Executioner Thor," the Druid instructed, her voice was strictly professional and completely unaffected by the crushing atmospheric pressure. "Please proceed by protocol. You must ask the target the two administrative questions before carrying out the termination warrant... We need this formally recorded for the Council archives."
Thor let out an exasperated sigh, her braided blonde hair crackling with stray arcs of blue static.
She rolled her shoulders, clearing her throat and suddenly looking incredibly serious as she prepared to officially address the rogue god.
She stood tall, her face setting into an expression of grim unyielding justice.
Then, she paused.
Thor blinked her bright electrical blue eyes.
She slowly bent over at the waist, leaning her head down toward the significantly shorter Druid, completely breaking her intimidating posture.
"Hey," Thor whispered loudly, her serious executioner persona entirely vanishing into cluelessness. "What the hell were the questions again? Was I supposed to bring a paper or something?"
The Druid closed her glowing white eyes.
She reached up with her free hand, violently pinching the bridge of her nose as she let out a long suffering sigh that echoed across the quiet desert.
’Why... What am I even doing with my life at this point?’
She had spent millennia studying the sacred texts of the world trees, only to end up babysitting an airheaded hammer-wielding thunder god who treated cosmic bureaucracy like a tedious tavern chore.
"Question one," the Druid whispered back through tightly gritted teeth, her patience hanging by a microscopic thread. "Ask the person their formal name and their divine title."
"Right! I knew that!" Thor perked up instantly, her serious expression snapping right back into place as she stood up straight and pointed her massive war hammer directly at the Sand God.
"You there! Dirt-man!" Thor commanded loudly with her voice booming like a war horn. "State your formal name and your divine title for the official Deity Council record! And speak clearly!"
Ititus sneered, his four golden arms crossing over his massive sculpted chest.

He actively welcomed the opportunity to hear his own voice echo across the realm. If he was going to execute this arrogant upstart, he would do so after properly announcing his glory though he already did so before.

"I am Ititus!" he proclaimed, his voice booming across the desert, instantly launching into a massive glaze fest. "I am the God of the Eternal Sands! The Architect of the Glass Mountains! The Sovereign of the Endless Dunes! I am the Slayer of the Primordial Crimson Dragon! The master of a million shifting grains! The Lord who shaped the western continents! I am the undying storm, the heat of the sun, the—"

"Yeah, yeah, whatever, that’s enough," Thor interrupted him instantly right in the middle of his glaze fest, completely waving off his legendary titles with her free hand like a bored bartender cutting off a rambling drunk.
Ititus’s jaw snapped shut with an audible click.
His golden eyes twitched violently with murderous fury at being so casually disrespected twice in the span of two minutes.
Thor leaned back down toward the exasperated Druid. "What’s the next one?"
"Ask him why they had violated the rules," the Druid supplied tiredly, not even bothering to open her eyes.
Thor nodded, turning her electrical blue eyes back to the complaining thoroughly pissed-off Sand God.

"Question two!" Thor shouted, pointing her hammer at the complaining man. "Why exactly did you violate the Sovereign rules by trying to directly murder these mortal challengers in your Secret Realm without a proper trial?!"
Ititus’s four arms dropped to his sides, the golden sand making up his body aggressively flaring with terrifying, localized heat that began to melt the ground beneath his boots.

"I defied those pathetic bureaucratic rules because I am a true Deity!" Ititus roared, his voice shaking the cracked amber sky above them. "I am a god of the old world! Some weak paper-pushing council of modern gods cannot tell me what to do in my own Secret Realm! These mortals are nothing but parasitic insects! They exist solely to feed my core!"
Ititus pointed a massive flawless golden finger directly at Thor, a sadistic, deeply arrogant smirk crossing his face as he openly declared his intentions.

"And regardless of whatever administrative nonsense you spout right now, executioner," Ititus threatened, his divine aura expanding violently outward, pushing against the crushing weight of Thor’s gravity. "Once you have turned around and left this realm, I will be brutally murdering every single one of these mortals for the sheer disrespect they showed me in my Vault! I will grind their bones into my sands!"
Thor didn’t flinch at the threat and she didn’t look intimidated.
Instead, a slow dangerous smile stretched across Thor’s flawless face. The static electricity in the air violently multiplied with the ozone stench becoming suffocating.

"Once I leave?" Thor repeated, her voice dropping into a low vibrating rumble of atmospheric thunder that sent shivers down Silas’s spine. "You delusional, fragile pile of sand... you will not be leaving this realm alive today."
Thor slowly lowered her war hammer, her blue eyes locking onto Ititus with absolute, unyielding righteous fury.

"I am generally not one for reading the rulebooks," Thor admitted casually, cracking her silver-armored neck with a sharp pop. "But you have directly threatened the innocent lives of Midgard’s people and that... that is more than enough to make me incredibly mad."
Thor was quite deeply intrigued by Midgard.

Her father, the All-Father Odin, had come from there. He had casually called it ’Earth’ in his initial stories, but ’Midgard’ was how the realm was officially known over in the golden towering halls of Asgard.
Midgard was a chaotic, beautiful, messy little blue sphere. It had incredible, violent entertainment, but mostly, it had food!
The mortals down there knew how to properly roast a massive haunch of boar.
They knew how to brew thick, dark ale that actually burned the throat, unlike the overly sweet, delicate meads the Elves of Alfheim constantly tried to push on her.
Thor loved Midgardian feasts. She loved the roaring fires, the loud taverns, and the unbridled resilience of humanity.
And last but absolutely not least, it was her Home world.
It didn’t matter if her father had married a deity to conceive her. It didn’t matter that she lived in a cosmic palace.
She was still technically part Midgardian. The blood of Earth, the stubborn unyielding grit of humanity ran directly through her immortal veins.
Which was exactly why she was going to fight for them today... She wasn’t going to let some washed-up narcissistic pile of sentient dirt murder her people just to stroke his own ego.
"What exactly are you going to do to me, little thunder-girl?" Ititus teased her, mocking her protective stance.
He raised all four of his massive arms with massive vortexes of black razor-sharp sand violently generating in his open palms. "You think you can execute me in my own domain?! I am immortal!"
Sensing the catastrophic shift in Thor’s aura, the bureaucratic Druid didn’t hesitate for a single microsecond.
The Druid violently slammed the butt of her wooden staff directly into the vitrified glass of the crater.
"Aegis of the Council!" the Druid chanted rapidly.
FWOOSH!
A massive translucent green barrier of pure, high-tier nature magic instantly erupted outward.

The spherical dome completely encapsulated the Druid, Silas, Aeliana, Valerius, Seraphina, Harper, Elora, and the rest of the surviving Lords, entirely sealing them safely away from the impending blast zone.

The Druid knew exactly what horrific world-ending things the Daughter of Odin was capable of when she stopped holding back, and she wasn’t about to let the mortal witnesses get vaporized as collateral damage.
Once the protective barrier was safely established behind her, sealing the Midgardians away from the fallout, Thor grinned.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Thor simply squeezed the handle of her weapon and swung her hammer in a casual, one-handed horizontal arc from fifty yards away.
The acceleration of the iron head completely tore the fabric of space.

The resulting sonic boom was so massive that the shockwave visibly rippled through the air, completely shattering the massive vortexes of sand generating in Ititus’s hands before they could even be launched.
Ititus was not even aware of the exact microsecond he started flying.
One moment, the Sand God was standing tall, arrogantly preparing to cast a desert-consuming sandstorm with a cruel sneer on his flawless face.
The next moment, a terrifying imperceptible blur of silver and blue lightning connected perfectly with his golden torso.
KRA-SHATTER!
Ititus felt an impossible world-ending force slam into his existence.
He realized, in a state of paralyzing shock, that he was currently flying backward through the air at Mach 20.

’What... what just happened?!’ Ititus panicked wildly in his thoughts with his divine consciousness violently spinning as he soared through the air as the horizon blurring into a smear of amber and black. ’I couldn’t even see her move! Where are my arms?! Why can’t I feel my arms?!’
He tried to look down at his perfect four-armed golden body to assess the damage.
He couldn’t.
His head was completely gone.
Hell, his entire physical body was completely gone.
The blunt-force trauma of Thor’s hammer swing hadn’t just broken his physical form... it had instantaneously atomized his massive eight-foot golden sand body into microscopic scattered dust!
The shockwave had literally deleted his physical body from reality in a fraction of a second.
Only his true, glowing, spherical Realm Core remained, completely exposed and violently shooting backward across the desert like a skipped stone.
The core crashed brutally through five massive sand dunes, carving a mile-long trench of vitrified glass before finally coming to a halt far away from the initial impact site.

’What is this monster?!’ Ititus screamed internally with terror flooding his soul for the first time in ten thousand years. ’She just deleted my entire physical body with a single swing! She didn’t even use a spell! She just hit me!’
Hovering over the ruined desert dunes, the naked, glowing Realm Core frantically pulsed with desperate energy.
It aggressively pulled upon the millions of tons of ambient sand surrounding it, desperate to reestablish a physical anchor.
FWOOSH!
Within three seconds, Ititus reformed himself. The desert sand violently coalesced, rushing upward to rebuild his flawless, four-armed golden physique.
But he was no longer arrogant.

He was panting with his golden chest heaving as his eyes were wide with panic. Ititius stared across the miles of desert at the blonde woman who was casually resting her hammer back on her shoulder, looking completely bored.
"Is that it?!" Thor yelled across the miles with her voice echoing like rolling thunder. "I thought you said you were a god!"
Ititus roared in absolute fury, his divine pride violently overriding his newfound terror.
KRA-KRA-THOOM!
The Sand God slammed all four of his massive golden palms directly into the desert floor.
He didn’t hold back a single drop of his remaining divine mana.
The entire tectonic plate of the Secret Realm groaned in agony as the desert actively rose up to answer his call.
"Die, you filth!" Ititus shrieked, blood vessels of glowing light bulging on his golden neck.

His willpower fought a brutal internal war against the divine gravity pressing down on his skull.

Silas’s heavy combat boots were planted firmly into the melted glass with his leg muscles bulging to the point of tearing, his veins pressing thick and blue against his neck as he forced his head to turn a fraction of an inch to look at the blonde executioner.

Every single millimeter of movement cost him an astronomical amount of physical stamina.
His lungs burned and his vision swam with dark spots.
’This...’ Silas thought, his golden-ringed eyes trembling as he stared at Thor’s relaxed uncaring posture. ’This is the actual terrifying difference between a Lord and a true Deity.’
The Lord in that moment realized in that suffocating microsecond that they were leagues, oceans, entire galaxies apart.
It wasn’t a matter of training harder or finding better skill tomes...
The gap was so fundamentally immense that most people could not even comprehend matching Thor’s baseline passive power in a hundred lifetimes.
She wasn’t even flexing her aura... she was just standing there, and her mere existence was crushing Lords into the dirt.
If Silas ever wanted to reach that ultimate peak, his Mythic Gold Core wasn’t a trump card... it was merely the starting line.

Thor let out an exasperated sigh, her braided blonde hair crackling with stray arcs of blue static.
She rolled her shoulders, clearing her throat and suddenly looking incredibly serious as she prepared to officially address the rogue god.
She stood tall, her face setting into an expression of grim unyielding justice.
Then, she paused.
Thor blinked her bright electrical blue eyes.
She slowly bent over at the waist, leaning her head down toward the significantly shorter Druid, completely breaking her intimidating posture.
"Hey," Thor whispered loudly, her serious executioner persona entirely vanishing into cluelessness.
"What the hell were the questions again?
Was I supposed to bring a paper or something?"
The Druid closed her glowing white eyes.
She reached up with her free hand, violently pinching the bridge of her nose as she let out a long suffering sigh that echoed across the quiet desert.
’Why...
What am I even doing with my life at this point?’
She had spent millennia studying the sacred texts of the world trees, only to end up babysitting an airheaded hammer-wielding thunder god who treated cosmic bureaucracy like a tedious tavern chore.
"Question one," the Druid whispered back through tightly gritted teeth, her patience hanging by a microscopic thread.
"Ask the person their formal name and their divine title."
"Right!
I knew that!" Thor perked up instantly, her serious expression snapping right back into place as she stood up straight and pointed her massive war hammer directly at the Sand God.
"You there!
Dirt-man!" Thor commanded loudly with her voice booming like a war horn.
"State your formal name and your divine title for the official Deity Council record!
And speak clearly!"
Ititus sneered, his four golden arms crossing over his massive sculpted chest.
He actively welcomed the opportunity to hear his own voice echo across the realm.
If he was going to execute this arrogant upstart, he would do so after properly announcing his glory though he already did so before.
"I am Ititus!" he proclaimed, his voice booming across the desert, instantly launching into a massive glaze fest.
"I am the God of the Eternal Sands!
The Architect of the Glass Mountains!
The Sovereign of the Endless Dunes!
I am the Slayer of the Primordial Crimson Dragon!
The master of a million shifting grains!
The Lord who shaped the western continents!
I am the undying storm, the heat of the sun, the—"

"Yeah, yeah, whatever, that’s enough," Thor interrupted him instantly right in the middle of his glaze fest, completely waving off his legendary titles with her free hand like a bored bartender cutting off a rambling drunk.
Ititus’s jaw snapped shut with an audible click.
His golden eyes twitched violently with murderous fury at being so casually disrespected twice in the span of two minutes.
Thor leaned back down toward the exasperated Druid.
"What’s the next one?"
"Ask him why they had violated the rules," the Druid supplied tiredly, not even bothering to open her eyes.
Thor nodded, turning her electrical blue eyes back to the complaining thoroughly pissed-off Sand God.
"Question two!" Thor shouted, pointing her hammer at the complaining man.
"Why exactly did you violate the Sovereign rules by trying to directly murder these mortal challengers in your Secret Realm without a proper trial?!"
Ititus’s four arms dropped to his sides, the golden sand making up his body aggressively flaring with terrifying, localized heat that began to melt the ground beneath his boots.
"I defied those pathetic bureaucratic rules because I am a true Deity!" Ititus roared, his voice shaking the cracked amber sky above them.
"I am a god of the old world!
Some weak paper-pushing council of modern gods cannot tell me what to do in my own Secret Realm!
These mortals are nothing but parasitic insects!
They exist solely to feed my core!"
Ititus pointed a massive flawless golden finger directly at Thor, a sadistic, deeply arrogant smirk crossing his face as he openly declared his intentions.

"And regardless of whatever administrative nonsense you spout right now, executioner," Ititus threatened, his divine aura expanding violently outward, pushing against the crushing weight of Thor’s gravity.
"Once you have turned around and left this realm, I will be brutally murdering every single one of these mortals for the sheer disrespect they showed me in my Vault!
I will grind their bones into my sands!"

chapters.title: Chapter 207: Thor’s Power [II]
paragraphs: Millions of tons of golden sand violently erupted into the sky, aggressively compressing and solidifying into a thousand massive fifty-foot-long spears of jagged, superheated desert glass.
The sky above Thor completely darkened, entirely eclipsed by an apocalyptic rain of divine artillery. The heat radiating from the glass spears began to actively boil the air.
With a sweeping desperate gesture of his four arms, Ititus launched the thousand glass spears directly at Thor.
It was a meteor shower of destruction, moving at terminal velocity.
From the safety of the Druid’s green barrier, Silas watched the incoming artillery strike with his mind calculating the math.
Any single one of those fifty-foot glass spears contained enough kinetic and magical power to completely wipe his entire group off the map.
To see a thousand of them descending at once was mind-numbing.
Thor didn’t even blink. She didn’t raise a shield neither did she cast a protective ward.
She stepped forward, casually spinning her massive war hammer by its thick leather strap.
"Let me introduce you to my armory, dirt-man!" Thor yelled cheerfully over the roaring wind of the descending spears.
She pulled her arm back, her muscles coiling tight, and threw her hammer directly into the sky.
"Mjölnir!" Thor announced proudly.
BOOOOOOM!
The iron hammer shot from her hand like a nuclear missile, trailing a massive tail of pure, white-hot lightning that illuminated the entire desert.
Mjölnir possessed true ancient traits that completely defied the modern magic system of the Sovereign Realm.
It didn’t just fly on a parabolic arc... it actively hunted. The hammer never, ever missed its designated target and it possessed a terrifying sentience of its own.
Mjölnir violently crashed into the descending storm of glass spears and the hammer aggressively ricocheted in mid-air at impossible, hyper-sonic speeds.
CRASH-CRASH-SHATTER-BOOM!
In less than two seconds, Mjölnir violently zigzagged thousands of times across the darkened sky, moving so fast it looked like a continuous web of unbroken lightning.

The hammer completely pulverized every single one of the thousand fifty-foot glass spears into completely harmless, glittering dust before they could even get within a hundred yards of Thor’s silver boots.
Ititus stared in horror as his ultimate spell was reduced to a shimmering shower of glitter.
Having absolutely annihilated the divine artillery strike, Mjölnir didn’t fall to the earth.
It instantly reversed its trajectory, defying all laws of momentum.
The heavy iron weapon flew backward through the air like a loyal lethal boomerang, perfectly snapping back into Thor’s waiting outstretched hand with a deafening sound.
THWACK!
But Thor wasn’t done showing off her gear.
Ititus, seeing his ultimate attack effortlessly swatted out of the sky by a flying piece of iron, screamed in frustration.
"AHHHHHHHHH!"
He refused to be humiliated as he raised his four arms again, channeling the deep moisture of the realm.

He summoned a massive, hundred-foot-tall, mile-wide tsunami of boiling, liquid glass mixed with hyper-condensed black sand, intending to completely wash over her position and bury her under a molten mountain.
The tidal wave roared across the desert, swallowing the dunes in its path.
Thor didn’t throw the hammer this time. She reached down with her free left hand, tapping a thick runed iron belt clasped tightly around her narrow waist.
"And this beauty," Thor boasted loudly, her voice booming with pride as she completely ignored the incoming mile-wide tsunami of liquid death, "is Megingjörð! My Belt of Power!"
The ancient runes carved into the iron belt violently flared with blinding oceanic blue light.
When Thor wore Megingjörð, her already immense god-like physical strength wasn’t just slightly enhanced by a percentage buff... it was literally doubled.
It perfectly explained to Silas exactly why her physical density was so astronomical.
It was the reason why she could casually brush off the atmospheric pressure of the realm, and why she could completely atomize an eight-foot god with a single one-handed swing.
’Her physical stats are broken beyond repair.’
Thor firmly planted her silver boots into the vitrified glass of the crater.
"Come!"
As the hundred-foot tsunami of boiling liquid glass crashed down directly toward her head, Thor simply raised her free left hand with her palm open as she was completely unguarded.
KRA-THOOM!
She literally caught the hundred-foot tsunami of liquid glass with her bare hand!
The doubled physical strength of her body completely arrested the millions of tons of momentum in an instant.
The massive tidal wave violently stopped dead in its tracks the microsecond it touched her palm.
The boiling glass buckled, groaned, and then catastrophically shattered against her hand like a fragile pane of window glass hitting a reinforced titanium wall.
Millions of gallons of liquid sand rained down harmlessly around her, completely unable to push her back a single inch.
"Impossible!" Ititus shrieked, clutching his perfect golden hair with all four of his hands with his mind breaking. "You cannot physically stop a mountain with flesh!"
Inside the green barrier, the bureaucratic Druid violently slammed her wooden staff against the floor, her white eyes flashing with deep irritation.

"Executioner Thor!" the Druid yelled over the roaring destruction. "Stop explaining your divine armory to the target! It is completely against Council protocol to monologue about your equipped artifacts! Just execute him and let us go home!"
Thor glanced back over her silver-plated shoulder, offering the exasperated rule-obsessed Druid a cheeky dismissive grin.

"Why should I bother keeping secrets, tree-hugger?" Thor yelled back, casually swatting away a massive falling chunk of molten glass with the flat side of Mjölnir. "He isn’t going to live past today anyway! Let the dirt-man know exactly what killed him! It’s polite!"
Thor turned her bright electrical blue eyes back to the terrified Sand God. She held up both of her hands, wiggling her armored fingers.
Covering both of her hands and forearms up to the elbows were thick incredibly intricate silver-and-iron gauntlets that aggressively sparked with continuous violent violet static.
"And these!" Thor continued her enthusiastic mid-battle exposition, practically glowing with pride as she showed off her gauntlets. "These beauties are Járngreipr! My Gauntlets!"
Ititus gritted his teeth, his panic evolving into desperate cornered-animal aggression.
He began rapidly channeling mana, attempting to form a massive, spinning buzzsaw of hyper-dense obsidian sand in his two upper arms, aiming to slice her in half.

"You see," Thor yelled across the battlefield, completely ignoring his charging attack, "my hammer, Mjölnir, is absolutely perfect. It really is. But the handle was forged too short! And do you know why?!"
Thor shook her head, a brief flash of deep sibling annoyance crossing her face.

"Because that treacherous, scheming, shape-shifting witch of a sister I have, Loki, completely interfered with the dwarven blacksmiths during its creation! She bit the blacksmith in the eye as a fly just to ruin the forging process!"
Thor sighed, shaking her head at the memory of Loki’s pranks.

"Because the handle is so short," Thor explained as she locked eyes with the god. "the catastrophic force of swinging it at full power would completely shatter my own hands into a bloody pulp! So, I must wear these magical iron gloves to wield it properly!"

’Why is she telling me this?!’ Ititus panicked in his internal thoughts with his mind fracturing under the humiliating absurdity of the situation. ’Why is this absolute monster giving me a weapon lore lesson while she systematically destroys my entire realm?! Why did I ever open this Secret Realm?! Why didn’t I just stay hidden in the Vault?!’
A soul-crushing wave of regret flooded his divine core.
He had picked a fight with mortals, and in return, the universe had sent him a walking natural disaster.
"Now that we’re properly acquainted," Thor announced.
Her bright smile instantly vanished, completely replaced by the cold terrifying frown of the Council’s Executioner.
The air temperature plummeted as the static electricity in the air became so thick it visibly arched between the sand dunes.
Thor tightened her iron-gauntleted grip around the short, leather-wrapped handle of Mjölnir.
"Let’s see if you can survive a direct hit, Ititus."
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Thor didn’t throw the hammer this time as she charged.
She exploded across the desert floor, completely breaking the sound barrier ten times over in a single step.
The concussive shockwave of her sprint violently kicked up a massive wake of pulverized glass and molten sand that trailed behind her like the fiery tail of a descending comet.

Ititus shrieked in terror as he threw the massive spinning obsidian buzzsaw directly at her face, while simultaneously erecting a dozen thick, heavily reinforced walls of compressed golden sand to block her path.
Thor didn’t even slow down, hell she didn’t attempt to dodge.
CRASH! SHATTER! KRA-THOOM!
She unga-bunga’d completely through his best defenses.
She swung Mjölnir in rapid devastating and crushing arcs.
The iron war hammer completely pulverized the incoming obsidian buzzsaw into microscopic dust with a single strike.

She didn’t weave around the massive sand walls... she violently smashed straight through the dead center of them, leaving massive, gaping holes in the heavily reinforced masonry as if she were walking through wet paper.
Ititus desperately tried to phase his golden body into intangible sand to escape the incoming strike with his four arms dissolving into grit.
But Thor was already there.
She leaped high into the air, her entire silhouette completely eclipsed by blinding, white-hot natural lightning.
She raised Mjölnir high above her head with both of her iron-gauntleted hands, channeling the maximum doubled physical strength of Megingjörð directly into the short handle.
"Midgard sends its regards!" Thor roared, her voice vibrating with apocalyptic thunder.
She brought the war hammer down directly toward the dead center of the Sand God’s skull.
The descending iron head of Mjölnir carried the apocalyptic weight of an entire falling moon.
It completely bypassed the physical laws of the Sovereign Realm.
It tore through the ambient oxygen, leaving a vacuum in its wake that completely deafened the battlefield.
For a fraction of a microsecond, as the war hammer plummeted directly toward the dead center of the Sand God’s flawless golden skull, time itself seemed to violently freeze.
In that frozen microsecond, suspended between absolute divinity and absolute oblivion, Ititus experienced a profound soul-tearing revelation.
’I am going to die,’ the Sand God realized with the terror completely eclipsing his narcissistic arrogance.
His divine consciousness frantically calculated the incoming trajectory.
There was no dodging... There was no blocking... The blonde monster above him was wielding an artifact forged to shatter planets, and she was doing it with mathematically doubled physical strength.

’Why did I open this realm?!’ Ititus screamed in his own thoughts with the regret tearing at his divine core. ’Why did I taunt those miserable mortals?! I should have stayed in the Vault! I should have stayed asleep!’
But Ititus was a veteran of the Ascension War.
He was a creature born from cosmic violence, and he was absolutely not going to simply kneel and let an executioner turn him into a glass parking lot.
If he was going to die, he would drag this arrogant thunder-girl into the void with him.
"I AM THE ARCHITECT!" Ititus roared, his voice completely defying the vacuum of space as his golden eyes ignited with blinding, suicidal white light.
In the face of death, the Sand God abandoned all pretense of physical preservation.
He bypassed the safety limiters of his own soul and forcefully triggered a catastrophic sacrificial state of divine existence.
He achieved True Singularity.
KA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A shockwave of utterly incomprehensible world-ending magnitude violently rippled across the entire Secret Realm.
It wasn’t just a blast of air.
Every single, microscopic grain of sand within a fifty-mile radius was aggressively, instantaneously magnetized toward the god’s core, completely stripping the desert floor bare.

The rolling golden dunes, the deep subterranean quicksand, the swirling storms... all of it violently shot outward in a massive, expanding dome of hyper-condensed terrestrial pressure, completely peeling the desert away to reveal the raw, blackened bedrock of the realm itself.
The Secret Realm was instantly rendered entirely barren.
The concentrated gravitational mass of millions of tons of sand violently compressing and expanding outward completely disrupted Thor’s downward momentum.
As Mjölnir descended, Ititus manifested a new grotesquely over-muscled arm of molten, vitrified glass directly from his Singularity core.
He didn’t try to punch the hammer as he aimed directly for the woman wielding it.
KRA-CRASH!
With a desperate suicidal roar, the Sand God managed to violently swipe Thor completely out of the sky!
The physical impact of the molten glass arm colliding with Thor’s silver-plated ribs generated a concussive shockwave that physically cracked the amber sky above them.
"AGH!" Thor grunted in genuine surprise.

She didn’t raise a shield neither did she cast a protective ward.
She stepped forward, casually spinning her massive war hammer by its thick leather strap.
"Let me introduce you to my armory, dirt-man!" Thor yelled cheerfully over the roaring wind of the descending spears.
She pulled her arm back, her muscles coiling tight, and threw her hammer directly into the sky.
"Mjölnir!" Thor announced proudly.
BOOOOOOM!
The iron hammer shot from her hand like a nuclear missile, trailing a massive tail of pure, white-hot lightning that illuminated the entire desert.
Mjölnir possessed true ancient traits that completely defied the modern magic system of the Sovereign Realm.
It didn’t just fly on a parabolic arc... it actively hunted.
The hammer never, ever missed its designated target and it possessed a terrifying sentience of its own.
Mjölnir violently crashed into the descending storm of glass spears and the hammer aggressively ricocheted in mid-air at impossible, hyper-sonic speeds.
CRASH-CRASH-SHATTER-BOOM!
In less than two seconds, Mjölnir violently zigzagged thousands of times across the darkened sky, moving so fast it looked like a continuous web of unbroken lightning.

The hammer completely pulverized every single one of the thousand fifty-foot glass spears into completely harmless, glittering dust before they could even get within a hundred yards of Thor’s silver boots.
Ititus stared in horror as his ultimate spell was reduced to a shimmering shower of glitter.
Having absolutely annihilated the divine artillery strike, Mjölnir didn’t fall to the earth.
It instantly reversed its trajectory, defying all laws of momentum.
The heavy iron weapon flew backward through the air like a loyal lethal boomerang, perfectly snapping back into Thor’s waiting outstretched hand with a deafening sound.
THWACK!
But Thor wasn’t done showing off her gear.
Ititus, seeing his ultimate attack effortlessly swatted out of the sky by a flying piece of iron, screamed in frustration.
"AHHHHHHHHH!"
He refused to be humiliated as he raised his four arms again, channeling the deep moisture of the realm.

He summoned a massive, hundred-foot-tall, mile-wide tsunami of boiling, liquid glass mixed with hyper-condensed black sand, intending to completely wash over her position and bury her under a molten mountain.
The tidal wave roared across the desert, swallowing the dunes in its path.
Thor didn’t throw the hammer this time.
She reached down with her free left hand, tapping a thick runed iron belt clasped tightly around her narrow waist.
"And this beauty," Thor boasted loudly, her voice booming with pride as she completely ignored the incoming mile-wide tsunami of liquid death, "is Megingjörð!
My Belt of Power!"
The ancient runes carved into the iron belt violently flared with blinding oceanic blue light.
When Thor wore Megingjörð, her already immense god-like physical strength wasn’t just slightly enhanced by a percentage buff... it was literally doubled.
It perfectly explained to Silas exactly why her physical density was so astronomical.
It was the reason why she could casually brush off the atmospheric pressure of the realm, and why she could completely atomize an eight-foot god with a single one-handed swing.
’Her physical stats are broken beyond repair.’
Thor firmly planted her silver boots into the vitrified glass of the crater.
"Come!"
As the hundred-foot tsunami of boiling liquid glass crashed down directly toward her head, Thor simply raised her free left hand with her palm open as she was completely unguarded.
KRA-THOOM!
She literally caught the hundred-foot tsunami of liquid glass with her bare hand!
The doubled physical strength of her body completely arrested the millions of tons of momentum in an instant.
The massive tidal wave violently stopped dead in its tracks the microsecond it touched her palm.
The boiling glass buckled, groaned, and then catastrophically shattered against her hand like a fragile pane of window glass hitting a reinforced titanium wall.
Millions of gallons of liquid sand rained down harmlessly around her, completely unable to push her back a single inch.
"Impossible!" Ititus shrieked, clutching his perfect golden hair with all four of his hands with his mind breaking.
"You cannot physically stop a mountain with flesh!"
Inside the green barrier, the bureaucratic Druid violently slammed her wooden staff against the floor, her white eyes flashing with deep irritation.
"Executioner Thor!" the Druid yelled over the roaring destruction.
"Stop explaining your divine armory to the target!
It is completely against Council protocol to monologue about your equipped artifacts!
Just execute him and let us go home!"
Thor glanced back over her silver-plated shoulder, offering the exasperated rule-obsessed Druid a cheeky dismissive grin.
"Why should I bother keeping secrets, tree-hugger?" Thor yelled back, casually swatting away a massive falling chunk of molten glass with the flat side of Mjölnir.
"He isn’t going to live past today anyway!
Let the dirt-man know exactly what killed him!
It’s polite!"
Thor turned her bright electrical blue eyes back to the terrified Sand God.
She held up both of her hands, wiggling her armored fingers.
Covering both of her hands and forearms up to the elbows were thick incredibly intricate silver-and-iron gauntlets that aggressively sparked with continuous violent violet static.
"And these!" Thor continued her enthusiastic mid-battle exposition, practically glowing with pride as she showed off her gauntlets.
"These beauties are Járngreipr!
My Gauntlets!"
Ititus gritted his teeth, his panic evolving into desperate cornered-animal aggression.
He began rapidly channeling mana, attempting to form a massive, spinning buzzsaw of hyper-dense obsidian sand in his two upper arms, aiming to slice her in half.
"You see," Thor yelled across the battlefield, completely ignoring his charging attack, "my hammer, Mjölnir, is absolutely perfect.
It really is.
But the handle was forged too short!
And do you know why?!"
Thor shook her head, a brief flash of deep sibling annoyance crossing her face.
"Because that treacherous, scheming, shape-shifting witch of a sister I have, Loki, completely interfered with the dwarven blacksmiths during its creation!
She bit the blacksmith in the eye as a fly just to ruin the forging process!"
Thor sighed, shaking her head at the memory of Loki’s pranks.
"Because the handle is so short," Thor explained as she locked eyes with the god.
"the catastrophic force of swinging it at full power would completely shatter my own hands into a bloody pulp!
So, I must wear these magical iron gloves to wield it properly!"

’Why is she telling me this?!’ Ititus panicked in his internal thoughts with his mind fracturing under the humiliating absurdity of the situation. ’Why is this absolute monster giving me a weapon lore lesson while she systematically destroys my entire realm?!
Why did I ever open this Secret Realm?!
Why didn’t I just stay hidden in the Vault?!’
A soul-crushing wave of regret flooded his divine core.
He had picked a fight with mortals, and in return, the universe had sent him a walking natural disaster.
"Now that we’re properly acquainted," Thor announced.
Her bright smile instantly vanished, completely replaced by the cold terrifying frown of the Council’s Executioner.
The air temperature plummeted as the static electricity in the air became so thick it visibly arched between the sand dunes.
Thor tightened her iron-gauntleted grip around the short, leather-wrapped handle of Mjölnir.
"Let’s see if you can survive a direct hit, Ititus."
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Thor didn’t throw the hammer this time as she charged.
She exploded across the desert floor, completely breaking the sound barrier ten times over in a single step.
The concussive shockwave of her sprint violently kicked up a massive wake of pulverized glass and molten sand that trailed behind her like the fiery tail of a descending comet.

Ititus shrieked in terror as he threw the massive spinning obsidian buzzsaw directly at her face, while simultaneously erecting a dozen thick, heavily reinforced walls of compressed golden sand to block her path.
Thor didn’t even slow down, hell she didn’t attempt to dodge.
CRASH!
SHATTER!
KRA-THOOM!
She unga-bunga’d completely through his best defenses.
She swung Mjölnir in rapid devastating and crushing arcs.
The iron war hammer completely pulverized the incoming obsidian buzzsaw into microscopic dust with a single strike.

She didn’t weave around the massive sand walls... she violently smashed straight through the dead center of them, leaving massive, gaping holes in the heavily reinforced masonry as if she were walking through wet paper.
Ititus desperately tried to phase his golden body into intangible sand to escape the incoming strike with his four arms dissolving into grit.
But Thor was already there.
She leaped high into the air, her entire silhouette completely eclipsed by blinding, white-hot natural lightning.
She raised Mjölnir high above her head with both of her iron-gauntleted hands, channeling the maximum doubled physical strength of Megingjörð directly into the short handle.
"Midgard sends its regards!" Thor roared, her voice vibrating with apocalyptic thunder.
She brought the war hammer down directly toward the dead center of the Sand God’s skull.
The descending iron head of Mjölnir carried the apocalyptic weight of an entire falling moon.
It completely bypassed the physical laws of the Sovereign Realm.
It tore through the ambient oxygen, leaving a vacuum in its wake that completely deafened the battlefield.
For a fraction of a microsecond, as the war hammer plummeted directly toward the dead center of the Sand God’s flawless golden skull, time itself seemed to violently freeze.
In that frozen microsecond, suspended between absolute divinity and absolute oblivion, Ititus experienced a profound soul-tearing revelation.
’I am going to die,’ the Sand God realized with the terror completely eclipsing his narcissistic arrogance.
His divine consciousness frantically calculated the incoming trajectory.
There was no dodging...
There was no blocking...
The blonde monster above him was wielding an artifact forged to shatter planets, and she was doing it with mathematically doubled physical strength.
’Why did I open this realm?!’ Ititus screamed in his own thoughts with the regret tearing at his divine core. ’Why did I taunt those miserable mortals?!
I should have stayed in the Vault!
I should have stayed asleep!’
But Ititus was a veteran of the Ascension War.
He was a creature born from cosmic violence, and he was absolutely not going to simply kneel and let an executioner turn him into a glass parking lot.
If he was going to die, he would drag this arrogant thunder-girl into the void with him.
"I AM THE ARCHITECT!" Ititus roared, his voice completely defying the vacuum of space as his golden eyes ignited with blinding, suicidal white light.
In the face of death, the Sand God abandoned all pretense of physical preservation.
He bypassed the safety limiters of his own soul and forcefully triggered a catastrophic sacrificial state of divine existence.
He achieved True Singularity.
KA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A shockwave of utterly incomprehensible world-ending magnitude violently rippled across the entire Secret Realm.
It wasn’t just a blast of air.
Every single, microscopic grain of sand within a fifty-mile radius was aggressively, instantaneously magnetized toward the god’s core, completely stripping the desert floor bare.

The rolling golden dunes, the deep subterranean quicksand, the swirling storms... all of it violently shot outward in a massive, expanding dome of hyper-condensed terrestrial pressure, completely peeling the desert away to reveal the raw, blackened bedrock of the realm itself.
The Secret Realm was instantly rendered entirely barren.
The concentrated gravitational mass of millions of tons of sand violently compressing and expanding outward completely disrupted Thor’s downward momentum.
As Mjölnir descended, Ititus manifested a new grotesquely over-muscled arm of molten, vitrified glass directly from his Singularity core.
He didn’t try to punch the hammer as he aimed directly for the woman wielding it.
KRA-CRASH!
With a desperate suicidal roar, the Sand God managed to violently swipe Thor completely out of the sky!
The physical impact of the molten glass arm colliding with Thor’s silver-plated ribs generated a concussive shockwave that physically cracked the amber sky above them.
"AGH!" Thor grunted in genuine surprise.

chapters.title: Chapter 208: Ititius’s Death
paragraphs: She lost her mid-air leverage.
The Daughter of Odin was violently sent flying backward like a silver bullet, skipping across the exposed bedrock of the barren realm.
"CURSE YOU, WHORE!" Ititus shrieked at the top of his lungs, his voice warped and distorted by the density of the True Singularity he had just achieved. "I WILL GRIND YOUR BONES INTO DUST!"
Thor didn’t crash into the horizon.
Fifty yards away from the impact site, Thor simply flipped backward in mid-air with her silver-armored boots digging into the empty air itself as if it were solid ground.
She skidded backward on nothing but atmospheric friction, completely steadying herself in the air with terrifying grace.
She slowly lowered Mjölnir to her side as she wasn’t injured, hell she wasn’t even bleeding.
In fact, she was smiling.
It was a bright warrior’s smile.
"Oh," Thor laughed, her blue eyes crackling with fresh violent static. "So the dirt-man actually knows how to throw a punch! Finally! I thought I was going to fall asleep!"
The residual shockwave of Ititus’s True Singularity had kicked up millions of tons of fine, abrasive dust into the air.
Thor casually raised her free left hand with the ancient runes of Járngreipr glowing violently across her iron gauntlet.
BZZZZZT!
Using the raw static electricity aggressively radiating from her own body, Thor violently magnetized the ambient sand in the air.
The abrasive grit actively began to swirl and orbit completely around her silver armor, forming a massive high-speed planetary ring of levitating dust that bent entirely to her electrical will.

Down on the barren bedrock, inside the massive glowing green dome of the Aegis barrier, the Druid violently slammed her wooden staff against the floor, pouring massive reserves of pure nature mana into the shield.
"Brace yourselves, mortals!" the Druid yelled, sweat beading on her pale forehead. "The target has initiated a divine Singularity! The output is going to be catastrophic!"
Silas Graves gritted his teeth as he shielded Aeliana behind his broad back.
His golden-ringed eyes were locked entirely on the sky as he was witnessing a tier of combat that completely shattered the established meta of the Sovereign Realm.
KRA-THOOM!
Ititus didn’t wait.
The Sand God’s new form was a towering, fifteen-foot monstrosity of hyper-condensed, molten glass and dark shifting singularity sand.
The heat radiating from his body was actively melting the bedrock beneath his feet.
He lunged upward, completely breaking the sound barrier with his four massive arms transforming into elongated, razor-sharp scythes of boiling obsidian.
He slashed at Thor with terrifying, crisscrossing arcs of pure death, each strike carrying enough power to bisect a mountain.
CLANG! CLANG! KRA-SHATTER!
Thor didn’t even bother casting a spell as she completely utilized her artifact-enhanced physical stats.
She effortlessly bobbed and weaved through the blindingly fast scythe attacks with her movements leaving afterimages in the static-charged air.
When Ititus managed to corner her, Thor simply raised her left forearm.
The iron gauntlet of Járngreipr effortlessly deflected the boiling obsidian scythes, completely shattering the divine weapons upon impact with a shower of molten sparks.
"Too slow!" Thor mocked him cheerfully, completely treating the cosmic duel like a training spar.
She swung Mjölnir in a tight brutal uppercut.
CRUNCH!
The iron hammer caught Ititus directly under his massive molten jaw.
The shockwave rippled through his entire fifteen-foot frame, violently lifting him completely off the ground and launching him upward into the sky.
’She isn’t even trying!’ Ititus screamed. ’I have sacrificed my immortal foundation for this Singularity, and she is playing with me! Why couldn’t the Council have sent anyone else?!’
"Is that all the Singularity gives you?!" Thor laughed, rocketing into the air to pursue him. "My father’s ravens hit harder than that!"
Ititus roared in desperation as he spread his four arms wide, manipulating the localized gravity of his core.
"Abyssal Siphon!" Ititus commanded.
Thousands of localized, hyper-dense gravity wells violently opened up in the air completely surrounding Thor.
The invisible vortexes aggressively attempted to pull her limbs in completely opposite directions, intending to literally tear the Daughter of Odin into quarters.
At the exact same time, Ititus manifested a massive swirling tornado of absolute-zero freezing glass, completely enveloping her position to shred her armor.
It was a multi-layered divine execution technique.
Ititus was putting in work, completely burning his lifespan to fuel the combination.
Inside the green barrier, Valerius dropped to his knees, clutching his head as the ambient pressure of the clashing divine spells threatened to crush his skull.
Seraphina watched with her red eyes wide, completely paralyzed by the scale of the elemental mastery.
"She’s trapped!" Harper gasped, her purple eyes tracking the massive glass tornado.
Silas narrowed his eyes.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
A cataclysmic explosion of pure white lightning aggressively detonated from the dead center of the glass tornado!
The electrical voltage instantly superheated the absolute-zero glass, completely vaporizing the tornado into harmless steam.
Thor floated perfectly unharmed in the center of the blast radius, the static electricity entirely short-circuiting Ititus’s gravity wells.
Thor casually brushed a speck of dust off her silver breastplate.
"Nice trick," Thor complimented him, completely sincere. "But you rely way too much on environmental area-of-effect spells! You lack fundamental core strength!"
Thor aggressively tapped the thick iron Belt of Power around her waist.
Megingjörð flared with blinding oceanic blue light. Her doubled physical strength spiked to impossible reality-breaking heights.
Thor disappeared as she simply moved faster than light itself.
BAM! BAM! BAM! KRA-THOOM!
She appeared directly in front of Ititus, delivering a brutal, rapid-fire combination of physical hammer strikes that completely defied comprehension.
She smashed his left shoulder, pulverizing the molten joint.
She spun, driving the iron head of Mjölnir directly into his ribs, caving the entire right side of his Singularity core inward.
She brought her heavy silver-plated boot up in a devastating front kick that completely shattered his jaw, sending him violently crashing back down into the exposed bedrock below.
The impact carved a crater three miles wide.
Down in the green barrier, the Druid was actively sweating. The shockwaves were brutally hammering against her Aegis shield.
"Executioner Thor!" the Druid screamed over the roaring destruction, tapping her runes with urgency. "Stop playing with your food! The termination window is rapidly closing!"
Thor, hovering high above the massive crater, casually leaned over, cupping a hand to her ear to hear the Druid over the thunder.
"What?!" Thor yelled back.

"I am officially reminding you that you have exactly one minute remaining on the temporal tether!" the Druid shrieked, completely exasperated. "If you do not terminate the target within sixty seconds, your combat performance will drop below a Grade A assessment for this quarter!"
Thor completely froze in mid-air.
Her cheerful manic battle-smile instantly vanished as her blue eyes widened in horror.

"One minute?!" Thor gasped, genuine panic entering her voice for the very first time. "What?! A Grade A?! Are you serious?! I need that quarterly performance bonus to afford the good mead in Valhalla!"
Down in the crater, Ititus was aggressively pulling himself out of the shattered bedrock with his Singularity core actively repairing his missing limbs with the surrounding dust.
"I WILL NOT BE IGNORED!" Ititus roared, completely misinterpreting her sudden pause as hesitation.
He gathered every single remaining drop of his divine mana, preparing to launch a final realm-destroying explosion.
Thor aggressively snapped her attention back to the Sand God.
She was no longer smiling as she looked stressed about her performance review.
"You!" Thor pointed Mjölnir directly at Ititus. "You are actively jeopardizing my mead budget and that is the final straw."
Thor raised her iron-gauntleted hands high into the air, holding Mjölnir perfectly vertical.
She didn’t tease him anymore as she simply called upon the primordial power of her bloodline.
KRA-KRA-KRA-CRACK!
The pitch-black, fractured sky of the Secret Realm violently tore completely open.
The very fabric of the dimension actively shattered like a delicate glass dome struck by a sledgehammer.
A single impossibly massive bolt of pure apocalyptic blue lightning aggressively descended from the cosmic void above.
It was a thousand times more powerful, a thousand times more dense than anything Harper had managed before.
It was a pillar of absolute celestial judgment.
The lightning violently struck Mjölnir, fully charging the legendary artifact until the iron head glowed with the intensity of a dying sun.
Ititus stared up at the descending apocalypse.
’I...’ the Sand God thought, the final pathetic remnants of his ego completely evaporating as he stared into the blinding light. ’...I really shouldn’t have traded my treasures for tha—’
"EXECUTION!" Thor roared at the top of her lungs.
She violently swung Mjölnir downward in a devastating, two-handed vertical strike.
KA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The blinding pillar of blue lightning completely detached from the hammer, screaming downward and impacting Ititus directly in the center of his chest.
The sound of the thunder booming afterward was so catastrophically loud that it completely shattered the physics of the realm.
The overwhelming electrical voltage didn’t just burn the Sand God... it instantaneously annihilated him.
The fifteen-foot Singularity body of molten glass and condensed sand was completely erased from the physical universe.
The lightning pillar drove straight through his deleted body and directly struck the massive golden Realm Core hovering near the bedrock below.
CRACK!
A fatal fissure violently spider-webbed directly through the center of the Realm Core as the light died and the ambient pressure instantly vanished.
The God of the Eternal Sands was permanently dead.
The dust slowly settled over the completely barren, blackened bedrock of the ruined Secret Realm.
The sky above remained a shattered, pitch-black void with the spatial integrity of the dimension critically failing now that the core was cracked.
CLINK!
With a soft metallic sound, Thor floated down from the sky, landing casually on the vitrified bedrock.
She smoothly spun Mjölnir by the strap, holstering the massive weapon comfortably at her hip.
The blinding white lightning faded from her silver armor, and her braided blonde hair finally stopped standing on end from the static.
She completely ignored the massive smoking crater where a god had existed ten seconds prior.
Instead, she immediately turned around and aggressively jogged over to the massive, glowing green dome where the Druid was standing.
"Well?!" Thor demanded eagerly, leaning down and staring intensely at the Druid through the magical barrier, her blue eyes wide with anticipation. "Did I make it?! Check the runes! Check the runes!"
The Druid let out a long exhausted sigh.
She slowly lowered her wooden staff, allowing the massive green Aegis barrier to safely dissipate into harmless green light, releasing the trapped humans.
The Druid tapped the glowing, bureaucratic runes carved into the shaft of her staff as she reviewed the cosmic telemetry data of the execution.
"Target Ititus confirmed permanently terminated," the Druid announced in her dry, monotone voice.
She glanced up at the incredibly stressed thunder god.
"Combat efficiency: Adequate. Time elapsed: Acceptable. Collateral damage: Astronomically high, but restricted to an unauthorized realm."
The Druid sighed again.
"You have been awarded an A-minus assessment for this execution, Daughter of Odin."
Thor completely froze then, she threw both of her iron-gauntleted fists high into the air.

"YES!" Thor cheered at the absolute top of her lungs, doing a small victorious little hop on the blackened bedrock. "A-minus! The mead budget is secured! Take that, Freyja! You stuck-up nature witch, my quarterly reviews are flawless!"
The surviving Lords stood perfectly still on the bedrock.
They were completely speechless.
They had just watched a divine entity shatter the sky, atomize a god, and then do a celebratory little dance over her corporate performance review.
Having successfully secured her bonus, Thor finally turned her attention completely toward the mortals she had just saved.
She aggressively swaggered over to the group of Humans with her silver armor clanking softly.
She offered them a bright cheerful smile.

"Greetings, people of Midgard!" Thor boomed pleasantly, resting her hands on her hips. "You all did remarkably well holding out against that delusional dirt-man! I apologize for the delay; cosmic traffic was absolutely dreadful today."
The elite didn’t know how to respond.

Valerius slowly lowered his mythril sword, completely dumbfounded. Seraphina avoided eye contact, deeply intimidated by the raw elemental supremacy she had just witnessed but as Thor’s electrical blue eyes casually swept over the group of surviving mortals, her gaze abruptly halted.
Her smile slightly faded, replaced by an expression of deep curiosity.
She locked eyes completely with one specific man standing near the back of the group.
Silas Graves.
The dark-haired Lord was standing with his broad shoulders squared, actively shielding Aeliana behind his body.
Thor tilted her head slightly with her divine instincts aggressively flaring.
This mortal... he was different.
