"What?!
A Grade A?!
Are you serious?!
I need that quarterly performance bonus to afford the good mead in Valhalla!"
Down in the crater, Ititus was aggressively pulling himself out of the shattered bedrock with his Singularity core actively repairing his missing limbs with the surrounding dust.
"I WILL NOT BE IGNORED!" Ititus roared, completely misinterpreting her sudden pause as hesitation.
He gathered every single remaining drop of his divine mana, preparing to launch a final realm-destroying explosion.
Thor aggressively snapped her attention back to the Sand God.
She was no longer smiling as she looked stressed about her performance review.
"You!" Thor pointed Mjölnir directly at Ititus.
"You are actively jeopardizing my mead budget and that is the final straw."
Thor raised her iron-gauntleted hands high into the air, holding Mjölnir perfectly vertical.
She didn’t tease him anymore as she simply called upon the primordial power of her bloodline.
KRA-KRA-KRA-CRACK!
The pitch-black, fractured sky of the Secret Realm violently tore completely open.
The very fabric of the dimension actively shattered like a delicate glass dome struck by a sledgehammer.
A single impossibly massive bolt of pure apocalyptic blue lightning aggressively descended from the cosmic void above.
It was a thousand times more powerful, a thousand times more dense than anything Harper had managed before.
It was a pillar of absolute celestial judgment.
The lightning violently struck Mjölnir, fully charging the legendary artifact until the iron head glowed with the intensity of a dying sun.
Ititus stared up at the descending apocalypse.
’I...’ the Sand God thought, the final pathetic remnants of his ego completely evaporating as he stared into the blinding light. ’...I really shouldn’t have traded my treasures for tha—’
"EXECUTION!" Thor roared at the top of her lungs.
She violently swung Mjölnir downward in a devastating, two-handed vertical strike.
KA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The blinding pillar of blue lightning completely detached from the hammer, screaming downward and impacting Ititus directly in the center of his chest.
The sound of the thunder booming afterward was so catastrophically loud that it completely shattered the physics of the realm.
The overwhelming electrical voltage didn’t just burn the Sand God... it instantaneously annihilated him.
The fifteen-foot Singularity body of molten glass and condensed sand was completely erased from the physical universe.
The lightning pillar drove straight through his deleted body and directly struck the massive golden Realm Core hovering near the bedrock below.
CRACK!
A fatal fissure violently spider-webbed directly through the center of the Realm Core as the light died and the ambient pressure instantly vanished.
The God of the Eternal Sands was permanently dead.
The dust slowly settled over the completely barren, blackened bedrock of the ruined Secret Realm.
The sky above remained a shattered, pitch-black void with the spatial integrity of the dimension critically failing now that the core was cracked.
CLINK!
With a soft metallic sound, Thor floated down from the sky, landing casually on the vitrified bedrock.
She smoothly spun Mjölnir by the strap, holstering the massive weapon comfortably at her hip.
The blinding white lightning faded from her silver armor, and her braided blonde hair finally stopped standing on end from the static.
She completely ignored the massive smoking crater where a god had existed ten seconds prior.
Instead, she immediately turned around and aggressively jogged over to the massive, glowing green dome where the Druid was standing.
"Well?!" Thor demanded eagerly, leaning down and staring intensely at the Druid through the magical barrier, her blue eyes wide with anticipation.
"Did I make it?!
Check the runes!
Check the runes!"
The Druid let out a long exhausted sigh.
She slowly lowered her wooden staff, allowing the massive green Aegis barrier to safely dissipate into harmless green light, releasing the trapped humans.
The Druid tapped the glowing, bureaucratic runes carved into the shaft of her staff as she reviewed the cosmic telemetry data of the execution.
"Target Ititus confirmed permanently terminated," the Druid announced in her dry, monotone voice.
She glanced up at the incredibly stressed thunder god.
"Combat efficiency: Adequate.
Time elapsed: Acceptable.
Collateral damage: Astronomically high, but restricted to an unauthorized realm."
The Druid sighed again.
"You have been awarded an A-minus assessment for this execution, Daughter of Odin."
Thor completely froze then, she threw both of her iron-gauntleted fists high into the air.
"YES!" Thor cheered at the absolute top of her lungs, doing a small victorious little hop on the blackened bedrock.
"A-minus!
The mead budget is secured!
Take that, Freyja!
You stuck-up nature witch, my quarterly reviews are flawless!"
The surviving Lords stood perfectly still on the bedrock.
They were completely speechless.
They had just watched a divine entity shatter the sky, atomize a god, and then do a celebratory little dance over her corporate performance review.
Having successfully secured her bonus, Thor finally turned her attention completely toward the mortals she had just saved.
She aggressively swaggered over to the group of Humans with her silver armor clanking softly.
She offered them a bright cheerful smile.
"Greetings, people of Midgard!" Thor boomed pleasantly, resting her hands on her hips.
"You all did remarkably well holding out against that delusional dirt-man!
I apologize for the delay; cosmic traffic was absolutely dreadful today."
The elite didn’t know how to respond.
Valerius slowly lowered his mythril sword, completely dumbfounded.

Seraphina avoided eye contact, deeply intimidated by the raw elemental supremacy she had just witnessed but as Thor’s electrical blue eyes casually swept over the group of surviving mortals, her gaze abruptly halted.
Her smile slightly faded, replaced by an expression of deep curiosity.
She locked eyes completely with one specific man standing near the back of the group.
Silas Graves.
The dark-haired Lord was standing with his broad shoulders squared, actively shielding Aeliana behind his body.
Thor tilted her head slightly with her divine instincts aggressively flaring.
This mortal... he was different.

chapters.title: Chapter 209: Out Of The Secret Realm
paragraphs: The other Lords in the group were okay but this dark-haired man was giving off the distinct feeling of a very fierce warrior who had clawed his way up from the bottom of the food chain.
But that wasn’t what caught her attention.
Thor focused her divine perception, looking completely past his physical flesh.
Hidden deep within his chest, suppressed and meticulously concealed beneath layers of mana, Thor sensed it.
It was a flawless Gold Lord Core.
Thor’s eyes widened a microscopic fraction.
Her Father, the All-Father Odin, had long ago awakened a Gold Lord core during his ancient travels through Midgard.
It was the unquestionable hallmark of a true predator.
It was the mark of a King. She knew exactly what kind of terrifying presence a Gold Core emitted, and she felt that exact same resonance radiating from this silent dark-haired man.
A slow knowing smirk stretched across Thor’s flawless face.
She stepped completely past Valerius and Seraphina, completely ignoring the elite nobles, and walked directly right up to Silas Graves.
She stopped mere inches away from his chest, forcing the Lord to look slightly up to meet her electrical blue eyes.
The passive pressure radiating from her body made Silas’s heart violently hammer against his ribs.
"Well, well, well," Thor purred softly.
She leaned in close, her blue eyes sparkling with amusement. "And what might your name be, little warrior?"
Silas Graves, The Lord of the Blessed Land who was quite a powerful Lord capable of beating hordes of monsters by himself... actually hesitated.
His brain short-circuited in the presence of an incredibly beautiful deity standing two inches from his face.
"S-Silas," Silas actually stuttered. "Silas Graves."
Thor’s smirk widened into a brilliant grin.
She didn’t say another word.
Thor casually reached out her right hand.

With the heavy runed iron gauntlet of Járngreipr aggressively sparking with static electricity, the Daughter of Odin gently patted Silas Graves directly on the top of his head, exactly like one would pet a very good dangerous hunting dog.
Pat. Pat.
Silas stood completely frozen in place with his golden-ringed eyes twitching violently, but his survival instincts screaming at him not to swat the hand of the god who had just deleted a mountain.
Behind his back, Aeliana’s eyes widened in absolute shock with her elven jaw dropping. Harper covered her mouth to hide a hysterical gasp.
Thor completely maintained the Lord’s secret.

She didn’t say a single word out loud about the Gold Core hidden in his chest. Even her Father had explicitly warned her centuries ago that being exposed as a Gold Core in Midgard meant inviting all of the political and military trouble in the entire world directly to your doorstep.
She respected the hustle and she wasn’t going to blow his cover to these pampered nobles.
"Keep surviving, Silas Graves." Thor whispered softly, pulling her hand back.
Before Silas could even formulate a response, the dry monotone voice of the Druid echoed from behind them.

"Executioner Thor," the Druid interrupted, tapping her wooden staff against the bedrock. "The spatial integrity of this Secret Realm is critically failing. The core is fractured and I respectfully request that we leave this dimension immediately before it completely collapses onto the void."
Thor sighed, her cheerful demeanor returning as she turned away from the Warlord.
"Duty calls!" Thor announced loudly to the group of utterly stunned Lords. "I wish you all the best of luck! May your mead be strong and your enemies be slow!"
She offered the Midgardians a final polite wave goodbye.
Thor casually turned around, facing the massive fractured golden Realm Core hovering near the edge of the crater.
She didn’t use a spell as she simply drew Mjölnir from her hip, casually tossed the heavy iron war hammer into the air, caught it by the handle, and threw it directly at the core.
KRA-SHATTER!
Mjölnir smashed completely through the massive golden sphere, permanently shattering the Realm Core into a million microscopic fragments of dead light!
The exact microsecond the core broke, the Secret Realm violently collapsed.
The gravity failed as the pitch-black, fractured sky instantly dissolved into a swirling vortex of spatial energy.
FWOOSH!
The surviving Lords were violently caught in the spatial backwash.
Their bodies instantly dissolved into streaks of white light, completely teleported out of the collapsing dimension and forcefully sent back directly to the surface of their own mortal world.
As the Midgardians vanished, Thor casually caught Mjölnir as it flew back into her hand.
The barren bedrock around them was actively crumbling into the cosmic void.
Thor let out a long exhausted sigh, aggressively stretching her arms above her head.

"You know, tree-hugger," Thor complained casually to the Druid, completely ignoring the apocalyptic dimension collapsing around them. "I really want to take a break. My shoulders are killing me... I think I’m going to use some of my PTO this weekend and hit the taverns in Alfheim."
The stoic Druid stared at the collapsing sky for a moment then uncharacteristically, she slowly nodded her head.
"Surprisingly," the Druid admitted, her voice dripping with exhaustion, "I completely agree with you as a break sounds optimal."
Thor gasped, her blue eyes lighting up with genuine joy.
"Did we just agree on something?!" Thor cheered.
She aggressively lunged forward, throwing her armored arms around the tiny Druid and pulling the stoic woman into a crushing bear hug.
The Druid let out a strangled wheeze of protest with her wooden staff clattering to the floor.
"Thor... release me—" the Druid gasped.
"See you on Monday!" Thor laughed.
KRA-THOOM!
Thor completely ignored the protest.
She violently launched herself directly into the sky, rocketing upward through the collapsing spatial tears and flying off into the cosmic void, leaving a massive trail of blue lightning in her wake.
The Druid was left completely alone standing on a rapidly shrinking piece of barren bedrock as the Secret Realm actively dissolved into the abyss around her.
The Druid slowly bent down, picking up her wooden staff.
She dusted off her vine-woven robes, adjusting her collar with an deep sense of fatigue.
As the ground beneath her boots finally gave way, the Druid let out one final sigh, her glowing white eyes staring blankly into the void.
’I really,’ the Druid thought to herself as she initiated her own emergency teleportation sequence, ’do not get paid enough for this.’
The transition between dimensions was never a smooth or forgiving process.
Silas Graves felt an incredibly nauseating sensation violently rip through his entire physical body.
It was the exact same kind of fundamentally "weird" stomach-churning spatial displacement that he had felt upon first entering the Secret Realm days ago.
The sudden shift in atmospheric density, the complete evaporation of the ambient mana, and the aggressive readjustment of gravity completely scrambled his brain a bit.
His vision swam with blinding streaks of white and blue cosmic light.
The roaring thunder of the collapsing Secret Realm was instantly muted, replaced by a sudden silence that rang loudly in his ears.
Right next to him, still holding tightly onto his arm, Aeliana’s flawless elven body suddenly violently shuddered.
"Lord Sy—" Aeliana began to speak, her green eyes widening in sudden realization.
Before she could even finish her sentence, the spatial laws of the mortal world forcefully reasserted themselves.
Aeliana’s physical form aggressively dissolved into a million brilliant, shimmering white sparks of starlight.
The sparks swirled rapidly in the air for a fraction of a microsecond before completely dissipating into the ether, leaving Silas grasping at empty air.
DING!
A mechanical chime echoed directly inside his skull as a translucent blue system screen immediately materialized in front of his eyes projecting crisp white text.
[The dimensional tether has been severed.]
[Hero: Aeliana (Starlight Arcanist) has been successfully unsummoned and returned safely to the Blessed Land Territory barracks.]
Silas blinked away the disorientation. It wasn’t just Aeliana.
All across the chaotic cluster of teleporting Lords, everyone’s summoned Heroes were vanishing in identical bursts of elemental light.
Elora’s Frost Mage dissolved into a flurry of blue snowflakes.
The mechanical-armed Archer serving Maya vanished in a blur of metallic polygons.

Mia, the ancient Grandmaster who had been securely perched on Valerius’s shoulder just moments ago, quietly faded into a splash of harmless evaporating water drops, forcefully pulled back to her master’s domain.
Without the supportive weight of his Hero, Silas felt the sudden aggressive pull of Earth’s gravity.
THUD!
The spatial vortex aggressively spat them out.
They fell from the glowing white portal, tumbling roughly through the air for several feet before hitting the ground heavily.
Silas hit the dirt in an automatic shoulder roll, mitigating the blunt force trauma.
He slid to a halt with his hands instantly pressing flat against the earth to anchor himself.
"Fuck..."
He coughed, his lungs aggressively rejecting the sudden influx of stale air of the place after spending days breathing the hyper-oxygenated atmosphere of a divine realm.
He slowly sat up, wiping a thick layer of grit from his face, and looked around to assess his immediate surroundings.
The sand that stretched across this barren world... the sand that had previously been a normal, mundane beige had completely lost all of its life.
The earth itself had become pitch black. It looked and felt like scorched, dead ash scattered across a massive graveyard.
The massive intricately carved stone pillars that held the portal aloft were dark.
The swirling volatile energy that usually drifted around the array was completely gone.

The glowing portal hovering between the pillars sputtered, sparked with a few dying arcs of residual static, and then permanently deactivated, plunging the place into the dim flickering light that came from above.
Silas let out a long exhausted breath.
All around him, the other Lords that had somehow miraculously survived the meat grinder of the expedition were picking themselves up off the black sand.
There were barely more than half a dozen of them left out of the twenty that had originally marched through those doors.
They were all covered in soot, dried blood, and severe lacerations. They looked like refugees fleeing a war zone.
Silas watched as they all began slowly standing up, brushing the dead black sand off their ruined armor.
The trauma of the experience was evident on every single one of their faces but human nature was incredibly resilient, and almost immediately, the shocked silence was broken by frantic chatter.
Some of the surviving elites were already frantically talking about Thor.

"Did you see the size of that hammer?!" one of the blue-core Lords gasped, his hands trembling violently as he leaned against the warehouse wall. "She completely deleted the sky! A single swing! I didn’t even see her cast a spell!"
"The Daughter of Odin..." the Spear Lord babbled hysterically, sitting on his knees in the black sand, completely ignoring the fact that he was missing a chunk of his armor.

The usually arrogant man was unashamedly glazing the Norse deity to anyone who would listen. "Her physical power was impossible! The gravity! She blocked a mountain of liquid glass with her bare hand! If she hadn’t arrived, we would all be dead! All hail Asgard!"
Silas listened to the frantic awe-struck worship echoing around the warehouse.
He didn’t join in. Instead, Silas slowly climbed to his feet, his jaw clenching so tight his teeth audibly ground together.
He aggressively brushed the dead black sand off his shirt with his golden-ringed eyes burning with a dark frustrated fire.

’I need to stop treating this shit like a game,’ Silas thought fiercely, his ego taking a massive beating. ’I need to stop taking it easy. I need to stop thinking I’m at the top of the food chain just because I can bully a few pampered aristocrats.’
In the apocalyptic world-shaking battle between Thor and Ititus, Silas had felt incredibly useless.
It was a bitter pill to swallow.
Which was only natural, of course, since he was fundamentally just a Human standing in the crossfire of two cosmic entities.
But he had a Mythic Gold Core.
He possessed the highest tier of magical potential recognized by the Sovereign realm.
Silas didn’t want to be a spectator.
He wanted to be the one swinging the hammer.

He wanted to be strong and completely undefeated like Thor. He wanted to possess the kind of terrifying baseline physical power that could make other Lords physically choke on the air just by standing in his general vicinity.
Silas looked down at his calloused right hand, slowly curling his fingers into a tight, bruising fist.

chapters.title: Chapter 210: Killing The Fragment Of A God
paragraphs: ’Mia said it herself,’ Silas recalled with his mind rapidly sorting through the intense magical lectures the ancient Grandmaster had drilled into his skull. ’To forcefully push my Gold Core into the second stage of Core Advancement, I cannot just rely on raw physical stats and a single element. I need to achieve Adept Mastery in at least eight different elemental affinities.’
He needed versatility.
He needed to be able to seamlessly chain fire, wind, earth, lightning, and water together without relying on his summoned Heroes to cover his blind spots.
Since Mia had been forcefully unsummoned back to Valerius’s territory and was no longer here to physically teach him the spells, he was going to have to do it the hard expensive way.
Silas was going to have to physically buy high-tier skill scrolls from the Lord Association (LA) Building’s premium marketplace and brute-force the knowledge directly into his brain.
While Silas was actively plotting his massive power-leveling trajectory, Elora Verinda walked over to him.
The City Lord’s daughter looked significantly worse for wear.
Her usually immaculate, icy blond hair was singed and tangled, and her expensive frost-silk robes were torn and stained with dried blood and black sand.
Maya, her loyal subordinate, was walking right beside her, supporting a deeply traumatized Jaxon.
Elora looked at Silas, her cold blue eyes completely lacking any of their usual superiority.

’If he isn’t the Lord of Blessed Land then I am a fool.’ Elora thought, he possessed more higher combat ability and mana than a standard Blue Core, not only that but he had been recognized by a god too?
"Silas," Elora addressed him.
She looked at Maya and Jaxon, then back to the dark-haired Lord.
"I am glad that we all managed to survive that nightmare. This expedition was a failure of intelligence and I’m sorry for wasting your time. Would you like to leave now?" She said and Silas nodded.
"Agreed. The less questions we have to answer about dead gods, the better."
They turned and began walking across the massive sand place, navigating around the scattered debris and parked luxury vehicles toward Elora’s sleek armored supercar parked near the exit ramp.
However, before they could even reach the vehicle, an armored hand clamped firmly onto Silas’s shoulder.
Silas turned. It was Valerius Sterling.
The blonde noble looked completely exhausted. His golden armor was severely dented, covered in soot, and missing a pauldron.
But despite the absolute beating he had taken over the last few days, a genuine un-arrogant smirk touched his bruised lips.

Valerius stepped past Silas, gently but firmly intercepting a deeply dazed silent Seraphina, who was currently staring blankly at the floor, still trying to process the fact that she had just been choked by a deity.

"I will handle it from here, Graves," Valerius told him quietly, subtly gesturing toward Seraphina. "I will make sure she gets back to her estate without causing a scene or setting the warehouse on fire."
Valerius extended his heavy iron-gauntleted right hand toward the Lord.

"Goodbye, Silas," Valerius said, his tone ringing with respect. "You fight like a demon and if the anyone tries to pin the casualties of this raid on your faction... you let me know. The Sterling house will block the motions."
Silas looked at the offered hand with a smile appearing on his face as he reached out, firmly gripping Valerius’s iron gauntlet.
Silas smiled. "Try not to get blown away by the wind next time, Sterling."
"Very funny," Valerius snorted, shaking his head.
They released their firm handshake.
Valerius gently guided the unresponsive Seraphina toward his own transport vehicle parked across the warehouse.
Silas turned back and gracefully slid into the passenger seat of Elora’s sleek, low-profile supercar.
The reinforced doors hissed shut with a pressurized seal, immediately locking out the sand and enveloping him in the quiet luxury of the vehicle’s interior.
As he settled into the plush leather seat, Silas let out another long sigh, resting his head back against the headrest.

’Fuck...’ Silas thought, a sudden wave of regret completely washing over his mind. ’I was so completely distracted by Thor’s arrival and the collapsing sky that I completely forgot to try and secure the last hit on that guy.’
It was a potential loss of Upgrade Points.
He had actively pumped gallons of pressurized Aqua mana directly into Ititus’s core during their skirmish, hoping to detonate the god from the inside out.
Sitting in the passenger seat, Silas casually raised his right hand.
He snapped his fingers, sending a microscopic calibrated pulse of mana through the ether, attempting to manually trigger the remote detonation of the Aqua mana he had injected into the Sand God.
Snap!
He waited for a second with his golden-ringed eyes closing as he focused his senses.
Nothing...
He felt absolutely nothing as the connection was completely dead and the mana signature had vanished.
Silas sighed once more, deeply disappointed.
’Damn her...’
The Daughter of Odin had been too thorough.
Mjölnir must have completely vaporized every single microscopic trace of the god, including the water mana Silas had planted inside him and now the loot was gone.
Outside the tinted windows of the supercar, the remaining Lords were scrambling to evacuate the premises.
Harper, still wearing Silas’s oversized black trench coat, practically sprinted toward her own armored corporate vehicle, desperate to escape the lingering glares of the other nobles.
One by one, the rumbling engines of the luxury transports roared to life.

The different portals that they had used to secretly enter the underground warehouse days ago were already open and each of the surviving Lords rapidly exited the facility, their tires screeching against the concrete as they fled back into the portals and to their cities.
And as the final vehicle cleared into the portal, the massive carved stone pillars in the center of the warehouse completely crumbled into useless mundane grey dust as the portal vanished forever.
However, what the Council of Deities, the Daughter of Odin, and the paranoid Lord did not realize... was that the universe was stubbornly resilient.

Deep inside the pitch-black scorched sand completely covered the floor, A single microscopic grain of brilliantly glowing gold sand silently, painstakingly crept out from the absolute center of the pulverized portal remnant.
It slowly, agonizingly rolled across the sand, landing softly onto more of the dead black sand.
It was Ititus.
The God of the Eternal Sands had miraculously managed to survive the apocalyptic deletion of his entire physical form.

Through a desperate million-to-one cosmic anomaly, a single infinitesimal fraction of his divine core had been violently ejected from the Secret Realm just a microsecond before Mjölnir struck, riding the spatial backwash of the teleporting Midgardians through the portal.
He was reduced to a literal singular grain of dirt. He possessed no physical strength, no magical reserves, and no voice.
But his divine consciousness remained completely intact.

’CURSE YOU!’ Ititus screamed in his internal soundless thoughts, the microscopic grain of gold sand vibrating with wrath as it laid there in the dark. ’CURSE THAT BLONDE, HAMMER-WIELDING WHORE! CURSE THAT TREE-HUGGING DRUID! AND CURSE EVERY SINGLE ONE OF THOSE MISERABLE PARASITIC LORDS!’
The fragmented god seethed with vengeance.
He was currently completely powerless, but he was immortal. He would bury himself deep into the bedrock of this disgusting place.
He would slowly gather ambient earth mana over the next thousand years.
He would rebuild his core, and then he would rise up and completely annihilate this entire—
Suddenly, the microscopic grain of gold sand violently twitched.
Something was wrong.
Deep within the microscopic atomic structure of his fragmented core, Ititus suddenly felt it.
It was an dense microscopic drop of Aqua mana.
It was the exact same water mana that Silas had forcefully pumped directly into the god’s chest during their battle on the surface.
When Ititus’s body had been atomized by Thor, this singular stubborn drop of mana had remained flawlessly attached to the surviving core fragment, lying completely dormant.
And then, back in a speeding car, Silas snapped his fingers.
’Won’t hurt to active it... meh!’
The remote detonation signal, traveling through the ether of the Sovereign system, instantly reached the drop of water.
The latent Aqua mana violently activated.
The microscopic grain of gold sand felt the freezing expanding pressure of the water violently ripping its atomic structure apart from the inside out.
’NO!’ Ititus panicked with despair flooding his final thought. ’CURSE THAT FUCKE—!’
POP!
With a completely silent microscopic explosion that wouldn’t have even startled a passing rat, the final grain of golden sand violently exploded apart.
The atomic structure of the core was completely annihilated by the expanding water.
The God of the Eternal Sands died completely and unconditionally in the middle of his own curse, reduced to nothing but another grain of sand among the black sand.
Meanwhile, smoothly cruising down the brightly illuminated neon-lit elevated highways of Valoria City, Elora’s sleek supercar revived a bit.
Silas was leaning his elbow against the passenger side window, watching the towering skyscrapers and holographic advertisements blur past.
He was lost in thought, calculating exactly how many Spirit Credits he would need to successfully purchase a lot of elemental spell scrolls.
Suddenly, Silas violently blinked.
DING!
A crisp chime echoed loudly in his skull as a bright unexpected translucent blue system tab aggressively materialized directly in front of his face, completely obscuring his view of the city.
[Target Eliminated: Tier 6 Ititius’s Fragment. +1000 UP]
[Current Balance: 4400 UP]
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes went completely wide.
He physically jerked backward in the plush leather seat, almost spitting out his own saliva in shock.
’One thousand?!’ Silas screamed in his thoughts with his heart hammering violently against his ribs. ’One thousand Upgrade Points?!’
He stared at the glowing blue numbers as his brain completely short-circuited.
He had absolutely not defeated Ititus in standard combat... He hadn’t even been in the same zip code when the god died.
Silas immediately made a rapid query, asking the System directly in his thoughts to explain the error.

[Entity ’Ititus’ miraculously survived the Executioner’s strike by jettisoning a microscopic fraction of his core into the mortal realm. However, the latent Aqua mana you previously injected into the target remained attached. Upon your manual detonation signal, the Aqua mana successfully expanded, permanently executing the surviving core fragment. As the sole initiator of the fatal strike, you have been awarded the full bounty for the Fragment.]
Silas gulped with a cold bead of sweat rolling down his sharp jawline.
He stared blankly at the dashboard of the supercar.

Not only was the completely powerless, microscopic, near-dead fragment of Ititus classified by the system as a massive Tier 6 entity... but it had casually dropped a thousand Upgrade Points just for dying.
Silas felt a shiver of thrill wash down his spine.

’If a microscopic piece of dirt was classified as a Tier 6...’ Silas thought with his hands trembling slightly in his lap. ’...then how astronomically high would the bounty have been if I had somehow managed to kill the true fully formed Ititus?’
He was miles... rather oceans... in fact different dimensions away from the true apex of power in this universe.
The realization only fueled the burning, relentless furnace of his Gold Core ambition.
He needed more power and he needed that power right now.
The supercar smoothly decelerated, pulling over to the curb on a quiet upscale residential street lined with towering apartment complexes.
Elora shifted the vehicle into park.
The heavy reinforced gull-wing doors hissed upward, allowing the crisp afternoon air of the city to enter the cabin.
Maya, looking completely exhausted, gently helped the deeply traumatized Jaxon out of the cramped backseat.
"Thank you for the extraction, Lady Elora," Maya said politely, bowing her head slightly.
She looked over at the passenger seat. "Silas. Despite our... differences in the desert, I acknowledge your strength."
Mia wanted to ask for a date but honestly she was too stressed out.
"Thank you." Silas replied calmly, offering a brief nod of respect. ’Even if you didn’t do anything.’

chapters.title: Chapter 211: Selling Items To Elora
paragraphs: Jaxon didn’t say a word.
He simply clutched his empty Hero Summoning Card to his chest with his eyes blank as he slowly walked toward the heavily fortified entrance of his family’s estate.
Elora watched them go, her face turning impassive.
Once they were safely inside the perimeter, she tapped the dashboard, and the heavy doors hissed shut, perfectly sealing the cabin once more.
She smoothly shifted the car back into drive, smoothly merging back into the flow of neon-lit city traffic.
Elora drove in complete silence for a few minutes with her hands resting lightly on the glowing steering wheel.
She glanced over at Silas through the reflection of the windshield.

"Do you want to be dropped off somewhere specific, Silas?" Elora asked, her tone carefully neutral. "Or do you have somewhere urgent to be? It has been four, almost five entire days since we initially entered the Sovereign Realm so your Territory might be a main priority."
Silas considered the question.
Aeliana had been safely unsummoned and returned directly to the Blessed Land barracks.
She would undoubtedly relay the full report to Eluned and Morwenna, apart from that, Blessed Land was not in danger.
"No," Silas replied, leaning his head back. "I am not urgently heading anywhere tonight. The territory is secured."
Elora nodded slowly, her icy blue eyes flashing with a sudden glint of determination.
"Good," Elora said softly. "Because there is somewhere specific I want to take you today."
Silas’s Warlord paranoia instantly spiked.
He narrowed his golden-ringed eyes, staring at the side of her flawless profile.
Taking him to a "secondary location" was usually code for an ambush.
But he was currently sitting on 4400 UP and possessed a Gold Core. If she tried to betray him, he would simply freeze her car from the inside out.
’I might be forced to kill her too.’
"Fine," Silas begrudgingly agreed, letting out a sigh as he casually crossed his arms over his chest.
He secretly clutched his right hand into a tight fist, keeping his mana pathways perfectly primed for instant combat as she drove silently through the city.
As they navigated the sprawling, elevated highways, Silas’s mind immediately pivoted entirely back to his primary objective.
Right now, more than anything else in the world, he desperately wanted to get his hands on some new high-tier spells as soon as humanly possible.
He needed destructive offensive elements like Fire or Lightning to complement his defensive water and ice magic since he needed to hit that Adept Mastery in eight elements.
But buying even Tier 1 spell scrolls from the Lord Association marketplace was expensive.
He already had a significant stash of Spirit Credits in his account but to purchase the volume of scrolls he needed, one required a whole lot more liquid capital.
Silas uncrossed his arms, turning slightly to look at Elora in the driver’s seat.

"Elora," Silas broke the silence. "Would you be interested in conducting a private transaction right now?... Do you want to trade a treasure or two that I acquired during the Secret Realm expedition in exchange for liquid Spirit Credits?"
Elora didn’t take her eyes off the glowing road, but her interest was visibly piqued.
The Verinda family possessed very high financial resources, but finding genuine uncorrupted Secret Realm loot was always highly valuable for networking.

"I am always open to mutually beneficial commerce, Silas," Elora replied smoothly with the City Lord’s daughter instantly slipping back into her corporate element. "What exactly would you like to trade? I don’t mind purchasing artifacts directly from your inventory, provided they meet standard quality protocols."
"Could you find where to park first?" Silas instructed.
Elora smoothly guided the supercar into a designated parking alcove on the side of the highway, engaging the privacy wards of the vehicle.
Silas didn’t hesitate.
He raised his right hand, opening his Lord Inventory interface.
A blue screen materialized in the air between them, illuminating the dark cabin of the car to Silas and then he reached into the digital screen.
With a soft hum of spatial magic, he brought out an ornate beautifully forged silver combat helmet.
It was the pristine Valkyrie helmet that he had taken from Harper in exchange for providing her a roof over her head back in the desert.

He had originally meant to share this specific piece of armor with Valerius as a gesture of goodwill, but given everything that happened after including tectonic collapse and the arrival of Thor, both of them had completely forgotten about the loot split.
Silas placed the heavy silver helmet gently onto the center console.
"This is a Tier 2 Defensive Artifact," Silas stated, tapping the side of the helm. "It increases baseline physical resistance by thirty percent and is in flawless condition."
He reached back into the glowing blue grid.
Clink!
He brought out a stunning intricate gold and sapphire necklace that practically hummed with water mana.
It was one of the fifteen treasures that Aeli had nabbed from the treasures that Valerius had gotten.

"This on the other hand is a Tier 2 Magical Catalyst," Silas added, placing the glowing sapphire necklace right next to the helmet. "It reduces mana consumption for water-affinity spells by fifteen percent and also flawless."
Elora leaned over the center console with her icy blue eyes critically analyzing the two artifacts.
She didn’t need to physically touch them since her own Lord interface automatically scanned the items, verifying their authenticity and structural integrity.
"Impressive," Elora murmured, clearly satisfied with the quality of the dungeon drops.

She tapped a series of complex commands into her own glowing, translucent interface hovering over the steering wheel. "I will purchase both of them from you for exactly three million Spirit Credits... That is ten percent above standard Association market value, considering their pristine condition."
Silas didn’t haggle. Three million was a windfall for two items he had literally gotten easily.
"Deal," Silas agreed instantly.
Elora swiped her hand across her interface.
DING!
His phone vibrated.
’The hell... how does she have my account?’ Silas thought but he didn’t say more after that.
Honestly he was okay as long as the money had arrived.
[Received: +3,000,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Current Financial Balance Updated.]
Silas watched the numbers completely skyrocket in his account with his heart fluttering at the satisfaction.
Combined with the money he had, he really had the liquid capital required to walk into the LA Building and buy whatever spell scrolls he wanted.
As soon as the credits hit his account, Elora gracefully reached over the console.

She tapped the physical items, and both the silver Valkyrie helmet and the glowing sapphire necklace instantly dissolved into a flurry of blue pixels, safely transferred directly into her own secure Lord Inventory.
’How do these people even link their cars to their Lord Inventories?’ Silas thought.
With the transaction flawlessly concluded, Elora smoothly merged the supercar back onto the highway, accelerating rapidly through the neon-lit canyons of the city.

They drove in comfortable silence for another fifteen minutes, navigating away from the dense towering residential sectors and moving toward the highly exclusive fortified commercial district of Valoria.
The supercar smoothly decelerated, pulling up a long perfectly paved driveway lined with glowing palm trees.
The car glided to a complete stop. Elora engaged the parking brake with the engine humming to a silent halt.
She reached for the handle and gracefully stepped out of the vehicle, her shoes clicking sharply against the polished pavement.
Silas frowned with his paranoia flaring again as he pushed his door open and stepped out of the car.
He stood up, adjusting his heavy trench coat, and looked around at their surroundings.
They were not at a restaurant... They were not at an estate either.
Instead they were standing on an incredibly massive illuminated guarded showroom floor.
They were at a... Car dealership?
But it wasn’t just any standard dealership.
It was a massive ultra-luxury vehicle showroom.
The floor was lined with dozens of incredibly sleek and armored magically reinforced supercars, hover-bikes, as well as assault transports that cost more than most small border bases.
Silas blinked, utterly confused.
He looked at Elora, who was standing confidently in front of her own vehicle.
"Elora," Silas asked, his voice dripping with profound confusion. "Why exactly are we here?"
Elora turned to him, offering a rare genuine and incredibly soft smile that completely melted her usual icy exterior.
She tucked a stray lock of blond hair behind her ear, her cheeks flushing a sudden brilliant shade of pink under the showroom lights.
"I brought you here to buy you a car," Elora answered smoothly, her voice carrying a completely uncharacteristic warm affection. "Isn’t that exactly what Girlfriends do for their boyfrien—"
Elora abruptly paused. Her mouth snapped shut with an audible click.

Her icy blue eyes went completely wide in panic as the brilliant pink flush on her cheeks violently exploded into a blinding shade of crimson that covered her entire face and traveled all the way down her neck.
In that critical horrifyingly embarrassing moment, Elora’s perfectly calculated genius-level noble mind realized exactly what she had just said.
In her eagerness to reward him for his bravery, she had completely fumbled the script.
Elora had mathematically skipped a whole fundamental stage in her intricate romantic plan.
She hadn’t even officially confessed her feelings to him yet!
Elora Verinda was a creature of uncompromising logic.
She was the City Lord’s daughter and she had been raised from birth to treat every single human interaction as a calculated game of chess.
’As Father advised me...’
She didn’t have friends... she had assets.
She didn’t have crushes... she had acquisition targets.
And her blueprint for acquiring Silas Graves had been incredibly simple, yet flawless in its design.
The major foundation of the blueprint dictated that during the extended downtime within this specific Secret Realm, she would execute Phase One.
She would find a secluded romantically charged moment in the desert to formally confess her attraction to him.
She would casually bring up the idea of dating, explicitly using the shared trauma and isolation of the Secret Realm as a psychological excuse to force them closer together.
Trauma bonded people worked... It was a proven psychological fact.
Once the initial dating protocol was formally established, she would initiate Phase Two: The Financial Flex.
She would use her massive near-infinite Verinda family wealth to casually buy him incredibly expensive gifts.
Heavy armor, skill tomes, mythril weapons. She would do it under the guise of ’investing in her partner’s survival.’
Proceeding smoothly from there into Phase Three, the constant influx of high-tier gifts and close physical proximity would naturally begin to break down his paranoia.
He would gradually get comfortable enough to drop his guard. He would start divulging the deep, heavily guarded secrets of his rapid growth, his territory, and the true nature of his power.
It was a perfect and completely foolproof corporate romance plot.

But as of right now, standing under the blindingly bright, fluorescent halogen lights of an ultra-luxury vehicle dealership at two in the afternoon, Elora realized with clarity that she had completely fumbled the execution.
She hadn’t just skipped Phase One.

She had aggressively bulldozed right past the first half Phase Two, completely bypassing the actual confession and the emotional groundwork, leaving them awkwardly stranded dead-center in the middle of Phase Three!
She had just offered to buy a multi-million-credit transport vehicle for a man she hadn’t even asked out to dinner yet...
Elora squeezed her eyes shut for a microsecond.
She took a deep shuddering breath with her icy blue aura subtly flaring to instantly cool the violent, embarrassed flush that was desperately trying to spread across her pale cheeks.
She was the daughter of the City Lord... She did not retreat from errors as instead she simply pushed entirely through them.
Elora opened her eyes, locking her piercing blue gaze directly onto Silas’s golden-ringed pupils.
"I love you," Elora confessed.
Her voice was completely deadpan, stripped of all pretense, and delivered with the uncompromising bluntness of a military casualty report.
Silas blinked.
He didn’t gasp, hell he didn’t even shift his posture.
He simply stood there on the pristine concrete of the dealership parking lot, his black shirt flapping slightly in the night breeze, staring at her with an expression of exhausted bewilderment.
’Again?’ Silas thought, mentally rubbing his temples.
For some completely inexplicable reason, his life had turned into a chaotic magnet for noble women with massive complexes.
First, it was Harper, throwing herself into a meat grinder of elites and practically getting herself impaled just to prove her twisted devotion.
Now, it was Elora Verinda.
The Ice Queen of Valoria City.
The woman who had wanted to recruit him a few days ago was now dropping a deadpan love confession in the parking lot of a luxury car dealership.
’Next, who exactly is it going to be?’ Silas aggressively wondered. ’Seraphina? Is she going to drop a solar fireball on my barracks and ask me to marry her in the ashes?!’

sentences.text: Jaxon didn’t say a word.
He simply clutched his empty Hero Summoning Card to his chest with his eyes blank as he slowly walked toward the heavily fortified entrance of his family’s estate.
Elora watched them go, her face turning impassive.
Once they were safely inside the perimeter, she tapped the dashboard, and the heavy doors hissed shut, perfectly sealing the cabin once more.
She smoothly shifted the car back into drive, smoothly merging back into the flow of neon-lit city traffic.
Elora drove in complete silence for a few minutes with her hands resting lightly on the glowing steering wheel.
She glanced over at Silas through the reflection of the windshield.
"Do you want to be dropped off somewhere specific, Silas?" Elora asked, her tone carefully neutral.
"Or do you have somewhere urgent to be?
It has been four, almost five entire days since we initially entered the Sovereign Realm so your Territory might be a main priority."
Silas considered the question.
Aeliana had been safely unsummoned and returned directly to the Blessed Land barracks.
She would undoubtedly relay the full report to Eluned and Morwenna, apart from that, Blessed Land was not in danger.
"No," Silas replied, leaning his head back.
"I am not urgently heading anywhere tonight.
The territory is secured."
Elora nodded slowly, her icy blue eyes flashing with a sudden glint of determination.
"Good," Elora said softly.
"Because there is somewhere specific I want to take you today."
Silas’s Warlord paranoia instantly spiked.
He narrowed his golden-ringed eyes, staring at the side of her flawless profile.
Taking him to a "secondary location" was usually code for an ambush.
But he was currently sitting on 4400 UP and possessed a Gold Core.
If she tried to betray him, he would simply freeze her car from the inside out.
’I might be forced to kill her too.’
"Fine," Silas begrudgingly agreed, letting out a sigh as he casually crossed his arms over his chest.
He secretly clutched his right hand into a tight fist, keeping his mana pathways perfectly primed for instant combat as she drove silently through the city.
As they navigated the sprawling, elevated highways, Silas’s mind immediately pivoted entirely back to his primary objective.
Right now, more than anything else in the world, he desperately wanted to get his hands on some new high-tier spells as soon as humanly possible.
He needed destructive offensive elements like Fire or Lightning to complement his defensive water and ice magic since he needed to hit that Adept Mastery in eight elements.
But buying even Tier 1 spell scrolls from the Lord Association marketplace was expensive.
He already had a significant stash of Spirit Credits in his account but to purchase the volume of scrolls he needed, one required a whole lot more liquid capital.
Silas uncrossed his arms, turning slightly to look at Elora in the driver’s seat.
"Elora," Silas broke the silence.
"Would you be interested in conducting a private transaction right now?...
Do you want to trade a treasure or two that I acquired during the Secret Realm expedition in exchange for liquid Spirit Credits?"
Elora didn’t take her eyes off the glowing road, but her interest was visibly piqued.
The Verinda family possessed very high financial resources, but finding genuine uncorrupted Secret Realm loot was always highly valuable for networking.
"I am always open to mutually beneficial commerce, Silas," Elora replied smoothly with the City Lord’s daughter instantly slipping back into her corporate element.
"What exactly would you like to trade?
I don’t mind purchasing artifacts directly from your inventory, provided they meet standard quality protocols."
"Could you find where to park first?" Silas instructed.
Elora smoothly guided the supercar into a designated parking alcove on the side of the highway, engaging the privacy wards of the vehicle.
Silas didn’t hesitate.
He raised his right hand, opening his Lord Inventory interface.
A blue screen materialized in the air between them, illuminating the dark cabin of the car to Silas and then he reached into the digital screen.
With a soft hum of spatial magic, he brought out an ornate beautifully forged silver combat helmet.
It was the pristine Valkyrie helmet that he had taken from Harper in exchange for providing her a roof over her head back in the desert.

He had originally meant to share this specific piece of armor with Valerius as a gesture of goodwill, but given everything that happened after including tectonic collapse and the arrival of Thor, both of them had completely forgotten about the loot split.
Silas placed the heavy silver helmet gently onto the center console.
"This is a Tier 2 Defensive Artifact," Silas stated, tapping the side of the helm.
"It increases baseline physical resistance by thirty percent and is in flawless condition."
He reached back into the glowing blue grid.
Clink!
He brought out a stunning intricate gold and sapphire necklace that practically hummed with water mana.
It was one of the fifteen treasures that Aeli had nabbed from the treasures that Valerius had gotten.
"This on the other hand is a Tier 2 Magical Catalyst," Silas added, placing the glowing sapphire necklace right next to the helmet.
"It reduces mana consumption for water-affinity spells by fifteen percent and also flawless."
Elora leaned over the center console with her icy blue eyes critically analyzing the two artifacts.
She didn’t need to physically touch them since her own Lord interface automatically scanned the items, verifying their authenticity and structural integrity.
"Impressive," Elora murmured, clearly satisfied with the quality of the dungeon drops.
She tapped a series of complex commands into her own glowing, translucent interface hovering over the steering wheel.
"I will purchase both of them from you for exactly three million Spirit Credits...
That is ten percent above standard Association market value, considering their pristine condition."
Silas didn’t haggle.
Three million was a windfall for two items he had literally gotten easily.
"Deal," Silas agreed instantly.
Elora swiped her hand across her interface.
DING!
His phone vibrated.
’The hell... how does she have my account?’ Silas thought but he didn’t say more after that.
Honestly he was okay as long as the money had arrived.
[Received: +3,000,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Current Financial Balance Updated.]
Silas watched the numbers completely skyrocket in his account with his heart fluttering at the satisfaction.
Combined with the money he had, he really had the liquid capital required to walk into the LA Building and buy whatever spell scrolls he wanted.
As soon as the credits hit his account, Elora gracefully reached over the console.

She tapped the physical items, and both the silver Valkyrie helmet and the glowing sapphire necklace instantly dissolved into a flurry of blue pixels, safely transferred directly into her own secure Lord Inventory.
’How do these people even link their cars to their Lord Inventories?’ Silas thought.
With the transaction flawlessly concluded, Elora smoothly merged the supercar back onto the highway, accelerating rapidly through the neon-lit canyons of the city.

They drove in comfortable silence for another fifteen minutes, navigating away from the dense towering residential sectors and moving toward the highly exclusive fortified commercial district of Valoria.
The supercar smoothly decelerated, pulling up a long perfectly paved driveway lined with glowing palm trees.
The car glided to a complete stop.
Elora engaged the parking brake with the engine humming to a silent halt.
She reached for the handle and gracefully stepped out of the vehicle, her shoes clicking sharply against the polished pavement.
Silas frowned with his paranoia flaring again as he pushed his door open and stepped out of the car.
He stood up, adjusting his heavy trench coat, and looked around at their surroundings.
They were not at a restaurant...
They were not at an estate either.
Instead they were standing on an incredibly massive illuminated guarded showroom floor.
They were at a...
Car dealership?
But it wasn’t just any standard dealership.
It was a massive ultra-luxury vehicle showroom.
The floor was lined with dozens of incredibly sleek and armored magically reinforced supercars, hover-bikes, as well as assault transports that cost more than most small border bases.
Silas blinked, utterly confused.
He looked at Elora, who was standing confidently in front of her own vehicle.
"Elora," Silas asked, his voice dripping with profound confusion.
"Why exactly are we here?"
Elora turned to him, offering a rare genuine and incredibly soft smile that completely melted her usual icy exterior.
She tucked a stray lock of blond hair behind her ear, her cheeks flushing a sudden brilliant shade of pink under the showroom lights.
"I brought you here to buy you a car," Elora answered smoothly, her voice carrying a completely uncharacteristic warm affection.
"Isn’t that exactly what Girlfriends do for their boyfrien—"
Elora abruptly paused.
Her mouth snapped shut with an audible click.

Her icy blue eyes went completely wide in panic as the brilliant pink flush on her cheeks violently exploded into a blinding shade of crimson that covered her entire face and traveled all the way down her neck.

In her eagerness to reward him for his bravery, she had completely fumbled the script.
Elora had mathematically skipped a whole fundamental stage in her intricate romantic plan.
She hadn’t even officially confessed her feelings to him yet!

chapters.title: Chapter 212: Luxury Dealership
paragraphs: Silas was so incredibly tired.
He had just fought a tectonic collapse... he had also just watched a Norse deity atomize a Sand God so was not in the mood for anime romance tropes.
Silas let out a long sigh, crossing his arms over his chest.
"Elora," Silas said dryly, his voice echoing with skepticism. "Stop joking. We literally just escaped a collapsing dimension... It’s not funny."
"I am not joking, Silas," Elora replied.
She stepped slightly closer.
The icy untouchable demeanor she usually wore like a suit of armor was entirely gone.
She looked up at him, her blue eyes shining with a rare seriousness that completely unsettled his eyes.

"I am completely serious," Elora told him, her voice softening just a fraction. "And I don’t want your answer right now. I am fully aware of my reputation, and I know exactly how intensely paranoid you are of the Valoria nobles such as myself."
She reached out with her pale hand but she didn’t grab his arm or his shoulder.
Elora gently slipped her slender fingers directly into his calloused right hand, interlocking their fingers with surprising warmth.

"I will give you all the time you require to think about it," Elora continued, her grip tightening slightly against his callouses. "But regardless of your paranoia... I want to do something genuinely good for the man that I love. You saved my life in the desert. You fought a god and you deserve a proper reward."
’Did she forget that it was we...?’
With that said, she didn’t wait for him to argue the logistics of the whole thing.
Elora simply turned and aggressively dragged him by the hand directly toward the massive fortified glass sliding doors of the dealership.

"Elora, wait," Silas protested with his heavy combat boots dragging slightly against the polished pavement as he tried to halt her momentum without physically throwing her off balance. "I appreciate the sentiment, but this is ridiculous... You can’t just buy me a car... I don’t even have a valid driver’s license."
Elora didn’t even break her stride as she casually rolled her icy blue eyes, pulling him harder toward the glass.

"Do not lie to me, Silas Graves," Elora scolded him without looking back with her memory flawlessly recalling everything. "I didn’t even need to read your public registry. I know for a fact that Valoria Academy hosted a mandatory transit event when our class turned seventeen... The Academy legally paid to have every single student in your slum district tested and certified for vehicular licenses to meet the City’s conscription quotas so you have a license."
Silas gritted his teeth.
She was right. He did, in fact, have a valid Class-C transit license gathering dust in his inventory.
It had been a miserable Tuesday when he was seventeen, sitting in a rusted Academy transport while an instructor yelled at him to check his mirrors.
But that wasn’t the point.
Before he could formulate another excuse to avoid accepting a massive financial handout from a noble, the massive, reinforced glass doors of the dealership automatically hissed open.
They stepped into the bright sterilized showroom floor of Apex Sovereign Motors.
The interior of the dealership was absolutely massive.
It smelled intensely of expensive leather, high-tier engine coolant and so much more that Silas couldn’t name.
The pristine white marble floor was lined with the pinnacle of modern engineering.

There were sleek aerodynamic supercars with anti-gravity thrusters, heavy-duty assault transports plated in depleted uranium, and high-speed interceptor bikes that looked like they belonged on a battlefield, not a highway.
’The hell...?’
The moment they stepped through the doors, a polished sharply dressed sales associate materialized from behind a glowing marble reception desk.
He wore a crisp, tailored suit and a forced perfectly practiced customer-service smile. But as the associate’s eyes landed on the two individuals who had just walked in, that smile completely froze.
The associate’s internal alarm bells aggressively went off.
Standing in his pristine showroom was a dark-haired man wearing a heavy, scuffed black shirt that was literally dripping with ried foul-smelling monster blood.
He had a lethal-looking mythril longsword strapped to his hip, and his golden-ringed eyes swept the room with a curious look.
And standing right next to him, holding his hand, was a woman whose highly expensive frost-silk robes were torn to shreds, covered in soot.
They looked like they had just crawled out of a mass grave!
"Welcome to Apex Sovereign Motors," the associate greeted them, his voice trembling slightly as he forced himself to bow.
He nervously eyed the dried blood on Silas’s boots. "How... how may I be of assistance this evening?"
"We are purchasing a vehicle," Elora stated coldly, instantly slipping back into her untouchable City Lord persona.
She completely ignored the man’s terrified stare. "A heavy-duty, high-performance Supercar so we require immediate access to the VIP inventory."
The sales associate blinked, his professional smile faltering into panic.

"O-Of course, Madam," the associate stammered, holding up his hands defensively. "However, company protocol strictly mandates... to access the heavily fortified VIP and military-grade inventory, I am legally required by the Valoria Lord Association to verify the identification and security clearance of both the purchaser and the intended recipient..."
He looked at Silas’s aesthetic with obvious poorly hidden disdain. He assumed they were scavengers who had struck it rich on a lucky drop.
Silas sighed heavily.
He reached into his coat pocket, pulling out his battered, scratched, standard-issue Lord Association ID card. He tossed it onto the marble desk with a dull clack.
The associate glanced at it.
[Silas Graves]
’Blue Core...? But still, he’s from Sector 4.’ The man thought.
"I’m sorry, sir," the associate said with his voice turning instantly patronizing. "But the VIP levels require a minimum Class-A aristocratic clearance. I cannot allow you down—"
Elora didn’t say a word.
She simply raised her left hand, projecting her glowing blue interface directly into the associate’s face.
The holographic crest of the Verinda family... a massive intricate snowflake wrapped in golden chains flashed brilliantly in the air, illuminating the entire reception desk in cold blue light.
"Are you done? I’m getting tired of this."
The sales associate’s eyes went comically wide as the blood instantly drained from his face.
He recognized the unquestionable authority of the City Lord’s bloodline.
The patronizing sneer vanished, replaced by pants-wetting terror.
He had just tried to deny access to the daughter of the man who literally owned the city!

"L-Lady Verinda!" the associate gasped, dropping to a full ninety-degree bow, his forehead nearly slamming into the marble desk. "My deepest apologies! I did not recognize you in... in your current attire! Please, forgive my insolence! Right this way! The VIP elevator is immediately available!"
He frantically scrambled out from behind the desk, practically sprinting toward a set of heavy blast-proof steel doors at the back of the showroom.
Silas smirked, thoroughly enjoying the sudden shift in tone.
’So this is what it means to be a Lord, huh?’ Silas thought as he casually picked his ID card off the desk, sliding it back into his coat as he let Elora pull him along.
Usually being a Blue core was enough for places like this but apparently this place was so influential that it didn’t even acknowledge giving him special treatment because he was one.
The heavy steel doors hissed open, and they stepped into the massive high-speed freight elevator.
The associate frantically keyed in a twelve-digit security code, his hands shaking, and the elevator aggressively descended deep into the lower levels of the dealership.

"You really don’t have to do this, Elora," Silas muttered, crossing his arms and leaning back against the steel wall as they descended. "I can just buy a regular transport from somewhere tomorrow. I don’t need a luxury tank."

"You are a Lord of a rapidly expanding territory, Silas, As your Hero’s strength proved..." Elora lectured him while looking straight ahead at the elevator doors. "You cannot show up to subjugation raids that I plan to invite you to by driving a rusted carrier. It projects extreme weakness to the other factions... You need a vehicle that accurately reflects your lethality."
’Why is she even going so far?’
"I project lethality by cutting people in half," Silas countered dryly. "Not by having expensive seats."
The elevator doors chimed and smoothly slid open.
They stepped out into a massive fortified and brilliantly illuminated underground bunker that served as the true VIP showroom.
This wasn’t a place for sleek fragile sports cars or vanity projects. This specific level was dedicated entirely to well... the peak.
Massive armored transports were parked in pristine and perfectly illuminated bays.

Some possessed mounted, retractable mana-turrets on the roof. Others featured thick, tank-tread tracks explicitly designed for traversing completely hostile uncharted Secret Realms or areas in the Sovereign Realm.
A few were sleek aggressive interceptors built purely for ramming through reinforced concrete barricades.
’What the hell is all this...?’
"Show us your top-tier terrestrial models," Elora commanded the associate, who was still actively sweating through his tailored suit.
"Right away, Lady Verinda!" the associate squeaked, eagerly leading them down the wide, polished aisle.
He gestured enthusiastically to a boxy plated transport vehicle painted in standard utilitarian military olive drab.

"This is the Goliath MK-IV..." the associate presented proudly, tapping the thick armor plating. "It features dual-layered titanium hull reinforcement, a baseline dampening field, and a massive rear cargo hold capable of comfortably transporting up to twelve big crates of raw materials. It is highly reliable, incredibly sturdy, and retails for a very reasonable eight hundred thousand Spirit Credits."
Elora looked at the boxy, uninspired, completely utilitarian vehicle and immediately turned up her nose in sheer aristocratic disgust.
"It looks like a garbage delivery truck," Elora dismissed it coldly. "I am not putting my partner in a glorified moving van... Show us something with actual presence."
Silas, however, narrowed his golden-ringed eyes. He actually really liked the Goliath.

"Wait," Silas interrupted, stepping toward the olive-drab transport and running his calloused hand over the thick cold titanium plating. ’This could actually fit into Blessed Land but I have to convince her...’

"This is very practical," Silas argued, looking at the massive tires and the high ground clearance. "It doesn’t draw unnecessary attention on the highway. It has excellent suspension for the rough unpaved terrain around my territory and that massive cargo space in the back? That is exactly what I need for hauling heavy dungeon loot, monster corpses, and building materials back to the base. I choose this one. Eight hundred thousand is reasonable."
Elora turned to him, her icy blue eyes narrowing in profound, absolute disapproval.
"Absolutely not," Elora vetoed his choice instantly.
She aggressively grabbed his arm, completely ignoring his arguments, and physically dragged him further down the illuminated aisle.
"I want to get you a real car... not a truck."
"Elora, I need cargo space!" Silas grumbled, his boots dragging.
"You are not a delivery boy!" she snapped back.
They stopped at the very end of the bunker, directly in front of the premier elevated display bay.
Sitting under a ring of perfectly angled spotlights was a monster of engineering.
It was a low-slung hyper-advanced supercar.
The exterior was coated in a flawless black finish that practically swallowed the glaring showroom lights.
It had an incredibly aerodynamic profile, sitting mere inches from the floor on four wide-track, run-flat performance tires.
The body was completely seamless.
It was forged from a dark mythril-alloy blend that looked sleek enough for a high-society gala in the central district, yet sturdy enough to survive a carpet bombing.
Subtle silver runic engravings lined the undercarriage, pulsing faintly with latent kinetic-redirection magic to keep the car glued to the asphalt at high speeds.

"This," the associate announced, his voice dropping into a hushed reverent whisper as if he were unveiling the Holy Grail, "is the Zenith IVR. It is the pinnacle of terrestrial luxury and survivability combined in one."
The associate practically vibrated with excitement as he rattled off the spec sheet.

"The chassis is a pure mythril-carbon weave. It handles like a premier track car on the city highways but possesses the structural resistance of a heavy Vanguard’s shield. Under the hood, you have a highly advanced, dual-core anti-gravity mana engine. It generates over twelve hundred horsepower, allowing for a seamless instantaneous transition between standard terrestrial driving and emergency hover-evasion."
He patted the matte-black hood with a gloved hand.

"The windows are forged from enchanted dragon-glass. They are completely shatterproof against anything below an Tier-3 elemental strike. Inside, the cabin is fully climate-controlled and outfitted with subtle spatial-expansion runes. It guarantees maximum ergonomic comfort and legroom, even for a driver of your... formidable physical stature."
The associate paused. He smoothed his tailored tie, gulping nervously as he looked toward Elora.
"However... it is our most exclusive daily-driver model in the entire facility. It retails for exactly three point eight million Spirit Credits."
Elora didn’t even blink at the astronomical price tag.
She slowly looked over the terrifyingly sleek black supercar then, she turned her head and looked right at Silas.
Her icy blue eyes took in his aesthetic with the black shirt and the naturally intimidating cold aura he constantly projected.
It was a flawless visual match.
"It matches you perfectly," Elora declared, her voice ringing with satisfaction.
She turned back to the associate, completely unfazed by the cost. "We will take this one."
"Elora, no," Silas argued fiercely, aggressively stepping between her and the vehicle.
Was she trying to make him go broke trying to pay her back?!
