"We are purchasing a vehicle," Elora stated coldly, instantly slipping back into her untouchable City Lord persona.
She completely ignored the man’s terrified stare.
"A heavy-duty, high-performance Supercar so we require immediate access to the VIP inventory."
The sales associate blinked, his professional smile faltering into panic.
"O-Of course, Madam," the associate stammered, holding up his hands defensively.

"However, company protocol strictly mandates... to access the heavily fortified VIP and military-grade inventory, I am legally required by the Valoria Lord Association to verify the identification and security clearance of both the purchaser and the intended recipient..."
He looked at Silas’s aesthetic with obvious poorly hidden disdain.
He assumed they were scavengers who had struck it rich on a lucky drop.
Silas sighed heavily.
He reached into his coat pocket, pulling out his battered, scratched, standard-issue Lord Association ID card.
He tossed it onto the marble desk with a dull clack.
The associate glanced at it.
[Silas Graves]
’Blue Core...?
But still, he’s from Sector 4.’ The man thought.
"I’m sorry, sir," the associate said with his voice turning instantly patronizing.
"But the VIP levels require a minimum Class-A aristocratic clearance.
I cannot allow you down—"
Elora didn’t say a word.
She simply raised her left hand, projecting her glowing blue interface directly into the associate’s face.
The holographic crest of the Verinda family... a massive intricate snowflake wrapped in golden chains flashed brilliantly in the air, illuminating the entire reception desk in cold blue light.
"Are you done?
I’m getting tired of this."
The sales associate’s eyes went comically wide as the blood instantly drained from his face.
He recognized the unquestionable authority of the City Lord’s bloodline.
The patronizing sneer vanished, replaced by pants-wetting terror.
He had just tried to deny access to the daughter of the man who literally owned the city!
"L-Lady Verinda!" the associate gasped, dropping to a full ninety-degree bow, his forehead nearly slamming into the marble desk.
"My deepest apologies!
I did not recognize you in... in your current attire!
Please, forgive my insolence!
Right this way!
The VIP elevator is immediately available!"
He frantically scrambled out from behind the desk, practically sprinting toward a set of heavy blast-proof steel doors at the back of the showroom.
Silas smirked, thoroughly enjoying the sudden shift in tone.
’So this is what it means to be a Lord, huh?’ Silas thought as he casually picked his ID card off the desk, sliding it back into his coat as he let Elora pull him along.
Usually being a Blue core was enough for places like this but apparently this place was so influential that it didn’t even acknowledge giving him special treatment because he was one.
The heavy steel doors hissed open, and they stepped into the massive high-speed freight elevator.
The associate frantically keyed in a twelve-digit security code, his hands shaking, and the elevator aggressively descended deep into the lower levels of the dealership.
"You really don’t have to do this, Elora," Silas muttered, crossing his arms and leaning back against the steel wall as they descended.
"I can just buy a regular transport from somewhere tomorrow.
I don’t need a luxury tank."
"You are a Lord of a rapidly expanding territory, Silas, As your Hero’s strength proved..." Elora lectured him while looking straight ahead at the elevator doors.
"You cannot show up to subjugation raids that I plan to invite you to by driving a rusted carrier.
It projects extreme weakness to the other factions...
You need a vehicle that accurately reflects your lethality."
’Why is she even going so far?’
"I project lethality by cutting people in half," Silas countered dryly.
"Not by having expensive seats."
The elevator doors chimed and smoothly slid open.
They stepped out into a massive fortified and brilliantly illuminated underground bunker that served as the true VIP showroom.
This wasn’t a place for sleek fragile sports cars or vanity projects.
This specific level was dedicated entirely to well... the peak.
Massive armored transports were parked in pristine and perfectly illuminated bays.
Some possessed mounted, retractable mana-turrets on the roof.
Others featured thick, tank-tread tracks explicitly designed for traversing completely hostile uncharted Secret Realms or areas in the Sovereign Realm.
A few were sleek aggressive interceptors built purely for ramming through reinforced concrete barricades.
’What the hell is all this...?’
"Show us your top-tier terrestrial models," Elora commanded the associate, who was still actively sweating through his tailored suit.
"Right away, Lady Verinda!" the associate squeaked, eagerly leading them down the wide, polished aisle.
He gestured enthusiastically to a boxy plated transport vehicle painted in standard utilitarian military olive drab.
"This is the Goliath MK-IV..." the associate presented proudly, tapping the thick armor plating.
"It features dual-layered titanium hull reinforcement, a baseline dampening field, and a massive rear cargo hold capable of comfortably transporting up to twelve big crates of raw materials.
It is highly reliable, incredibly sturdy, and retails for a very reasonable eight hundred thousand Spirit Credits."
Elora looked at the boxy, uninspired, completely utilitarian vehicle and immediately turned up her nose in sheer aristocratic disgust.
"It looks like a garbage delivery truck," Elora dismissed it coldly.
"I am not putting my partner in a glorified moving van...
Show us something with actual presence."
Silas, however, narrowed his golden-ringed eyes.
He actually really liked the Goliath.

"Wait," Silas interrupted, stepping toward the olive-drab transport and running his calloused hand over the thick cold titanium plating. ’This could actually fit into Blessed Land but I have to convince her...’
"This is very practical," Silas argued, looking at the massive tires and the high ground clearance.
"It doesn’t draw unnecessary attention on the highway.
It has excellent suspension for the rough unpaved terrain around my territory and that massive cargo space in the back?
That is exactly what I need for hauling heavy dungeon loot, monster corpses, and building materials back to the base.
I choose this one.
Eight hundred thousand is reasonable."
Elora turned to him, her icy blue eyes narrowing in profound, absolute disapproval.
"Absolutely not," Elora vetoed his choice instantly.
She aggressively grabbed his arm, completely ignoring his arguments, and physically dragged him further down the illuminated aisle.
"I want to get you a real car... not a truck."
"Elora, I need cargo space!" Silas grumbled, his boots dragging.
"You are not a delivery boy!" she snapped back.
They stopped at the very end of the bunker, directly in front of the premier elevated display bay.
Sitting under a ring of perfectly angled spotlights was a monster of engineering.
It was a low-slung hyper-advanced supercar.
The exterior was coated in a flawless black finish that practically swallowed the glaring showroom lights.
It had an incredibly aerodynamic profile, sitting mere inches from the floor on four wide-track, run-flat performance tires.
The body was completely seamless.
It was forged from a dark mythril-alloy blend that looked sleek enough for a high-society gala in the central district, yet sturdy enough to survive a carpet bombing.
Subtle silver runic engravings lined the undercarriage, pulsing faintly with latent kinetic-redirection magic to keep the car glued to the asphalt at high speeds.
"This," the associate announced, his voice dropping into a hushed reverent whisper as if he were unveiling the Holy Grail, "is the Zenith IVR.
It is the pinnacle of terrestrial luxury and survivability combined in one."
The associate practically vibrated with excitement as he rattled off the spec sheet.
"The chassis is a pure mythril-carbon weave.
It handles like a premier track car on the city highways but possesses the structural resistance of a heavy Vanguard’s shield.
Under the hood, you have a highly advanced, dual-core anti-gravity mana engine.
It generates over twelve hundred horsepower, allowing for a seamless instantaneous transition between standard terrestrial driving and emergency hover-evasion."
He patted the matte-black hood with a gloved hand.
"The windows are forged from enchanted dragon-glass.
They are completely shatterproof against anything below an Tier-3 elemental strike.
Inside, the cabin is fully climate-controlled and outfitted with subtle spatial-expansion runes.
It guarantees maximum ergonomic comfort and legroom, even for a driver of your... formidable physical stature."
The associate paused.
He smoothed his tailored tie, gulping nervously as he looked toward Elora.
"However... it is our most exclusive daily-driver model in the entire facility.
It retails for exactly three point eight million Spirit Credits."
Elora didn’t even blink at the astronomical price tag.
She slowly looked over the terrifyingly sleek black supercar then, she turned her head and looked right at Silas.
Her icy blue eyes took in his aesthetic with the black shirt and the naturally intimidating cold aura he constantly projected.
It was a flawless visual match.
"It matches you perfectly," Elora declared, her voice ringing with satisfaction.
She turned back to the associate, completely unfazed by the cost.
"We will take this one."
"Elora, no," Silas argued fiercely, aggressively stepping between her and the vehicle.
Was she trying to make him go broke trying to pay her back?!

chapters.title: Chapter 213: Zenith IVR
paragraphs: His brain was actively screaming at the ridiculous waste of capital.

"Three point eight million is a joke!" Silas argued fiercely, stepping between Elora and the gleaming black supercar. "I am not driving a stealth interceptor to the grocery store or the Association building! The Goliath transport was perfectly fine for hauling dungeon drops since I can take it to my territory too! I don’t need a twelve-hundred-horsepower anti-gravity engine just to commute from Silverleaf!"
They stood in the middle of the subterranean VIP showroom, aggressively arguing back and forth for several minutes.
The acoustics of the concrete bunker echoed with their voices as they clashed over the necessity of aesthetics versus practical ground-level utility.

Elora Verinda, entirely determined to crush his stubborn independence and secure her romantic investment, actively attempted to flex her massive wealth to convince him the price tag simply didn’t matter.
’It shouldn’t be a problem if I tell him what I have right?’ Elora thought, it had been a long time since she had actually tried to convince someone so Elora was a bit confused.

"Silas, you are being completely ridiculous!" Elora huffed, crossing her arms tightly over her chest and glaring right back at him. "Three point eight million is pocket change to the Verinda estate and me in extension! Do you have any idea how many vehicles I personally own?!"
She gestured wildly around the massive illuminated room.

"I have a customized, diamond-plated hover-yacht that cost twenty-five million credits just sitting in a private dock at my summer estate! I haven’t even used the damn thing in two years! I have three different sports cars specifically tuned for ice-terrain racing that I only take out on holiday weekends! I am paying for this vehicle regardless of your protests! It doesn’t affect my bottom line in the slightest! Just let me spoil you..."
However, her massive financial flex completely backfired.
Instead of being impressed by her vast resources, Silas blinked with a confused expression.
’Huh...? Are those Billionaire activities I hear?’ Silas thought.
One would probably think that he cared about the slums because he was from there but honestly...
’Fuck those fuckers!’
He didn’t care about the slums, he didn’t have any lingering trauma about starving families in Sector 4 either. Those fuckers had bullied him for his money when he was quite weak.
’But I have to say I’m very jealous.’ Silas thought.
He had lived two lives and in those two lives, he had to pull himself from the ground up and hustle and then there were people like this... Who were born with this.
"Twenty-five million credits for a yacht you don’t even use?!" Silas growled, his golden-ringed eyes flashing with genuine deep-seated anger.
Or as one could say, Jealousy.
He took a heavy step toward her with his towering muscular frame casting a long shadow over her pale blonde hair.

"Do you have any idea what twenty-five million credits buys?!" Silas snapped, offended by the strategic stupidity of it all. "That buys five full sets of Tier 3 to Tier 4 full body armor! It buys a literal mountain of high-tier elemental spell scrolls and enough raw mana crystals to power a fortress for a decade! You could lock down a city block from a dragon strike with that capital, and you just let it sit in a dock rotting... And now you want to drop nearly nine million on a stealth supercar just because it ’matches my coat’?! I am not letting you waste that kind of raw capital on a vanity project!"
Elora instantly realized her massive error.
She had approached this entirely wrong as she had tried to impress a ruthless efficiency-obsessed Lord with frivolous vanity spending.
Flexing dead assets was the exact opposite of what he respected.
She immediately dropped the financial flexing as she pivoted flawlessly to a different and infinitely more potent weaponized approach.
She stepped incredibly close to him, completely invading his personal space.
She looked up into his angry golden eyes with her expression softening entirely into one of pure vulnerability.
"Silas," Elora whispered softly, her voice barely carrying over the ambient hum of the showroom lights. "Please."
She didn’t talk about money anymore as she talked about loyalty, reputation, and the brutal politics of the Sovereign Realm.

"Just let me do this for you," Elora pleaded, her icy blue eyes wide and entirely sincere. "If you drive back to your estate or pull up to the Valoria Lord Association in a delivery truck... the other Valoria people won’t just mock you. They will openly disrespect you. They will look at your vehicle, assume your territory is starved for resources, and they will think you are weak."
’That’s why I keep going in cabs!’ Silas thought but honestly cabs were quite expensive
She gently placed her pale hand flat against his chest, right over his rapidly beating heart, feeling the thrum of his core beneath his ribs.
’If only I could see the color...’

"In this city, perception is reality," Elora whispered, delivering the killing blow. "And I cannot bear the thought of them disrespecting the man I love. I want them to look at what you drive and know exactly how dangerous you are so just take the Zenith. For me."
Silas stood there with his jaw locked so incredibly tight his teeth ached.
He stared down at her pleading blue eyes.
’Sigh... this woman... I have no idea what this woman is planning so I can’t say however if I keep rejecting her, that might affect my relationship with her in the future.’ She thought.

If she wanted to go on more Secret Realm raids, would she call him if he offended her? The answer was quite literally a no... and even if the first Secret Realm raid he ever did was quite trashy, there was at least some good to be found there.
’Like I actually got to see Thor in action...’
Thor was very strong and it helped him set a goal... He wanted to be like that, before Silas wanted to head to Asgard, he would be as strong as Thor.
’Besides...’
According to Elora, she wasn’t buying it to show off; she was buying it to protect his territorial reputation.
He let out a long defeated groan that echoed through the quiet showroom.
"Fine," Silas grumbled, aggressively rubbing his temples to soothe an incoming stress headache. "I will take the damn supercar."
Elora’s face instantly lit up with a brilliant victorious smile.
"Excellent choice, My Lord!" the sales associate cheered from the sidelines, practically skipping over to the nearby marble control console.
He was thrilled to secure the massive, multi-million-credit commission.

"Before we finalize the paperwork and the legal transfer of ownership," the associate offered eagerly, his fingers dancing across the glowing runic keyboard. "you are fully authorized to take the Zenith IVR for a live test drive! Our underground reinforced testing facility is located directly beneath this floor. It is specifically designed to handle high-speed telemetry."
Silas didn’t argue.
If he was getting a nearly nine-million-credit supercar, he wanted to see exactly what that kind of capital actually felt like behind the wheel.
He walked over to the massive black machine.
The heavy, aerodynamic gull-wing doors hissed open automatically, gliding upward on perfectly silent hydraulic hinges as the interface registered his physical proximity.
He slid down into the low-slung armored driver’s seat.
The interior was once again a marvel of engineering.
It didn’t smell like a cheap factory assembly line... it smelled like raw concentrated power if one could smell it.
The seats were heavily bolstered, wrapped in dark durable and magically treated monster-leather that immediately contoured to his broad shoulders, providing flawless lumbar support.
The dashboard was a sleek, minimalist array of glowing, holographic displays and tactical HUDs.

The moment he sat down, the system actively synced with his visual perception, projecting his speed, mana-engine temperature, and structural integrity directly onto the polarized dragon-glass windshield.
The steering wheel was thick and grip-taped with anti-slip material, it felt perfectly weighted in his calloused hands.
Even with his towering frame, the subtle spatial-expansion runes woven into the cabin’s architecture gave him an incredible amount of legroom.
Elora gracefully slid into the passenger seat beside him, pulling the multi-point racing harness over her chest and securing it with a satisfying, metallic click.
"Start the engine," Elora instructed him with a little gleam sparking in her icy blue eyes.
She was quite proud that she had convinced him into agreeing to buy this car.
’I’d like to see Harper try to do this...’
Silas reached out and pressed the glowing runic red ignition button located on the carbon-fiber center console.
VROOOOOOOOOOM!
The massive dual-core anti-gravity mana-engine roared to life.
It sounded like an ancient slumbering storm dragon being violently woken up from a century-long nap.
The entire bunker actively shook from the overwhelming acoustic power of the twelve-hundred-horsepower engine activating for the first time.

A deep vibration traveled straight up through the steering column, flowed up his muscular arms, and settled directly into Silas’s chest, perfectly resonating with the aggressive thrumming hum of his own Gold Core.
The heavy blast doors directly in front of the vehicle hissed open.
They revealed a massive reinforced underground testing track.
It was a sprawling, multi-stage facility over a mile long, illuminated by harsh overhead arc lights.
It was filled with long straightaways, simulated rough terrain, massive concrete barricades, holographic targeting arrays, and sweeping hairpin turns.
Silas grabbed the heavy, polished shifter, seamlessly slamming the vehicle into drive.
He didn’t ease into it and he didn’t gently test the pedals.
’Given how expensive it is... I won’t hold back.’
He treated the hyper-advanced vehicle exactly like an extension of his own body.
SKREEEEEEECH!
Silas slammed his heavy combat boot directly down onto the accelerator pedal, completely flooring it instantly.
The sleek Zenith IVR violently launched forward like a fired railgun slug.
The terrifying torque pinned both Silas and Elora completely back into their heavily bolstered leather seats with an incredible bone-crushing amount of G-force.
Well that was why the car was meant for lords.
The acceleration was so instantaneous that it temporarily forced the breath entirely from his lungs.
’It’s quite good.’ Silas thought while breathing in.
They tore down the subterranean testing track at terrifying speeds with the concrete walls of the tunnel blurred into a continuous dizzying streak of gray.
Approaching the first major obstacle... a massive solid concrete pillar.
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes narrowed in deep focus as he didn’t even tap the brakes.
He aggressively whipped the heavy steering wheel to the left, throwing the multi-ton supercar into a high-speed screaming drift.
VROOOOOM! SCREEEECH!
The advanced anti-gravity suspension flawlessly absorbed the intense shock.
The massive wide-track treaded tires gripped the polished concrete with terrifying tenacity, screaming in protest but refusing to spin out or lose traction.
The kinetic-redirection runes etched into the undercarriage flared with bright silver light, actively pushing the car down against the centrifugal force, keeping them perfectly anchored to the floor.

Silas effortlessly wove the sleek interceptor through a narrow dangerous series of simulated barricades and tight chicane turns at over a hundred and fifty miles per hour but he didn’t lose a single ounce of control.
The steering responded to his micro-adjustments immediately too.

He hit a simulated rock incline specifically designed to test the vehicle’s off-road and evasion capabilities so instead of hitting the brakes to carefully navigate the bumps, Silas aggressively accelerated.
The heavy Mythril suspension actively engaged.
The dual-core anti-gravity thrusters mounted beneath the chassis momentarily fired with a loud pressurized hiss, generating a cushion of repelling force.

The massive supercar effortlessly bounded completely over the jagged vertical terrain but it didn’t transfer a single drop of turbulence into the luxurious cabin... it felt exactly like they were gliding on frictionless glass.
Hitting the final straightaway, Silas pushed the mana-engine to its redline with the digital speedometer projected on the windshield rapidly climbing past two hundred miles per hour.
He hit the ceramic brakes at the very end of the track, throwing the steering wheel hard to the right to execute a final 180-degree power-slide.
’It almost feels like I’m in Need For Speed...’ Silas thought, ’Well without the police chasing me and all that.’
He was only doing this because this was a very expensive car, if it wasn’t, he would have driven it normally.
The Zenith IVR came to a flawless halt directly in front of the heavy steel exit doors.
The cabin was completely silent for a moment, save for the heavy idling hum of the massive engine and the sharp ticking of rapidly cooling mythril.
Silas sat there in the driver’s seat with his hands gripping the steering wheel tight.
His heart was hammering violently against his ribs as pure adrenaline flooded his veins.
He looked at the glowing holographic dashboard, then ran his hand affectionately over the smooth flawless leather of the wheel.
He hated to admit it. but he loved the car.
It was perfection.
The car was aggressive, it was virtually indestructible too and the physical power of the engine felt like a direct mechanical translation of his own Gold Core aura.
Silas slowly turned his head, looking over at Elora in the passenger seat.
The City Lord’s daughter was breathing a bit from the intense G-force of the drift with her chest rising and falling against the racing harness.

Her pale blonde hair was slightly messy, completely blown out of its perfect cascading waves by the velocity of the maneuver but a wildly triumphant satisfied smirk was plastered across her flawless face.
"I like how it feels," Silas admitted quietly, completely unable to hide the satisfaction in his rough voice.

Approaching the first major obstacle... a massive solid concrete pillar.
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes narrowed in deep focus as he didn’t even tap the brakes.
He aggressively whipped the heavy steering wheel to the left, throwing the multi-ton supercar into a high-speed screaming drift.
VROOOOOM!
SCREEEECH!
The advanced anti-gravity suspension flawlessly absorbed the intense shock.
The massive wide-track treaded tires gripped the polished concrete with terrifying tenacity, screaming in protest but refusing to spin out or lose traction.
The kinetic-redirection runes etched into the undercarriage flared with bright silver light, actively pushing the car down against the centrifugal force, keeping them perfectly anchored to the floor.

Silas effortlessly wove the sleek interceptor through a narrow dangerous series of simulated barricades and tight chicane turns at over a hundred and fifty miles per hour but he didn’t lose a single ounce of control.
The steering responded to his micro-adjustments immediately too.

He hit a simulated rock incline specifically designed to test the vehicle’s off-road and evasion capabilities so instead of hitting the brakes to carefully navigate the bumps, Silas aggressively accelerated.
The heavy Mythril suspension actively engaged.
The dual-core anti-gravity thrusters mounted beneath the chassis momentarily fired with a loud pressurized hiss, generating a cushion of repelling force.

The massive supercar effortlessly bounded completely over the jagged vertical terrain but it didn’t transfer a single drop of turbulence into the luxurious cabin... it felt exactly like they were gliding on frictionless glass.
Hitting the final straightaway, Silas pushed the mana-engine to its redline with the digital speedometer projected on the windshield rapidly climbing past two hundred miles per hour.
He hit the ceramic brakes at the very end of the track, throwing the steering wheel hard to the right to execute a final 180-degree power-slide.
’It almost feels like I’m in Need For Speed...’ Silas thought, ’Well without the police chasing me and all that.’
He was only doing this because this was a very expensive car, if it wasn’t, he would have driven it normally.
The Zenith IVR came to a flawless halt directly in front of the heavy steel exit doors.
The cabin was completely silent for a moment, save for the heavy idling hum of the massive engine and the sharp ticking of rapidly cooling mythril.
Silas sat there in the driver’s seat with his hands gripping the steering wheel tight.
His heart was hammering violently against his ribs as pure adrenaline flooded his veins.
He looked at the glowing holographic dashboard, then ran his hand affectionately over the smooth flawless leather of the wheel.
He hated to admit it. but he loved the car.
It was perfection.
The car was aggressive, it was virtually indestructible too and the physical power of the engine felt like a direct mechanical translation of his own Gold Core aura.
Silas slowly turned his head, looking over at Elora in the passenger seat.
The City Lord’s daughter was breathing a bit from the intense G-force of the drift with her chest rising and falling against the racing harness.

Her pale blonde hair was slightly messy, completely blown out of its perfect cascading waves by the velocity of the maneuver but a wildly triumphant satisfied smirk was plastered across her flawless face.
"I like how it feels," Silas admitted quietly, completely unable to hide the satisfaction in his rough voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 214: Picking Lia Up
paragraphs: Elora’s smirk widened into a genuine smile of victory.
’Good... Now I need to get him to go on a date or something with me and we’ll be good.’ Elora thought.
She needed them to start dating as soon as possible or instead be very close to each other, enough for him to spill his secrets to her.
’But for now, I need to focus.’
She tapped a rapid series of commands into the glowing holographic interface on the passenger-side dashboard.
She was wirelessly connecting her personal encrypted financial account directly to the dealership’s secure mainframe.
DING!
[Payment Authorized.]
[Deduction: -8,300,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Transaction Complete. Transfer of Ownership Finalized.]
"The vehicle is now yours, Silas..." Elora announced smoothly, unbuckling her safety harness with a soft click.
Silas flinched slightly at the casual, instant deletion of nearly nine million credits but he didn’t argue this time.
He knew he had thoroughly lost this specific battle of wills, and he wasn’t going to look a gift-supercar in the mouth.
Elora pushed the heavy passenger door open.
It hissed upward on its hydraulic hinges, and she gracefully stepped out of the idling vehicle with her expensive heels landing perfectly on the polished concrete of the testing track.
She turned back, leaning into the sleek cabin to look at him one last time.

"Do not bother worrying about the cost, Silas," Elora told him softly, her icy blue eyes locking onto his with intense affection, at least that was how Silas sore it... It was the same look in Harper’s eyes after all. "It is an investment in your safety so I fully expect to see this transport parked proudly in the Valoria central district the next time you visit the city."
She offered him a final intimate smile.
"Goodbye, Silas Graves," Elora whispered into the cabin. "Sleep well. I will contact you soon."
With that, Elora turned around and walked briskly toward the VIP freight elevator at the far end of the track.
She was heading back upstairs to the main showroom to retrieve her own parked vehicle.
The heavy steel elevator doors hissed shut behind her, leaving Silas completely alone in the testing facility.
Silas sat in the driver’s seat of his brand-new supercar as the heavy mana-engine hummed aggressively around him.
He leaned back in the comfortable leather seat, letting out a long exhausted sigh.
He was finally alone.
The dead god was gone and the Secret Realm had collapsed.
The chaotic noblewomen had officially departed and not only that but he had a massive mountain of Upgrade Points, a fat bank account from selling his dungeon loot, and an indestructible supercar.
It was time to go home.
It was time to drive back to his estate in Silverleaf, check on his house and territory, and begin plotting his massive power-leveling training arc so he could finally master eight elements.
Silas grabbed the heavy shifter, preparing to throw the vehicle back into drive then, he paused.
He blinked his golden-ringed eyes, looking out the reinforced dragon-glass windshield.
He was currently parked dead center in the middle of a fortified subterranean testing track located several floors beneath the actual street level of the city.
The only exit he could see was the massive freight elevator Elora had just used which was explicitly designed for walking passengers, not low-slung hyper-advanced supercars.
Silas slowly rolled down the armored driver’s side window.
He leaned his head out of the sleek cabin, looking up toward a glowing security camera mounted high on the concrete wall.
"Hey," Silas called out, his deep voice echoing loudly in the massive empty underground bunker.
He waited for a few seconds, listening until the sales associate finally clicked on the intercom overhead.
"Yes, Lord Graves?" the associate’s nervous voice crackled through the speaker. "Is there an issue with the vehicle?"
"So..." Silas asked the camera, feeling completely stupid for the very first time in his career as a Lord. "...how exactly do I get this thing to the surface?"
Lia Graves sat on the polished white marble bench outside the towering iron gates of Valoria Academy.
She let out a soft bored sigh.
"Haah~"
She kicked her small feet back and forth with her pristine academy loafers lightly tapping against the stone base of the bench.
In her right hand, she absentmindedly spun a sleek silver fountain pen through her fingers.
It was a nervous habit she had picked up over the last few days.
She missed her brother.
It had been exactly five days since Silas had left the estate.
Five long, agonizing days since he had packed his heavy mythril longsword, put on that dark trench coat, and walked out the door to raid an unmapped Secret Realm in the middle of a blazing desert.
For a normal sibling, five days was just a business trip but in the Sovereign world, five days inside an unmapped dungeon was an eternity.
Secret Realms were meat grinders.
Lords went in and simply never came out. They were swallowed by abyssal monsters, crushed by tectonic traps or murdered by rival nobles over a chest of glowing rocks.
Lia tried not to think about that since Silas was strong and he promised that he would always come back.
’Maybe I should have not searched the mortality rates of a Secret Realm raid...’
It was because of that reason that anxiety still gnawed at the back of her mind, Secret Realms had a 50-60% mortality rate!
"Is your brother always this late, Lia-chan?" a soft polite voice asked beside her.
Lia stopped spinning the pen and turned her head.
Sitting right next to her on the marble bench was a girl named Kaede.
She was a new friend Lia had made on Tuesday during their basic mana-theory class.
Kaede was an exchange student from the Shogunate Isles... this world’s exact cultural equivalent of Japan.
She had straight immaculate black hair cut into a perfect hime-style fringe, and she carried herself with the quiet discipline of an eastern noble clan.
"He’s not usually late," Lia defended him quickly, puffing out her cheeks. "He’s just... working. He’s a Lord and he has territory stuff to do."
Kaede nodded thoughtfully, adjusting the strap of her expensive leather school bag.

"I understand," Kaede said softly. "My elder brother is also a Lord. He operates a Level 10 territory near the coast of the Sovereign Realm. He is always very busy with maritime subjugation quests but he promised to pick me up today."
They sat in comfortable silence for a few minutes, watching the bustling courtyard of Valoria Academy.
It was Friday afternoon. The sprawling impeccably manicured campus was currently flooding with students from the lower cohorts.
The sons and daughters of wealthy merchants, corporate executives, and established Lords were all chatting loudly, comparing their weekly allowances, and showing off their low-tier magical trinkets.
Lia felt entirely out of place here.
She had only started at the Academy on Monday.
For her entire life, she had grown up in the filthiest slums of Sector 4.

She was used to dodging gang violence and rationing nutrient paste. Now, she was wearing a tailored uniform that cost more than her old apartment, sitting on a marble bench, and waiting for her brother to pick her up.
The whiplash was real.
HONK!
A sleek silver corporate sedan pulled up to the designated loading zone directly in front of the academy gates.
Kaede’s dark eyes instantly lit up.
The driver’s side door opened, and a tall, respectable-looking young man in a tailored suit stepped out.
He had a glowing blue core Lord insignia pinned to his lapel, indicating his status as a Lord.
"That is my brother!" Kaede said happily, standing up and smoothing her uniform skirt.
She turned back to Lia, offering a polite perfectly executed bow.
"It was very nice speaking with you today, Lia-chan," Kaede smiled. "I hope your brother arrives safely. Have a wonderful weekend."
"You too, Kaede," Lia smiled back, waving her hand. "See you on Monday."
Kaede trotted over to the silver sedan, hugging her brother before sliding into the passenger seat.
The car smoothly pulled away, merging into the bustling afternoon traffic of Valoria City.
Lia watched them go.
She slumped back against the marble bench, letting out another long sigh.
She was completely alone again. The courtyard was slowly emptying out.
The sun was beginning to dip lower in the amber sky, casting long dark shadows across the pristine academy grounds.
’Where are you, Big Brother?’ Lia thought, looking down at her silver pen. ’You promised you’d be back by Friday.’
Ten minutes passed and then, the atmosphere of the academy courtyard changed instantly.
It didn’t happen quietly though.
VROOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A roar violently echoed through the city streets as it sounded like an ancient dragon clearing its throat.
Every single remaining student, instructor, and private security guard loitering in the courtyard instantly stopped talking.
Heads whipped around, eyes wide, desperately searching for the source of the noise.
Turning the corner and gliding smoothly into the academy’s loading zone was a monster.
It was the Zenith IVR.
The multi-million-credit armored Supercar looked amazing.
The hyper-advanced supercar sat mere inches off the ground, its impossibly deep black finish absorbing the afternoon sunlight like a localized black hole.
It didn’t look like a vehicle meant for picking up a school student... It looked like it was designed to ram through a reinforced bank vault and survive a direct orbital strike!

The massive wide-track tires rolled to a flawless halt directly in front of the iron gates as the heavy anti-gravity mana-engine idled with a deep aggressive purr that made the air itself thrum with tension.
Lia completely froze, her pen dropping from her fingers.
The wealthy aristocratic girls standing a few yards away began furiously whispering to each other, their eyes wide as they stared at the matte-black beast.
"What class of transport is that?!" one of the senior girls gasped, clutching her designer bag. "Is that a...?!"

"Look at the plating," another girl whispered frantically, pointing a manicured finger at the undercarriage. "Those are active kinetic-redirection runes! That car costs more than my father’s entire corporate building!"
Then, the armored driver’s side door hissed.
With a pressurized release, the massive gull-wing door smoothly glided upward on completely silent hydraulic hinges.
A combat boot stepped out onto the pristine academy pavement as Silas Graves emerged from the vehicle.
He hadn’t stopped at the estate to change his clothes as he had driven straight from the dealership to the academy.
He was still wearing his black shirt with the thick fabric was visibly scuffed, torn at the hem, and splattered a bit with the dried blood of subterranean monsters.
The hilt of his mythril longsword was strapped openly to his hip, resting casually against his thigh but it wasn’t just his clothes that commanded attention.
It was his aura.
Silas had no idea he was doing it.
He had just spent the last five days completely immersed in a brutal, kill-or-be-killed Secret Realm.

He had slaughtered Dire Wolves, butchered a veteran Sand General, survived a tectonic collapse, and stood mere inches away from a Norse deity who had just atomized a god... after facing against the god too.
So he was passively leaking out his presence... his very presence made most of the people there swoon as Silas simply looked like a devastatingly handsome serial killer.
The girls standing nearby completely lost their minds.
A collective, highly audible gasp rippled through the female student body.
Several of them physically took a step back, intimidated by the bloodlust, but completely captivated by the rugged aesthetic.
"Oh my god," one of the senior girls breathed out with her face flushing completely red as she stared at Silas’s broad shoulders. "Who is that?!"
Another girl, a classmate of Lia’s, frantically turned around and grabbed Lia’s shoulder.
"Lia!" the girl squeaked, pointing a shaking finger at the towering Warlord standing beside the stealth supercar. "Lia, is that... is that really your big brother?!"
Lia didn’t answer her and she didn’t care about the terrifying aura.
She didn’t care about the dried monster blood or the intimidating mythril sword.
She only saw Silas.
"BIG BROTHER!" Lia screamed at the top of her lungs.
She abandoned her silver pen entirely.
She grabbed the strap of her school bag, vaulted completely over the marble bench, and sprinted across the courtyard as fast as her legs could carry her.
Silas heard his name.
His glowing golden eyes softened completely as the terrifying aura of violence violently retracted back into his chest.
Silas let out a long exhausted sigh of genuine relief with a small soft smile touching his bruised lips as he saw his little sister running toward him.
He opened his arms.
"Oof!"

chapters.title: Chapter 215: Going Home
paragraphs: Lia slammed directly into his torso, wrapping her small arms as tightly as she possibly could around his waist.
She buried her face completely into the thick fabric of his dark shirt, squeezing her eyes shut.
Silas wrapped his arms around her, resting his calloused hand gently on the back of her head, pulling her close.
"I missed you," Lia mumbled into his chest, her voice slightly muffled by the coat.
"I missed you too, Lia..." Silas replied softly, resting his chin on the top of her head.
They stood there for a long moment, completely ignoring the dozens of staring whispering academy students surrounding them.
Then, Lia suddenly pulled her head back. She wrinkled her nose, looking up at him with a deeply offended expression.
"Ugh," Lia complained loudly, taking a half-step back and waving her hand in front of her face. "Big brother, you smell terrible! You smell like burnt rocks and dirty dogs!"
Silas blinked, then let out a highly genuine, barking laugh.
"Yeah, that’s fair," Silas agreed, looking down at his ruined coat. "That would be the scent of dead gods, pulverized sand, and monster guts. It hasn’t been a very glamorous week."
Lia’s eyes darted away from his coat and landed entirely on the massive, completely absurd vehicle idling silently right behind him.
Her jaw dropped.
She slowly walked around Silas, her eyes wide with awe as she took in the sleek, matte-black curves, the wide tires, and the glowing silver runes of the Zenith IVR.
"Silas..." Lia breathed out, reaching out to gently touch the cold mythril plating. "What is this?"
"It’s a car, Lia," Silas replied dryly, leaning casually against the open gull-wing door.

"I know it’s a car!" Lia snapped, looking back at him with wide eyes. "But it looks like a spaceship! You actually bought a car?! That means you must have gotten a whole lot of wealth in the Secret Realm, right?!"
Silas internally winced.

He did not want to explain to his teenage sister that a psychopathic aristocratic Ice Queen had essentially emotionally blackmailed him into accepting a multi-million-credit supercar as a twisted romantic investment.
That was a conversation he was never, ever going to have.
"Yeah," Silas lied smoothly, crossing his arms and nodding his head. "We cleared the Vault and found some decent loot so I sold it to the Association."
Lia’s eyes narrowed slightly. She looked at the incredibly advanced anti-gravity thrusters mounted beneath the chassis.
"How much did this thing cost?" Lia asked suspiciously.
Silas didn’t even hesitate.
He deployed the most basic survival tactic: he lied through his teeth with unblinking confidence.
"Five hundred thousand Spirit Credits," Silas stated firmly. "And I bought it used. The previous owner was a Lord who didn’t like the color."
If Silas himself couldn’t handle the price initially, there was no way Lia would do so.
"Five hundred thousand?!" Lia gasped, completely buying the lie. "That’s still so much money! But it looks brand new!"
"I buffed out the scratches," Silas deadpanned. "Get in the car, Lia."
Lia practically squealed with excitement. She scrambled past him, eagerly sliding into the spacious incredibly luxurious passenger seat of the supercar.
Silas walked around the front of the vehicle, completely ignoring the lingering, awe-struck stares of the academy girls, and slid down into the bolstered driver’s seat.
He tapped a glowing rune on the center console, and both heavy gull-wing doors hissed downward, perfectly sealing the cabin and cutting off the noise of the courtyard.
He grabbed the heavy shifter, putting the massive anti-gravity engine into drive.
With a deep rumble, Silas smoothly pulled the Zenith IVR away from the curb, seamlessly merging into the heavy afternoon traffic of Valoria City.
Inside the cabin, it was a completely different world.
The dampening runes blocked out the sounds of the highway entirely as the climate control was perfectly set to a crisp comfortable temperature.

Lia was actively bouncing in her leather seat, her eyes wide as she pressed her hands against the polarized dragon-glass window, watching the towering skyscrapers and neon billboards of the city blur past.
"This is so cool!" Lia cheered, looking around at the glowing holographic displays.
Silas smirked, keeping one hand casually on the heavy steering wheel while his golden-ringed eyes scanned the traffic ahead.
"Where is Martha?" Lia asked suddenly, turning to look at him. "Usually, she would be the one waiting for me at the gates."
"I called her from the road," Silas explained, shifting lanes effortlessly. "I told her to stay home and prepare the estate so I wanted to be the one to pick you up today."
"Oh," Lia smiled, clearly touched by the gesture.

"So," Silas continued, his tone shifting into that of a protective older brother. "It’s Friday. You officially started classes on Monday. It has been a full week... Tell me everything. How was the academy? Are the instructors treating you well? Did any of the brats try to cause problems for you?"
Lia settled back into her luxurious leather seat, resting her school bag on her lap.

"It was actually pretty good!" Lia reported happily. "The instructors are really strict about mana theory, but I’m keeping up and nobody has bothered me at all! Most of the noble kids just stick to their own cliques. I even made a new friend! Her name is Kaede and she’s from the Eastern Isles."
"The Shogunate territories?" Silas raised an eyebrow. "Those clans are entirely obsessed with honor and swordplay. They produce a lot of high-tier Lords."
"Yeah!" Lia nodded eagerly. "Her big brother is a Level 10 Lord as he picked her up right before you arrived."
Silas listened quietly as he navigated the sprawling elevated highways of the city.
He absorbed every detail she gave him with his brain subconsciously mapping out the social dynamics of her cohort.

"Just remember what I told you," Silas advised her with his voice turning serious. "You can make friends, but keep your guard up. The children of the Valoria elite are raised to be manipulative... If any of those kids try to look down on you because you grew up in Sector 4, you don’t argue with them. You just walk away and let me know. I will personally have an uncomfortable conversation with their parents."
"I know, Big Brother," Lia smiled, rolling her eyes playfully. "You don’t need to threaten to decapitate a CEO just because someone looked at me funny."
"I willthough," Silas corrected her deadpan.
Silas tapped the glowing holographic GPS display projected onto the windshield, adjusting their route.
"I need to make a quick detour before we head back to the Silverleaf estate," Silas announced, glancing at the navigation lines. "I need to stop by one of the central Lord Association Buildings."
Lia tilted her head, looking at him in confusion. "Why?"

"I need to hit the Marketplace," Silas explained, his jaw tightening slightly as he mentally prepared himself for the impending financial damage. "I need to purchase a massive stack of Tier 1 elemental spell scrolls since I’m expanding my magical affinities this weekend."
Lia stared at him for a solid five seconds.
Her expression was completely blank.

"Silas," Lia said slowly, as if she were speaking to an elderly man who didn’t understand how a television remote worked. "Why in the world would you physically drive all the way to a brick-and-mortar LA Building just to buy basic spell scrolls?"
Silas frowned, his hands gripping the steering wheel. "Because I need to browse the inventory?"
Lia let out a loud groan, slapping her palm against her forehead.

"You absolute boomer!" Lia groaned, shaking her head in sheer disbelief. "You literally have a Lord Association account! You don’t need to walk into a building and carry physical paper scrolls out in a shopping cart! You can just order them online! That’s what Kaede’s brother does!"
Silas blinked.
He actually stuttered.
"I... I can order magic spells on the internet?"
Actually he could... that was the plan initially before he met Lia in his house that day.

"Yes!" Lia yelled, throwing her hands up in the air. "There is an entire digital marketplace on the LA portal! You literally just click ’Add to Cart’, pay the premium delivery fee, and they instantly deliver the scrolls directly to you! It takes five seconds!"
Silas sat in the driver’s seat in stunned silence.
His brain completely short-circuited.
"I..." Silas muttered with his cheeks flushing a faint shade of pink from sheer embarrassment. "I completely forgot about the internet."
Lia burst into hysterical laughter, kicking her feet against the floorboards.
Silas grumbled, aggressively tapping the holographic GPS to cancel the detour.
He merged the supercar into the express lane, significantly increasing their speed as they headed straight toward the wealthy district of Silverleaf.
Twenty minutes later, the massive, matte-black Zenith IVR smoothly pulled up to the towering wrought-iron gates of the place where they lived.
The automated security scanners mounted on the stone pillars instantly recognized the vehicle’s unique mana signature.
The massive iron gates silently glided open, allowing Silas to drive up the long paved tree-lined driveway.
’I did pay for new gates to be done... I’m glad that they’re working.’
Standing dead center in the middle of the circular driveway, wearing her immaculate black-and-white maid uniform, was Martha.
The middle-aged woman was aggressively waving her hands in the air with her face completely lit up in joy as she saw the strange new vehicle pull up.
Silas smoothly engaged the parking brake with the heavy anti-gravity engine humming to a complete silent halt.
He pushed the driver’s side gull-wing door open and stepped out onto the pristine cobblestone driveway.
The microsecond his heavy combat boots touched the ground, Martha completely lost her mind.
"MASTER!" Martha shrieked at the top of her lungs.
She didn’t just run over to greet him. The maid literally threw herself forward, completely abandoning her dignity.
THUD!
Martha violently fell directly to her knees on the hard cobblestone.
She aggressively threw her arms completely around Silas’s muscular calves, hugging his legs with a death grip as she burst into loud unprofessional tears.

"Master Silas!" Martha sobbed loudly, burying her face directly into the dirty fabric of his trousers. "You came back! You didn’t die in the dirt! I was so terrified that the estate was going to be liquidated!"
Silas stood there in the driveway frozen, he was completely unprepared for a crying middle-aged woman attached to his legs.
He let out a long, deeply exhausted sigh, looking down at the top of her head.
"Martha," Silas said firmly, trying to gently pry her arms off his calves. "Get up. You are ruining your uniform on the cobblestones. I’m fine."
But Martha refused to let go. In fact, her devotion escalated to terrifying heights.
She actively leaned forward and began rapidly, desperately kissing the scuffed leather of his heavy combat boots.

"Thank the heavens!" Martha praised through her tears, kissing the dirt off his boots. "I am so incredibly glad you returned safely! I didn’t want to lose my Master so suddenly! The pay here is too good, and you actually let me eat real food! Please, never leave us for a Secret Realm again!"
Silas’s face flushed red with awkwardness.
"Martha, seriously, stop kissing my boots!" Silas demanded, forcefully but gently pulling his legs free from her grip and taking a large step backward. "I am not going to leave so just stand up."
Lia hopped out of the passenger side of the supercar, slinging her school bag over her shoulder.
She walked over, looking down at the crying maid with an amused teasing smile.
"It’s okay, Martha," Lia comforted the maid, reaching down to pat her shoulder. "You don’t have to pretend... I know you were just crying all week because you missed cooking his favorite meals."
Martha sniffled, wiping her nose with the sleeve of her immaculate uniform as she finally pulled herself up off the cobblestones.
"I was very worried, Miss Lia," Martha admitted, bowing her head respectfully. "The news broadcasts regarding expeditions like that are completely terrifying."
’Tell me about it...’ Lia thought.
"Well, we’re all home now," Silas declared, turning toward the massive oak doors of the place. "Let’s go inside."
