chapters.title: Chapter 216: Ordering From LAB
paragraphs: They headed into the sprawling luxurious foyer of the estate.

"Miss Lia," Martha offered instantly, slipping right back into her professional maid persona. "Would you like me to draw you a bath? Or perhaps I could assist you with your academy assignments in the study?"
"Assignments first," Lia decided responsibly, heading toward the grand staircase. "I have a massive mana-theory essay due on Monday."
"Excellent choice," Martha nodded approvingly. She turned to Silas. "And for you, Master Silas? A hot meal?"

"No," Silas grumbled, unbuckling the heavy mythril scabbard from his hip and leaning the sword against the marble wall. "I just need a bath. I am covered in the residual ash of a lot of things, and my muscles feel like they’ve been put through a meat grinder. I will be upstairs."
Silas turned and heavily trudged up the sweeping carpeted staircase with his heavy boots thudding against the wood.
Ten minutes later, Silas was submerged up to his neck in the massive, sunken marble bathtub located in his sprawling bathroom.
The scalding hot water was heaven.

He had poured half a bottle of restorative bath salts into the water, and he could literally feel the soothing concentrated mana aggressively sinking into his pores, forcefully repairing his micro-torn muscle fibers and soothing his bruised Warlord ribs.
’I need to go see Eluned and the others...’ Silas thought.
He leaned his head back against the smooth marble edge of the tub, closing his golden-ringed eyes as the steam filled the room.
The adrenaline of the extraction had finally worn off, leaving him with nothing but pure physical and mental exhaustion.
Eluned’s lap would do a lot of things for him right now.
As he soaked in the boiling water, Silas’s mind naturally drifted back to the apocalyptic events of the afternoon.

’Thor is really strong, huh?’ Silas thought as he specifically remembered the world-ending terror he had felt when the sky cracked open and the Norse deity descended. ’The power to crack through a Secret Realm has to be insane...’
He also remembered the crushing gravitational pressure of Thor’s presence.
’I really want to get stronger... I can’t be this useless, given the fact that I’m a Gold core, If this was a novel then I should be the Protagonist right?’ Silas thought.

He remembered standing completely frozen as Thor stepped directly into his personal space and he also re remembered the blinding electrical blue of her eyes looking directly into his soul, probably recognizing the hidden Gold Core in his chest.
And most vividly, he remembered the Daughter of Odin reaching out with her heavy, heavily runed iron gauntlet, gently but firmly patting him directly on the top of his head.
Silas slowly opened his eyes in the steam-filled bathroom, staring blankly at the vaulted ceiling.
’Wait...’ Silas thought, his golden-ringed eyes widening in the bathtub. ’Did I... did I actually like that?’
He sat up slightly, the hot water sloshing over his muscular chest.
’No. Absolutely not,’ Silas aggressively mentally denied it. ’She was a terrifying cosmic entity who could have deleted me from reality with a sneeze. I was paralyzed by fear. That’s it.’
But his traitorous brain provided a counter-argument.
’But her hands were so incredibly firm... and she called me a fierce warrior...’
Silas physically violently dunked his entire head under the scalding hot bathwater, aggressively attempting to drown his own thoughts.
’I refuse to have an awakening kink for overpowering deities,’ Silas screamed in his thoughts under the water. ’I refuse! I am a Lord! I do the dominating!’
He breached the surface a few seconds later, gasping for air, violently wiping the water from his sharp face.
He aggressively scrubbed the residual monster blood from his skin, determined to completely scrub Thor out of his head even if she was one of the most beautiful women he had ever seen.
Thirty minutes later, Silas stepped out of the bathroom.
He was wearing nothing but a pair of loose comfortable gray sweatpants, a towel draped casually around his broad neck.
His dark hair was still completely damp, sticking to his forehead.
He walked across the sprawling incredibly luxurious master bedroom and headed straight for the far right corner of the room.
Sitting on a massive, heavy oak desk was a highly advanced top-of-the-line desktop computer system that had come pre-installed with the estate.
The monitor was massive, curving slightly to provide maximum visual immersion.
Silas sat down in the heavy leather desk chair.
He cracked his knuckles, rolling his broad shoulders as he tapped the glowing power button on the base of the monitor.
The screen instantly flared to life.
"It’s time to order..."
Silas opened the secure web browser and navigated directly to the official URL for Lord Association Online.
The homepage loaded instantly.
It was a sleek professional interface dominated by deep blues and golds, featuring a massive scrolling banner advertising subjugation quests and upcoming corporate auctions.
Silas clicked the ’Secure Login’ button in the top right corner.
He typed in his Lord ID and his highly encrypted password.
DING.
A prompt appeared on the screen.
[Two-Factor Authentication Required. Please check your registered mobile device for the 6-digit security code.]
Silas reached into the pocket of his discarded trousers lying on the bed, pulling out his smartphone.
He unlocked the screen, opening the text message from the Association.
He stared at the six-digit code with a smirk crossing his face.

’It doesn’t matter if you’re living on Earth or fighting dragons in a magical Sovereign dimension...’ Silas thought dryly, typing the code into the computer. ’Corporate bureaucracy and annoying 2FA logins are a universal constant. Some things never change.’
The screen refreshed, logging him securely into his private Lord dashboard.
Silas didn’t waste time browsing the vanity items or the weapon catalogs as he immediately clicked the ’Magic Market’ tab and selected the ’Skill Scrolls’ sub-category.
His strategy was incredibly simple and broken too.
To forcefully evolve his Gold Core to the second stage of Refinement, he needed to reach ’Adept Mastery’ in eight completely different elemental affinities.
He already possessed Water and Ice from Mia’s teachings. That meant he needed six entirely new elements while refining ice.
’Which Morwenna should know too...’
However, Silas didn’t need to purchase incredibly expensive spell scrolls to learn the magic.
Because he possessed the Absolute Upgrade System, he only needed the foundational ones.
He just needed the cheapest, lowest-tier spell scroll available to officially register the element in his body.
Once the basic Tier 1 spell scroll was in front of him, he could simply dump his UP directly into the skill scroll, making it increase in Tiers.
"Alright," Silas muttered to himself, leaning forward in his chair. "Let’s go shopping."
He clicked on the [Pyromancy] tab first.
He sorted the inventory by ’Price: Low to High’.
He scoffed at the results.
Even the lowest most pathetic Tier 1 fire spell was exorbitantly priced due to the high demand for offensive magic.
"Tier 1: Lesser Fireball," Silas read the description on the screen. "Generates a sphere of thermal energy equivalent to a standard campfire... Cost: 20,000 Spirit Credits."
"Twenty grand to light a campfire?" Silas grumbled, shaking his head. "The Association is completely scamming Lords man."
But he needed them to feed his system.

To ensure the element was properly anchored into his Gold Core, he couldn’t just buy one spell per element... he decided to purchase exactly three different Tier 1 scrolls per element to build a solid foundation.
He rapidly clicked ’Add to Cart’.
[Tier 1: Lesser Fireball (20,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Ember Cloak (22,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Flame Spark (18,000 SC)]
He backed out of the Pyromancy tab and clicked into [Aeromancy].
[Tier 1: Wind Cutter (25,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Zephyr Step (24,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Minor Gust (20,000 SC)]
He navigated to [Geomancy] as Earth spells were slightly more expensive due to their defensive utility in dungeons.
[Tier 1: Stone Spike (30,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Earthen Shield (32,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Tremor (28,000 SC)]
He clicked into [Electromancy].
Lightning was the premium offensive element, dominated by corporate elites like Harper’s family so the prices reflected the monopoly.
[Tier 1: Static Shock (35,000 SC).]
[Tier 1: Lightning Tether (34,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Voltaic Dash (35,000 SC).]
Silas continued his aggressive shopping spree, navigating through the various elemental tabs.
The Lord Association marketplace had sections for nearly everything except for the highly restricted and regulated affinities like Soul Magic or Darkness.
He picked up three Tier 1 scrolls for [Luminomancy] (Light Magic) and three for [Umbramancy] (Shadow Magic).

Having successfully gathered three foundational spells for six completely different elements, Silas finally moved his cursor to the top right corner of the screen and clicked the glowing golden [Proceed to Checkout] button.
The screen refreshed, displaying his final itemized invoice.
Silas stared at the monitor.
His heart stopped beating for a solid two seconds.
The total cost for eighteen absolutely basic low-tier completely pathetic Tier 1 spell scrolls was sitting there in bold, uncompromising red font.
[Subtotal: 475,000 Spirit Credits.]
[30-Minutes Delivery Fee (Premium): 25,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Valoria City Arcane Tax (10%): 50,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Total Amount Due: 550,000 Spirit Credits.]
Silas sat completely frozen in his desk chair.
He physically felt as though a broadsword had been violently driven directly through his chest.
’Even if I have the money... I still can never get used to spending so much money especially for low tier items!
Half a million credits?
’What if I was trying to buy Tier 3 spells...?’
He was spending half a million credits on garbage magic just to feed his system.
He closed his eyes, taking a deep shuddering breath.
Silas reminded himself of the math. Elora had just given him nearly four million so he could easily afford this.
This was an investment in his survival.
If he unlocked the second stage of his Gold Core, the return on investment would be exponential.
"Pain is temporary," Silas whispered to himself, trying to soothe his crying wallet. "Power is forever."
With a trembling hand, Silas moved the mouse cursor.
He clicked [Confirm Purchase].
DING!
His smartphone sitting on the desk instantly chimed loudly.
Silas picked it up, staring at the notification from the Valoria Central Bank.
[-550,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Thank you for shopping with the Lord Association! Your items are on the way!]
Silas groaned, dropping his forehead directly onto the heavy oak desk with a dull thud.
The financial damage physically hurt his soul. He didn’t care how rich he currently was... losing half a million credits in one click was pure agony.
Before Silas could even lift his head to check the screen, the heavy oak door to his master bedroom violently burst open.
BANG!
The door slammed aggressively against the wall.
Lia Graves stormed into the bedroom.
She was fuming.
Her face was flushed bright red with outrage as she was marching toward his desk with the uncompromising momentum of a Lord charging the frontline.
In her small hand, she was aggressively clutching her smartphone, holding the glowing screen out like a weapon.
"Silas Graves!" Lia yelled, entirely abandoning the ’Big Brother’ honorific.
Silas whipped his head up from the desk, his golden-ringed eyes wide with confusion.
"Lia? What’s wrong? Did Martha burn dinner?"
"I decided to look up the car!" Lia shrieked, completely ignoring his question.
She violently shoved her smartphone directly into his face.
Displayed brightly on the screen was the official corporate webpage for Apex Sovereign Motors.
Specifically, it was the landing page for the exact vehicle currently sitting in their driveway.
[Zenith IVR]
[Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price: 4,100,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Fully Loaded Options: +4,200,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Total Value: 8, 300,000 Spirit Credits.]
Silas completely froze.
He stared at the eight million figure on the screen.
’Fuck she shouldn’t know this...’
Lia lowered the phone, glaring at him with fury.
"Five hundred thousand used?!" Lia screamed, her voice echoing loudly through the building. "Big Brother... why in the hell WOULD YOU BUY A CAR WORTH EIGHT MILLION SPIRIT CREDITS?!"

sentences.text: They headed into the sprawling luxurious foyer of the estate.
"Miss Lia," Martha offered instantly, slipping right back into her professional maid persona.
"Would you like me to draw you a bath?
Or perhaps I could assist you with your academy assignments in the study?"
"Assignments first," Lia decided responsibly, heading toward the grand staircase.
"I have a massive mana-theory essay due on Monday."
"Excellent choice," Martha nodded approvingly.
She turned to Silas.
"And for you, Master Silas?
A hot meal?"
"No," Silas grumbled, unbuckling the heavy mythril scabbard from his hip and leaning the sword against the marble wall.
"I just need a bath.
I am covered in the residual ash of a lot of things, and my muscles feel like they’ve been put through a meat grinder.
I will be upstairs."
Silas turned and heavily trudged up the sweeping carpeted staircase with his heavy boots thudding against the wood.
Ten minutes later, Silas was submerged up to his neck in the massive, sunken marble bathtub located in his sprawling bathroom.
The scalding hot water was heaven.

He had poured half a bottle of restorative bath salts into the water, and he could literally feel the soothing concentrated mana aggressively sinking into his pores, forcefully repairing his micro-torn muscle fibers and soothing his bruised Warlord ribs.
’I need to go see Eluned and the others...’ Silas thought.
He leaned his head back against the smooth marble edge of the tub, closing his golden-ringed eyes as the steam filled the room.
The adrenaline of the extraction had finally worn off, leaving him with nothing but pure physical and mental exhaustion.
Eluned’s lap would do a lot of things for him right now.
As he soaked in the boiling water, Silas’s mind naturally drifted back to the apocalyptic events of the afternoon.

’Thor is really strong, huh?’ Silas thought as he specifically remembered the world-ending terror he had felt when the sky cracked open and the Norse deity descended. ’The power to crack through a Secret Realm has to be insane...’
He also remembered the crushing gravitational pressure of Thor’s presence.
’I really want to get stronger...
I can’t be this useless, given the fact that I’m a Gold core, If this was a novel then I should be the Protagonist right?’ Silas thought.

He remembered standing completely frozen as Thor stepped directly into his personal space and he also re remembered the blinding electrical blue of her eyes looking directly into his soul, probably recognizing the hidden Gold Core in his chest.
And most vividly, he remembered the Daughter of Odin reaching out with her heavy, heavily runed iron gauntlet, gently but firmly patting him directly on the top of his head.
Silas slowly opened his eyes in the steam-filled bathroom, staring blankly at the vaulted ceiling.
’Wait...’ Silas thought, his golden-ringed eyes widening in the bathtub. ’Did I... did I actually like that?’
He sat up slightly, the hot water sloshing over his muscular chest.
’No.
Absolutely not,’ Silas aggressively mentally denied it. ’She was a terrifying cosmic entity who could have deleted me from reality with a sneeze.
I was paralyzed by fear.
That’s it.’
But his traitorous brain provided a counter-argument.
’But her hands were so incredibly firm... and she called me a fierce warrior...’
Silas physically violently dunked his entire head under the scalding hot bathwater, aggressively attempting to drown his own thoughts.
’I refuse to have an awakening kink for overpowering deities,’ Silas screamed in his thoughts under the water. ’I refuse!
I am a Lord!
I do the dominating!’
He breached the surface a few seconds later, gasping for air, violently wiping the water from his sharp face.
He aggressively scrubbed the residual monster blood from his skin, determined to completely scrub Thor out of his head even if she was one of the most beautiful women he had ever seen.
Thirty minutes later, Silas stepped out of the bathroom.
He was wearing nothing but a pair of loose comfortable gray sweatpants, a towel draped casually around his broad neck.
His dark hair was still completely damp, sticking to his forehead.
He walked across the sprawling incredibly luxurious master bedroom and headed straight for the far right corner of the room.
Sitting on a massive, heavy oak desk was a highly advanced top-of-the-line desktop computer system that had come pre-installed with the estate.
The monitor was massive, curving slightly to provide maximum visual immersion.
Silas sat down in the heavy leather desk chair.
He cracked his knuckles, rolling his broad shoulders as he tapped the glowing power button on the base of the monitor.
The screen instantly flared to life.
"It’s time to order..."
Silas opened the secure web browser and navigated directly to the official URL for Lord Association Online.
The homepage loaded instantly.
It was a sleek professional interface dominated by deep blues and golds, featuring a massive scrolling banner advertising subjugation quests and upcoming corporate auctions.
Silas clicked the ’Secure Login’ button in the top right corner.
He typed in his Lord ID and his highly encrypted password.
DING.
A prompt appeared on the screen.
[Two-Factor Authentication Required.
Please check your registered mobile device for the 6-digit security code.]
Silas reached into the pocket of his discarded trousers lying on the bed, pulling out his smartphone.
He unlocked the screen, opening the text message from the Association.
He stared at the six-digit code with a smirk crossing his face.

’It doesn’t matter if you’re living on Earth or fighting dragons in a magical Sovereign dimension...’ Silas thought dryly, typing the code into the computer. ’Corporate bureaucracy and annoying 2FA logins are a universal constant.
Some things never change.’
The screen refreshed, logging him securely into his private Lord dashboard.
Silas didn’t waste time browsing the vanity items or the weapon catalogs as he immediately clicked the ’Magic Market’ tab and selected the ’Skill Scrolls’ sub-category.
His strategy was incredibly simple and broken too.
To forcefully evolve his Gold Core to the second stage of Refinement, he needed to reach ’Adept Mastery’ in eight completely different elemental affinities.
He already possessed Water and Ice from Mia’s teachings.
That meant he needed six entirely new elements while refining ice.
’Which Morwenna should know too...’
However, Silas didn’t need to purchase incredibly expensive spell scrolls to learn the magic.
Because he possessed the Absolute Upgrade System, he only needed the foundational ones.
He just needed the cheapest, lowest-tier spell scroll available to officially register the element in his body.
Once the basic Tier 1 spell scroll was in front of him, he could simply dump his UP directly into the skill scroll, making it increase in Tiers.
"Alright," Silas muttered to himself, leaning forward in his chair.
"Let’s go shopping."
He clicked on the [Pyromancy] tab first.
He sorted the inventory by ’Price: Low to High’.
He scoffed at the results.
Even the lowest most pathetic Tier 1 fire spell was exorbitantly priced due to the high demand for offensive magic.
"Tier 1: Lesser Fireball," Silas read the description on the screen.
"Generates a sphere of thermal energy equivalent to a standard campfire...
Cost: 20,000 Spirit Credits."
"Twenty grand to light a campfire?" Silas grumbled, shaking his head.
"The Association is completely scamming Lords man."
But he needed them to feed his system.

To ensure the element was properly anchored into his Gold Core, he couldn’t just buy one spell per element... he decided to purchase exactly three different Tier 1 scrolls per element to build a solid foundation.
He rapidly clicked ’Add to Cart’.
[Tier 1: Lesser Fireball (20,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Ember Cloak (22,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Flame Spark (18,000 SC)]
He backed out of the Pyromancy tab and clicked into [Aeromancy].
[Tier 1: Wind Cutter (25,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Zephyr Step (24,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Minor Gust (20,000 SC)]
He navigated to [Geomancy] as Earth spells were slightly more expensive due to their defensive utility in dungeons.
[Tier 1: Stone Spike (30,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Earthen Shield (32,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Tremor (28,000 SC)]
He clicked into [Electromancy].
Lightning was the premium offensive element, dominated by corporate elites like Harper’s family so the prices reflected the monopoly.
[Tier 1: Static Shock (35,000 SC).]
[Tier 1: Lightning Tether (34,000 SC)]
[Tier 1: Voltaic Dash (35,000 SC).]
Silas continued his aggressive shopping spree, navigating through the various elemental tabs.
The Lord Association marketplace had sections for nearly everything except for the highly restricted and regulated affinities like Soul Magic or Darkness.
He picked up three Tier 1 scrolls for [Luminomancy] (Light Magic) and three for [Umbramancy] (Shadow Magic).

Having successfully gathered three foundational spells for six completely different elements, Silas finally moved his cursor to the top right corner of the screen and clicked the glowing golden [Proceed to Checkout] button.
The screen refreshed, displaying his final itemized invoice.
Silas stared at the monitor.
His heart stopped beating for a solid two seconds.
The total cost for eighteen absolutely basic low-tier completely pathetic Tier 1 spell scrolls was sitting there in bold, uncompromising red font.
[Subtotal: 475,000 Spirit Credits.]
[30-Minutes Delivery Fee (Premium): 25,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Valoria City Arcane Tax (10%): 50,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Total Amount Due: 550,000 Spirit Credits.]
Silas sat completely frozen in his desk chair.
He physically felt as though a broadsword had been violently driven directly through his chest.
’Even if I have the money...
I still can never get used to spending so much money especially for low tier items!
Half a million credits?
’What if I was trying to buy Tier 3 spells...?’
He was spending half a million credits on garbage magic just to feed his system.
He closed his eyes, taking a deep shuddering breath.
Silas reminded himself of the math.
Elora had just given him nearly four million so he could easily afford this.
This was an investment in his survival.
If he unlocked the second stage of his Gold Core, the return on investment would be exponential.
"Pain is temporary," Silas whispered to himself, trying to soothe his crying wallet.
"Power is forever."
With a trembling hand, Silas moved the mouse cursor.
He clicked [Confirm Purchase].
DING!
His smartphone sitting on the desk instantly chimed loudly.
Silas picked it up, staring at the notification from the Valoria Central Bank.
[-550,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Thank you for shopping with the Lord Association!
Your items are on the way!]
Silas groaned, dropping his forehead directly onto the heavy oak desk with a dull thud.
The financial damage physically hurt his soul.
He didn’t care how rich he currently was... losing half a million credits in one click was pure agony.
Before Silas could even lift his head to check the screen, the heavy oak door to his master bedroom violently burst open.
BANG!
The door slammed aggressively against the wall.
Lia Graves stormed into the bedroom.
She was fuming.
Her face was flushed bright red with outrage as she was marching toward his desk with the uncompromising momentum of a Lord charging the frontline.
In her small hand, she was aggressively clutching her smartphone, holding the glowing screen out like a weapon.
"Silas Graves!" Lia yelled, entirely abandoning the ’Big Brother’ honorific.
Silas whipped his head up from the desk, his golden-ringed eyes wide with confusion.
"Lia?
What’s wrong?
Did Martha burn dinner?"
"I decided to look up the car!" Lia shrieked, completely ignoring his question.
She violently shoved her smartphone directly into his face.
Displayed brightly on the screen was the official corporate webpage for Apex Sovereign Motors.
Specifically, it was the landing page for the exact vehicle currently sitting in their driveway.
[Zenith IVR]
[Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price: 4,100,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Fully Loaded Options: +4,200,000 Spirit Credits.]
[Total Value: 8, 300,000 Spirit Credits.]
Silas completely froze.
He stared at the eight million figure on the screen.
’Fuck she shouldn’t know this...’
Lia lowered the phone, glaring at him with fury.
"Five hundred thousand used?!" Lia screamed, her voice echoing loudly through the building.
"Big Brother... why in the hell WOULD YOU BUY A CAR WORTH EIGHT MILLION SPIRIT CREDITS?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 217: Scrolls
paragraphs: The sharp persistent electronic buzzing of the front gate intercom echoed through the quiet halls of the Silverleaf building.
Silas groaned, rolling his broad shoulders as he descended the grand staircase.
He was currently still shirtless, wearing nothing but a pair of loose, dark gray sweatpants that hung low on his waist.
His bare chest and arms were covered in a sheen of sweat from his grueling calisthenics routine.
’That I just picked up from the official LAB site...’ Silas thought.
Even with his Gold Core constantly regulating his physique, he refused to let his physical conditioning slip.
A Lord who relied solely on magic was a Lord waiting to be decapitated in the dark.
The buzzer rang again, louder this time.
"I’m coming, damn it," Silas muttered, dragging a calloused hand through his damp messy dark hair.
He crossed the foyer with his bare feet padding softly against the polished marble floor, and pulled open the heavy oak front door.
He walked down the long paved driveway with the heat radiating off the cobblestones, until he reached the towering reinforced wrought-iron security gates.
Standing on the other side of the bars was a young exhausted delivery courier wearing the crisp, standardized blue-and-gold uniform of the Lord Association’s Premium Marketplace division.
Behind him idled a sleek, corporate-issued hover-bike loaded with secure cargo containers.
Silas pressed the security rune on the wall panel. With a mechanical hum, the smaller pedestrian-sized side gate hissed open.
’I really do love these gates...’
Silas stepped into the threshold, towering over the courier.
The delivery guy looked up, and his professional customer-service greeting instantly died in his throat.
The courier’s eyes went completely wide with his face flushing an immediate shade of crimson as he took in the intimidating and flawlessly sculpted physique of the Lord standing before him.

’Fucking hell...’ the delivery guy cursed violently in his own thoughts, desperately trying to maintain eye contact and actively failing. ’Look at this guy! Fucking perfect noble genetics... Sitting in his mansion, built like a damn war god, probably sleeping with a dozen supermodels while I’m out here sweating for minimum wage! Life is so unfair!’
"Package for Graves?" Silas asked, his deep voice completely oblivious to the man’s internal existential crisis.

"U-Uh, yes! Yes, Lord Graves!" the courier stammered, frantically scrambling to pull a heavy runic-sealed metallic lockbox from his satchel, along with a glowing digital datapad. "Premium delivery from the Central Association Marketplace! I just need your biometric signature right here, please!"
Silas took the datapad, pressing his thumb against the glowing screen.
As the pad chimed to confirm his identity, Silas reached up with his free hand, casually massaging the back of his neck.
His muscles were still incredibly sore from the Secret Realm, but the small headache was finally starting to recede.
He was also mentally exhausted from the sheer psychological warfare he had waged against his sister the previous night.

After Lia had violently burst into his bedroom, screaming about the eight-million-credit price tag of the Zenith IVR parked in their driveway, Silas had been forced to deploy the greatest and most intricate lie of his entire life.

He had desperately, frantically managed to convince Lia that Elora Verinda had simply ’gifted’ him one of her incredibly old and depreciated beat-up track cars out of pity, and that the eight million figure was just the original retail price from a decade ago.
It was a flimsy duct-taped excuse, but it had barely worked.
If Lia had realized that he or Elora had genuinely dropped eight million Spirit Credits in a single evening, his sister might have actually run crazy and had a stress-induced aneurysm.
"Here," Silas said, handing the datapad back to the flustered courier.
Silas took the heavy metallic lockbox containing his eighteen elemental spell scrolls, tucking it casually under his muscular arm as if it weighed absolutely nothing.
"Thank you, Lord Graves," the courier said, quickly stowing the datapad. "Oh, wait! Before I forget!"
The courier reached back into his uniform pocket and pulled out a small, sleek, highly polished silver wristband that pulsed with a blue light as he held it out to Silas.

"The Marketplace management included this as a complimentary VIP gift for your incredibly large purchase," the delivery guy explained, his professional tone returning. "It’s a Lord Association Synchronization Band."
Silas raised an eyebrow, taking the silver band.
It felt cold and heavy in his palm. "What does it do?"

"It’s a spatial tether, My Lord," the guy told him eagerly, happy to explain the tech. "The Band can be directly, wirelessly connected to your personal Lord Inventory. Once you sync it, you don’t even have to wait for physical delivery guys like me anymore for standard-sized items! The Association can legally bypass the physical realm and send purchased items directly into your Lord Inventory through the Band’s signal."
Silas gaped a bit, his golden-ringed eyes widening in genuine surprise.
"Direct to inventory? Without a physical drop-off?"

"Exactly!" the man nodded, gesturing to the silver metal. "And it doesn’t stop there. The Band can be connected into external high-tier mechanical devices. Things like advanced smartphones, estate vaults, or luxury cars. That’s precisely why the top-tier Valoria nobles have them installed in their vehicles. It keeps their cars directly linked to their Lord Inventory, able to bring items out and store items in the trunk without having to manually summon the interface while driving!"
Silas blinked.

’No wonder,’ Silas thought, everything was instantly clicking into place. ’That perfectly explains how Elora’s supercar had the same function... She transferred those millions of credits and pulled my loot into her storage without even lifting her hands off the steering wheel. The vehicle itself is an extension of the inventory!’
Despite the incredible convenience of the technology, Silas’s paranoia instantly flared.
Giving a corporate entity a wireless back-door channel into his personal Lord Inventory sounded like a massive security risk waiting to happen.
So he still wasn’t exactly trusting of the band, regardless of how shiny it looked.
"Right. Good to know," Silas said smoothly, offering a polite nod as he casually slid the silver band deep into the pocket of his sweatpants. "Thanks for the delivery."
"Have a wonderful weekend, Lord Graves!" the guy wished him goodbye.
The courier hopped back onto the saddle of his idling hover-bike, revving the anti-gravity thrusters, and smoothly sped off down the private road of the Silverleaf district.
Silas stepped back inside the perimeter with the heavy wrought-iron gate automatically hissing closed and locking securely behind him.
He walked back up the long sun-baked driveway, completely ignoring the heat on his bare shoulders, and re-entered the sprawling mansion.
He bypassed the grand foyer and headed straight toward the dining room.
Sitting at the polished mahogany dining table was Lia.
She was hunched over a massive, incredibly thick, leather-bound textbook, furiously scribbling notes onto a piece of paper.
Standing right beside her, wearing her immaculate black-and-white maid uniform, was Martha, holding a silver tray of fresh pastries and actively trying to help the teenager study.
"I don’t understand this formula at all," Lia groaned loudly, burying her face in her hands. "The Academy instructors act like we should just intrinsically know how mana degrades in a vacuum!"

"Now, now, Miss Lia," Martha comforted her gently, placing a warm pastry onto a small plate next to her notebook. "Magic theory is incredibly complex... Even the greatest scholars at the Association struggle with these foundational laws so just take a deep breath and look at the variables again."
Silas walked into the dining room, setting the heavy metallic lockbox onto the mahogany table with a loud thud.
Lia whipped her head up, pointing her silver fountain pen directly at him. "Big Brother! You went to the Academy! You took this exact class! Help me with this!"
Silas sighed, leaning over the table.
He rested his calloused hands on the wood, looking down at the incredibly complex and convoluted mathematical mana-theory equation written in the textbook.
It was a massive string of alchemical symbols, degradation coefficients, and elemental output ratios.
’Haah... I hate these questions.’
Martha showed him the specific problem, pointing to the end of the equation.
"She has to calculate the exact terminal output of a fractured pyromancy spell when exposed to a zero-oxygen environment."
Silas didn’t pull out a calculator.
He didn’t even grab a pen.
He simply tossed his head from left to right, cracking his neck with a loud, satisfying pop, before casually looking back down at the book.
"The answer is one," Silas stated simply.
Lia blinked, looking at the massive, two-page equation, and then back at him. "One? Just... one?"

"Yes," Silas nodded. "It’s a trick question... The Academy instructors use it to weed out the idiots who rely purely on math instead of practical combat experience. Fire requires oxygen to maintain itself right? In a complete zero-oxygen vacuum, the spell doesn’t degrade mathematically... it fails to ignite and so the output coefficient of a failed spell is always one."
Martha stood there, her jaw dropping open in surprise.
She looked at the towering Lord as if he had just recited the secrets of the universe.
"Master Silas..." Martha gasped. "How did you possibly calculate that so simply? I thought you were... well, a combat specialist!"
Silas smirked with an arrogant expression crossing his face.
"There’s a reason I got a full academic scholarship to Valoria Academy from the slums, Martha," Silas declared smoothly. "I wasn’t just recruited to hit things with a sword."
Ignoring their awestruck stares, Silas turned his attention to the heavy metallic lockbox.
He pressed his thumb against the runic lock... The seal hissed, and the lid popped open.
Inside the velvet-lined box were eighteen perfectly pristine tightly rolled parchment scrolls.
Silas reached in and brought out a single scroll.
It was tied with a crimson silk ribbon, indicating its pyromancy affiliation.
He untied the ribbon and carefully unfurled the parchment, laying it flat against the mahogany table.
Both Lia and Martha leaned in, looking at it strangely.
It wasn’t a standard book or a manual.
The scroll was covered in completely different kinds of text... ancient, glowing golden runes that seemed to actively shift and writhe on the paper.
It wasn’t just instructions... it seemed to be a pure magical chant.
"What is that?" Lia asked, squinting at the glowing letters. "It looks like the text is vibrating."

"It is," Silas explained, his golden-ringed eyes tracking the runes. "This is a Tier 1 spell scroll. The reason why scrolls are so incredibly expensive and highly valued in the Sovereign Realm is that, unlike standard spells, the actual chants are bound directly into the fiber of the paper so they are completely different from normal spells."
Silas tapped the edge of the parchment.

"Normally, a Lord has to spend weeks to months, sometimes yers memorizing the exact phonetic cadence, mana circulation, and visual matrix of a spell to cast it," Silas continued his lecture. "The reason I learn spells quite quickly, even without scrolls, is based solely on the processing power of my Blue Core but for most Lords, these scrolls are a shortcut."
He picked the scroll back up, holding it lightly in his hands.

"By pressing the scroll directly against your head... furled or unfurled... one instantly absorbs the complete knowledge of what is inside," Silas told them. "The magic forces the chant and the mana pathways directly into your brain so you will instantly be able to perform the spell perfectly on the very first try."
"That’s basically cheating!" Lia gasped, amazed.

"It is," Silas agreed. "And of course, there is a massive catch. The text grows significantly dimmer after that first absorption. Which simply means the next time someone tries to use this exact same scroll, the magical knowledge flowing into their brain might not be as completely perfect as the original. It degrades."
Silas sighed heavily, rolling the scroll back up.

’And that’s for the Higher Tier spells,’ Silas thought bitterly, looking at the box of cheap Tier 1 garbage. ’These cheap Tier 1 spells completely dissolve into ash after a single, full use. It’s a one-and-done consumable. Well, nothing to cry over. I’ll upgrade the scrolls To Tier 3 once I’m in the Sovereign Realm.’

Standing right beside her, wearing her immaculate black-and-white maid uniform, was Martha, holding a silver tray of fresh pastries and actively trying to help the teenager study.
"I don’t understand this formula at all," Lia groaned loudly, burying her face in her hands.
"The Academy instructors act like we should just intrinsically know how mana degrades in a vacuum!"
"Now, now, Miss Lia," Martha comforted her gently, placing a warm pastry onto a small plate next to her notebook.
"Magic theory is incredibly complex...
Even the greatest scholars at the Association struggle with these foundational laws so just take a deep breath and look at the variables again."
Silas walked into the dining room, setting the heavy metallic lockbox onto the mahogany table with a loud thud.
Lia whipped her head up, pointing her silver fountain pen directly at him.
"Big Brother!
You went to the Academy!
You took this exact class!
Help me with this!"
Silas sighed, leaning over the table.
He rested his calloused hands on the wood, looking down at the incredibly complex and convoluted mathematical mana-theory equation written in the textbook.
It was a massive string of alchemical symbols, degradation coefficients, and elemental output ratios.
’Haah...
I hate these questions.’
Martha showed him the specific problem, pointing to the end of the equation.
"She has to calculate the exact terminal output of a fractured pyromancy spell when exposed to a zero-oxygen environment."
Silas didn’t pull out a calculator.
He didn’t even grab a pen.
He simply tossed his head from left to right, cracking his neck with a loud, satisfying pop, before casually looking back down at the book.
"The answer is one," Silas stated simply.
Lia blinked, looking at the massive, two-page equation, and then back at him.
"One?
Just... one?"
"Yes," Silas nodded.
"It’s a trick question...
The Academy instructors use it to weed out the idiots who rely purely on math instead of practical combat experience.
Fire requires oxygen to maintain itself right?
In a complete zero-oxygen vacuum, the spell doesn’t degrade mathematically... it fails to ignite and so the output coefficient of a failed spell is always one."
Martha stood there, her jaw dropping open in surprise.
She looked at the towering Lord as if he had just recited the secrets of the universe.
"Master Silas..." Martha gasped.
"How did you possibly calculate that so simply?
I thought you were... well, a combat specialist!"
Silas smirked with an arrogant expression crossing his face.
"There’s a reason I got a full academic scholarship to Valoria Academy from the slums, Martha," Silas declared smoothly.
"I wasn’t just recruited to hit things with a sword."
Ignoring their awestruck stares, Silas turned his attention to the heavy metallic lockbox.
He pressed his thumb against the runic lock...
The seal hissed, and the lid popped open.
Inside the velvet-lined box were eighteen perfectly pristine tightly rolled parchment scrolls.
Silas reached in and brought out a single scroll.
It was tied with a crimson silk ribbon, indicating its pyromancy affiliation.
He untied the ribbon and carefully unfurled the parchment, laying it flat against the mahogany table.
Both Lia and Martha leaned in, looking at it strangely.
It wasn’t a standard book or a manual.
The scroll was covered in completely different kinds of text... ancient, glowing golden runes that seemed to actively shift and writhe on the paper.
It wasn’t just instructions... it seemed to be a pure magical chant.
"What is that?" Lia asked, squinting at the glowing letters.
"It looks like the text is vibrating."
"It is," Silas explained, his golden-ringed eyes tracking the runes.
"This is a Tier 1 spell scroll.

The reason why scrolls are so incredibly expensive and highly valued in the Sovereign Realm is that, unlike standard spells, the actual chants are bound directly into the fiber of the paper so they are completely different from normal spells."
Silas tapped the edge of the parchment.
"Normally, a Lord has to spend weeks to months, sometimes yers memorizing the exact phonetic cadence, mana circulation, and visual matrix of a spell to cast it," Silas continued his lecture.
"The reason I learn spells quite quickly, even without scrolls, is based solely on the processing power of my Blue Core but for most Lords, these scrolls are a shortcut."
He picked the scroll back up, holding it lightly in his hands.
"By pressing the scroll directly against your head... furled or unfurled... one instantly absorbs the complete knowledge of what is inside," Silas told them.
"The magic forces the chant and the mana pathways directly into your brain so you will instantly be able to perform the spell perfectly on the very first try."
"That’s basically cheating!" Lia gasped, amazed.
"It is," Silas agreed.
"And of course, there is a massive catch.
The text grows significantly dimmer after that first absorption.
Which simply means the next time someone tries to use this exact same scroll, the magical knowledge flowing into their brain might not be as completely perfect as the original.
It degrades."
Silas sighed heavily, rolling the scroll back up.
’And that’s for the Higher Tier spells,’ Silas thought bitterly, looking at the box of cheap Tier 1 garbage. ’These cheap Tier 1 spells completely dissolve into ash after a single, full use.
It’s a one-and-done consumable.
Well, nothing to cry over.
I’ll upgrade the scrolls To Tier 3 once I’m in the Sovereign Realm.’

chapters.title: Chapter 218: Bloom Estate
paragraphs: Silas was fully aware that with his massive stockpile of Upgrade Points, he could easily push these spells to Tier 4 and above.
But honestly, he had done the math.
He had a massive pool of mana thanks to his core, but Tier 4 spells were mana wasters.
Sure, they packed catastrophic destructive punches, but they completely drained stamina for very little efficiency in a drawn-out dungeon crawl.
He would maintain his spells at a efficient lethal Tier 3 for now and mix it up with some Tier 4s.
Silas looked down at his calloused hands.

’And I also need to increase the ranks of the girls today...’ Silas thought, his Warlord ambition burning fiercely. ’I need to push Tasmin, Brida and the rest of their ranks to S-Rank. The higher their ranks, the faster they can level up in the field, and probably their classes would uniquely evolve as well.’
Silas currently possessed exactly 4400 UP. He was most definitely going to test out the limits of the Absolute Upgrade System today.
For now, he kept the scrolls back inside the heavy metallic box, sealing the lid tight.

"Alright," Silas announced, picking up the box and turning to the two women. "I will be heading back to my territory right now... I have a lot of administrative and magical work to process. I will most probably be gone for several days so keep the estate locked down, and keep yourselves safe."
He reached into the pocket of his sweatpants, pulling out a sleek black key card stamped with the Zenith IVR logo.
He tossed it onto the table in front of the maid.

"Martha," Silas instructed her. "That is the access card for the new transport parked in the garage. You have my full authorization to drive it wherever you need to go for groceries or errands, as long as you do not crash it."
Martha stared at the matte-black key card as if it were a live grenade.

"M-Master Silas!" Martha gasped, aggressively waving her hands in rejection. "I absolutely cannot accept this! That vehicle is a Supercar! I am just a humble maid! I could never pilot such a majestic machine! I will take the bus!"
"You are the maid of my house," Silas told her, his tone completely uncompromising. "You do not take the public bus, you’ll drive the car. Do it."
Martha gulped loudly, her hands trembling as she slowly, reverently picked up the key card.
She bowed her head deeply. "Y-Yes, My Lord! I understand!"
She quickly tucked the card into her apron and then rapidly rushed into the adjacent sprawling kitchen.
She returned a moment later, holding a beautifully wrapped, incredibly large bento box.
"I packed you a hot lunch for your journey, Master Silas!" Martha announced proudly, holding it out to him.

Her face flushed slightly with embarrassment. "Though I know my humble Earth-based cooking might not be nearly as incredibly good or magically enriching as what the women in your territory cook... I sincerely hope you enjoy it."
Silas looked at the lunchbox.
His heart actually softened.
It had been years since someone had just... made him lunch without wanting a favor in return.
’On Earth at least.’ Silas thought.
He reached out, taking the warm lunchbox with his left hand and then, his right hand moved on its own.
Without a single second of conscious thought, Silas reached forward and affectionately patted Martha directly on the top of her head.
Pat! Pat!
Silas completely froze.
’Fuck,’ Silas cursed violently in his thoughts. ’I did it completely out of reflex... I shouldn’t pat an older woman’s hea—’
"Oh my!" Martha gasped.
The middle-aged maid instantly blushed a furious deep shade of crimson.
She brought her hands up to her cheeks, looking up at the towering shirtless Warlord with an expression of overwhelmed delight.
"I am so incredibly glad you would bestow such an honor on me, Master Silas!" Martha squeaked, bowing repeatedly.
Lia sat at the dining table with her jaw hanging open, looking between her brother and the blushing maid.
She burst into a fit of hysterical giggles, completely unable to contain herself.
"Have a good trip, Big Brother!" Lia teased him mercilessly, waving her pen. "Don’t forget to pat your terrifying monsters when you get there!"
"I’m leaving," Silas grumbled, his face flushing red as he turned around and practically fled the dining room.
He took the metallic box of scrolls as well as the packed lunch and headed straight upstairs.
As he ascended the grand staircase, he swiped his hand through the air, completely dropping both items directly into his digital Lord Inventory.
Once he got to his sprawling master bedroom, he quickly stepped inside and closed the heavy oak door firmly behind him, engaging the lock.
He walked over and laid back heavily onto the plush mattress of his bed.

He was currently completely shirtless, wearing just the gray sweatpants, but he knew that once he got back to the Blessed Land barracks, he would probably just wear one of the comfortable magic-woven shirts Eluned had personally crafted for him.
Silas closed his eyes, centering his breathing.
He raised his hand and pulled up the glowing blue holographic system tab in front of his face.
He clicked the [Descend] command.
Instantly, the entire world became pitch dark.

The ambient noise of the Valoria city traffic completely vanished as Silas disappeared entirely from the physical plane of the living, his body dissolving into white light as he was violently, instantly pulled across the cosmic void and back into the Sovereign Realm.
Meanwhile, hundreds of miles away, in fact across the continent from the gleaming skyscrapers of Valoria.
In the sprawling bounds of Terres City.
A massive heavy-duty golden transport vehicle pulled smoothly up to the curb directly in front of the towering and imposing obsidian-and-crimson iron gates of the Bloom Clan Estate.
This was the ancestral seat of power where Seraphina was from.
She was Seraphina Bloom of the Bloom Clan.
Valerius Sterling engaged the parking brake with the transport humming to a halt.
He turned his head, looking at the fiery crimson-haired noblewoman sitting silently in the passenger seat beside him.
She looked completely exhausted with her armor shattered.
"Seraph," Valerius asked quietly. "Is the promise still active?"
She knew exactly what he was asking.
She had fiercely promised Valerius that she would not do anything drastic or politically lethal to Silas Graves.
But she still had to face her family.
She still had to tell her intensely powerful Father exactly what had happened in the dungeon, and why half the Lords were dead.
Seraphina slowly nodded, her red eyes staring out at the massive gates of her home.
"Yes," Seraphina confirmed softly.
She turned to look at the blonde Lord, her expression filled with genuine uncharacteristic gratitude. "Val... thank you. For getting me out of there."
Valerius offered a small, respectful nod.
Seraphina pushed the heavy transport door open and gracefully got out of the car.
Valerius didn’t linger.
He immediately shifted the heavy transport back into drive and smoothly drove off down the wide avenue, heading straight back to his own family’s sprawling estate in the neighboring district.
Seraphina turned and walked through the massive obsidian gates, completely entering the Bloom Estate.
The aesthetic of the place was overwhelming.
The air itself was noticeably hotter here, heavy with the scent of sulfur, burning wood, and sweat.
Massive crimson banners bearing the blazing sun crest of the Bloom family hung from the high stone walls.
As she walked up the grand central pathway, the booming sounds of martial discipline echoed through the air.
"HA! HA! HA!"
Hundreds of people, dressed in uniform red martial arts gis, were actively practicing fierce and aggressive combat forms in the wide, sprawling training courtyard to her left.
With every single synchronized punch and kick they threw, massive, concussive bursts of highly pressurized fire aggressively erupted from their knuckles and boots, scorching the training dummies.
They were the lower ranks of the Bloom Clan... the bastards, the branch families, and the elite retainers.
And soon, Seraphina would need to officially choose a right hand from among them to be her permanent sworn servant.
As she passed the courtyard, the lead Instructor caught sight of her ruined armor.
"Lady Seraphina!" the Instructor barked, instantly dropping his stance and bowing deeply.
The entire courtyard of hundreds of martial artists instantly froze, turning toward her and dropping into identical, ninety-degree bows of absolute submission.
Usually, Seraphina would simply ignore them, maintaining the cold impossibly strict untouchable persona of the elite Fire Lord.
But today, she was exhausted.
’I have seen the power of a God and compared to that...’
Seraphina was nothing so she stopped walking.
She looked at the hundreds of bowing lower ranks, and she gently, warmly waved her hand at them in greeting.
The entire courtyard completely lost their minds.
Every single martial artist, including the hardened men and the fierce women, instantly became incredibly flustered.
Their faces flushed red, their perfect formations breaking as they stared in shock.
Lady Seraphina was usually so incredibly strict! Why was she waving?!
Seraphina continued walking up the wide stone steps and entered the massive ornate main double doors of the ancestral mansion.
A squad of a dozen perfectly synchronized trained maids welcomed her to the front of the estate.
Within seconds, they were actively, gently stripping away her ruined, soot-covered armor, unbuckling the shattered leather straps, and unwinding the burnt fabric.
They quickly wrapped her bruised, exhausted body in a thick, incredibly comfortable expensive silk fabric robe.
Two maids knelt down and gently took off her heavy, melted combat boots.
Another senior maid stepped forward, holding her hands out.
"Let cleansing winds wash away the worldly ash..." the maid chanted perfectly with the seven-word incantation rolling off her tongue with practiced ease.
FWOOSH.
A gentle gust of concentrated, purifying green wind magic completely washed over Seraphina’s body.
The spell instantly stripped away every single speck of dirt, dried blood, and subterranean ash from her skin and hair, leaving her feeling perfectly clean and refreshed.
"Where are my Mother and Father?" Seraphina asked, tying the silk robe securely around her waist.
"They are currently receiving reports in the primary study, My Lady," the head maid answered instantly, bowing low.
Seraphina nodded.

She passed the squad of maids and began walking deep through the winding, incredibly luxurious fire-lit halls of the ancestral mansion, quietly admiring the massive portraits and ancient weaponry hung on the walls.
As she walked, she passed by a large, open-air indoor training room.
Inside, her younger sister was furiously practicing sword forms against a heavily reinforced wooden dummy.
BAM! BAM! BAM!
The young girl was sweating profusely with her wooden practice blade turning into a blur of motion but there was no fire.
There was no glowing aura either since her younger sister hadn’t awakened yet.
She was normal.
Unlike Seraphina, who had awakened her Lord Core and bonded with a Primordial Spirit when she was only five years old which was a testament to her terrifying once-in-a-generation talent...
Her sister was struggling just to manifest a single spark.
"I want to be as strong as her!" her younger sister was screaming in frustration, violently hacking at the wooden dummy with tears in her eyes. "I want to be as strong as Big Sis!"
Suddenly, the little sister paused. She sensed someone looking at her as she whipped her head around, looking directly at the open doorway, panting heavily but she saw nobody.
On the outside of the training room, hiding in the dark hallway, Seraphina had completely pressed herself flat against the cold stone wall, holding her breath.
Her red eyes were wide with a pang of guilt twisting in her chest.

’I am the last person she wants to see right now,’ Seraphina thought bitterly, knowing her presence only highlighted her sister’s failure to awaken so she silently slipped away from the door, continuing down the hall.
A few minutes later, she finally arrived at the massive solid mahogany doors of the primary Study.
Seraphina took a deep breath, steeling her nerves, and pushed the doors open.
She entered the massive, luxurious room, prepared for a serious high-level political debriefing.
Instead, she was greeted by humiliation.
Sitting in the center of the room was her Father.
He was an incredibly powerful, internationally feared Magistrate of the World Council as he possessed a terrifying aura that could crush buildings.
But right now, he was currently on his hands and knees, acting exactly like a submissive human chair.
Sitting incredibly comfortably directly on his broad back was her Mother.
The Matriarch of the Bloom Clan was a stunning and terrifyingly dominant woman with flowing crimson hair.
She was casually lounging on her husband’s back, eating sweet delicacies from a silver tray.

As Seraphina walked in, her Mother violently shoved her sticky fingers directly into her Father’s face, completely degrading him as he eagerly licked the sugar off her fingertips like an obedient dog.
Seraphina didn’t even blink.
This was exactly what she was used to.

chapters.title: Chapter 219: Returning Home
paragraphs: Her Father might be one of the most important and politically powerful people in the entire world, but here... in this guarded household... he had merely married into the ancient Bloom bloodline.
He was a political asset, not a ruler.
And as her Mother loved to constantly brutally remind him: "Once a loser, always a loser."
Which was exactly what he was in her eyes.

"Seraphina! My beautiful spark!" her Mother greeted her with a warm brilliant smile, entirely ignoring the man she was sitting on. "You have returned! Please, tell me immediately, what exactly happened in the Secret Realm?"
"Welcome home, pumpkin!" her Father chimed in cheerfully from the floor, trying to look up at her.
THWACK!
Her Mother aggressively, violently kicked him directly in the ribs with her sharp heel. "Shut up! I am speaking to my daughter!"
Her Father instantly went silent while whimpering softly.
Seraphina sighed, walking over to the massive mahogany desk in the center of the room.

"The Secret Realm of Ititus was a complete waste of time and resources, Mother," Seraphina recounted. "The Sand God was a narcissistic relic. He barely had any actual treasures to offer the us, and he trapped us in a tectonic collapse."
She raised her right hand. Her palm glowed with a bright, spatial blue light as she accessed her Lord Inventory.
"But," Seraphina continued, "I still managed to secure some high-tier assets during the subterranean descent before the collapse."
She swiped her hand across the desk.
CLATTER!
Several highly valuable items materialized and dropped heavily onto the polished wood.
A massive, violently glowing, obsidian-horned monster skull.

A perfectly forged Tier 3 mythril dagger that pulsed with latent shadow magic and several other glowing, highly condensed mana crystals and ancient treasures that would massively bolster the territory’s raw power.
Her Mother’s eyes widened, highly impressed by the haul.

"I must also officially report," Seraphina continued, her voice tightening slightly as she recounted the sheer terror of the event. "I was almost killed by the deity as he atomized my armor. But before he could execute the coalition, we met another far more powerful deity."
Seraphina looked at her parents with her red eyes turning serious.
"Thor. The Daughter of Odin. She descended from the sky and completely atomized the Sand God with a single swing of her hammer. It was... terrifying."
Her Mother’s smile vanished, instantly replaced by deep maternal worry. She slid off her husband’s back, rushing forward to check her daughter for injuries.
"Oh, my sweet girl!" her Mother gasped, cupping Seraphina’s face. "You survived a divine execution zone! You are so incredibly strong! I am so proud of you!"
Seraphina took a deep breath, her heart hammering against her ribs. It was time for the hardest part of the report.

"There is... one other thing, Mother," Seraphina murmured, her face instantly flushing a violent, blinding shade of crimson. "There was a man in the dungeon. A Lord and he... he saved my life against the deity."
Her Mother’s delicate eyebrows raised in sharp, aristocratic curiosity. "Oh? A man? A hero?"
"He also..." Seraphina stammered, completely unable to meet her mother’s eyes. "...he also saw me completely naked during when I was... I was... peeing."
The entire temperature in the massive study instantly plummeted.
VROOOOOOOOOM!
A terrifying aura of pure murderous intent violently exploded from the floor!
Her Father had instantly snapped.
The submissive dog was gone as the Magistrate of the World Council completely lost his mind at the disrespect to his daughter’s honor.
The gravity in the room increased tenfold, physically cracking the mahogany desk.
"WHAT IS HIS NAME?!" her Father roared, his voice distorted with demonic rage as he stood up, ready to completely glass whatever territory this man belonged to.
Before he could even take a step, the emotional shock of his daughter’s ruined modesty caught up to him.
His eyes rolled back into his head, and the terrifying Magistrate completely collapsed back down to the ground, passed out cold from a rage-induced aneurysm.
Seraphina panicked, waving her hands frantically at her stunned Mother.

"No! Please, do not punish him!" Seraphina shouted desperately, completely interrupting her Mother before she could summon the family assassins. "Silas is actually an incredibly strong and terrifyingly capable Lord! He fought the god hand-to-hand for a bit!"
Seraphina squeezed her eyes tightly shut, her face burning hotter than a solar flare.
She threw her hands down to her sides, bracing herself for the chaos she was about to unleash.
"Since he saw me naked," Seraphina shouted at the absolute top of her lungs. "I want to get married to him!"
Her Mother stood perfectly frozen in the center of the shattered study.
The Matriarch of the Bloom Clan looked down at her blushing, screaming daughter, and for the very first time in her entire noble life... she was completely speechless.
The torrential rain of Valoria City battered violently against the massive, floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows of the ultra-luxury penthouse apartment.
Inside the sprawling decorated living room, the atmosphere was a stark contrast to the violent thunderstorm raging outside.
The apartment was a masterclass in corporate wealth as the floors were laid with imported, polished obsidian.
The furniture was crafted from rare, magically preserved mahogany and draped in the finest temperature-regulating frost-silk.
Sitting right in the absolute center of a massive, U-shaped white leather couch was Harper.
The Lightning Lord wasn’t wearing her expensive and perfectly tailored corporate-sponsored combat armor, nor was she wearing her sleek suit.
She was dressed down in a simple oversized gray sweatshirt and a pair of loose black sleep shorts, her vibrant purple hair tied up in a messy chaotic bun that completely defied her usual perfection.

Despite constantly calling her father ’Papa’ in public and possessing a seemingly unbreakable psychological attachment to the man who funded her very existence, Harper did not live with him in the main family estate.
Since her mother had passed away years ago, the man had remarried.
He had taken his new significantly younger wife and shoved Harper and her little sister into this isolated golden-cage penthouse to live completely out of sight.

He had effectively buried his first family in a high-rise tower so he could focus entirely on his new political acquisitions without the messy baggage of his past even though he used them for missions.
’What was I thinking...?’
Sitting on the thick plush rug on the floor of the living room, surrounded by a small mountain of academy textbooks and glowing holographic datapads, was Harper’s little sister, Penelope.
Penelope looked up from her foundational mana-theory homework, adjusting her sleek wire-rimmed glasses.

She looked incredibly similar to Harper, sharing the exact same vibrant purple hair and sharp features, but she completely lacked the violent static energy that constantly crackled around her older sister.

"The infiltration plan with Lia is progressing perfectly, Big Sis," Penelope reported with her voice sounding very serious, it was far too mature for an eleven-year-old girl. "I officially solidified my position as Lia’s second best friend today during the lunch period. Kaede from the Shogunate Isles is currently her first, but I am rapidly closing the social gap."
Penelope paused, her violet eyes dropping to the floor.
She nervously gripped the edges of her textbook.
She genuinely liked Lia Graves.
The girl from Sector 4 was funny, fiercely loyal, and completely lacked the toxic manipulative venom that infected the rest of the Valoria Academy student body.
Penelope wanted to just be normal friends with her.
"I... I honestly really like her," Penelope admitted quietly with her voice softening into something resembling actual childhood innocence. "She isn’t like the other nobles. She’s genuine."
Harper didn’t even blink. Her purple eyes were cold and focused on the objective.

"That is completely irrelevant to the mission, Penelope," Harper stated. "Your personal feelings do not dictate the strategy as we need to maintain an unbreakable proximity to Silas Graves’s bloodline. Lia is the absolute center of his psychological anchor. If we completely control his sister’s social circle, we maintain a direct unfiltered line of influence to the Lord. Do not lose sight of the objective just because the girl shared her lunch with you."
Is what she would have loved to say but she didn’t say anything at all... she only looked down.
"Okay sis."
Harper let out a long and deeply exhausted sigh.
She looked down at her lap.
Resting across her thighs, completely dominating the pristine white leather of the couch, was a massive and heavy scuffed black trench coat.
It was Silas’s coat.
During the chaos of the Secret Realm extraction, he didn’t ask for it back.
It was stained with dried monster blood, ash, and his own scent.
Harper gently, almost reverently, ran her pale fingers over the torn fabric.
Her violet eyes began to glow with a dark intensity as she traced the stitching where his broad shoulders usually rested.
"Penelope," Harper asked quietly with her voice echoing softly in the massive rain-battered living room. "How much do you actually think Dad cares about us?"
Penelope physically flinched.
She completely stopped writing in her notebook as she stared up at her older sister in genuine shock.
Harper never, under any circumstances, referred to their father as ’Dad’ unless she was experiencing a violent spike of emotional instability.
It was always ’Papa’ when she was playing the role of the perfect obedient corporate daughter.
Hearing the word ’Dad’ meant the carefully constructed dam was actively breaking.
Penelope swallowed hard, carefully considering her words. She looked away, staring at the polished obsidian floor.

"He... he stuffed us in this apartment to stay with his new wife," Penelope recounted softly, quoting the exact harsh reality they had lived with for years. "Which he had been cheating on our Mother with for months before she even passed away. And well... it’s pretty low. He pays for the penthouse and the tutors, but he doesn’t actually look at us. We’re just liabilities to him."
Harper didn’t respond immediately.
She slowly stood up from the white leather couch.
She picked up the black trench coat and effortlessly swung it over her narrow shoulders.
Because it belonged to a towering Lord like Silas, it was comically large on her.
The dark hem dragged slightly against the obsidian floor, and the broad shoulders completely swallowed her slender frame but the second she put it on, something fundamentally shifted in her psyche.
She didn’t know exactly why, but when she was completely enveloped in the scent of Silas Graves...
She felt an astronomical surge of pure confidence.
’I feel like... I can do anything.’ Harper thought.
Harper turned around, looking down at her little sister.
The static electricity in the luxury penthouse violently spiked as the heavy crystal chandelier hanging above the dining table began to flicker and hum with dangerous voltage.

"Penelope," Harper purred with a dark unhinged smile stretching across her flawless face. "How exactly do you think it’ll feel if I just walk over to the main estate right now... and blast him directly in the face with some high-voltage lightning?"
Penelope stared at her older sister.
She didn’t scream, hell she didn’t try to talk her out of it.
She simply adjusted her wire-rimmed glasses with her own deep-seated quiet resentment toward their father bleeding through her noble conditioning.
"I think," Penelope replied calmly, her violet eyes totally deadpan. "that it will hurt him. A lot."
Harper’s smile widened into a brilliant psychotic grin.

The violet lightning violently crackled to life, actively glowing inside her purple eyes, illuminating the dark living room with harsh flashes of electricity that perfectly matched the thunderstorm raging outside.
"Sure~" Harper sang cheerfully, her voice dripping with sweetness as she adjusted the heavy collar of Silas’s trench coat around her neck. "Let me go do that quickly~"
A world away, completely separated from the toxic neon-lit politics and torrential rain of Valoria City, the world shifted.
The absolute pitch-black void of the dimensional tether evaporated.
Silas materialized directly in the center of his sprawling, dimly lit master bedroom inside the Blessed Land Keep.

The transition from the high-tech bureaucratic reality of Earth to the primal, mana-dense atmosphere of the Sovereign Realm was completely instantaneous, leaving him standing barefoot on the thick rugs of his sanctuary.
He was home.
He didn’t even have a single second to fully exhale the stale air of the human world from his lungs before the wooden door to his bedroom was violently thrown open.
"MY LORD!"
Eluned didn’t just walk into the room... she practically teleported across the floorboards.
The stunning SSS-Rank Goddess sprinted directly forward and threw her entire body against him.
She wrapped her arms tightly around his neck, burying her flawless face directly into his bare, muscular chest.
"Thank you... Thank you... for coming back to me, my Lord..." Eluned breathed out, her voice trembling with genuine relief.
