chapters.title: Chapter 220: Back In Blessed Land
paragraphs: "Mwah! Mwah! Mwah!"
She aggressively kissed his bare muscle, ignoring his personal space.
She had spent the last week pacing the Keep, her anxiety slowly driving her to the brink of insanity as the territory’s tether violently fluctuated with the Secret Realm’s collapse. T
he thought of losing her anchor to the world had nearly broken her newly restored sanity.
Silas let out a deep rumbling chuckle that vibrated pleasantly through his chest.
He was not around strangers so any sort of paranoia he had here completely died down... These were his women.
He raised his calloused hand, gently but firmly patting Eluned’s vibrant silver-green hair.
"I told you I wasn’t going to die in the dirt," Silas murmured, leaning his head back.
Before Eluned could fully monopolize his arrival, the doorway darkened.
Morwenna stepped into the room.
The terrifying Pirate Queen was wearing her usual tattered captain’s coat and heavy leather boots.
She leaned against the doorframe, crossing her arms over her chest and aggressively attempting to maintain her tough bloodthirsty persona.
"Hmph! Don’t think I care that you came back..."
She glared at him with her feral gray eyes narrowing as her jaw set tight however she lasted exactly three seconds.
The tough exterior completely shattered as Morwenna let out a very uncharacteristic sound and aggressively pushed off the doorframe.
She marched completely past Eluned and joined the embrace, throwing her incredibly strong arms around Silas’s waist and violently squeezing the breath right out of his lungs.
"Welcome back, Captain." Morwenna muttered fiercely into his ribs, refusing to let go.

"Argh!" Silas groaned loudly, his ribs genuinely protesting the crushing pressure of two incredibly powerful SSS-Rank women clinging to him simultaneously. "Alright. Timeout. Timeout! You’re going to snap my spine in half!"
They begrudgingly let him go, taking a half-step back but refusing to leave his immediate proximity.
"Thank you for waiting for me," Silas told them sincerely, his golden-ringed eyes softening as he looked at his two most powerful Divine beings he had.
Eluned immediately grabbed his right hand with her bright green eyes flashing in intense excitement.

"We have been preparing for your return all evening, my Lord!" Eluned announced proudly, aggressively pulling him toward the open doorway. "Kaelia and I as well as Morwenna have been painstakingly making dinner, and you must come down to the Mess Hall and try today’s feast!"
’She called Morwenna by her name...?’ Silas thought, perhaps Eluned had done it befoer but it was still surprising. ’How close did they get?’
As Eluned dragged the shirtless Warlord out into the stone hallway, Morwenna completely abandoned all decorum.
The Pirate Queen sprinted over to the massive open-air stone window of the Keep. She leaned her entire upper body out over the courtyard, cupping her hands around her mouth.

"LISTEN UP, YOU MISERABLE BILGE-RATS!" Morwenna screamed at the top of her lungs, her voice carrying the concussive force of a cannon blast across the entire Blessed Land territory. "LORD SILAS HAS RETURNED TO THE BLESSED LAND! HE IS ALIVE!"
The second the words left her mouth, the entire territory violently erupted.
Massive cheers sounded from the barracks, the training grounds, and the perimeter walls.
The noise of dozens of fiercely loyal Warlord combatants celebrating their Master’s survival echoed into the sky, startling the ambient mana beasts hiding in the distant treelines.
Eluned dragged Silas down the spiraling stone staircase and directly into the main sprawling living area of the Keep.
Silas paused at the bottom of the stairs, looking over at the massive, comfortable leather couch in the center of the room.
Sitting there, looking completely relaxed, was Talira.
The ancient and devastatingly powerful Crimson Dragon was currently trapped in her humanoid form.
She was wearing one of Silas’s oversized white button-down shirts with the fabric hanging loosely off her shoulders as her vibrant crimson hair tumbled down her back.
’Oh... she looks cute to be honest.’
She was currently playing a complex carved chess-like tactical board game with Aeliana.
’I think Elu made that when I showed them that chess board... but do they know the rules?’
Aeliana looked up from the board.
The moment the Starlight Arcanist’s green eyes landed on Silas, her entire face brilliantly lit up with pure joy.
She dropped her game piece, ready to sprint across the room.
However, the exact same thing could not be said about Talira.
The Crimson Dragon’s vertical reptilian pupils zeroed in on him.
Her flawless face visibly darkened and she crossed her arms over her chest, letting out a highly annoyed arrogant huff as the entire Keep descended into joyous chaos around her.
"Hmph! There’s nothing special about a human..."
Silas completely ignored the dragon’s tantrum as he offered Aeliana a warm smile and continued walking toward the heavy oak doors leading outside.
Silas stepped out into the cool night air of the sprawling courtyard.
The other girls, including the muscled Thora, were already actively gathering in a massive, chaotic semi-circle directly in front of the Keep.
They were cheering wildly, banging their weapons against their shields, chanting his name repeatedly.
"LORD SILAS! LORD SILAS! LORD SILAS!"
Silas blinked, completely overwhelmed by the volume of the reception as he raised his hand.
"I’m back!" Silas announced loudly.
The moment the words left his mouth, the cheers grew exponentially louder. It was deafening.
Kaelia, the sweet talented chef of the territory, desperately pushed her way to the very front of the crowd.
She was wearing a flour-stained apron as her eyes shone with excitement.
"Lord Silas!" Kaelia asked eagerly, bouncing on her heels. "Would you love to try some of the new dishes I made from the cookbook?! I added my own magical twists to the marinades!"
Silas was absolutely starving as he opened his mouth to tell her yes but he was instantly swarmed.
Several of the other girls violently pushed forward, completely surrounding him.
"Lord Silas, can you check out my new sword skills?!" one of the girls shouted, holding up a heavy broadsword.
"Lord Silas, please come to the range! I want you to check out my new elemental magic!" another mage begged, grabbing his arm.
"No, me first!" Rowenna shouted, pushing through the crowd. "My Lord, you have to check out the new spell I developed! It’ll be worth your time I swear!"
Silas raised a calloused hand to his face, pinching the bridge of his nose to ward off the impending migraine.
The volume of seventy dangerous and devoted women screaming for his attention all at once was infinitely more terrifying than fighting a god.
He opened his mouth, preparing to release a pulse of Gold Core mana to force them to calm down.
Suddenly, a weight slammed onto his back.
Thora had completely bypassed the crowd by physically leaping through the air and aggressively climbing directly onto his broad shirtless back.
She wrapped her thick arms around his head and locked her muscular legs around his neck, treating him like a jungle gym.
"ALRIGHT, EVERYBODY CALM DOWN!" Thora roared over the chaos with her booming voice completely silencing the bickering girls.
She pointed a heavy finger at the crowd.

"Come to him one after the other tomorrow!" Thora commanded, taking charge of the logistics. "Besides, our Lord hasn’t eaten any actual good food in a while! According to Aeliana’s debrief, he barely ate anything but dry rations in that disgusting desert! He needs a feast!"
The girls instantly gasped, realizing their Lord was starving.
"A feast!" Rowenna agreed loudly.
The girls cheered in unified agreement.
Before Silas could even protest the indignity of being carried, he was physically corralled and forced by the mob of highly enthusiastic women directly into the massive sprawling Warlord Barracks.
’I can get used to this...’ Silas thought.
The Mess Hall of the Barracks was absolutely chaotic.
The long heavy oak tables were overflowing with massive platters of roasted meats, highly seasoned vegetables, and overflowing tankards of alcohol.
Everyone was seated in their own designated spots, laughing, drinking, and loudly recounting the day’s training.
Silas was seated directly at the absolute head of the primary table.
It was a coveted and dangerous seating arrangement.
Eluned was seated directly on his right side with her posture perfect and incredibly smug.
Morwenna was seated directly on his left, casually resting her elbows on the wood while Aeliana was seated exactly opposite him, smiling sweetly as she ate.
And Talira, the Crimson Dragon, was seated opposite as well while watching the spectacle with narrowing eyes.
It was four incredibly powerful entities sitting at a single table at the same time and the girls were actively competing for his attention.
"Here have mine, my Lord!"
"No, mine!"
"If you wouldn’t mind Lord Sy... you could have mine."
Eluned was pushing a forkful of roasted boar toward his mouth, while Morwenna was trying to force him to chew on a seasoned piece of wolf meat, and Aeliana was gently offering him a sweet pastry.
"I have a solution."
Silas completely abandoned all table manners.

He simply opened his mouth, actively eating from all three of the women’s forks at the exact same time as he chewed the chaotic mixture of flavors, swallowing heavily before reaching for his tankard of alcohol.
’I sure hope Thora didn’t spike this shit again.’
Talira sat there, quietly watching the entire interaction unfold.
She slowly chewed on a piece of meat with her vertical crimson pupils tracking the genuine affectionate smiles on Eluned and Morwenna’s faces.

’Why...?’ Talira thought, her draconic mind completely confused by the emotional dynamic. ’I am a true, Primordial Crimson Dragon. I am the apex of the food chain and I thrive on being the absolute center of attention. But... I haven’t seen Morwenna or Eluned smile like this for me in the days I’ve known them. Why is their smile so wide just for him?’
She was a dragon.
Her existence demanding worship got old quickly, and that was a normal expected reality.
However Silas simply returning from a dungeon was actively sending massive joyous ripples across the entire territory.
They genuinely loved him. It was a concept her ancient brain struggled to fully compute.
"This is incredible," Silas commended loudly, wiping his mouth with the back of his hand. "Kaelia’s cooking has improved massively and so did you, Thora."
Eluned and Morwenna instantly nudged his ribs from both sides simultaneously.
"We cooked too, Captain!" Morwenna protested loudly, glaring at him.
"I personally seasoned the boar, my Lord." Eluned added, lifting her chin proudly.
Silas chuckled, leaning back in his chair.
"Alright, fine. You both did an amazing job. The food is perfect. You are both culinary masters."
From the far end of the long oak table, one of the younger girls stood up, holding her tankard.
"Lord Silas!" she called out, silencing the immediate area. "How long exactly will you be staying with us this time without going back to the Human world?!"
The entire Mess Hall instantly went completely quiet.
Every single girl turned to look at him as their eyes went wide with anticipation.
The girls wanted their Lord entirely to themselves!
It had almost been a full week of him jumping from the human world back to the territory, constantly dividing his time.
Silas looked around the room, taking in their hopeful faces.
He let out a long sigh, setting his tankard down onto the wood.
"I will be here for the foreseeable future," Silas announced loudly, projecting his voice so the entire hall could hear.
Silas smiled, leaning his elbows on the table.

’I’ll be here for a very long time,’ Silas thought with ambition burning hot in his chest. ’I am not leaving this territory until I reach the second stage of my Gold Core and the only way to do that is by locking myself in the training grounds and manually mastering eight entirely different elemental affinities.’
The fact that he would be staying here for an extended period brought up another massive unified cheer from the girls as tankards slammed against the tables in celebration.
Silas turned his head, looking directly at Eluned on his right, and then at Morwenna on his left. He formally, respectfully bowed his head just a fraction of an inch toward his top combatants.
"Actually," Silas requested, his voice shifting to serious business. "I need to ask a massive favor from both of you. I need you to formally teach me... I want to fully master Ice and Nature magic."
Eluned’s flawless face instantly glittered with joy as she leaned forward, completely ignoring the massive crowd, and kissed him directly on the cheek.
"My Love," Eluned declared loudly. "I will teach you anything you want to know. My Nature magic is yours."
Morwenna, however, didn’t celebrate immediately. The Pirate Queen blinked her feral gray eyes looking at him with deep confusion.
"Wait," Morwenna interrupted, her brow furrowing. "Captain, what about Water magic? That’s the foundation for Ice. You need to learn the fluid dynamics first."
Silas didn’t think.
"Water? "Oh, I was already learning about Water magic while I was out in the Secret Realm," Silas answered casually, waving his hand dismissively.
To demonstrate, Silas brought out his right hand, hovering it directly over the center of the oak table.

He effortlessly manipulated his Gold Core as he drew ambient moisture from the air, rapidly condensing it until he summoned a massive and perfectly spherical swirling ball of highly pressurized water.

he thought of losing her anchor to the world had nearly broken her newly restored sanity.

Morwenna stepped into the room.
The terrifying Pirate Queen was wearing her usual tattered captain’s coat and heavy leather boots.
She leaned against the doorframe, crossing her arms over her chest and aggressively attempting to maintain her tough bloodthirsty persona.
"Hmph!
Don’t think I care that you came back..."
She glared at him with her feral gray eyes narrowing as her jaw set tight however she lasted exactly three seconds.
The tough exterior completely shattered as Morwenna let out a very uncharacteristic sound and aggressively pushed off the doorframe.
She marched completely past Eluned and joined the embrace, throwing her incredibly strong arms around Silas’s waist and violently squeezing the breath right out of his lungs.
"Welcome back, Captain." Morwenna muttered fiercely into his ribs, refusing to let go.
"Argh!" Silas groaned loudly, his ribs genuinely protesting the crushing pressure of two incredibly powerful SSS-Rank women clinging to him simultaneously.
"Alright.
Timeout.
Timeout!
You’re going to snap my spine in half!"
They begrudgingly let him go, taking a half-step back but refusing to leave his immediate proximity.
"Thank you for waiting for me," Silas told them sincerely, his golden-ringed eyes softening as he looked at his two most powerful Divine beings he had.
Eluned immediately grabbed his right hand with her bright green eyes flashing in intense excitement.
"We have been preparing for your return all evening, my Lord!" Eluned announced proudly, aggressively pulling him toward the open doorway.
"Kaelia and I as well as Morwenna have been painstakingly making dinner, and you must come down to the Mess Hall and try today’s feast!"
’She called Morwenna by her name...?’ Silas thought, perhaps Eluned had done it befoer but it was still surprising. ’How close did they get?’
As Eluned dragged the shirtless Warlord out into the stone hallway, Morwenna completely abandoned all decorum.
The Pirate Queen sprinted over to the massive open-air stone window of the Keep.
She leaned her entire upper body out over the courtyard, cupping her hands around her mouth.
"LISTEN UP, YOU MISERABLE BILGE-RATS!" Morwenna screamed at the top of her lungs, her voice carrying the concussive force of a cannon blast across the entire Blessed Land territory.
"LORD SILAS HAS RETURNED TO THE BLESSED LAND!
HE IS ALIVE!"
The second the words left her mouth, the entire territory violently erupted.
Massive cheers sounded from the barracks, the training grounds, and the perimeter walls.
The noise of dozens of fiercely loyal Warlord combatants celebrating their Master’s survival echoed into the sky, startling the ambient mana beasts hiding in the distant treelines.
Eluned dragged Silas down the spiraling stone staircase and directly into the main sprawling living area of the Keep.
Silas paused at the bottom of the stairs, looking over at the massive, comfortable leather couch in the center of the room.
Sitting there, looking completely relaxed, was Talira.
The ancient and devastatingly powerful Crimson Dragon was currently trapped in her humanoid form.
She was wearing one of Silas’s oversized white button-down shirts with the fabric hanging loosely off her shoulders as her vibrant crimson hair tumbled down her back.
’Oh... she looks cute to be honest.’
She was currently playing a complex carved chess-like tactical board game with Aeliana.
’I think Elu made that when I showed them that chess board... but do they know the rules?’
Aeliana looked up from the board.
The moment the Starlight Arcanist’s green eyes landed on Silas, her entire face brilliantly lit up with pure joy.
She dropped her game piece, ready to sprint across the room.
However, the exact same thing could not be said about Talira.
The Crimson Dragon’s vertical reptilian pupils zeroed in on him.
Her flawless face visibly darkened and she crossed her arms over her chest, letting out a highly annoyed arrogant huff as the entire Keep descended into joyous chaos around her.
"Hmph!
There’s nothing special about a human..."
Silas completely ignored the dragon’s tantrum as he offered Aeliana a warm smile and continued walking toward the heavy oak doors leading outside.
Silas stepped out into the cool night air of the sprawling courtyard.
The other girls, including the muscled Thora, were already actively gathering in a massive, chaotic semi-circle directly in front of the Keep.
They were cheering wildly, banging their weapons against their shields, chanting his name repeatedly.
"LORD SILAS!
LORD SILAS!
LORD SILAS!"
Silas blinked, completely overwhelmed by the volume of the reception as he raised his hand.
"I’m back!" Silas announced loudly.
The moment the words left his mouth, the cheers grew exponentially louder.
It was deafening.
Kaelia, the sweet talented chef of the territory, desperately pushed her way to the very front of the crowd.
She was wearing a flour-stained apron as her eyes shone with excitement.
"Lord Silas!" Kaelia asked eagerly, bouncing on her heels.
"Would you love to try some of the new dishes I made from the cookbook?!
I added my own magical twists to the marinades!"
Silas was absolutely starving as he opened his mouth to tell her yes but he was instantly swarmed.
Several of the other girls violently pushed forward, completely surrounding him.
"Lord Silas, can you check out my new sword skills?!" one of the girls shouted, holding up a heavy broadsword.
"Lord Silas, please come to the range!
I want you to check out my new elemental magic!" another mage begged, grabbing his arm.
"No, me first!" Rowenna shouted, pushing through the crowd.
"My Lord, you have to check out the new spell I developed!
It’ll be worth your time I swear!"
Silas raised a calloused hand to his face, pinching the bridge of his nose to ward off the impending migraine.
The volume of seventy dangerous and devoted women screaming for his attention all at once was infinitely more terrifying than fighting a god.
He opened his mouth, preparing to release a pulse of Gold Core mana to force them to calm down.
Suddenly, a weight slammed onto his back.
Thora had completely bypassed the crowd by physically leaping through the air and aggressively climbing directly onto his broad shirtless back.
She wrapped her thick arms around his head and locked her muscular legs around his neck, treating him like a jungle gym.
"ALRIGHT, EVERYBODY CALM DOWN!" Thora roared over the chaos with her booming voice completely silencing the bickering girls.
She pointed a heavy finger at the crowd.
"Come to him one after the other tomorrow!" Thora commanded, taking charge of the logistics.
"Besides, our Lord hasn’t eaten any actual good food in a while!
According to Aeliana’s debrief, he barely ate anything but dry rations in that disgusting desert!
He needs a feast!"
The girls instantly gasped, realizing their Lord was starving.
"A feast!" Rowenna agreed loudly.
The girls cheered in unified agreement.
Before Silas could even protest the indignity of being carried, he was physically corralled and forced by the mob of highly enthusiastic women directly into the massive sprawling Warlord Barracks.

Silas was seated directly at the absolute head of the primary table.

chapters.title: Chapter 221: Pacifying SSS-Rank Beings [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Then, without missing a beat, he seamlessly pushed his mana through the spell.
’Let’s impress her a bit, shall we?’
He used Ice Transformation and the entire swirling ball of water instantly, flawlessly froze solid, turning into a massive sphere of absolute-zero ice.
He smiled proudly, turning to look at Morwenna to show off his progress.
"See, how is it?"
But the Pirate Queen wasn’t smiling.
Morwenna’s face had violently darkened.
The temperature around her physically plummeted as the shadows in the Mess Hall actively seemed to violently stretch and warp around her seated form.
’I think I fucked up...’
Silas could literally only see deep suffocating shadows completely obscuring her upper face, except for her eyes.
Her feral gray eyes had turned red.
CREEEEEEAAK!
The solid steel fork she was holding in her right hand audibly bent and snapped completely in half under the pressure of her grip.
Silas flinched with his survival instincts screaming at maximum volume.
"My Lord," Morwenna asked.
Her voice wasn’t loud... instead it was a terrifying demonic whisper that vibrated the alcohol in his tankard.
"What exact woman have you been out there cheating on me with?!"
Silas’s eyes went completely wide. "Morwenna, I didn’t—"

"Tell me exactly who she is so I can violently cut her head off!" Morwenna snarled, standing up from the bench with the dark watery aura of the abyss actively leaking from her body. "You... you cheater! I am the one meant to teach you Water magic! It is my affinity! Mine!"
Silas panicked. He desperately reached out, grabbing her tightly by the shoulder to prevent her from drawing her sword in the middle of the Mess Hall.

"Morwenna, stop, it isn’t like that!" Silas told her rapidly, his brain frantically searching for the correct de-escalation method. "The person that taught me that... she is nothing to me! She’s just an old crone!"
Aeli’s face twitched.
’Old crone?’ She thought but then she couldn’t deny it, her Aunt was quite old.
He looked deeply into her red eyes, delivering the ultimate pacifier.
"Morwenna, you are my everything."
Morwenna instantly froze.
The dark aura completely evaporated as the violent red faded from her eyes.
She blushed a deep intense shade of crimson, looking away from him as she sat back down, completely mollified.
"Obviously," Morwenna muttered, crossing her arms and acting tough, though a massive smile was fighting to break through.
Silas let out a sigh of relief... He had successfully defused the SSS-Rank bomb.
"Huh?"
Silas froze.
He slowly turned his head to the right.
Eluned was staring at him.
Her green eyes were completely lacking any sort of warmth at all.
Her flawless face was locked into an expression of rage as the wooden table beneath her hands was actively beginning to sprout aggressive razor-sharp thorns.
"If that filthy, washed-up pirate is your everything," Eluned asked with her voice dropping into a terrifyingly calm tone. "then what exactly am I?"
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes widened in horror.
In a desperate attempt to calm down Morwenna, the Lord had accidentally let a far greater and infinitely more destructive power be unleashed!
The silence that descended upon the Barracks Mess Hall was so heavy and so physically suffocating, that even the ambient crackle of the roasting torches along the stone walls seemed to die out.
Silas sat completely frozen at the head of the massive oak table with his bare chest rising and falling as he looked between the two terrifying elemental catastrophes he had accidentally primed.

Around the hall, all the seasoned subjects of Blessed Land... Shieldmaidens, Mages, Archers, the tailor... everyone who would happily charge an adult dragon without blinking collectively held their breath, slowly reaching for their tankards and sliding inch by inch away from the primary table.
Even Aeliana opposite him had frozen with her pastry halfway to her mouth with her green eyes going wide in silent alarm.
Silas swallowed hard, his mind racing at a thousand calculations per second.

’How can I possibly salvage this situation?’ Silas thought. ’If I tell Eluned that she’s my primary woman or that I love her more to calm down her thorns, Morwenna will literally draw the Astral Corsair and attempt to destroy the table! If I try to logically explain that I was just de-escalating a murder threat, both of their egos will shatter and they’ll turn the entire barracks into a crater! And that’s not even mentioning the crowd...’
Silas flicked his golden-ringed eyes past the two rival S-Rank alphas.
All down the length of the hall, Aeliana, Thora, Rowenna, Kaelia, and every single other girl in his faction were staring at him with strange intense and very expectant expressions.
They weren’t just watching a fight... they were actively waiting to hear where they stood in their Lord’s hierarchy.
If he elevated one above the rest, the carefully balanced morale of his entire combat force would collapse.
There was only one mathematical way out of an SSS-Rank encirclement.
He had to completely abandon shame and lean into uncompromising greed.
Silas took a deep breath, expanding his broad chest, and slammed both of his calloused palms flat onto the oak table, ignoring the thorns that scraped against his skin.

"All of you!" Silas exclaimed, projecting his deep voice with enough concussive Gold Core force to rattle the rafters of the Mess Hall. "Every single one of you in this territory... you’re my everything! I can’t live without any of you!"
The silence hung for a single suspended second and then, the emotional dam completely broke.
Across the entire Mess Hall, seventy hardened female combatants instantly turned the color of ripe tomatoes.
Weapons clattered against shields as hands flew up to cover burning cheeks.
"M-my Lord..." Rowenna squeaked from the third table down with her spell completely fizzling out as she buried her face in her arms.
"He... he said he can’t live without us!" one of the heavy Shieldmaiden girls stammered, fanning her flushed face with a napkin.
Even Aeliana dropped her pastry onto her plate with her delicate elven ears turning brilliant crimson as she looked down as a soft helpless smile touched her lips.
On his right, the aggressive thorns sprouting from the table violently retracted, melting back into harmless wood as Eluned gasped.
Her arrogant scowl completely vanished, replaced by a radiant flattered blush that spread all the way down her neck.
She brought her hands up to her cheeks, looking away with a haughty sniff that completely failed to hide her delight.
On his left, Morwenna’s abyssal aura evaporated into thin air.
The Pirate Queen opened her mouth to argue, closed it, and then aggressively crossed her arms over her chest, looking fixedly at the ceiling while her ears burned a bright red.
"Tch. Greedy Captain..." Morwenna muttered under her breath, though the small pleased smirk breaking across her face betrayed her entirely.
Sitting on the table, Talira slowly raised her tankard of alcohol to her lips with her vertical crimson pupils narrowing as she observed the collective blushing meltdown of the entire territory.

’Shameless,’ the Crimson Dragon called him out coldly in her internal draconic thoughts, taking a long sip. ’Utterly, despicably, unimaginably shameless. To look at so many armed females directly in the eye and deploy such flattery without his pulse even spiking... Human males are truly the most deceitful insatiable predators in the mortal realm. Very disgusting.’
Despite her internal sneer, Talira’s tail swished restlessly under the table with her ancient mind secretly cataloging the effectiveness of the maneuver.
With the SSS-Rank detonation successfully defused, Silas quickly pivoted to business before their embarrassment could transform back into rivalry.
He turned toward Eluned, clearing his throat.
"So," Silas asked, leaning slightly closer to the nature mage. "When exactly are we going to start the training? I want to get my hands on those elemental spells as soon as possible."
Eluned’s green eyes lit up with renewed purpose. She leaned into his bare shoulder with her confidence returning tenfold.

"We can start immediately after we are completely done eating, my Love," Eluned told him softly, her voice dripping with affectionate promise. "Your physical stamina must be fully replenished before we attempt high-tier mana manipulation."
To ensure his stamina was met, Eluned immediately picked up a fresh silver fork, loaded it with a thick juicy slice of seasoned boar meat, and gently pressed it to his lips.
Silas didn’t argue... he opened his mouth and accepted the bite, chewing the rich savory meat.
Not to be outdone by even a fraction of a second, Morwenna instantly stabbed a massive piece of roasted tentacle with her own replacement fork and aggressively shoved it toward his face.
"Eat up, Captain," Morwenna instructed firmly, feeding him directly after Eluned.
As Silas chewed the spiced seafood, the Pirate Queen leaned across his chest, glaring right at the nature mage.

"And hold your horses, weed. I am letting you teach him your nature tricks first today... but only if he proves he has actually mastered his water foundations enough to satisfy me. If his fluid control is sloppy, I’m keeping him in the arena until his forms are clean."
"My Lord’s control is flawless, pirate," Eluned sniffed arrogantly, feeding Silas another slice of boar. "He will pass your petty tests in moments, and then he will belong to the forest."

Silas simply sat between them, dutifully chewing and swallowing as the two SSS-Rank divine beings stuffed him full of protein with his mind already shifting into combat gear for the grueling hours ahead.
Ten minutes later, the meal was cleared, and the heavy wooden doors of the Mess Hall swung shut behind them.
Silas, Morwenna, and Eluned walked in focus across the open courtyard of the Blessed Land Citadel, heading directly toward the primary fortified structure.
While the exterior of the Keep looked like a traditional, massive medieval fortress built from white stone and timber, its true architectural value lay deep beneath the earth.
Because Silas had upgraded the Keep to a bona fide Tier 3 stronghold, the system had automatically expanded its underground footprint, carving out specialized facilities directly out of the bedrock.
’So in other words, I have an underground bat cave.’
They descended a long wide stone staircase that spiraled down past the living room as the air grew progressively cooler and denser with mana the deeper they went.
Finally, they stopped in front of a pair of massive, twelve-foot-tall double doors forged from reinforced mythril-alloy and dark obsidian, etched with glowing blue dampening runes.

The Citadel possessed a sprawling outdoor training ground next to it which was where him and Morwenna had first done the first style in the rain, but it also possessed this... a personal restricted training vault explicitly designed for Lords and high-tier Heroes to unleash destruction without leveling the living quarters above.
Up until today, Silas had been so continuously occupied with either handling the territory and more so he had never actually felt the need to step foot inside this subterranean vault.
Silas reached out, placing his palm against the runic plate in the center of the obsidian doors.
The array flashed golden as it read his Lord signature, and the heavy doors slid open with a smooth pressurized hiss.
A massive training ground came into view.
The vault was easily two hundred yards across and vaulted fifty feet high, supported by massive columns of reinforced self-healing runic masonry.

Along the upper edges of the walls, intricate arrays of mechanical and magical circulation vents steadily cycled fresh chilled air from the surface, creating a cool atmosphere that prevented the room from turning into a humid furnace during intense physical exertion.
The floor was paved with thick interlocking slabs of dark runic stone designed to absorb impact and automatically reconstruct themselves after taking structural damage.
Before Silas could even take a full step over the threshold, a blur of tattered leather and gray fabric rushed past him.
Morwenna practically sprinted into the room with her shoulder brushing against his chest with enough force to almost knock him off balance.

The Pirate Queen skidded to a halt ten yards into the vault, slowly turning in a full circle as her feral gray eyes swept across the massive high-ceilinged expanse, the reinforced pillars, and the high-tier elemental dampening wards.

"We had a room like this?!" Morwenna exclaimed with her jaw dropping slightly in genuine shock as she looked back at Silas. "Are you kidding me, Captain?! We could have taken advantage of this all this time! Do you have any idea how many times I had to hold back my Tidal slashes out in the courtyard so I didn’t accidentally decapitate a squad of girls or blow the roof off Kaelia’s kitchen?!"

She blushed a deep intense shade of crimson, looking away from him as she sat back down, completely mollified.
"Obviously," Morwenna muttered, crossing her arms and acting tough, though a massive smile was fighting to break through.
Silas let out a sigh of relief...
He had successfully defused the SSS-Rank bomb.
"Huh?"
Silas froze.
He slowly turned his head to the right.
Eluned was staring at him.
Her green eyes were completely lacking any sort of warmth at all.
Her flawless face was locked into an expression of rage as the wooden table beneath her hands was actively beginning to sprout aggressive razor-sharp thorns.
"If that filthy, washed-up pirate is your everything," Eluned asked with her voice dropping into a terrifyingly calm tone.
"then what exactly am I?"
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes widened in horror.
In a desperate attempt to calm down Morwenna, the Lord had accidentally let a far greater and infinitely more destructive power be unleashed!
The silence that descended upon the Barracks Mess Hall was so heavy and so physically suffocating, that even the ambient crackle of the roasting torches along the stone walls seemed to die out.
Silas sat completely frozen at the head of the massive oak table with his bare chest rising and falling as he looked between the two terrifying elemental catastrophes he had accidentally primed.
Around the hall, all the seasoned subjects of Blessed Land...

Shieldmaidens, Mages, Archers, the tailor... everyone who would happily charge an adult dragon without blinking collectively held their breath, slowly reaching for their tankards and sliding inch by inch away from the primary table.
Even Aeliana opposite him had frozen with her pastry halfway to her mouth with her green eyes going wide in silent alarm.
Silas swallowed hard, his mind racing at a thousand calculations per second.

’How can I possibly salvage this situation?’ Silas thought. ’If I tell Eluned that she’s my primary woman or that I love her more to calm down her thorns, Morwenna will literally draw the Astral Corsair and attempt to destroy the table!
If I try to logically explain that I was just de-escalating a murder threat, both of their egos will shatter and they’ll turn the entire barracks into a crater!
And that’s not even mentioning the crowd...’
Silas flicked his golden-ringed eyes past the two rival S-Rank alphas.
All down the length of the hall, Aeliana, Thora, Rowenna, Kaelia, and every single other girl in his faction were staring at him with strange intense and very expectant expressions.
They weren’t just watching a fight... they were actively waiting to hear where they stood in their Lord’s hierarchy.
If he elevated one above the rest, the carefully balanced morale of his entire combat force would collapse.
There was only one mathematical way out of an SSS-Rank encirclement.
He had to completely abandon shame and lean into uncompromising greed.
Silas took a deep breath, expanding his broad chest, and slammed both of his calloused palms flat onto the oak table, ignoring the thorns that scraped against his skin.
"All of you!" Silas exclaimed, projecting his deep voice with enough concussive Gold Core force to rattle the rafters of the Mess Hall.
"Every single one of you in this territory... you’re my everything!
I can’t live without any of you!"
The silence hung for a single suspended second and then, the emotional dam completely broke.
Across the entire Mess Hall, seventy hardened female combatants instantly turned the color of ripe tomatoes.
Weapons clattered against shields as hands flew up to cover burning cheeks.
"M-my Lord..." Rowenna squeaked from the third table down with her spell completely fizzling out as she buried her face in her arms.
"He... he said he can’t live without us!" one of the heavy Shieldmaiden girls stammered, fanning her flushed face with a napkin.
Even Aeliana dropped her pastry onto her plate with her delicate elven ears turning brilliant crimson as she looked down as a soft helpless smile touched her lips.
On his right, the aggressive thorns sprouting from the table violently retracted, melting back into harmless wood as Eluned gasped.
Her arrogant scowl completely vanished, replaced by a radiant flattered blush that spread all the way down her neck.
She brought her hands up to her cheeks, looking away with a haughty sniff that completely failed to hide her delight.
On his left, Morwenna’s abyssal aura evaporated into thin air.
The Pirate Queen opened her mouth to argue, closed it, and then aggressively crossed her arms over her chest, looking fixedly at the ceiling while her ears burned a bright red.
"Tch.
Greedy Captain..." Morwenna muttered under her breath, though the small pleased smirk breaking across her face betrayed her entirely.
Sitting on the table, Talira slowly raised her tankard of alcohol to her lips with her vertical crimson pupils narrowing as she observed the collective blushing meltdown of the entire territory.
’Shameless,’ the Crimson Dragon called him out coldly in her internal draconic thoughts, taking a long sip. ’Utterly, despicably, unimaginably shameless.
To look at so many armed females directly in the eye and deploy such flattery without his pulse even spiking...
Human males are truly the most deceitful insatiable predators in the mortal realm.
Very disgusting.’
Despite her internal sneer, Talira’s tail swished restlessly under the table with her ancient mind secretly cataloging the effectiveness of the maneuver.
With the SSS-Rank detonation successfully defused, Silas quickly pivoted to business before their embarrassment could transform back into rivalry.
He turned toward Eluned, clearing his throat.
"So," Silas asked, leaning slightly closer to the nature mage.
"When exactly are we going to start the training?
I want to get my hands on those elemental spells as soon as possible."
Eluned’s green eyes lit up with renewed purpose.
She leaned into his bare shoulder with her confidence returning tenfold.
"We can start immediately after we are completely done eating, my Love," Eluned told him softly, her voice dripping with affectionate promise.
"Your physical stamina must be fully replenished before we attempt high-tier mana manipulation."
To ensure his stamina was met, Eluned immediately picked up a fresh silver fork, loaded it with a thick juicy slice of seasoned boar meat, and gently pressed it to his lips.
Silas didn’t argue... he opened his mouth and accepted the bite, chewing the rich savory meat.
Not to be outdone by even a fraction of a second, Morwenna instantly stabbed a massive piece of roasted tentacle with her own replacement fork and aggressively shoved it toward his face.
"Eat up, Captain," Morwenna instructed firmly, feeding him directly after Eluned.
As Silas chewed the spiced seafood, the Pirate Queen leaned across his chest, glaring right at the nature mage.
"And hold your horses, weed.
I am letting you teach him your nature tricks first today... but only if he proves he has actually mastered his water foundations enough to satisfy me.
If his fluid control is sloppy, I’m keeping him in the arena until his forms are clean."
"My Lord’s control is flawless, pirate," Eluned sniffed arrogantly, feeding Silas another slice of boar.
"He will pass your petty tests in moments, and then he will belong to the forest."

Silas simply sat between them, dutifully chewing and swallowing as the two SSS-Rank divine beings stuffed him full of protein with his mind already shifting into combat gear for the grueling hours ahead.
Ten minutes later, the meal was cleared, and the heavy wooden doors of the Mess Hall swung shut behind them.
Silas, Morwenna, and Eluned walked in focus across the open courtyard of the Blessed Land Citadel, heading directly toward the primary fortified structure.
While the exterior of the Keep looked like a traditional, massive medieval fortress built from white stone and timber, its true architectural value lay deep beneath the earth.
Because Silas had upgraded the Keep to a bona fide Tier 3 stronghold, the system had automatically expanded its underground footprint, carving out specialized facilities directly out of the bedrock.
’So in other words, I have an underground bat cave.’
They descended a long wide stone staircase that spiraled down past the living room as the air grew progressively cooler and denser with mana the deeper they went.
Finally, they stopped in front of a pair of massive, twelve-foot-tall double doors forged from reinforced mythril-alloy and dark obsidian, etched with glowing blue dampening runes.

The Citadel possessed a sprawling outdoor training ground next to it which was where him and Morwenna had first done the first style in the rain, but it also possessed this... a personal restricted training vault explicitly designed for Lords and high-tier Heroes to unleash destruction without leveling the living quarters above.
Up until today, Silas had been so continuously occupied with either handling the territory and more so he had never actually felt the need to step foot inside this subterranean vault.
Silas reached out, placing his palm against the runic plate in the center of the obsidian doors.
The array flashed golden as it read his Lord signature, and the heavy doors slid open with a smooth pressurized hiss.
A massive training ground came into view.
The vault was easily two hundred yards across and vaulted fifty feet high, supported by massive columns of reinforced self-healing runic masonry.

Along the upper edges of the walls, intricate arrays of mechanical and magical circulation vents steadily cycled fresh chilled air from the surface, creating a cool atmosphere that prevented the room from turning into a humid furnace during intense physical exertion.
The floor was paved with thick interlocking slabs of dark runic stone designed to absorb impact and automatically reconstruct themselves after taking structural damage.
Before Silas could even take a full step over the threshold, a blur of tattered leather and gray fabric rushed past him.
Morwenna practically sprinted into the room with her shoulder brushing against his chest with enough force to almost knock him off balance.

The Pirate Queen skidded to a halt ten yards into the vault, slowly turning in a full circle as her feral gray eyes swept across the massive high-ceilinged expanse, the reinforced pillars, and the high-tier elemental dampening wards.
"We had a room like this?!" Morwenna exclaimed with her jaw dropping slightly in genuine shock as she looked back at Silas.
"Are you kidding me, Captain?!
We could have taken advantage of this all this time!
Do you have any idea how many times I had to hold back my Tidal slashes out in the courtyard so I didn’t accidentally decapitate a squad of girls or blow the roof off Kaelia’s kitchen?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 222: Training Montage [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas let out a long sigh as he and Eluned stepped over the threshold with the heavy obsidian doors hissing shut and locking securely behind them.

"If you ever bothered to read the territory manifests I leave on the desk in my office instead of using the paper to clean your cutlass, Morwenna, you would have known it was down here..." Silas deadpanned, stretching his arms over his head until his shoulders popped.
"Reading is for bureaucrats and land-lubbers," Morwenna dismissed instantly with her eyes already gleaming with battle-lust as she paced across the stone tiles, testing their grip.
Silas ignored her, taking a deep breath of the crisp chilled air.

It was going to be an intense training montage today. He had six new elemental affinities waiting in his Lord inventory to be unlocked, but first, he had to satisfy the two strict taskmasters standing before him.
Eluned stepped close to his side, her pale hands reaching out to gently, affectionately take his right hand. Her emerald eyes looked up into his, overflowing with tender encouragement.

"You should not feel nervous, my Lord," Eluned told him softly, squeezing his calloused fingers. "The transition to Nature magic can feel foreign to a warrior accustomed to brute force, but I will be right here with you every step of the way... I will teach you as much as humanly possible, guiding your mana pathways until you become the absolute strongest you can be."
Silas smiled with a genuine warm emotion swelling in his chest.
Looking down at her beautiful, supportive face, he felt an overwhelming instinctive urge to pull his goddess close and press his lips to hers before the grueling work began.
He shifted his weight with his hand tightening around hers as he leaned his head down toward her lips—
WHACK!
A heavy projectile spun through the air and slammed violently against Silas’s bare chest, bouncing off his pectoral muscle with a sharp wooden crack.
Silas’s reflexes snapped into action.
His right hand released Eluned and shot out like a striking viper, snatching the spinning object out of the air mid-rebound before it could hit the floor.
He looked down at his hand.

It was a wooden practice sword. It was carved from heavy Ironwood which meant it was simply a training weapon designed to simulate the exact weight and balance of a true battle blade without the lethal cutting edge.
Silas lowered the wooden blade and looked across the arena.
Thirty yards away, Morwenna was standing with her feet planted wide, holding an identical Ironwood practice sword in her right hand.
Her feral gray eyes were narrowed into dangerous slits, and she was gritting her teeth so hard her jaw muscles bulged.

"Stop flirting!" Morwenna barked, pointing her wooden blade directly at his face. "This is a training room, not a honeymoon suite! And I already told you, weed... it doesn’t matter if he learned a few basic water tricks from some washed-up old crone in the desert! He doesn’t get to touch your nature spells until I sign off on his form!"
Morwenna dropped her center of gravity, shifting her weight into a flawless disciplined combat stance.
She raised the wooden blade, angling the tip exactly fifteen degrees to the right which was the universal unmistakable starting posture of her signature martial art.

"Come at me, Captain," Morwenna challenged him with her voice dropping into a thrilling bloodthirsty growl. "Show me the first style of the Tidal-Blade Arts that I taught you! Execute it cleanly against me right here, right now, or else I will not let you take a break by sitting around learning Nature magic!"
Silas grinned.
The warmth in his eyes vanished, instantly replaced by the golden-ringed focus of a predator entering the arena.
He let go of Eluned’s hand entirely, rolling his neck as he stepped forward onto the open stone tiles, leaving the nature goddess safely near the perimeter wards.
He gave the heavy Ironwood blade two rapid experimental practice swings with the dense wood whistling sharply as it cut through the chilled air.
"Alright," Silas agreed, settling into a loose athletic stance opposite his Pirate Queen.
He paused, tilting his head slightly. "Do we actually need to spar this time, Morwenna? Can’t I just execute the form against a target dummy?"
Silas was supremely confident in his ability to pull off the technique.
Ever since his Mythic Gold Core had stabilized his internal circulation, his understanding of fluid dynamics and leverage had skyrocketed.

The only reason he hadn’t spammed the technique continuously during the brutal meat grinder of the Secret Realm was simple efficiency... out in the desert, raw unga-bunga physical cleaves cost significantly less mental processing power than cycling heavy-water slashes while dodging glass artillery.
But he knew he had the mechanics locked down.
Morwenna didn’t even blink as her feral grin widened, displaying her sharp canines.

"Yes," Morwenna stated instantly, without a shred of hesitation. "In a full spar... A dummy doesn’t hit back, Captain. A dummy doesn’t test if your edge alignment holds when your wrists are vibrating from feedback so let’s see what you’re made of!"
The second the word left her mouth, the stone tile beneath Morwenna’s boots violently shattered.
BANG!
She didn’t give him a count of three and she didn’t wait for him to set his feet.
Morwenna exploded forward like a cannonball fired from a lower deck with her speed so terrifyingly unnatural that she left a vacuum wake in the chilled air of the vault.
She closed the thirty-yard gap in a fraction of a heartbeat, intent on taking her Lord completely off guard and putting him on the defensive before his mana could even cycle.

She appeared directly inside his guard with her Ironwood blade sweeping upward in a vicious diagonal slash aimed straight for his collarbone, carrying enough raw physical force to decapitate a siege beast.
But Silas wasn’t the same green Lord who had stumbled through his first lessons in the mud.

His golden-ringed eyes tracked the blur of her shoulder as his right foot slid back two inches, anchoring into the runic stone, and he twisted his hips, bringing his own wooden blade down in a crushing timed parry.
CRACK!
The collision of the two Ironwood blades sounded like a thunderclap echoing inside a sealed cave.

Even without sharp edges, the force of their clashing strength created a visible, concussive shockwave that rippled outward across the arena, blowing the dust off the floorboards and making Eluned’s hair whip wildly around her face at the perimeter.
"My Lord..."

Silas successfully parried the diagonal trajectory, preventing the wooden blade from taking his head off but while his technique was flawless, Morwenna’s power as a fully realized combatant were still a terrifying mountain to overcome.
The overwhelming kinetic torque behind her swing overpowered his leverage.
"Guh!" Silas grunted as his boots were violently ripped from the floor.
He was sent flying backward through the air like a fired projectile, soaring across twenty yards of open space directly toward the towering runic stone wall of the vault.
As he tumbled backward through the air, Silas didn’t panic.
His mind remained icy cold.
’This is good too...’

Instead of flailing or bracing for a bone-crushing collision with his spine, he rapidly angled his torso mid-flight, tucking his knees toward his chest and spinning his body so that he faced the approaching vertical wall.
THUD!
His heavy combat boots slammed square against the vertical runic masonry.

The impact was brutal with the force traveling up his calves and thighs, but he actively used the natural shock-absorption of his muscled legs like coiled springs, compressing his knees to completely arrest his backward momentum.
In that exact split-second of contact, Silas aggressively pumped a massive surge of Gold Core mana directly into the soles of his boots.
The golden mana flashed, creating a pressurized adhesive grip against the stone.
Instead of pushing off or falling back to the floor below, Silas pushed his legs straight and started sprinting horizontally across the vertical wall!
He ran along the masonry with amazing speed, his black sweatpants whipping around his legs with his Ironwood blade held low and ready as he orbited the arena twenty feet above the ground.
Down on the floor, Morwenna spun on her heel, her gray eyes locking onto his high-speed wall-running trajectory with glee.
"Nice footwork, Captain!" Morwenna roared, her free left hand snapping out toward him with her fingers spread wide. "Let’s see how you handle a broadside!"
She didn’t cast a slow incantation as she simply tapped into her innate oceanic affinity.
’I’m proud of you...’
VWOOSH! VWOOSH! VWOOSH! VWOOSH!
In the span of two heartbeats, Morwenna aggressively blasted a rapid-fire barrage of condensed high-velocity balls of dark blue water directly from her open palm.
The water bullets were compressed to the point of behaving like solid iron cannonballs with each one screaming through the chilled air toward Silas’s airborne silhouette at high speeds.
Silas’s golden eyes widened.
He accelerated his sprint along the vertical wall, his boots leaving glowing golden footprints on the stone as he desperately outran the incoming artillery.
BOOM! CRASH! SHATTER! BOOM!
The high-velocity water balls slammed into the wall inches behind his trailing heels.
The concussive impacts were so devastating that they blasted massive three-foot-wide craters directly into the reinforced runic masonry.
Stone fragments and pulverized dust sprayed violently into the air as the wall shook from the bombardment.
As soon as the water cannonballs detonated, the defensive arrays woven deep into the Keep’s architecture flared with bright gold light.
The smoking craters left behind by Morwenna’s attacks immediately hissed with the broken stone granules actively pulling themselves back together and healing the structural damage in real-time.
But Silas didn’t wait around to admire the self-healing walls.
Seeing three more compressed water balls predicting his path directly ahead, Silas violently halted his sprint.
He compressed his legs against the masonry one final time and aggressively jumped completely off the wall, launching himself back out into the open center of the arena.
WHOOSH!

The explosive force of his launch was so astronomical that his boots left massive web-like spider-crack fractures spreading six feet wide across the vertical stone before the healing arrays could even begin to register the trauma.
He soared through the air, thirty feet above the arena floor with his body unsupported by gravity.
Down below, Morwenna’s eyes flashed red.

She tracked his airborne arc, her wooden sword lowering as she pulled back her left hand, gathering a massive swirling vortex of pressurized water in her palm that was three times larger than the previous projectiles.
"You’re completely open in the air, Captain!" Morwenna called out triumphantly, launching the massive water cannonball directly upward at his exposed midsection. "Take the hit!"
The massive sphere of dark blue water shot toward the ceiling like a rising meteor, entirely unavoidable.
Silas, suspended mid-air, didn’t flinch as a grin crossed his face.
’Open?’ Silas thought, his Gold Core roaring to life inside his chest. ’Not even close.’
Instead of trying to contort his body out of the path of the massive projectile, Silas aggressively extended his left hand downward, pointing his open palm directly at the incoming sphere of water.
He instantly seized uncompromising control over the spell itself!
Because he had spent days practicing under Mia and analyzing fluid dynamics, his Gold Core effortlessly invaded the structure of Morwenna’s spell.
In a single reality-defying second, Silas aggressively forced his mana into the liquid and triggered a instantaneous Ice Transformation!
KRACK-KRA-KRA-SHATTER!
The massive, rushing sphere of dark blue water violently froze solid mid-flight, instantly converting from liquid energy into an absolute-zero boulder of solid glacial ice mere yards below his boots!
And Silas didn’t stop there.

The exact moment the liquid solidified into ice, Silas aggressively manipulated the elemental properties of the mass, forcefully applying a gravity manipulation by increasing its density and weight tenfold!
The physics of the attack completely inverted.

Instead of continuing its upward trajectory to smash into Silas, the frozen glacial boulder suddenly became thousands of pounds heavier than its momentum could support as the momentum was instantly canceled out.
WHOOSH CRASH!

The massive ice boulder violently plummeted straight back downward toward the floor like a dropped anvil, completely missing Silas and crashing harmlessly onto the stone tiles below with a deafening shatter that sent fragments of ice flying across the arena.
A few smaller, stray secondary water bullets Morwenna had fired in tandem still shot past the falling ice, screaming toward his shoulders.
Silas smoothly twisted his torso mid-air, effortlessly dodging the stray projectiles by mere inches, letting the high-velocity water harmlessly part his damp dark hair.
As gravity finally reclaimed him, Silas descended rapidly toward the floor with his heavy Ironwood blade raised high above his head with both hands.
’Oh wow... Such quick thinking, it’s making me wet.’ Morwenna thought.
It had been a while since her Captain touched her and she craved for his touch, however she blinked, Morwenna didn’t retreat from the falling anvil or the descending Lord.
Her gray eyes lit up with pride and excitement at his elemental counter as she lifted their practice sword, planting her boots wide, and swung upward to meet his descent.
CLANG-CRACK-BZZZZZT!
They clashed once again in the dead center of the arena floor.

He compressed his legs against the masonry one final time and aggressively jumped completely off the wall, launching himself back out into the open center of the arena.
WHOOSH!

The explosive force of his launch was so astronomical that his boots left massive web-like spider-crack fractures spreading six feet wide across the vertical stone before the healing arrays could even begin to register the trauma.
He soared through the air, thirty feet above the arena floor with his body unsupported by gravity.
Down below, Morwenna’s eyes flashed red.

She tracked his airborne arc, her wooden sword lowering as she pulled back her left hand, gathering a massive swirling vortex of pressurized water in her palm that was three times larger than the previous projectiles.
"You’re completely open in the air, Captain!" Morwenna called out triumphantly, launching the massive water cannonball directly upward at his exposed midsection.
"Take the hit!"
The massive sphere of dark blue water shot toward the ceiling like a rising meteor, entirely unavoidable.
Silas, suspended mid-air, didn’t flinch as a grin crossed his face.
’Open?’ Silas thought, his Gold Core roaring to life inside his chest. ’Not even close.’
Instead of trying to contort his body out of the path of the massive projectile, Silas aggressively extended his left hand downward, pointing his open palm directly at the incoming sphere of water.
He instantly seized uncompromising control over the spell itself!
Because he had spent days practicing under Mia and analyzing fluid dynamics, his Gold Core effortlessly invaded the structure of Morwenna’s spell.
In a single reality-defying second, Silas aggressively forced his mana into the liquid and triggered a instantaneous Ice Transformation!
KRACK-KRA-KRA-SHATTER!
The massive, rushing sphere of dark blue water violently froze solid mid-flight, instantly converting from liquid energy into an absolute-zero boulder of solid glacial ice mere yards below his boots!
And Silas didn’t stop there.

The exact moment the liquid solidified into ice, Silas aggressively manipulated the elemental properties of the mass, forcefully applying a gravity manipulation by increasing its density and weight tenfold!
The physics of the attack completely inverted.

Instead of continuing its upward trajectory to smash into Silas, the frozen glacial boulder suddenly became thousands of pounds heavier than its momentum could support as the momentum was instantly canceled out.
WHOOSH CRASH!

The massive ice boulder violently plummeted straight back downward toward the floor like a dropped anvil, completely missing Silas and crashing harmlessly onto the stone tiles below with a deafening shatter that sent fragments of ice flying across the arena.
A few smaller, stray secondary water bullets Morwenna had fired in tandem still shot past the falling ice, screaming toward his shoulders.
Silas smoothly twisted his torso mid-air, effortlessly dodging the stray projectiles by mere inches, letting the high-velocity water harmlessly part his damp dark hair.
As gravity finally reclaimed him, Silas descended rapidly toward the floor with his heavy Ironwood blade raised high above his head with both hands.
’Oh wow...
Such quick thinking, it’s making me wet.’ Morwenna thought.
It had been a while since her Captain touched her and she craved for his touch, however she blinked, Morwenna didn’t retreat from the falling anvil or the descending Lord.
Her gray eyes lit up with pride and excitement at his elemental counter as she lifted their practice sword, planting her boots wide, and swung upward to meet his descent.
CLANG-CRACK-BZZZZZT!
They clashed once again in the dead center of the arena floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 223: Training Montage [II/Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The impact was so immense that actual sparks of golden and deep-blue mana friction violently erupted from the point of contact between the two wooden blades.
BOOOOM!
The air pressure between them violently compressed, generating a windstorm that pushed the shattered ice fragments away in a wide circle.
Silas pressed down with all his weight with his muscles bulging as he tried to force her to her knees.
Morwenna held her ground with her boots grinding into the runic stone as she looked up at him across the vibrating wooden crossguards, the wide grin still on her face.

"Brilliant elemental conversion, Captain!" Morwenna commented loudly over the screech of grinding mana armor, genuinely impressed by his battle smarts. "Using ice transformation to kill the momentum of a water spell mid-flight? Your combat IQ is getting scary!"
"I learn from the best..." Silas grunted, his arms trembling as he tried to find a leverage angle.
"You sure do!" Morwenna laughed bared-toothed. "But smarts alone won’t win a blade lock against an oceanic ocean!"
Morwenna’s biceps violently bulged beneath her coat as she didn’t use a spell but instead she simply flexed her overwhelming physical strength to its absolute limit.
With a guttural roar, she violently twisted her wrists, redirecting his downward force, and aggressively shoved upward with a massive burst of raw power.
BAM!
Silas’s guard was completely blown wide open.

The physical torque sent him flying violently in the exact opposite direction across the arena with his boots skidding and bouncing over the stone tiles as he was forcefully ejected from the center of the room.

As Silas was rushing backward, trying to dig his heels into the floor to arrest his momentum, he gritted his teeth, keeping his right hand locked tightly around the leather grip of his practice sword.

’Damn it...’ Silas cursed in his thoughts, his eyes darting across her posture as he finally slid to a halt twenty yards away with his chest heaving. ’I can’t seem to get a clean opening... Every time I try to set my feet for a Tide-Blade sweep, she closes the distance or overpowers my guard with brute force. Her defense is completely airtight.’
It was overwhelmingly clear to Silas that Morwenna wanted to keep this high-speed intense combat exchange going for as long as humanly possible.
He could tell that much from the wild and thoroughly ecstatic grin plastered across her face as she slowly paced in a circle, waiting for him to catch his breath.
Across the arena, as Morwenna watched Silas adjust his grip and lower his stance, her wide grin slightly faltered.
A brief sudden flash of self-consciousness flickered through her feral gray eyes.
’Did Captain realize?’ Morwenna thought, biting her lower lip for a fraction of a second as she gripped her wooden hilt. ’Did he figure out what I’m actually doing?’
Morwenna’s overarching training plan for the afternoon had been quite simple and born out of affectionate greed.

By utilizing the legitimate guise of a rigorous spar, she was intentionally going to hold on and drag the combat out for as long as possible, effectively monopolizing his time and making the entire training session solely about them and their martial bond!
She wanted to push him until his muscles burned and his instincts were razor-sharp.

Her secret lesson plan dictated that once she had completely exhausted his standard offensive options and watched him repeatedly fail to breach her guard, she would formally call for him to stop trying to force an opening through brute strength.

Then, right there in the center of the vault, while he was panting and focused on her, she was going to step close and personally teach him the Second Style of the Tide-Blade Arts... a specialized and fluid technique explicitly designed to help a swordsman find dynamic balance, manipulate an opponent’s center of gravity, and actively break openings into airtight defenses where none previously existed.
It was the next step in his evolution, and she wanted to be the only one to give it to him!
But Silas was not a man who waited around for lessons to be handed to him on a silver platter.
Silas let out a long sigh with his breath clouding slightly in the chilled air of the vault as he looked at her pacing form.

’If I can’t find an opening on the ground where her leverage is absolute,’ Silas thought with his grip tightening until the leather wrap of his hilt groaned, ’then I’ll just have to generate my own opening from an angle where she can’t anchor her weight.’
This was what it meant to be strong... He didn’t want to completely rely on his Heroes, Silas wanted to think for himself too.
’I want to rely on them but at the same time... I want them to be able to rely on me too.’ Silas thought.

Without warning, Silas compressed his leg muscles and exploded straight upward into the air, launching himself twenty feet above the stone floor in a high leaping parabolic arc directly toward her position.
Morwenna looked up, raising her wooden sword to prepare for another aerial clash, assuming he was attempting the same descending strike as before.
She was wrong.
As Silas reached the apex of his leap, his body suspended mid-air, he actively closed his eyes for a fraction of a second.

He engaged the foundational breathing techniques she had drilled into him in the freezing rain a while ago as he drew the abundant chilled atmospheric moisture of the vault directly into his internal circuits, cycling the water mana rapidly through his Gold Core until his veins felt like roaring rivers.
He opened his glowing golden eyes and he angled his Ironwood practice blade exactly fifteen degrees to the right, aligning the blunt wooden edge with the atmospheric pressure of the room.
Even entirely unsupported by gravity in mid-air, Silas flawlessly dropped his internal center of gravity, violently pivoting his hips and twisting his torso with tremendous coiled rotational torque!
He gathered the entirety of his circulating water mana directly into the iron-dense wood of his blade.
He was performing the First Style of the Tide-Blade Arts: Severing Horizon... not from a grounded stance, but completely mid-air!
"TAKE THIS!" Silas roared at the top of his lungs, releasing the coiled rotational torque in a devastating high-speed horizontal slash directly at her airborne silhouette from twenty feet away!
VWOOOOOOOOOSH!
A blinding explosion of pressurized deep-blue phantom heavy-water violently erupted from the blunt edge of his wooden sword!

Because Morwenna had been so deeply lost in her own affectionate, possessive internal thoughts regarding her secret lesson plan and their bond, her defensive instincts were delayed by a single fatal microsecond.
And that microsecond was all that Silas needed...
She was caught entirely off guard by the terrifying density, speed, and rotational of the airborne strike!
The massive crescent-shaped arc of golden-tinted sea mana screamed through the air, expanding to thirty feet wide as it tore across the vault, entirely consuming the space between them.
"What?!" Morwenna gasped, her eyes going wide as she hurriedly brought her Ironwood blade up horizontally, channeling her own oceanic mana to form a hasty defensive guard.
KA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The phantom heavy-water arc slammed directly into Morwenna’s guard with the force of a breaking tsunami or something similar.
What immediately followed was a massive explosion of pressurized water and spray that completely engulfed the entire right side of the training arena.
Gallons of phantom sea mana detonated outward, washing over the stone floor, shattering the remaining ice boulders into fine mist, and sending a concussive shockwave echoing off the vaulted ceilings.

Silas smoothly completed his aerial rotation, falling through the dispersing mist and landing flawlessly on his heavy combat boots with his Ironwood blade held out to his side as he slid two yards across the wet stone tiles before coming to a complete halt.
When the dense curtain of water mist finally cleared, the destructive power of the strike was revealed.
Morwenna had been violently sent flying backward across the entire length of the arena.
Her boots had skidded over fifty feet across the stone tiles before her body was forcefully slammed directly into the reinforced runic masonry of the far wall!
CRACK!
The physical impact of her body hitting the wall was so intense that it left a massive spider-webbing crack directly in the stone masonry behind her shoulders.
The defensive arrays immediately flashed gold, the stone grinding and hissing as it slowly began to push itself back together to repair the damage left by the Pirate Queen’s impact.
Morwenna stood frozen against the cracking wall.
Her tattered captain’s coat was completely, thoroughly drenched in dripping water.
Her hair was plastered to her face, and water dripped steadily from the tip of her Ironwood practice sword onto the floor.
She blinked her feral gray eyes once.
Twice.
She looked down at her drenched clothes, then looked across the fifty yards of destroyed, water-soaked arena at Silas, who was standing tall and breathing heavily.
The shock on her face vanished, instantly replaced by an expression of absolute, overwhelming, heart-melting Warlord pride.
"Captain..." Morwenna breathed out, her voice trembling slightly with awe. "...you really mastered it. An aerial Severing Horizon with full heavy-water conversion... That was incredible!"
Silas stood his ground, taking a deep, ragged breath to calm his racing Gold Core.
He opened his mouth to reply, wiping a splash of water from his own cheek—
But Morwenna had already moved.
She didn’t run... she simply ignored distance entirely. In a single, blinding flash of gray speed, she closed the fifty-yard gap before Silas could even take his second breath.

Before he could raise his wooden blade or defend himself, Morwenna lunged forward, dropped her wooden sword to the floor with a clatter, and aggressively threw both of her incredibly strong arms completely around his waist.
With zero effort, utilizing her terrifying physical supremacy, she lifted Silas’s massive towering two-hundred-pound frame completely off the ground!

"I am so incredibly proud of you!" Morwenna shouted joyously, spinning him around in a circle in the middle of the wet arena, pressing her face tightly against his bare sweating chest. "That was so clean! The edge alignment was absolute perfection! Now it’s officially time for us to learn the rest of the styles! Before you even know it, you’re going to be a Grandmaster of Swordsmanship just like me! We’re going to conquer every sea in the realm together!"
She was so happy, so wildly intoxicated by his progress and their shared bond, that her affection became suffocating.
"Mmmm~ Captain~ We need to celebrate. Come touch me all you want!"

"Morwenna... you’re crushing my ribs again!" Silas wheezed out, his bare feet dangling six inches off the floor as he patted her wet shoulder. "Thank you! Seriously, thank you, but please let go! I need to breathe!"
Instead of releasing him, Morwenna’s eyes glowed with affection, and she actively squeezed him even harder against her drenched coat, refusing to surrender her prize.
"Never! You’re my apprentice! You stay right here!"
From the perimeter of the arena, where she had been patiently watching the entire destructive martial display unfold, Eluned finally stepped forward.
Her emerald-green eyes narrowed as she looked at the drenched pirate monopolizing her Lord.
"That is quite enough, you insatiable bilge-rat..." Eluned announced.
She raised her pale hands and clapped them together with a sharp smack.
RUMBLE-CRACK-SWISH!
The solid runic stone tiles directly beneath Morwenna’s boots violently buckled and fractured.
From deep within the earth below the Keep, a dozen thick living emerald-green roots aggressively erupted from the stone.

The roots moved like striking serpents, wrapping tightly around Morwenna’s ankles, calves, and waist, forcefully anchoring the Pirate Queen to the floor and gently but firmly prying her crushing embrace off Silas’s body.
Silas dropped back down to the floor, landing safely on his feet and taking a massive gulp of air as he stepped out of the root-encircled drop zone.
"Hey! What is the meaning of this, weed?!" Morwenna snarled, glaring at the nature mage as she was physically restrained by the thick, living timber.

"Your allotted combat time has officially expired, pirate," Eluned declared haughtily, walking gracefully across the wet stone floor toward them with her chin lifted in triumph. "You stated yourself that once he proved his mastery over water, he would be mine and he has clearly exceeded your brutal tests. Well... now it is officially my turn to teach My Love Nature magic."

Morwenna gritted her teeth, her gray eyes flashing dangerously. Her right hand twitched toward her hilt as she could easily summon her abyssal aura and violently slice the thick wooden roots to pieces in a fraction of a second to free herself.
But she didn’t.

Instead, Morwenna let out an annoyed huff and began smoothly wriggling, twisting, and tangling her way out of the root constriction through pure bodily contortion and flexibility, carefully pulling her limbs free one by one without breaking the wood.
