chapters.title: Chapter 224: Training Montage [III]
paragraphs: She did this for one very practical reason: Eluned absolutely hated it when anyone violently ripped apart or sliced her living roots.
If Morwenna destroyed the plants, the nature Goddess would go feral and they would end up in a magic duel that would ruin the rest of Silas’s afternoon.

"Fine! Take him!" Morwenna grumbled, successfully untangling herself from the last root and stepping back, wringing the water out of her hair. "But don’t break him with your weird flower chants, weed! He’s a swordsman!"
Eluned completely ignored the pirate’s heckling.
She stepped directly up to Silas with her emerald eyes softening into pools of liquid warmth as she looked up at his sweating bare-chested frame.
She reached out, gently smoothing down the waistband of his sweatpants and placing her palm tenderly against his beating heart.

"My Love," Eluned spoke softly. "You are officially going to be learning Nature magic today... Because your Gold Core is so incredibly pure, and because you possess such a deep protective instinct over your territory, you possess an astronomical potential for it."
She paused, biting her lower lip slightly with a sudden uncharacteristic shyness flickering across her usually arrogant features.
Her cheeks flushed a delicate shade of pink.

"However..." Eluned murmured, looking down at his chest for a second before meeting his golden eyes again. "...I actually possess a way for you to reach a high point of mastery at using Nature magic as soon as humanly possible. A shortcut that would bypass months of basic meditation."
Silas raised an eyebrow, his Warlord efficiency instincts instantly piqued.
A shortcut to master one of his eight required elemental affinities? That was exactly what he needed...
"What way?" Silas asked curiously, leaning in slightly.
Eluned’s blush deepened until her ears turned completely red. She stammered with her regal composure faltering under his intense gaze.
"D-Dual Cultivation," Eluned stuttered out, the words barely louder than a whisper.
Silas blinked, caught entirely off guard.
"Dual Cultivation?" Silas repeated.

"Y-Yes," Eluned explained hurriedly, her hands fidgeting against his chest. "I... I have obviously never done it before in my entire immortal existence, my Lord. My core has remained entirely untouched but... if you and I were to intimately intertwine our physical bodies and merge our bodies together in synchronization... the exchange of pure elemental energy would deeply enrich your mana core! Your foundational understanding and mastery over the natural realm would increase exponentially overnight!"
Before Silas could even process the very tempting implications of dual cultivating with an SSS-Rank nature goddess to level up his core, a loud obnoxious bark of laughter echoed across the arena.

"HA!" Morwenna yelled from ten yards away, pointing a mocking finger directly at the blushing nature Goddess. "Dual cultivation?! Are you kidding me right now?! That is literally just sex, you hypocrite! Stop trying to dress it up in fancy academic terminology! You are literally just horny and want to jump the Captain’s bones!"
Silas looked down at Eluned, fully expecting the arrogant nature goddess to fiercely deny the accusation or threaten to bury the pirate in a forest of thorns but she didn’t.
Eluned didn’t deny it even a single fraction of a percent.
Instead, she simply lifted her chin with her face burning crimson, and cleared her throat loudly with a dignified ahem, entirely refusing to look Morwenna in the eye.

"Just... keep it in your thoughts for later tonight, my Love," Eluned told Silas softly, giving his chest a possessive little pat before taking a step back to create a teaching perimeter. "Let us focus strictly on your foundational elemental magic for now."
Silas let out a breath he didn’t realize he was holding with a wry smirk crossing his face.
’This territory is going to be the death of me,’ he thought, shaking his head as he focused his golden eyes on her hands.
"Alright," Silas said, setting his stance. "What is the first step?"

"The first foundational spell I will be teaching you today is Nature Transformation," Eluned lectured him, her posture straightening as she slipped seamlessly into her role as a divine mentor. "You must understand something vital, Silas. For Nature magic... unlike Pyromancy, Electromancy, or all other standard forms of destructive, mathematical magic... you absolutely do not really need to rely on rigid, phonetic incantations or complex runic chants."
She spread her pale arms wide with her palms facing the stone floor of the vault.

"Nature is not a weapon you force into submission through calculations," Eluned explained, her voice echoing softly off the self-healing masonry. "It is a living, breathing resonance. As long as you possess a completely pure heart, an unwavering protective intent, and a genuine love for the natural world and those who embody it... it will—"
The moment the words left her lips, Eluned’s SSS-Rank nature aura gently, breathtakingly bloomed outward from her bare feet.
It didn’t explode with power like Morwenna’s water or Thor’s lightning. It pulsed with a warm, brilliant, golden-green light that silently washed over the entire two-hundred-yard vault.
Where the light touched, miracles occurred.

The cold hard interlocking runic stone tiles of the floor were instantly, seamlessly covered in a thick and lush soft blanket of emerald-green grass. The grass spread at terrifying speed, climbing up the bases of the reinforced masonry pillars and scaling the self-healing walls.
Within seconds, thousands of vibrant, breathtaking wildflowers... crimson roses, deep blue orchids, golden lilies, and glowing white star-blossoms sprouted aggressively from the newly formed turf.
The chilled air of the underground training ground was instantly transformed, filled with the intoxicating fragrant aroma of fresh soil, morning dew, and blooming summer flowers.

In less than three heartbeats, the brutal training vault had been entirely, miraculously transformed into a breathtaking paradisiacal green garden that looked like a slice of heaven carved out of the underworld.
Even Morwenna stopped her pacing with her feral gray eyes wide with quiet awe as she looked down at the soft green grass and wildflowers tickling the tops of her leather combat boots.
In the center of the miraculous garden, surrounded by glowing motes of floating pollen and soft golden light, Eluned gracefully dropped to one knee.
She reached down into the lush turf and gently, reverently picked a single, perfectly formed, luminescent white flower by its stem.
She stood back up with her emerald eyes locked entirely onto Silas’s golden-ringed pupils with an expression of pure devotion.
"I love that look on your face..."
She took a slow step forward, stopping mere inches from his bare chest. Eluned then lifted the luminescent white flower directly to her lips.
With a gentle, tender breath, Eluned blew across the blossom.

The glowing white petals detached from the stem, scattering into the air and floating softly, beautifully directly across Silas’s sharp face, brushing against his cheeks and leaving a tingling trail of pure, life-giving nature mana that instantly sank into his Gold Core, causing his internal circuits to hum with vibrant new warmth.

Looking up into his eyes through the scattering shower of glowing white petals, Eluned smiled... a soft breathtaking expression that completely stripped away every ounce of her usual arrogance that she kept for Morwenna, leaving only the goddess who had loved her Lord.
"-Be alright, so as long as you love me my Lord, you will be able to perform Nature Magic as much as you can."
"As much as I love you?" Silas asked with his voice steady against the cool quiet stone of the underground training hall.
Eluned nodded without a single instant of hesitation.
Her emerald eyes shone like polished jewels in the soft ambient light of the room.

"The foundational principle of Nature Transformation was created in the dawn of the realms to spread life, warmth, and joy wherever its roots touched," Eluned explained softly, her voice carrying a sweet melodious tone that resonated with the environment. "In that golden era, when the first green shoot pushed through the barren stone of creation, it was meant to nurture every living soul without condition and regardless of what mortals, beasts, or other civilizations have done to the earth over the centuries... the fires they set, the forests they cleared, the iron they drove deep into the soil... Nature itself never holds hatred for them. It does not harbor spite. It simply continues to give, enduring all wounds to offer sustenance again and again."
During her inspirational explanation, Eluned raised her pale left hand.
A slender, emerald-green vine coiled gracefully around her wrist like a living bracelet, sprouting two vibrant leaves.
From those leaves, two round, bright red apples materialized, swelling to their full, plump maturity in a matter of seconds.
It was a charming technique she had picked up from the Earth Gardening guidebook Silas had bought for her back at the time he went back to Valoria.
She snapped the stems with a soft click and handed one apple to Silas and the other to Morwenna.
Morwenna raised a skeptical eyebrow, examining the smooth, polished skin of the fruit before taking a large unceremonious bite.
A crisp crunch echoed across the stone floor as sweet juice dripped down her chin.

"Damn~" the pirate queen muttered, wiping her mouth with the back of her sleeve and staring at the fruit with new respect. "That’s surprisingly sweet. It’s far better than the salted rations we used to keep in the ship’s hold."
Silas took a bite of his own apple, savoring the rich, refreshing flavor that burst across his tongue.
"Really sweet. Good job, Elu. You’ve been reading that book."
Eluned beamed at his praise, lifting her chin proudly before continuing her lesson.

"Now, for the fundamental basics of the magic itself. Nature magic responds directly to visualization and emotional intent... You must not try to force your mana through the ground like a battering ram or calculate it like an alchemical formula."
With a delicate sweep of her fingers, Eluned retracted the flower field she had demonstrated earlier.
The lush green grass and vibrant blossoms dissolved into motes of sparkling emerald dust, leaving the cold dark runic stone floor bare once again.
She stepped back, gesturing with an open palm for Silas to take her position in the center of the vault.

"Before your hand touches the ground, you must first gather the nature energy," Eluned educated him firmly, her green eyes locked onto his face. "Feel the wild, untamed life force drifting in the air around us. Do not rush. Draw it steadily into your core, let it merge completely with your own aura, and then release it into the stone all at once. And remember, my Love... because I created Nature Transformation myself, as long as you love me, the magic will answer your call without restriction."
Silas took three slow measured breaths to center his mind.
He closed his eyes, shutting out the distractions of the room and focusing on his internal circulation.
He could feel the atmospheric energy drifting through the subterranean vault... it was cool and rich with unrefined natural power brought down by the circulation vents from the land above.
He opened his golden-ringed eyes and began drawing that green energy drifting through the room directly into his chest.
He pulled it inward, condensing the atmospheric power inside his Gold Core alongside his own aura, building the internal pressure until his veins thrummed with a warm vibrant feeling.
’I need to do this... I love Elu... It shouldn’t be that hard to be honest.’
He crouched low, moving his right hand toward the cold floor tiles.
Eluned watched his posture attentively with her hands clasped tightly against her chest.

’I already know my Love loves me...’ She thought, a gentle warmth blooming throughout her spirit. ’I can feel his sincere devotion every single time his eyes meet mine but when that bond is converted directly into nature energy, how vast will his output be?’
Silas placed his calloused palm flat onto the stone floor, releasing the gathered energy all at once.
"Nature Transformation!"
A blinding wave of emerald-and-gold light erupted from beneath his palm!
It was not a small patch of grass and it was not a modest garden...
The spell exploded outward in a sweeping, unstoppable tide of life that covered the entire two-hundred-yard vault in a heartbeat!
Thick, impossibly soft green turf blanketed every inch of the stone floor.
Towering ancient trees, thick as siege columns, burst upward through the bedrock with a deafening rumble.
Their trunks expanded rapidly, their bark thickening as their branches spread wide, reaching fifty feet into the air to brush against the ceiling.
Vines surged up the support pillars, climbing all the way to the roof and weaving together to form a dense canopy brimming with glowing moss, hanging orchids, and pale white star-blossoms.
The woodland Silas created was easily twice as large and dense as the garden Eluned had demonstrated just moments prior.
It transformed the austere underground training bunker into a primeval forest that reached all the way to the vaulted stone roof!
Eluned let out a delighted gasp. She began hopping up and down on her bare feet, her hands clapping together in pure joy.

"I knew it! I knew it!" Eluned cheered, her face glowing with immense pride as she twirled among the wildflowers. "My Lord simply loves me too much! Look at how vast this forest is! The canopy is breathtaking!"

chapters.title: Chapter 225: Training Montage [IV]
paragraphs: Morwenna stood near the base of an enormous oak tree, looking up at the thick branches blocking the overhead arc lights.
She crossed her arms over her tattered captain’s coat, letting out a dismissive huff. "Yay. So what? He made a bunch of tall wood.... Big deal. Show-off."
Just as the pirate queen spoke, a thick leafy shrub grew right beside her boots. A cluster of bright, round, orange-colored fruits sprouted from its branches, bobbing gently against her hip.
Morwenna blinked, reaching out to pluck one of the round fruits, turning it over in her palm with a suspicious scowl.
"What kind of fruit is this supposed to be? It’s not an apple."
In the center of the clearing, Silas let out a long breath and lifted his palm from the stone.

Maintaining active spell pressure at that scale was exhausting for his current elemental conduits, but even after he broke physical contact, the grand forest remained standing, looking very firm and vibrant.
Silas couldn’t hold active control for long, but the abundant life energy he had summoned stayed rooted in the earth, leaving the woodland completely intact.
Eluned walked gracefully over to Silas with her eyes sparkling like emeralds.
"For your very first time executing Nature Transformation, this is simply too good! Your natural affinity for the earth is exceptional, my Love! In fact..."
She paused, sensing the refined elemental energy lingering within his core conduits, and gasped. "You have already reached Adept mastery in a single attempt!"
Silas blinked, wiping a bead of sweat from his brow with his forearm. "So quick?"

"Naturally!" Eluned affirmed, stepping close and cupping his sharp jaw with her warm palm. "Even if I am no longer seated on my throne as the main Goddess of the World Tree, I was once a proper deity. And because I love you and you love me, your talent receives the full backing of my ancient authority. It is only natural that you would advance this fast!"
Silas looked down at her radiant, gorgeous face, hearing her earnest devoted words. "Elu..."
Looking at that beautiful smile lighting up her features, Silas felt a fierce protective instinct swell inside his chest.
He wanted to keep that smile right there no matter what trials or rivals threatened their territory in the future.
Eluned turned around, laughing like a ringing bell as she patted the rough bark of the oak tree Silas had grown.
"Look at them! Nature has a spirit of its own, my Lord. Come, play with the trees for a moment! Feel their resonance!"
Silas joined her beneath the verdant canopy, watching as the living branches responded gently to their presence, swaying in a non-existent breeze as if bowing to greet their creator.
Even Morwenna, despite her grumpy scowling and folded arms, ended up trailing along behind them.

The pirate queen stood beneath a sweeping weeping willow, and to her utter surprise, the thin supple branches reached down and began gently weaving through her messy gray hair, acting like natural combs to untangle the sea-salt knots and straighten her unruly locks with delicate precision.

"Tch," Morwenna grumbled, though she didn’t pull away with her shoulders relaxing as she secretly enjoyed the woodland pampering. "What a useful tree~ Elara could have learned a thing or two from you..."
A moment later, Morwenna walked over to where Silas and Eluned were standing, still holding the round orange fruit in her hand.
"Hey, weed. What is this thing anyway? Can you eat it like the apple?"
"That is called an orange, pirate," Eluned explained with patient grace.
She took the fruit from Morwenna’s hands and used her thumbnail to split the thick outer skin, expertly peeling away the bitter rind to reveal the bright, juicy segments inside.
Eluned separated a single segment and popped it directly into Morwenna’s mouth.
Morwenna chewed once, and her gray eyes instantly went wide.
The sweet tangy flavor burst across her tastebuds with a refreshing zest she had never experienced on the open ocean.

In a flash, the tough pirate queen transformed into an orange glutton. She marched right back over to the shrub Silas had grown, plucking three more oranges and attempting to bite directly into them, rind and all.
"Wait, don’t eat the peel," Silas chuckled, walking over and grabbing her wrist before she could take a bite. "It’s bitterso watch how she did it."
Both Silas and Eluned spent the next ten minutes showing Morwenna how to properly peel an orange without getting sticky juice all over her sleeves and coat.
Eluned even used a gentle pulse of nature energy to compress several oranges above a hollowed-out wooden cup she formed from a root, creating fresh, chilled orange juice on the spot.
Morwenna drank the entire cup in one long continuous gulp, letting out a deeply satisfied breath as she wiped her mouth.
"Holy sweet mother of the sea... that orange juice is incredible! Captain, grow ten more of these orange bushes right now! We need these on the supply wagons!"
"We’re here to train, Morwenna, not start a commercial fruit farm," Silas laughed, shaking his head at her newfound addiction.
Once they were all rested and the lighthearted atmosphere settled, Eluned stepped into the center of the forest clearing.
"Now that you have mastered the foundational art of growth and life," Eluned announced. "I will teach you the next essential concept. Nature energy can also be used for attacking as well."
Silas straightened his broad posture, his attention instantly sharpening as he rolled his shoulders.
"An attack spell?"

"Precisely," Eluned nodded, her green eyes serious. "The spell is called Sylvan Spear. You must gather the nature energy slumbering within the earth, compress its fibers until the wood becomes as rigid as dark steel, and launch it forward like a thrown javelin."
She demonstrated the concept without a word of chant.
With a simple flick of her pale fingers, the grass beneath her feet stirred.

A six-foot-long, razor-sharp spike of petrified, dark ironwood erupted from the dirt at startling velocity, sailing across the clearing and burying itself halfway into a distant stone support pillar with a resounding sound.
THUD!
"You try, my Love," Eluned encouraged him, stepping back to give him room.
Silas closed his eyes, drawing upon his newfound Adept Nature mastery.
He pictured the dense compacted structure of petrified timber. He channeled his Gold Core mana, sending a commanding pulse down through his boots and directly into the turf below.
CRACK!
A five-foot spike of hardened, dark wood erupted from the floor five yards away, shooting forward across the room and shattering a stone target dummy into a cloud of gray fragments.
"Flawless execution!" Eluned praised, her eyes flashing with sudden battle intent. "Now... let us test your application in a real combat spar! Defend your ground!"
Before Silas could even formulate a reply, Eluned’s gentle nurturing aura changed completely.
BOOM!
The entire forest vibrated as Eluned unleashed a fraction of her true SSS-Rank nature authority.

The ground groaned beneath their feet, and dozens of thick, petrified wooden spears erupted from the dirt around her, hovering in mid-air like an array of siege ballista bolts pointing straight at his chest.
"Defend yourself, my Lord!" Eluned called out, sweeping her hand forward and sending the entire volley of wooden spears screaming toward him at breakneck speed!
Silas’s reflexes kicked in instantly.
He drew his Ironwood practice sword from his side, coating the blunt blade in a swirling layer of pressurized water and ice to enhance its impact, and charged straight into the incoming volley!
CLANG! CRASH! SHATTER!
Silas wove through the incoming barrage with his practice blade a blur of motion as he parried three wooden spears mid-flight, turning their rigid tips into splinters of harmless bark.
He closed the thirty-yard distance rapidly, pivoting on his heel and executing a sweeping horizontal cut aimed at her midsection.
Eluned didn’t back down or retreat.

She simply raised her open palm, and a thick barrier of tangled, iron-hard roots burst upward from the floor tiles, absorbing his sword strike with a hollow echoing thud that vibrated up Silas’s forearms.
’These women... really are amazing and I can tell they’re holding back.’
Silas kept up with her pace at first, using his physical agility to bound off the trunks of the living trees he had created, maneuvering around her defenses with fluid leaps.
While airborne, he gathered nature mana into his left hand and fired two Sylvan Spears of his own. The wooden projectiles whistled through the air, curving slightly to target her exposed flanks.
Eluned smiled warmly with her movements light as a falling leaf riding a summer breeze.
"Nice!" She side-stepped his spears with effortless grace, her body blurring as she bypassed his line of sight entirely, merging with the greenery around her.

Before Silas could track her trajectory upon landing, thick, living vines rose from the turf like striking serpents, wrapping tightly around his ankles and pulling his feet straight out from under him!
"Whoa...! Not again!" Silas grunted, hitting the soft turf floor on his chest with a heavy thud, his sword clattering a few feet away.
Before he could push himself back up onto his hands and knees, Eluned landed gracefully on top of him and sat directly on his upper back, using his broad, muscled shoulders as her personal bench.
She smoothed her skirt over her knees, letting out a soft, playful sigh of triumph.
"Now that I’ve taught you at least two nature spells and tested your reflexes," Eluned declared, resting her delicate hands on her thighs as she pinned him to the dirt, "I feel quite tired, my Love."
As her concentration relaxed, the grand woodland around them began dispelling.

The towering oak trees, thick climbing vines, and sweet-smelling orange bushes dissolved into glowing green particles, fading away into the air until the vast vault returned to its original runic stone state.
Silas gritted his teeth against the floor, attempting to channel his own internal mana to hold the greenery together and stop the forest from vanishing. "Wait... I can maintain the trees..."
"Let it go, my Lord," Eluned told him gently, reaching down to pat his messy dark hair with a fond smile. "You do not need to waste your reserves keeping foliage alive in a stone basement."
Silas let out a breath, letting his mana circulation drop.
The last of the emerald leaves vanished, leaving them alone on the bare, dark floor tiles of the hall.
Then, Eluned kicked his upper back a bit with her bare heel, nudging his shoulder blades.
"My Lord," Eluned requested, her voice carrying a sweet demanding tone. "I request to be carried like a princess up the stairs to the upper levels."
Silas turned his head sideways against the stone floor, looking up at her out of the corner of his eye while still pinned beneath her weight.
"I can’t do that with you sitting on my back, Elu."
Eluned giggled softly at her own oversight. "Oh, right!"
She got up, stepping gracefully off his shoulders and onto the stone floor tiles.
Silas pushed himself off the ground, dusting the gray dust from his sweatpants and rolling his shoulders.
He stood tall, stepped close, and smoothly scooped Eluned up into his arms, carrying her against his broad chest.
Eluned wrapped her arms securely around his neck, resting her cheek against his shoulder with a deeply satisfied smile.
"Much better," she purred, closing her eyes.
Suddenly—
WHOOSH!
A sharp wind whistled across the open vault!
Morwenna came rushing out of nowhere, her Ironwood practice sword swinging directly toward Silas’s head at startling speed!
Silas’s combat instincts flared instantly but he didn’t drop Eluned.
He rapidly dipped his torso, pivoting his feet on the stone tiles and spinning backward in a tight evasive arc, letting the wooden blade pass a mere inch above his nose!
"Morwenna, what are you doing?!" Silas asked as he re-established his balance, holding Eluned tight.
Morwenna came to a stop ten feet away, spinning her practice blade with a wild feral grin baring her teeth.
"This is good secret training for your sensory awareness, Captain! A true Lord needs to learn how to maneuver and dodge high-speed attacks while holding someone important in his arms!"
Before Silas could argue the logic of her sudden assault, Morwenna attacked again, thrusting her wooden blade forward in a rapid three-strike combination aimed at his lower ribs and thighs!
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
Silas moved like a shadow across the floor.
He ducked, side-stepped, and twisted his torso through the air, weaving around every single thrust with precision footwork while keeping Eluned securely tucked out of harm’s way.
Eluned held tightly onto his neck, laughing delightfully as they glided around the pirate’s strikes without taking a hit.
"Make sure that the brutish pirate doesn’t hit us, my Lord!"
"For that comment, I’ll make sure to rough you up hehe~!" Morwenna cackled, raising her sword and giving chase across the cavernous stone vault.

sentences.text: Morwenna stood near the base of an enormous oak tree, looking up at the thick branches blocking the overhead arc lights.
She crossed her arms over her tattered captain’s coat, letting out a dismissive huff.
"Yay.
So what?
He made a bunch of tall wood....
Big deal.
Show-off."
Just as the pirate queen spoke, a thick leafy shrub grew right beside her boots.
A cluster of bright, round, orange-colored fruits sprouted from its branches, bobbing gently against her hip.
Morwenna blinked, reaching out to pluck one of the round fruits, turning it over in her palm with a suspicious scowl.
"What kind of fruit is this supposed to be?
It’s not an apple."
In the center of the clearing, Silas let out a long breath and lifted his palm from the stone.

Maintaining active spell pressure at that scale was exhausting for his current elemental conduits, but even after he broke physical contact, the grand forest remained standing, looking very firm and vibrant.
Silas couldn’t hold active control for long, but the abundant life energy he had summoned stayed rooted in the earth, leaving the woodland completely intact.
Eluned walked gracefully over to Silas with her eyes sparkling like emeralds.
"For your very first time executing Nature Transformation, this is simply too good!
Your natural affinity for the earth is exceptional, my Love!
In fact..."
She paused, sensing the refined elemental energy lingering within his core conduits, and gasped.
"You have already reached Adept mastery in a single attempt!"
Silas blinked, wiping a bead of sweat from his brow with his forearm.
"So quick?"
"Naturally!" Eluned affirmed, stepping close and cupping his sharp jaw with her warm palm.
"Even if I am no longer seated on my throne as the main Goddess of the World Tree, I was once a proper deity.
And because I love you and you love me, your talent receives the full backing of my ancient authority.
It is only natural that you would advance this fast!"
Silas looked down at her radiant, gorgeous face, hearing her earnest devoted words.
Looking at that beautiful smile lighting up her features, Silas felt a fierce protective instinct swell inside his chest.
He wanted to keep that smile right there no matter what trials or rivals threatened their territory in the future.
Eluned turned around, laughing like a ringing bell as she patted the rough bark of the oak tree Silas had grown.
"Look at them!
Nature has a spirit of its own, my Lord.
Come, play with the trees for a moment!
Feel their resonance!"
Silas joined her beneath the verdant canopy, watching as the living branches responded gently to their presence, swaying in a non-existent breeze as if bowing to greet their creator.
Even Morwenna, despite her grumpy scowling and folded arms, ended up trailing along behind them.

The pirate queen stood beneath a sweeping weeping willow, and to her utter surprise, the thin supple branches reached down and began gently weaving through her messy gray hair, acting like natural combs to untangle the sea-salt knots and straighten her unruly locks with delicate precision.
"Tch," Morwenna grumbled, though she didn’t pull away with her shoulders relaxing as she secretly enjoyed the woodland pampering.
"What a useful tree~ Elara could have learned a thing or two from you..."
A moment later, Morwenna walked over to where Silas and Eluned were standing, still holding the round orange fruit in her hand.
"Hey, weed.
What is this thing anyway?
Can you eat it like the apple?"
"That is called an orange, pirate," Eluned explained with patient grace.
She took the fruit from Morwenna’s hands and used her thumbnail to split the thick outer skin, expertly peeling away the bitter rind to reveal the bright, juicy segments inside.
Eluned separated a single segment and popped it directly into Morwenna’s mouth.
Morwenna chewed once, and her gray eyes instantly went wide.
The sweet tangy flavor burst across her tastebuds with a refreshing zest she had never experienced on the open ocean.
In a flash, the tough pirate queen transformed into an orange glutton.
She marched right back over to the shrub Silas had grown, plucking three more oranges and attempting to bite directly into them, rind and all.
"Wait, don’t eat the peel," Silas chuckled, walking over and grabbing her wrist before she could take a bite.
"It’s bitterso watch how she did it."
Both Silas and Eluned spent the next ten minutes showing Morwenna how to properly peel an orange without getting sticky juice all over her sleeves and coat.
Eluned even used a gentle pulse of nature energy to compress several oranges above a hollowed-out wooden cup she formed from a root, creating fresh, chilled orange juice on the spot.
Morwenna drank the entire cup in one long continuous gulp, letting out a deeply satisfied breath as she wiped her mouth.
"Holy sweet mother of the sea... that orange juice is incredible!
Captain, grow ten more of these orange bushes right now!
We need these on the supply wagons!"
"We’re here to train, Morwenna, not start a commercial fruit farm," Silas laughed, shaking his head at her newfound addiction.
Once they were all rested and the lighthearted atmosphere settled, Eluned stepped into the center of the forest clearing.
"Now that you have mastered the foundational art of growth and life," Eluned announced.
"I will teach you the next essential concept.
Nature energy can also be used for attacking as well."
Silas straightened his broad posture, his attention instantly sharpening as he rolled his shoulders.
"An attack spell?"
"Precisely," Eluned nodded, her green eyes serious.
"The spell is called Sylvan Spear.
You must gather the nature energy slumbering within the earth, compress its fibers until the wood becomes as rigid as dark steel, and launch it forward like a thrown javelin."
She demonstrated the concept without a word of chant.
With a simple flick of her pale fingers, the grass beneath her feet stirred.

A six-foot-long, razor-sharp spike of petrified, dark ironwood erupted from the dirt at startling velocity, sailing across the clearing and burying itself halfway into a distant stone support pillar with a resounding sound.
THUD!
"You try, my Love," Eluned encouraged him, stepping back to give him room.
Silas closed his eyes, drawing upon his newfound Adept Nature mastery.
He pictured the dense compacted structure of petrified timber.
He channeled his Gold Core mana, sending a commanding pulse down through his boots and directly into the turf below.
CRACK!
A five-foot spike of hardened, dark wood erupted from the floor five yards away, shooting forward across the room and shattering a stone target dummy into a cloud of gray fragments.
"Flawless execution!" Eluned praised, her eyes flashing with sudden battle intent.
"Now... let us test your application in a real combat spar!
Defend your ground!"
Before Silas could even formulate a reply, Eluned’s gentle nurturing aura changed completely.
BOOM!
The entire forest vibrated as Eluned unleashed a fraction of her true SSS-Rank nature authority.

The ground groaned beneath their feet, and dozens of thick, petrified wooden spears erupted from the dirt around her, hovering in mid-air like an array of siege ballista bolts pointing straight at his chest.
"Defend yourself, my Lord!" Eluned called out, sweeping her hand forward and sending the entire volley of wooden spears screaming toward him at breakneck speed!
Silas’s reflexes kicked in instantly.
He drew his Ironwood practice sword from his side, coating the blunt blade in a swirling layer of pressurized water and ice to enhance its impact, and charged straight into the incoming volley!
CLANG!
CRASH!
SHATTER!
Silas wove through the incoming barrage with his practice blade a blur of motion as he parried three wooden spears mid-flight, turning their rigid tips into splinters of harmless bark.
He closed the thirty-yard distance rapidly, pivoting on his heel and executing a sweeping horizontal cut aimed at her midsection.
Eluned didn’t back down or retreat.

She simply raised her open palm, and a thick barrier of tangled, iron-hard roots burst upward from the floor tiles, absorbing his sword strike with a hollow echoing thud that vibrated up Silas’s forearms.
’These women... really are amazing and I can tell they’re holding back.’
Silas kept up with her pace at first, using his physical agility to bound off the trunks of the living trees he had created, maneuvering around her defenses with fluid leaps.
While airborne, he gathered nature mana into his left hand and fired two Sylvan Spears of his own.
The wooden projectiles whistled through the air, curving slightly to target her exposed flanks.
Eluned smiled warmly with her movements light as a falling leaf riding a summer breeze.
"Nice!" She side-stepped his spears with effortless grace, her body blurring as she bypassed his line of sight entirely, merging with the greenery around her.

Before Silas could track her trajectory upon landing, thick, living vines rose from the turf like striking serpents, wrapping tightly around his ankles and pulling his feet straight out from under him!
"Whoa...!
Not again!" Silas grunted, hitting the soft turf floor on his chest with a heavy thud, his sword clattering a few feet away.
Before he could push himself back up onto his hands and knees, Eluned landed gracefully on top of him and sat directly on his upper back, using his broad, muscled shoulders as her personal bench.
She smoothed her skirt over her knees, letting out a soft, playful sigh of triumph.
"Now that I’ve taught you at least two nature spells and tested your reflexes," Eluned declared, resting her delicate hands on her thighs as she pinned him to the dirt, "I feel quite tired, my Love."
As her concentration relaxed, the grand woodland around them began dispelling.

The towering oak trees, thick climbing vines, and sweet-smelling orange bushes dissolved into glowing green particles, fading away into the air until the vast vault returned to its original runic stone state.
Silas gritted his teeth against the floor, attempting to channel his own internal mana to hold the greenery together and stop the forest from vanishing.
"Wait...
I can maintain the trees..."
"Let it go, my Lord," Eluned told him gently, reaching down to pat his messy dark hair with a fond smile.
"You do not need to waste your reserves keeping foliage alive in a stone basement."
Silas let out a breath, letting his mana circulation drop.
The last of the emerald leaves vanished, leaving them alone on the bare, dark floor tiles of the hall.
Then, Eluned kicked his upper back a bit with her bare heel, nudging his shoulder blades.
"My Lord," Eluned requested, her voice carrying a sweet demanding tone.
"I request to be carried like a princess up the stairs to the upper levels."
Silas turned his head sideways against the stone floor, looking up at her out of the corner of his eye while still pinned beneath her weight.
"I can’t do that with you sitting on my back, Elu."
Eluned giggled softly at her own oversight.
"Oh, right!"
She got up, stepping gracefully off his shoulders and onto the stone floor tiles.
Silas pushed himself off the ground, dusting the gray dust from his sweatpants and rolling his shoulders.
He stood tall, stepped close, and smoothly scooped Eluned up into his arms, carrying her against his broad chest.
Eluned wrapped her arms securely around his neck, resting her cheek against his shoulder with a deeply satisfied smile.
"Much better," she purred, closing her eyes.
Suddenly—
WHOOSH!
A sharp wind whistled across the open vault!
Morwenna came rushing out of nowhere, her Ironwood practice sword swinging directly toward Silas’s head at startling speed!
Silas’s combat instincts flared instantly but he didn’t drop Eluned.
He rapidly dipped his torso, pivoting his feet on the stone tiles and spinning backward in a tight evasive arc, letting the wooden blade pass a mere inch above his nose!
"Morwenna, what are you doing?!" Silas asked as he re-established his balance, holding Eluned tight.
Morwenna came to a stop ten feet away, spinning her practice blade with a wild feral grin baring her teeth.
"This is good secret training for your sensory awareness, Captain!
A true Lord needs to learn how to maneuver and dodge high-speed attacks while holding someone important in his arms!"
Before Silas could argue the logic of her sudden assault, Morwenna attacked again, thrusting her wooden blade forward in a rapid three-strike combination aimed at his lower ribs and thighs!
SWISH!
SWISH!
SWISH!
Silas moved like a shadow across the floor.
He ducked, side-stepped, and twisted his torso through the air, weaving around every single thrust with precision footwork while keeping Eluned securely tucked out of harm’s way.
Eluned held tightly onto his neck, laughing delightfully as they glided around the pirate’s strikes without taking a hit.
"Make sure that the brutish pirate doesn’t hit us, my Lord!"
"For that comment, I’ll make sure to rough you up hehe~!" Morwenna cackled, raising her sword and giving chase across the cavernous stone vault.

chapters.title: Chapter 226: A Wall
paragraphs: Morwenna chased them around the room with her boots slapping against the tiles as Silas bounded from pillar to pillar, and all three of them laughed as their voices echoed warmly through the Keep.
[Later that Evening]
Silas sat behind the heavy mahogany desk in his private office on the second floor of the Blessed Land Keep.

Outside the high arched stone windows, cold night had fallen over the territory, with genuine snow beginning to fall softly from the dark sky, coating the courtyard and the stone parapets in a pristine layer of white.
Silas leaned back in his leather chair, looking out at the drifting snowflakes through the glass.
"Snowing already," he complained quietly of the weather, shaking his head at how rapidly the seasons shifted in this magical domain.

He reminisced with a smile that after their intense training session in the vault, the girls had all gone together with Thora and Kaelia in order to brew a new kind of alcohol using fresh ingredients and herbs harvested from where Eluned grew crops.
Their loud cheers and laughter had faded toward the outbuildings, giving Silas a rare quiet evening to himself in his office.
He pulled up his Lord Inventory interface with a swipe of his hand, bringing out the wooden bento lunch box that Martha had carefully packed for him back at the Silverleaf estate in Valoria.
He opened the lid and began eating with his chopsticks, loving the comforting taste of the warm home-cooked meal... tender grilled beef, seasoned vegetables, and fluffy white rice.
"Martha really knows how to cook," he muttered with deep satisfaction, enjoying the familiar flavors of Earth amidst the magical keep.
At the same time, he also brought out the metallic container of scrolls from his inventory, setting it down onto the mahogany desk beside his meal.
Silas focused his mind, opening the translucent blue interface of his secret cheat... the Absolute Upgrade System.
He highlighted the metal box sitting before him and opened the Upgrade Tab to examine his options.
A glowing system prompt materialized directly before his vision, projecting crisp white text in the dimly lit office:
[Target Container: 18x Tier 1 Elemental Spell Scrolls]
[Upgrade Path Selected: Tier 1 -> Tier 3 (Batch Optimization)]
[Total Upgrade Cost: 3000 UP]
[Current UP Balance: 4400 UP]
[Remaining UP Balance After Execution: 1400 UP]
Silas stared at the numbers floating in front of him.
To upgrade all eighteen elemental spells inside the box simultaneously, it would cost exactly 3000 UP, which left him with 1400 UP left in his reserve pool.
"Three thousand UP for eighteen Tier 3 spells..." Silas muttered, a satisfied grin spreading across his face as he ran the numbers.
He immediately realized that this was a good price... an exceptional bargain that would advance his elemental repertoire without requiring years of tedious library study.
’I honestly expected it to be much more...’
He pressed [Y] on the floating holographic tab to confirm the transaction.
A warm radiant golden light enveloped the metallic box sitting on his desk.
The glow seeped through the seams of the lid for a single second before fading away completely.
All of the spell scrolls inside were instantly upgraded from basic Tier 1 scrolls to top-tier Tier 3 Spell scrolls.
Silas set his chopsticks down and opened the lid.
The rough cheap paper was gone, replaced by thick high-density parchment bound with golden silk ties with the runic inscriptions along the edges pulsing with refined elemental power.
"Haah~ What a good day~"
Immediately, as he was chewing a mouthful of rice, Silas reached into the box, took out the first upgraded scroll... Pyroclastic Comet and pressed the furled parchment directly against his forehead.
WHOOSH!
It felt like he had reached an epiphany!

A sudden electrifying surge of pure understanding flooded his brain, burning the Tier 3 spell structure, internal circulation paths, and everything else about the spell permanently into his Gold Core conduits.
He learned the spell instantly, which made him surprised at how seamless and natural the integration felt within his spirit.
’If this is how versatile scrolls are... How about I do all of them?’
Usually one had to take breaks in between absorbing knowledge from scrolls as it was tiring but for a Gold core user like him, he didn’t even feel a bit exhausted.
Silas didn’t stop there.
He set the spent scroll aside, picked up the second scroll from the container, and pressed it to his temple, absorbing its magical knowledge in a flash of insight.
[Mantle of the Inferno.]
[Incineration Ray.]
[Gale Guillotine]
[Cyclone Slipstream]
[Hurricane Repulsion]
[Obsidian Impaler]
[Aegis of the Monolith]
[Tectonic Rupture]
[Fulgur Annihilation]
[Voltaic Execution Chain]
[Thunderclap Blitz]
[Solar Flare Detonation]
[Radiant Cellular Reconstruction]
[Prismatic Refraction]
[Shadow Submersion]
[Shadow Constriction]
[Night-Stalker Eyes]
He did it for all of them, taking each golden scroll and pressing it against his forehead.
Eighteen distinct Tier 3 magical weaves poured into his consciousness one after another.
Fire, Wind, Earth, Lightning, Light, and Shadow anchored themselves firmly into his spirit alongside his existing Water and Ice mastery.
When the final scroll dissolved its stored knowledge into his mind, Silas leaned back heavily in his leather chair, breathing heavily once he was done.
’I feel very different.... Much stronger...’
His chest rose and fell in deep gasps as his Gold Core thrummed, expanding its internal pathways to hold eight complete elemental foundations simultaneously.
The mental weight of absorbing so many spell structures at once was immense, but his physique handled the strain.

He finished the last bite of his food, summoned away his empty lunch box with a wave of his hand, and put the spent spell scrolls back into the metal container, dropping the box back into his Lord Inventory.
"When are they coming?"
Suddenly, his heightened senses sharpened. He sensed presences coming down the stone hallway toward his office door.
The oak door of his office opened smoothly.

Aeli stepped into the room first, leading two female combatants from the barracks behind her... Brida, the fierce warrior clad in polished plate armor and Tasmin, the silent Huntress wearing dark leather with twin chained blades strapped to her waist.
Once they arrived in front of his mahogany table, all three of them bowed respectfully in unison.
Aeli reported with her voice crisp and attentive as she looked at her Lord.
"Lord Silas, Brida and Tasmin have arrived as instructed from the training grounds."
After delivering her report, Aeli walked around the desk and stood quietly at his right side, taking her natural place as his loyal secretary.
Brida and Tasmin stood at attention before the desk, looking up at him expectantly, waiting for his orders.
Silas rested his forearms on the polished wood of his desk, crossing his fingers beneath his chin.
He looked at the two women who had fought for his territory, his face turning a bit somber as he studied their posture.
"You two must wonder why I’ve called you right now," Silas said quietly with his deep voice carrying across the quiet office.
Brida and Tasmin looked up at him expectantly, their eyes focused and ready for whatever quest or assignment he was about to hand down.
Silas leaned forward slightly, looking directly into their eyes as his expression turned serious.
"Do you think you’ve hit a wall?"
Tasmin and Brida looked at each other in the dim light of the office with their expressions changing as the full weight of Silas’s question hung in the air between them.
The wind outside howled against the stone walls of the Keep, rattling the leaded windowpanes and scattering fresh snowflakes against the glass.
Inside, the quiet was punctuated only by the crackle of the hearth and the slow tense breaths of the two female combatants standing before the dark mahogany desk.
Both women simultaneously gulped, their throats tightening as an unspoken anxiety finally bubbled to the surface.
Brida adjusted her stance, the thick iron plates of her pauldrons clinking together in the quiet room.
She looked up at Silas, her amber eyes shadowed by a frustration she had kept bottled up for quite a while during their border patrols and sweeps.

"As of late, My Lord..." Brida began, her voice sounding tight with an emotion she struggled to keep under control. "I am not getting any stronger... It doesn’t matter how many monsters I kill in the forest or how many patrols I run through the wilderness. Despite all the beasts that I have slain... it seems my level has become completely stagnant."
She gripped the heavy leather strap of her shield hilt, her jaw setting in a hard, pained line.

"I reached Level 30 a week ago," she continued, her broad shoulders tense under her armor. "And since that moment, not a single drop of experience has registered in my core... My body feels ready for more strength and my muscles feel primed to carry heavier weight, but nothing accumulates. The energy simply dissipates into the air, as if my body refuses to hold it."
Tasmin stepped forward alongside her frontline comrade, nodding in grim agreement.
Her slender frame was still dressed in her dark leathers, the steel chains of her twin daggers hanging silently at her hips.

"It is the exact same for me, Lord Silas," the scout reported, her dark eyes solemn and sharp. "I feel like I could move faster... I feel like my reflexes want to expand and push past my current limits, but there is something physically blocking my conduits. It is as if an invisible wall is keeping me from going any further, no matter how hard I push myself in training or in live combat."
Silas leaned back into his heavy leather chair, listening quietly to their reports.
He didn’t look shocked by their words, nor did he offer a sudden burst of frustration or disappointment.
Instead, he simply let out a long, quiet sigh, resting his broad, calloused hands flat against the polished mahogany surface of his desk.

"It isn’t a fluke, and it isn’t a mistake on your part," Silas told them calmly, his golden-ringed eyes meeting theirs in turn. "What you are experiencing right now is simply the natural limit of your class."
He held their gaze, letting the fundamental reality of the Sovereign Realm’s rules settle over the room.

"Normally, every class below A-Rank has hard limiters built directly into its core design," Silas explained, laying out the stark mechanics that governed every summoned Troop across the Sovereign Realm. "Even standard A-Rank classes eventually hit a ceiling at Level 80. For C-Rank classes like yours... Shieldmaiden and Wilderness Huntress, Level 30 is the absolute end of the road. This is where the natural system fated you to be."
Brida’s lips trembled.
The tough battle-hardened warrior who had stood unflinching against charging beasts along the eastern border looked down at her broad, calloused palms.
Her fingers slowly curled into tight, trembling fists.
"So that’s all we are?" Brida muttered, her voice cracking slightly as the bitter truth washed over her. "Limited by our potential... trapped behind a limit..."
A heavy suffocating cloud of despair settled over the two combatants as reality was bitter and unforgiving.

The other women in the territory... beings who were born or summoned as higher entities like Eluned, Morwenna, or Aeli could keep growing, continuously scaling to terrifying heights of power as the domain expanded.
They could face high-tier dungeon lords and corporate strike forces without fear of being left behind.
Meanwhile, Brida and Tasmin would remain trapped at Level 30 for the rest of their lives.
They would never be able to advance.
They would never be able to grow stronger or keep pace with the Lord they served.
They were static pieces on an evolving board, condemned to watch from the sidelines as the battles grew fiercer.
Brida stared down at the floorboards with her thoughts spiraling into a dark desperate place.

’If this is my limit...’ Brida thought bitterly, her chest aching with a sense of inadequacy. ’If I am stuck as a basic C-Rank Shieldmaiden forever... then how am I supposed to stand beside my Lord? How am I supposed to protect his back when real threats come for our territory? How can I call myself his shield if my arm shatters against the first real boss we encounter? How am I supposed to have his children... Who would want children with a weak woman like me?’
Tasmin gritted her teeth so hard her jaw muscles bulged beneath her pale skin.
She looked up at Silas with her decision made out of a painful self-sacrificing sense of duty to Blessed Land.

"Due to this reason, My Lord," Tasmin said, forcing the words past her tight throat, "I would like to officially resign from being a Commander. I am simply not strong enough to lead our scouts into high-tier zones, and I cannot allow my lack of potential to harm the others or drag down the efficiency of our patrols."
Standing beside Silas’s desk, Aeli looked at the two women with profound sadness in her silver eyes.
The elven arcanist gently pressed her hand against her chest with her heart aching for her comrades.
She couldn’t believe they were being forced to step down and surrender their command simply because of the realm’s rigid class boundaries.
Yet, as the room filled with gloom, Silas didn’t look troubled in the slightest.
Instead, a broad confident smile slowly spread across his face, lighting up his sharp features.
"Do you think I can’t fix it?" Silas asked, his gravelly voice cutting cleanly through their despair.

He finished the last bite of his food, summoned away his empty lunch box with a wave of his hand, and put the spent spell scrolls back into the metal container, dropping the box back into his Lord Inventory.
"When are they coming?"
Suddenly, his heightened senses sharpened.
He sensed presences coming down the stone hallway toward his office door.
The oak door of his office opened smoothly.
Aeli stepped into the room first, leading two female combatants from the barracks behind her...
Brida, the fierce warrior clad in polished plate armor and Tasmin, the silent Huntress wearing dark leather with twin chained blades strapped to her waist.
Once they arrived in front of his mahogany table, all three of them bowed respectfully in unison.
Aeli reported with her voice crisp and attentive as she looked at her Lord.
"Lord Silas, Brida and Tasmin have arrived as instructed from the training grounds."
After delivering her report, Aeli walked around the desk and stood quietly at his right side, taking her natural place as his loyal secretary.
Brida and Tasmin stood at attention before the desk, looking up at him expectantly, waiting for his orders.
Silas rested his forearms on the polished wood of his desk, crossing his fingers beneath his chin.
He looked at the two women who had fought for his territory, his face turning a bit somber as he studied their posture.
"You two must wonder why I’ve called you right now," Silas said quietly with his deep voice carrying across the quiet office.
Brida and Tasmin looked up at him expectantly, their eyes focused and ready for whatever quest or assignment he was about to hand down.
Silas leaned forward slightly, looking directly into their eyes as his expression turned serious.
"Do you think you’ve hit a wall?"
Tasmin and Brida looked at each other in the dim light of the office with their expressions changing as the full weight of Silas’s question hung in the air between them.
The wind outside howled against the stone walls of the Keep, rattling the leaded windowpanes and scattering fresh snowflakes against the glass.
Inside, the quiet was punctuated only by the crackle of the hearth and the slow tense breaths of the two female combatants standing before the dark mahogany desk.
Both women simultaneously gulped, their throats tightening as an unspoken anxiety finally bubbled to the surface.
Brida adjusted her stance, the thick iron plates of her pauldrons clinking together in the quiet room.
She looked up at Silas, her amber eyes shadowed by a frustration she had kept bottled up for quite a while during their border patrols and sweeps.
"As of late, My Lord..." Brida began, her voice sounding tight with an emotion she struggled to keep under control.
"I am not getting any stronger...
It doesn’t matter how many monsters I kill in the forest or how many patrols I run through the wilderness.
Despite all the beasts that I have slain... it seems my level has become completely stagnant."
She gripped the heavy leather strap of her shield hilt, her jaw setting in a hard, pained line.
"I reached Level 30 a week ago," she continued, her broad shoulders tense under her armor.
"And since that moment, not a single drop of experience has registered in my core...
My body feels ready for more strength and my muscles feel primed to carry heavier weight, but nothing accumulates.
The energy simply dissipates into the air, as if my body refuses to hold it."
Tasmin stepped forward alongside her frontline comrade, nodding in grim agreement.
Her slender frame was still dressed in her dark leathers, the steel chains of her twin daggers hanging silently at her hips.
"It is the exact same for me, Lord Silas," the scout reported, her dark eyes solemn and sharp.
"I feel like I could move faster...
I feel like my reflexes want to expand and push past my current limits, but there is something physically blocking my conduits.
It is as if an invisible wall is keeping me from going any further, no matter how hard I push myself in training or in live combat."
Silas leaned back into his heavy leather chair, listening quietly to their reports.
He didn’t look shocked by their words, nor did he offer a sudden burst of frustration or disappointment.
Instead, he simply let out a long, quiet sigh, resting his broad, calloused hands flat against the polished mahogany surface of his desk.
"It isn’t a fluke, and it isn’t a mistake on your part," Silas told them calmly, his golden-ringed eyes meeting theirs in turn.
"What you are experiencing right now is simply the natural limit of your class."
He held their gaze, letting the fundamental reality of the Sovereign Realm’s rules settle over the room.

"Normally, every class below A-Rank has hard limiters built directly into its core design," Silas explained, laying out the stark mechanics that governed every summoned Troop across the Sovereign Realm.
"Even standard A-Rank classes eventually hit a ceiling at Level 80.
For C-Rank classes like yours...
Shieldmaiden and Wilderness Huntress, Level 30 is the absolute end of the road.
This is where the natural system fated you to be."
Brida’s lips trembled.
The tough battle-hardened warrior who had stood unflinching against charging beasts along the eastern border looked down at her broad, calloused palms.
Her fingers slowly curled into tight, trembling fists.
"So that’s all we are?" Brida muttered, her voice cracking slightly as the bitter truth washed over her.
"Limited by our potential... trapped behind a limit..."
A heavy suffocating cloud of despair settled over the two combatants as reality was bitter and unforgiving.

The other women in the territory... beings who were born or summoned as higher entities like Eluned, Morwenna, or Aeli could keep growing, continuously scaling to terrifying heights of power as the domain expanded.
They could face high-tier dungeon lords and corporate strike forces without fear of being left behind.
Meanwhile, Brida and Tasmin would remain trapped at Level 30 for the rest of their lives.
They would never be able to advance.
They would never be able to grow stronger or keep pace with the Lord they served.
They were static pieces on an evolving board, condemned to watch from the sidelines as the battles grew fiercer.
Brida stared down at the floorboards with her thoughts spiraling into a dark desperate place.
’If this is my limit...’ Brida thought bitterly, her chest aching with a sense of inadequacy. ’If I am stuck as a basic C-Rank Shieldmaiden forever... then how am I supposed to stand beside my Lord?
How am I supposed to protect his back when real threats come for our territory?
How can I call myself his shield if my arm shatters against the first real boss we encounter?
How am I supposed to have his children...
Who would want children with a weak woman like me?’
Tasmin gritted her teeth so hard her jaw muscles bulged beneath her pale skin.
She looked up at Silas with her decision made out of a painful self-sacrificing sense of duty to Blessed Land.
"Due to this reason, My Lord," Tasmin said, forcing the words past her tight throat, "I would like to officially resign from being a Commander.
I am simply not strong enough to lead our scouts into high-tier zones, and I cannot allow my lack of potential to harm the others or drag down the efficiency of our patrols."
Standing beside Silas’s desk, Aeli looked at the two women with profound sadness in her silver eyes.
The elven arcanist gently pressed her hand against her chest with her heart aching for her comrades.
She couldn’t believe they were being forced to step down and surrender their command simply because of the realm’s rigid class boundaries.
Yet, as the room filled with gloom, Silas didn’t look troubled in the slightest.
Instead, a broad confident smile slowly spread across his face, lighting up his sharp features.
"Do you think I can’t fix it?" Silas asked, his gravelly voice cutting cleanly through their despair.

chapters.title: Chapter 227: S-Rank Duo!
paragraphs: Both women whipped their heads up, staring at him in wide-eyed shock.
Silas’s smile grew even wider, his golden-ringed eyes glowing with a quiet authority.

"I can upgrade anything, can’t I?" Silas reminded them, gesturing casually around the room. "I upgraded the stone walls of this Keep. I upgraded our weapons and I upgraded the very place where you sleep. What’s to say I can’t upgrade your classes?"
The shift in the room was instant.
The heavy cloud of hopelessness completely vanished, replaced by an electric jolt of sudden realization that made both women hold their breath.
Brida and Tasmin perked up immediately, their postures straightening as their eyes shone with sudden hope.
They felt a wave of deep self-reproach wash over them... they should have never doubted their Lord at all!
Of course he had a way!
He was Silas Graves, the Lord who shattered every rule the world tried to enforce!
Silas chuckled, reaching up to scratch the side of his face as he added a casual thoughtful observation.

"Well, increasing in ranks does mean that your lifespan will naturally increase as well," Silas noted, looking at them with an amused glint in his golden eyes. "So as long as you don’t mind spending a great deal of your life stuck here with me..."
Brida looked at him as if he were completely dense for even phrasing it as a question.

"I would love to spend the rest of my life with you, My Lord!" Brida declared loudly, her voice ringing out through the office without an ounce of hesitation with her cheeks flushing a brilliant crimson.
Tasmin, not wanting to be outdone by the heavy infantry unit for even a single second, immediately took a step forward.
Her dark eyes locked onto his with sharp fierce intensity.
"Even if we die, My Lord," Tasmin countered smoothly. "I wouldn’t mind going to the afterlife with you."
Brida instantly turned her head, glaring at the scout with a dramatic pout.
"Hey! Stop trying to make my declaration sound weak, you sneaky cat!"
Aeli let out a soft, delighted laugh from the side, and Silas chuckled along with them as the tension melted completely into warm familiar banter.
"Alright, settle down," Silas said, waving his hand to calm them. He looked at the slender scout first. "Tasmin, come here first."
Tasmin didn’t hesitate for a fraction of a second.
She stepped briskly around the corner of the mahogany desk, stopping directly in front of his chair.
Her chest rose and fell with eager breathless anticipation as she stood at attention.
Silas stood up from his leather chair, reaching across the table.
He pressed his hand firmly against her chest, right over her core, and focused his mind on his system interface.
’I want to upgrade her Class.’
Instantly, the glowing blue panel of the Absolute Upgrade System materialized before his vision.
[Would you like to upgrade Tasmin’s C-Rank [Wilderness Huntress] to S-Rank [Shadow Commander]?]
[Cost: 500 UP]
[Y / N]
Silas paused for a brief second, his golden eyes scanning the text floating in the air.
’Shadow?’ Silas thought with a question mark popping up in his mind as he analyzed the text. ’How does her Huntress class evolve into a Shadow Commander?’
It was a strange unexpected evolutionary branch, but Silas didn’t care about the odd naming convention.
An S-Rank class was an S-Rank class, and 500 UP was a remarkably cheap price to pay to secure a permanent S-Rank commander for his scouting forces.
Silas smiled and selected ’Y’.
The second the choice registered, a surge of dark bubbling energy erupted directly out of Tasmin’s chest!
"Ah...!" Tasmin gritted her teeth, an involuntary moan escaping her lips as her entire body went rigid under his palm.
She stumbled back two steps, clutching her stomach as the dark ethereal power flooded her internal conduits with overwhelming force.
"My... my body feels weird..." Tasmin gasped out, her skin turning pale as her internal structure was forcibly torn apart and rebuilt.
Suddenly, a strange intense purification process began.
Her sweat pores began swelling across her arms, neck, and face, forcing out tiny beads of pitch-black viscous liquid that quickly covered her skin in a dark sheen.
Brida scrunched her nose in disgust, taking a quick step backward and fanning the air.
"Ugh! Tasmin, you’re disgusting! What is that stuff coming out of you?!"
Tasmin, even while trembling from the intense internal heat washing through her body, raised her hand and flipped Brida off without even looking at her.
"Shut... up..." Tasmin grunted between her teeth.
The black liquid oozing from her skin didn’t drip onto the woven rug.
Instead, it reacted instantly to the dark energy flooding the room, transforming into physical writhing shadows!
The shadows rose up around her like dark, pressurized cables, coiling tightly around her limbs and torso until they formed a solid opaque cocoon that completely sealed her inside.
Inside the dark pod, Tasmin felt the power moving up her spine, expanding her conduits, reshaping her muscles, and refining her neural pathways to incredible speeds.
"Ahn~ So much..."
POP!
With a sharp resounding sound, the shadow cocoon completely shattered into fine dark dust, revealing Tasmin standing proudly in the center of the office.
The physical changes were striking and immediate.
Her previously solid black hair now had brilliant, shimmering strands of pure silver running through the locks.

Her skin was impossibly smooth, glowing with a healthy vitality, and her figure had matured significantly... her waist was narrow, and her chest was visibly fuller and curvier against her leather armor.

However, accompanied by her striking new appearance came a foul and extremely pungent odor that rapidly filled the office which was the lingering scent of all the deep physical impurities that had been purged from her body during the transformation.
Tasmin’s cheeks flushed bright red as she caught a whiff of herself.
She looked deeply embarrassed to smell like that in front of Silas, but her embarrassment was quickly washed away by the volume of power humming through her limbs.
"I... I feel so much stronger!" Tasmin exclaimed, her eyes wide as she looked down at her hands.
To test her new body, she raised her right hand.
A swirl of pitch-black shadow materialized instantly around her palm like a dark, living flame.
"What about physical power?" Brida asked, "Shadows aren’t nothing compared to physical pow—"
She threw three lightning-fast punches into the air.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!.
Her movements were so rapid that her forearms turned into continuous blurs of motion!
She drew one of her chained daggers and casually dropped it toward the floor.
Before the steel could touch the rug, the shadow beneath her boots opened like a dark mouth, swallowing the blade whole.
A second later, the shadow cast by Silas’s mahogany table opened, and the dagger shot out, burying its tip cleanly into the side of the wood!
Silas blinked, thoroughly impressed by the seamless spatial trick. He focused his vision, opening her brand-new status screen to inspect the full breakdown.
[Name]: Tasmin
[Title]: Wilderness Huntress —> [Shadow Commander]
[Rank]: S-Rank
[Loyalty]: 100 (Diehard / Love)
[Vitality]: 400
[Active & Passive Skills]:

[Shadow-Submersion Drift]: Allows Tasmin to physically sink into shadows and spatial seams, granting temporary invulnerability to physical attacks and rendering her entirely invisible to sensory or optical wards. (Cost: 100 Mana/minute)

[True Severing Edge]: Enforces an armor-piercing property onto her twin blades and chains. Attacks bypass 50% of the target’s physical and magical armor hardness, applying a lingering void-bleed that resists low-to-mid tier healing magic. (Passive)

[Voltaic Chain Execution]: Channels high-voltage, super-heated crimson flames through her Eclipse-Thread chains to bind, isolate, and decapitate targets from up to 30 meters away (Cost: 250 Mana/cast)
[Phantom Leap / Blitz]: Accelerates her neural reflexes to supersonic speeds, leaving residual shadow illusions in her wake as she blinks directly into an opponent’s blind spot. (Cost: 150 Mana/cast)

[Predator’s Mark]: Locks her gaze onto a single high-value target or monster core, highlighting their weak points in glowing red and granting a 30% critical damage boost against them. (Cost: 80 Mana/cast)
[Shadow Strengthening]: By merging her shadow with her physical body, Tasmin can double all of her stats including her mana. (Cost: 100 Mana/cast).
Silas’s eyes widened as he read through the skill list.
Her stat increases were massive, her mana pool was huge, and her ability to double her output with shadow merging made her a menace in high-tier combat.
"Congratulations, Tasmin," Silas said, smiling warmly at her. "You really turned into something fierce."
Tasmin didn’t just thank him with words. Overcome with pure joy and the intoxicating rush of S-Rank power, she instantly activated [Phantom Leap]!
ZIP!

She vanished from her spot and reappeared right at Silas’s side behind the desk and then she threw her arms tightly around his neck, hugging him with all her strength despite the foul smell radiating from her skin.
Tasmin then leaned up and kissed him on the cheek.
"Thank you, My Lord!" Tasmin cried out softly, her voice overrun with joy. "I feel so much stronger... I’m so glad I get to keep my position as your Commander!"
Silas patted her head, though he winced slightly as his fingers touched her slimy hair.
"I’m glad too, Tasmin," Silas said, pulling back slightly with an amused smirk. "Now go take a bath. You smell terrible."
Tasmin’s face burned redder than a hot iron.
She hurriedly yanked her dagger out of his desk, sheathed it at her waist, and practically sprinted out of the office to find the washrooms.
Once the door closed behind her, Brida stepped up to the table.
She had been remarkably patient, watching her friend’s transformation with wide awe-filled eyes.
"Is it my turn yet, My Lord?" Brida asked, leaning forward eagerly over the mahogany wood.
"Come over," Silas nodded, gesturing to the space before him.
Brida stepped up to the desk, standing tall and bracing herself.
Silas reached out, placing his hand flat against her chest armor, and opened his system interface once more.
[Would you like to upgrade Brida’s C-Rank [Shieldmaiden] to S-Rank [Grand Titan Bastion] ?]
[Cost: 500 UP]
[Y / N]
Silas pressed ’Y’ without hesitation.
FLASH!
A bright golden-brown energy burst out from his hand, enveloping Brida’s entire frame in a pillar of radiant light!
Her transformation unfolded completely differently from Tasmin’s shadow evolution.
Instead of swelling her body into a massive bulky shape, the divine power actually deflated her visible muscle volume slightly...
Her physique streamlined, turning compact and perfectly balanced.
Her bone density increased tenfold, and her newly refined muscles coiled tight like steel cables beneath her skin.
The golden energy formed a glowing pod around her, coiling in thick radiant bands as she absorbed the massive influx of power.
Brida could feel every cell in her body expanding, her physical durability multiplying at a terrifying rate.
’All this is because of my Lord...’
Feeling the surge of power reaching its peak inside her chest, Brida threw her head back and let out a booming battle roar that shook the dust from the rafters.
"RAHHH!"
CRACK!
She flexed her entire body, completely shattering the energy pod from the inside out.
Golden light scattered across the office like falling glass before fading into the air.
Brida stood there, panting lightly as she looked down at her hands. She felt lighter, faster, yet infinitely sturdier than she had ever been in her life... a walking fortress anchored to the earth.
She perked up immediately, smoothing her hands down her streamlined sides, and looked up at Silas expectantly.
"My Lord! How do I look?!"
Silas looked at her refined form and smiled approvingly. "You look incredible, Brida.."
He pulled up her status screen to inspect the upgrade:
[Title]: Shieldmaiden —> [Grand Titan Bastion]
[Rank]: S-Rank
[Loyalty]: 100 (Diehard / Fanatical)
[Vitality]: 5000
[Active & Passive Skills]:

[Unyielding Bedrock Body]: Expands her muscle and bone density to extraordinary levels. Grants complete immunity to stagger, physical knockback, and displacement effects from targets below S-Rank. (Passive)

[Full Counter]:: Her shield absorbs 50% of all incoming physical and elemental impact energy, storing the force within the central boss to detonate outward as a concussive shockwave upon command. (Cost: 150 Mana/activation)

[Domain Barrier: Bastion Ground]: Slams her shield into the dirt, erecting an impenetrable 30-yard spatial defensive dome around herself and her squad that blocks high-tier spell artillery and heavy kinetic strikes. (Cost: 400 Mana/cast)

[Earth-Shattering Cleave]: Infuses her weapon with compressed earth energy, executing a heavy downward strike that splits the ground open in a 30-meter line and crushes enemy formations. (Cost: 300 Mana/cast)
[Aegis Charge]: Surges forward like a runaway locomotive behind her shield, forcefully plowing through enemies and violently ragdolling anything standing in her path. (Cost: 180 Mana/cast)
Silas stared at her Vitality stat.
Five thousand? She was a literal walking fortress now, capable of taking hits that would flatten a whole lot of things.
"Congratulations, Brida," Silas said warmly. "You’re an absolute tank."
Brida’s eyes softened completely.
She crept closer to the table with her tough soldier facade completely melting away.
Like Tasmin, the deep purification process had forced black foul-smelling impurities from her pores, leaving her skin covered in a dark sheen, but she didn’t care about the smell in this moment.
She dropped onto both knees directly in front of his desk, looking up at him with deep tearful emotion in her amber eyes.
"My Lord..." Brida said softly, her voice trembling.
"Yes?" Silas asked gently.
The Bonus Chapters will come tomorrow.
