Her bone density increased tenfold, and her newly refined muscles coiled tight like steel cables beneath her skin.
The golden energy formed a glowing pod around her, coiling in thick radiant bands as she absorbed the massive influx of power.
Brida could feel every cell in her body expanding, her physical durability multiplying at a terrifying rate.
’All this is because of my Lord...’
Feeling the surge of power reaching its peak inside her chest, Brida threw her head back and let out a booming battle roar that shook the dust from the rafters.
"RAHHH!"
CRACK!
She flexed her entire body, completely shattering the energy pod from the inside out.
Golden light scattered across the office like falling glass before fading into the air.
Brida stood there, panting lightly as she looked down at her hands.
She felt lighter, faster, yet infinitely sturdier than she had ever been in her life... a walking fortress anchored to the earth.
She perked up immediately, smoothing her hands down her streamlined sides, and looked up at Silas expectantly.
"My Lord!
How do I look?!"
Silas looked at her refined form and smiled approvingly.
"You look incredible, Brida.."
He pulled up her status screen to inspect the upgrade:
[Title]: Shieldmaiden —> [Grand Titan Bastion]
[Rank]: S-Rank
[Loyalty]: 100 (Diehard / Fanatical)
[Vitality]: 5000
[Active & Passive Skills]:
[Unyielding Bedrock Body]: Expands her muscle and bone density to extraordinary levels.
Grants complete immunity to stagger, physical knockback, and displacement effects from targets below S-Rank. (Passive)

[Full Counter]:: Her shield absorbs 50% of all incoming physical and elemental impact energy, storing the force within the central boss to detonate outward as a concussive shockwave upon command. (Cost: 150 Mana/activation)

[Domain Barrier: Bastion Ground]: Slams her shield into the dirt, erecting an impenetrable 30-yard spatial defensive dome around herself and her squad that blocks high-tier spell artillery and heavy kinetic strikes. (Cost: 400 Mana/cast)

[Earth-Shattering Cleave]: Infuses her weapon with compressed earth energy, executing a heavy downward strike that splits the ground open in a 30-meter line and crushes enemy formations. (Cost: 300 Mana/cast)
[Aegis Charge]: Surges forward like a runaway locomotive behind her shield, forcefully plowing through enemies and violently ragdolling anything standing in her path. (Cost: 180 Mana/cast)
Silas stared at her Vitality stat.
Five thousand?
She was a literal walking fortress now, capable of taking hits that would flatten a whole lot of things.
"Congratulations, Brida," Silas said warmly.
"You’re an absolute tank."
Brida’s eyes softened completely.
She crept closer to the table with her tough soldier facade completely melting away.
Like Tasmin, the deep purification process had forced black foul-smelling impurities from her pores, leaving her skin covered in a dark sheen, but she didn’t care about the smell in this moment.
She dropped onto both knees directly in front of his desk, looking up at him with deep tearful emotion in her amber eyes.
"My Lord..." Brida said softly, her voice trembling.
"Yes?" Silas asked gently.
The Bonus Chapters will come tomorrow.

chapters.title: Chapter 228: Going Back To The Library [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Thank you," Brida whispered with tears welling up in her eyes and leaving clean tracks through the dark impurities on her cheeks. "Without you... without you... I wouldn’t be here with all these people I’ve come to love as my family and without you, I might have been somewhere else, wasting my life away in some forgotten corner of the world... You’re my most special person, so I’ll make sure that I protect you without fail. No one touches my Lord while I breathe."
Brida brought her face up, offering him a radiant tearful smile.
"I love you."
Silas smiled back at her with his voice sincere and full of warmth. "I love you too, Brida."
Brida stumbled slightly where she knelt with her face going redder than a hot forge. "Uh... can we..."
She puckered her lips, leaning forward across the desk for a kiss.
Silas sniffed the air as the pungent smell of purged impurities hit his nose, and held up a hand with a laugh.
"Uh, after you take a bath."
Brida paused mid-pucker. She blinked, caught a whiff of her own arms, and her eyes went wide as saucers.
"AH!" Brida shrieked, her face burning with pure embarrassment. "I-I’m so sorry! I’ll go right now!"

She scrambled up from her knees, stuttering uncontrollably as she turned and ran out of the office at top speed, slamming the heavy oak door behind her as her footsteps echoed down the stone corridor.
Silas let out a long sigh, shaking his head with a chuckle as he ran a calloused hand through his dark hair.

’This is good... They’re upgraded and they’re happy, still 500 UP per person is insanity... We need to slaughter more monsters so I can upgrade Aeli next and then Fenna. I’ll take this step by step and increase the others too, maybe I don’t need to increase them all to S-Rank at once though.
Suddenly, a pair of soft warm arms wrapped gently around his neck from behind.
Silas didn’t flinch. Instead he leaned his head back against Aeli’s chest as she rested her chin softly on top of his head.
The elven arcanist smiled down at him, her green eyes filled with quiet, affection.
"My Lord, we truly are blessed to have you."
Silas chuckled, a deep sound that vibrated against Aeliana’s arms as she gently held him from behind in the quiet firelit office.

"Well," Silas mused, a dry smirk touching his lips as he rested his head back against the soft fabric covering her chest. "It is the Blessed Land after all. It only makes sense that all of us end up blessed."
Aeli let out a soft laugh that echoed warmly in the quiet stone room.
"Hehehe~"
Her green eyes crinkled with genuine amusement with her hold on his shoulders relaxing slightly.
She leaned over his shoulder and her delicate nose twitched once then twice.
She pulled back a fraction of an inch, looking down at his collar with a raised eyebrow and a playful tilt of her head.
"My Lord..." Aeli asked, a teasing glint in her eyes. "Do you require cleaning?"
Silas paused, letting out a long sigh that made his shoulders slump.
He didn’t even need to look down at his clothes to know what she was talking about.
Tasmin had enthusiastically thrown her arms around him right after her class upgrade, hugging his chest and kissing his cheek while her body was still actively purging dark viscous impurities.
The foul, pungent odor of the shadow purification was still clinging stubbornly to his tunic and coat.
"Yeah," Silas grumbled, rubbing his temple with two fingers. "Tasmin was a bit overly enthusiastic about her new stats. I smell like an unwashed dungeon sewer right now."

"Do not worry, My Lord," Aeli assured him smoothly, a sweet radiant smile gracing her face as she stepped around the side of the mahogany desk. "I actually learned a specialized Cleansing spell from my aunt back during my time in the Royal Palace as a Royal Elf."
She raised her slender right hand, her long graceful fingers tracing a brief intricate pattern in the cool office air.
A soft shimmering orb of pristine, silver-white magic materialized over her open palm, humming with a quiet frequency. With a gentle flick of her wrist, she pushed the magic toward him.
FWOOSH!
A cool refreshing breeze swept over Silas’s entire body.
The silver light washed down from his broad shoulders all the way to his boots, completely vaporizing the dark, slimy residue and neutralizing the foul odor in a fraction of a second.
His tunic looked as crisp and fresh as if it had just been pulled from a linen chest, smelling like fresh morning dew.
Silas looked down at his clean shirt, thoroughly impressed by the utility of the spell.
He reached out and gave Aeli a gentle, affectionate pat on the head, scratching lightly behind her delicate elven ear.

"Thanks, Aeli. That saved me a trip to the bath," Silas said, resting his hand on her head for a moment before turning his gaze toward the heavy oak door. "By the way, do you know where Thora is right now? I have a bit of business to discuss with her regarding the territory’s projects."
Aeliana leaned into his palm, her green eyes closing briefly in pure satisfaction as her long ears twitched.

"Thora is still downstairs in the Culinary Haven, My Lord," Aeli reported, her tone crisp and informative as she opened her eyes. "She and Kaelia have been working continuously on brewing that new batch of alcohol using the spirit herbs harvested from Eluned."
"Alright, I’ll go check on them," Silas said, pushing his heavy leather chair back and preparing to stand up from his desk.
Before he could fully rise, Aeli stepped directly into his path, blocking his exit.
She looked up at him with an eager hopeful expression, her fingers fidgeting slightly with the hem of her robes.
"My Lord... if I may ask," Aeli began, her voice dropping into a soft hesitant whisper that caught his attention. "Could you perhaps spare a bit of time for something with me first?"
Silas paused, looking closely at her face.
He saw the genuine anticipation shining in her eyes, mixed with a nervous energy that was rare for his usually composed elf.
"Sure," Silas replied without hesitation, offering her a warm easy smile. "I’ve got time. What do you need, Aeli?"
Aeliana’s entire face lit up instantly. She extended her slender, pale hand toward him with her fingers reaching out expectantly in the soft light.
"It will take a bit of time," she told him softly, her voice brimming with quiet excitement.
Silas reached out and took her hand, wrapping his broad calloused fingers tight around her warm palm.
"I’m completely free," Silas grinned, standing up to his full height. "Carry me anywhere you want."
Aeli giggled, her silver eyes flashing with a sudden intense surge of spatial mana.
ZIP!
The spatial air around them warped instantly.
In a blinding flash of silver starlight and crackling spatial pressure, the stone office vanished from around them, replaced in an instant by the cool open night air of the territory.
A fraction of a second later, their boots settled onto the snow-dusted stone pavement right in front of the Keep’s grand Library.
Silas blinked, stabilizing his footing as he looked up at the massive magnificent building standing before them.
The library was a towering structure of carved marble and ancient timber, its tall arched windows glowing with warm yellow light from within.
Snowflakes drifted down softly from the dark night sky, dusting the arched roof and the carved pillars framing the main entrance.
’It’s still beautiful man...’
Even in the middle of a cold winter evening, Silas noticed something sitting along the covered stone porch that brought a warm satisfied smile to his face.
Arranged in neat, orderly rows along the raised wooden racks were dozens of pairs of boots, slippers, and combat footwear left behind by the territory’s girls.
It was clear proof that the combatants were actively taking advantage of the facility he had built for them.

They weren’t just training their muscles, swinging broadswords, and firing spells in the dirt... they were spending their precious free time reading, expanding their minds, learning history, and studying elemental theory!
’I really need to make time to read more in here myself,’ Silas thought, admiring the peaceful studious atmosphere radiating from the structure.

Following the established rules of the house, Silas and Aeli stepped onto the stone porch, slipped off their heavy footwear, and set them neatly beside the others before pushing open the heavy oak double doors.
Stepping inside, the warm, magic-heated air of the library wrapped around them like a comfortable blanket, carrying the comforting scent of old books, polished wood, leather bindings, and dried ink.
The main lobby was wide, grand, and brilliantly lit by floating mana lanterns that drifted lazily near the vaulted ceiling.
Several female combatants were seated around the long reading tables scattered across the ground floor lobby.
Near one of the tall stained-glass windows, an older girl clad in a simple linen shirt was sitting right beside a younger Scout, patiently teaching her how to read.
The older girl held her finger against a thick, leather-bound textbook, pointing directly at a word and pronouncing it clearly.
"S-O-V-E-R-E-I-G-N."
The younger girl stared intently at the page, carefully repeating the pronunciation out loud before jotting it down in her notebook with a small piece of charcoal.
Silas smiled genuinely at the sight, feeling a deep sense of pride settling into his chest.
’It’s like we’re all one big family... I love it.’ Silas thought.
As they walked past the quiet study area, Aeli leaned in close to him with her breath warm against his shoulder as she reported in a quiet whisper.
"During the time that we were away in the Secret Realm, My Lord, I left Reina in charge of managing the daily operations of the library."
The exact moment her name was spoken, a pair of sharp fluffy wolf ears twitched atop the main reception counter across the lobby.
"Wooh?~"
Reina perked up immediately, popping her head up from behind a stack of tall cataloging ledgers and leather logs.
Seeing her Lord and Aeli standing together in the lobby, her face gave a sudden involuntary blush behind her counter before she quickly caught herself.
Her face twitched slightly as she desperately tried to suppress her excitement and maintain her stern professional librarian demeanor.
Sitting right beside her on the polished wooden counter was one of the Blessed Wolf pups... Princess.
"Yip!"
The little wolf pup let out a tiny enthusiastic sound that echoed softly through the quiet hall.
It immediately sat up straight on its hind legs, waving its small front paw at Silas in an adorable energetic greeting.
Reina bowed respectfully from behind the desk.
"Welcome back, Lord Silas, Lady Aeliana."
Silas chuckled, waving his hand back at the energetic wolf pup.

"Hey there, girl." He looked over at Reina and gave her an approving, appreciative nod. "Great job keeping the place running while we were gone, Reina. Your hard work really shows. I’ll make sure to reward you properly later."
Reina’s ears perked up even higher at his words, a visible blush dusting her cheeks as she bowed deeply again behind the counter. "Thank you, My Lord! It is my honor and duty!"
Aeli smiled gently at the exchange, then took Silas’s hand again, guiding him past the ground floor study tables toward the grand, spiraling wooden staircase situated at the back of the central hall.

They ascended the steps smoothly with their socked feet making barely a sound against the polished timber, stepping onto the quiet elevated balcony level where the higher-tier texts, rare spell books, and historical archives were stored.
Aeli led him down a quiet secluded aisle between two towering bookshelves filled with ancient tomes.
She stopped at a cozy, private reading table set right beside an arched window overlooking the snow-covered courtyard below.

Sitting squarely in the center of the dark oak table were several thick, leather-bound journal books... the exact same high-quality journals that Silas had bought for her at the market when he was giving everyone gifts.
Silas looked down at the neatly stacked journals, then turned his golden eyes to Aeliana.
The elven arcanist nervously shifted her footing with her long fingers intertwining in front of her dress as she looked down at the table.
Her cheeks flushed a delicate lovely shade of pink.

"Ever since you gave me these books, My Lord..." Aeli confessed softly. "I have thought about what to write for so long... Back then, when I first told you that I wanted to write a story, it felt so simple and easy to just say the words out loud but once I actually sat down with the blank pages and picked up the quill, I realized just how difficult it truly is to weave a whole world together."

chapters.title: Chapter 229: The Blessed Drink [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She paused, looking up at him through her long fluttering eyelashes with a small self-deprecating chuckle escaping her lips.

"Hehe~ But after everything that has happened recently... after watching you fight in the Secret Realm, watching our territory grow day by day, and living through all these moments together... I finally have the very first Chapter written down. I... I really wanted you to check it out first before anyone else sees it."
She picked up the top leather journal with gentle care, holding it out toward him with slightly trembling hands.
"Who knows?" Aeli joked nervously, trying to ease her own mounting anxiety. "I could maybe become a best-selling author throughout the realm one day... though I highly doubt it."
Silas reached out, gently taking the heavy journal from her hands. He looked deeply into her green eyes with his expression turning warm and reassuring.

"Don’t be so hard on yourself, Aeli," Silas told her firmly. "Never lack confidence in your own work and for what it’s worth, I actually have quite a bit of experience reading web novels back on Earth. I’ll check it out right now and give you an honest review."
Aeli’s eyes sparkled with deep, overwhelming gratitude. "Thank you, My Lord!"
Silas pulled out the plush wooden chair set at the table and sat down, opening the dark leather cover of the journal.
He flipped past the blank flyleaf to the very first page, glancing at the neat elegant and perfectly uniform elven handwriting covering the paper from top to bottom.
"How many pages is this first Chapter?" Silas asked, thumbing through the thick paper leaves.
"It’s about three pages, My Lord," Aeli answered attentively, stepping closer and leaning eagerly over his shoulder to watch him read.
Silas paused, looking up at her with a raised eyebrow and a dry look. "Three pages? That’s awfully short for a single novel Chapter."
Aeliana’s face instantly reddened.
She looked thoroughly confused by his statement, tilting her head slightly as her delicate ears twitched in confusion.
"Is... is it?" Aeli asked innocently, her voice filled with genuine curiosity and panic. "How long is one Chapter supposed to be?"
Silas chuckled softly, reaching up to pat her shoulder gently to calm her sudden panic.

"Relax, Aeli. In modern web novel formatting back where I come from, a solid proper Chapter is usually at least four to six thousand words... around ten to fifteen dense pages if you’re writing it out by hand but three pages is totally fine for a first draft. Let me see what you’ve got here."
Aeli nodded rapidly, her heart pounding as she stood closely beside his chair with her hands clasped against her ribs while Silas focused his attention back on her handwritten page.
He looked at the very first sentence written at the top of the Chapter, reading the words internally in his thoughts.

’The grand dragon-slaying Lord pinned the trembling elven maiden against the cold silk sheets, his massive two meter pillar of pure masculine dominance throbbing with unspeakable desire as he prepared to claim her maidenhood...’
Silas froze completely solid.
His golden-ringed eyes widened as far as they physically could.
He read the sentence a second time just to make sure his Gold Core wasn’t suffering from magical hallucinations or exhaustion.
He blinked once, twice, staring at the exquisite, graceful elven handwriting ink on the paper, before slowly turning his head to look up at Aeliana standing beside him.
"Aeli..." Silas said, his voice completely flat and dripping with utter disbelief. "...are you writing smut?"
Aeliana’s entire face instantly exploded into a bright, blinding shade of crimson!
Her long elven ears burned red clear to the tips, but she didn’t run away, cover her face, or hide.
Instead, she stood her ground right next to his chair, looking at him with wide and completely innocent eyes.

"Y-Yes, My Lord!" Aeli admitted stammeringly, her cheeks burning like hot coals. "Back when I used to live in the Royal Palace as a Royal Elf... my aunt used to sneak those exact kinds of romance books into the court libraries! So... so I don’t think they are bad at all..."
She tilted her head slightly, looking down at his expression with a mix of intense anxiety and naive curiosity.
"...Do you?"
Silas felt an uncharacteristic warm blush creeping up his own neck.
He cleared his throat loudly, shifting slightly in the wooden chair as he desperately tried to maintain his composure as a stern Warlord.
"I... I don’t either..." Silas muttered, raising a hand to rub the back of his neck. "I was just... taken aback. I wasn’t expecting pillars on page one, line one."
Aeli gulped nervously with her heart hammering wildly against her ribs like a trapped bird as Silas turned his focus back to the leather-bound journal.

’Does he like it?!’ Aeli thought frantically in her head, her fingers tightly clenching the fabric of her dress as her silver eyes watched his pupils move line by line across her handwriting. ’What if he thinks it’s completely ridiculous?! What if he hates it and tells me to stop writing?! I tried my hardest on the descriptions... and I really, really hope he doesn’t realize that the female lead in the story is literally modeled after me, and the male lead is literally him!’
Silas spent the next ten minutes reading through the entire first Chapter carefully, word by word.
Aside from the shockingly explicit, uninhibited adult themes woven directly into the romantic encounter, Aeliana’s prose was surprisingly vivid and engaging.
Her descriptions of the setting, the weight behind the characters’ dialogue, the underlying longing and the building tension were remarkably well-crafted for a first-time author.
She had an undeniable natural talent for storytelling.
’I mean she’s an Elf so it should be expected right?’
When he reached the final line at the bottom of the third page, Silas closed the leather journal with a soft click and set it down on the dark oak table.
He leaned back in his chair, folding his arms as he looked up at the visibly shaking, anxious elf standing beside him.

"Overall," Silas announced, a genuine, warm smile breaking across his face, "it’s actually really good, Aeli... Your descriptive writing is incredible, and the pacing holds the reader’s attention really well."
Aeli let out a massive audible breath of relief, her entire body slumping as if a massive weight had just been physically lifted off her shoulders. "R-Really, My Lord?!"

"Really," Silas nodded firmly. "You’ve got a real gift for prose but since you asked for my critique and advice, there are a few technical things you definitely need to work on. First off... your scale and measurements are completely wild."
Silas picked up the journal again, flipping it open to page two and pointing his calloused finger at a specific line halfway down the sheet.

"Right here," Silas pointed out, chuckling softly. "You wrote that the male lead’s sword was ’two meters long’ when describing his personal weapon during the bed scene. Aeli... two meters is over six feet long. That isn’t a human anatomical organ... that is a literal siege spear or a war pike. You mistook inches for meters."
Aeli stared at the line he was pointing at, her eyes widening as she calculated the horror of what she had written.
She instantly covered her entire face with both hands, letting out a mortified high-pitched squeak that echoed softly down the library aisle.
"Oh gods!" Aeli squealed through her fingers, her ears drooping. "Two meters?! I... I mixed up the units from the trade books!"
Silas laughed warmly, standing up from the chair and giving her shoulder a reassuring, firm pat.

"It’s fine. It’s an easy fix. Just adjust the measurements to realistic numbers, expand the setup and buildup a bit more before jumping straight into the heavy action, and you’re good to go. You’ve got real potential, Aeli."
Aeli slowly uncovered her blushing face, looking up at him with a deeply flattered heart-melting smile that lit up her green eyes.
She picked up the leather journal from the table, holding it tightly against her chest as if it were a prized treasure, and bowed deeply to him.

"Thank you so much, My Lord!" Aeli said earnestly, her voice filled with newfound determination and confidence. "I will take every single piece of your advice into consideration and rewrite the entire Chapter immediately!"
"Good luck," Silas smiled, giving her soft silver hair one last pat. "Just don’t stay up all night writing. We have work to do tomorrow."
Silas turned and walked back toward the spiraling wooden stairs, descending smoothly to the ground floor.

He exchanged friendly greetings with a few more of the Vanguard and other girls studying at the tables, waved a quiet goodbye to Reina and the little wolf pup at the reception counter, and pushed open the heavy oak double doors, stepping back out into the snow-filled courtyard.

He pulled his black coat tight around his broad shoulders against the falling snow with his boots crunching quietly as he walked across the courtyard toward the territory’s dedicated kitchen facility... the Culinary Haven.
He reached the heavy timber doors of the building, reaching out his hand to push them open.
"Let’s see how this brewing project is going..." Silas muttered quietly to himself as he stepped over the threshold.
However, the second the heavy wooden door swung fully open, Silas’s eyes went wide.
He froze completely dead in his tracks with his feet glued to the floorboards as his brain desperately struggled to process the apocalyptic chaos unfolding inside the room.
He truly did not expect what he saw.
The Culinary Haven was in disarray.
Standing right in the center of the main room, right next to the smoking copper brewing stills, was Morwenna.
The tough legendary Pirate Queen was holding a massive wooden tankard filled to the brim with a strange, glowing, thick white liquid.
With a fierce grin, she threw her head back and downed the entire cup in a single continuous and terrifying gulp.
GULP! GULP! GULP!
The exact second the white liquid hit her stomach, Morwenna’s feral gray eyes went completely blank.
Her knees instantly buckled beneath her, and the fearsome pirate collapsed sideways like a felled tree, landing face-first onto the wooden floorboards with a thud, completely knocked out cold!
Beside her at the long dining table was Eluned. The ancient SSS-Rank Nature Goddess was already completely face-down on the oak table, thoroughly knocked out cold.
’Eluned, knocked out? How strong is that thing?!’
Her long silver-green hair was splayed wildly across the wood, and her lips were moving softly as she mumbled coherent nonsense into the tablecloth.
"Thorns... sweet apples... my Lord’s chest is so warm... pirate is a filthy bilge-rat... mmm..."

Off to the right side of the room, Kaelia, the territory’s elite master chef, was slumped over a pile of flour sacks, fast asleep with a sweet peaceful smile on her face, completely out cold from tasting her own creation.
Even Talira, the devastatingly arrogant Primordial Crimson Dragon, was caught directly in the middle of the carnage.
The terrifying dragon was sitting cross-legged in the far corner of the room, her flawless face burning an intense glowing bright shade of crimson.

Her vertical reptilian pupils were totally unfocused and crossed as she played mindlessly with her small scaled dragon wings, gently petting her own red feathers and whispering softly to them in a high-pitched voice.
"Good girls... you’re such good little wings... yes you are... best wings in the world..."
That was how Silas knew without a single shadow of a doubt that the ancient dragon was thoroughly blasted drunk.
And standing right in the dead center of the main dining table, towering over the fallen, unconscious bodies of her comrades like a conquering warlord, was Thora.
The heavily muscled dwarf forge-mistress was completely wild.
She had stripped off her thick leather blacksmith apron and her tunic, standing atop the wooden furniture in just her undershirt and trousers.
Held high in her right hand, being spun vigorously around her head like a victory lasso, was Kaelia’s lacy white bra!
Thora executed a hilarious victory dance on top of the oak table, her booming voice echoing off the rafters as she roared at the top of her lungs.
"WOOOOOOOH! WE CREATED ALCOHOL, LADIES! LET’S CALL IT THE BLESSED DRINK!"
"What the hell are you all doing?" Silas demanded, his voice flat as he stood in the open doorway of the Culinary Haven, staring at the chaotic scene before him.
Thora snapped her head toward the entrance with a wild victorious grin spreading across her flushed face.
She wiped a stray drop of sweat from her brow, tossing her head back with a booming laugh that shook the copper kettles hanging from the ceiling beams.

"Welcome to the Culinary Haven, My Lord!" Thora shouted over the humming heat of the brewing stills, waving her arm wide in a grand dramatic flourish. "You’re just in time to witness history in the making!"

paragraphs: Silas stepped inside, closing the heavy wooden door behind him to block out the swirling winter wind.
The air inside the room was thick and warm, smelling heavily of fermented star-apples, sweet floral nectar, and a sharp bite that made his nose sting.
"Care to explain what happened here?" Silas asked, gesturing toward the bodies scattered across the furniture and floorboards. "It looks like a battle took place."
Thora hopped down from the main oak table with a heavy thud of her iron-soled boots, though she stumbled slightly before catching her balance against the edge of a bench.
She grabbed a small glass vessel sitting atop a brass tray and held it up proudly into the ambient light.
Inside the glass was a thick, luminescent liquid that swirled with dark crimson and gold threads.

"We’ve just finished producing a brand-new, ultra-concentrated variant of alcohol!" Thora declared proudly with her chest puffing out. "It’s a completely original blend! We gathered the golden star-apples and divine floral nectar harvested from Eluned’s personal trees, combined them with the raw energy of the Sovereign Realm’s atmosphere, and refined it all through three cycles of heat distillation!"
She raised the small glass vial higher, tapping her finger against the crystal rim.
"And for the final catalyst, we introduced a drop of purified, high-tier monster blood extracted from the core beasts in the eastern forest!"
Silas blinked, his eyebrows drawing together as he stared at the glowing crimson fluid in her hands.
"Isn’t that just poisoning yourselves?" Silas asked drily. "You’re literally drinking monster blood and raw divine nectar."

"Nonsense!" Thora barked with a dismissive wave of her calloused hand. "The monster blood was completely purified through my forge filters! All the toxic impurities were burnt away by Talira’s fire before we added it to the batch! It doesn’t poison the body... it just delivers a massive instantaneous rush of elemental energy directly to the bloodstream! It’s completely safe!"
Silas looked past the dwarf forge-mistress, eyeing the four women strewn across the room in various states of unconsciousness.
Right beside the copper distillation stills, Morwenna was sprawled out face-first on the wooden floor with her gray eyes entirely glossed over while her arms dangled limp at her sides.
At the central table, Eluned lay face-down against the oak planks, her long silver-green hair spread out like a fan over scattered parchment sheets.
Over by the pantry sacks, Kaelia was curled up on her side, fast asleep with a peaceful, foolish smile on her face, completely oblivious to her surroundings.
And in the far corner of the room sat Talira still sat there playing with her wings.
Silas let out a slow, long sigh, rubbing the bridge of his nose.

The fact that a primordial dragon from what Aeli had told him about her strength and an SSS-Rank nature deity were both completely incapacitated proved that Thora’s concoction worked, but managing the aftermath was going to be a headache.
"Right," Silas muttered, looking over the room once more. "If only Aeli was her—"
ZIP!
A sudden sharp ripple of spatial energy tore through the air right beside his left arm.
In a flash of pale silver light, Aeliana materialized out of thin air, standing perfectly composed beside him with her hands folded neatly over her robes.
"You called me, My Lord?" Aeli asked softly, her silver eyes looking up at him with instant, crisp readiness.
Silas flinched slightly, taking a half-step back in surprise. "Whoa. I wasn’t expecting you to appear that fast."
Aeli’s long elven ears twitched, a delicate pink blush creeping up her cheeks as she lowered her head slightly.
"Ah..." Aeli stammered softly, her eyes flickering with sudden nervousness. "Did... did you not want me here, My Lord? I can return to the library if I am intruding..."

"No, no, that’s not it at all," Silas interrupted smoothly, holding up a hand to reassure her. "I actually really need your help right now. Look at this mess. I need you to carry these four back to where they belong so they don’t freeze on the floor."
He pointed toward the table where the nature deity and the pirate queen were slumped over.

"Take both Eluned and Morwenna up to my private quarters in the Keep and put them on the bed," Silas instructed. "As for Talira and Kaelia, take them over to the Barracks quarters so they can sleep it off."
"Understood, My Lord," Aeli replied without a moment’s hesitation.
The elven arcanist walked briskly across the room, stepping past the discarded cups and copper tubing.
She reached the table and effortlessly scooped Eluned into her left arm, then reached down and pulled Morwenna up over her right shoulder.
With a brief surge of silver spatial mana coiling around her boots, Aeli vanished from the room in a silent blur.
Thora crossed her arms over her chest, letting out a loud disappointed pestering sound.
"Tch! The fun was just getting started! You’re no fun, Captain!"
Silas ignored her complaint and walked straight up to the dwarf forge-mistress. He stopped directly in front of her, looking down into her wide brown eyes with a serious expression.
"Get on," Silas said calmly. "I have a favor to ask of you."
Thora paused, her eyes widening in genuine surprise.
She stared up at him, her mouth opening slightly.
Her Lord was usually a man of few words when it came to physical actions... he usually just grabbed her collar or hauled her up by her belt whenever he needed her on his shoulders.
He had never used his actual mouth to explicitly ask her to climb onto him like that before.
’Or has he...? I don’t actually remember however... Is this situation that serious?’ Thora thought, her heart giving a strange fluttery beat inside her chest.
Without arguing or throwing out her usual cheeky remarks, Thora set the vial of purified monster blood carefully down on the table.
She reached up with both hands, gripping Silas’s broad shoulders, and pulled herself up with ease, swinging her legs around to settle comfortably atop his neck and shoulders.
Silas turned around and began walking toward the exit.
Just as his hand touched the iron latch of the door, another silver flash erupted in the corner of the room.
Aeli reappeared beside the fallen forms of Talira and Kaelia. She gathered the sleeping dragon and the unconscious chef into her arms, preparing to teleport away once more.
Silas glanced over his shoulder, catching Aeli’s eye.
"Thank you, Aeli," Silas told her warmly.
Aeli’s face lit up with a breathtaking, radiant smile.
"It is my pleasure, Lord Silas," she whispered, and with another soft shimmer of silver light, she vanished from the Culinary Haven completely.
Silas pushed open the timber door and stepped out into the crisp, cold air, pulling the door shut behind them.
The winter storm was sweeping through the Keep’s courtyard in full force now.
Gentle powdery white snowflakes drifted down from the pitch-black night sky, coating the stone walkways, roof tiles, and wooden fences in a pristine, untouched layer of white.
The cold wind bit against Silas’s face, instantly clearing away the lingering fumes of fermented alcohol and magic herbs from his senses.
Thora rested her hands on top of Silas’s head, leaning forward slightly as she looked up at the sky.

"By the Ancestors..." Thora murmured, her voice dropping into a rare quiet awe. "It really is beautiful out here tonight, isn’t it? Back in the underground mountain holds where I grew up, we had stone caverns and lava flows, but we never had sky-fall like this. I’ve barely seen real snow in my entire life before coming to your territory."
Silas walked at a steady pace with his heavy boots crunching through the fresh layer of snow covering the cobblestones.
"Yeah," Silas agreed softly, gazing out across the quiet glowing courtyard. "It’s beautiful."
Thora let out a playful chuckle from above his head, her mood shifting back to her usual boisterous self.
She patted his forehead twice with her thick palm.
"Well, My Lord, I know I’m beautiful," Thora boasted smugly, tilting her chin up. "But why did you call me out here like this? What’s this favor you need?"
Silas adjusted his footing, keeping his balance as he carried her across the open square.
"I need your help," Silas said plainly. "I need a disguise."
Thora blinked, leaning over his forehead to stare down at his face in total confusion.
"A disguise?" Thora asked, her nose scrunching up. "Why the hell would you need a disguise? You’re handsome, you’re built like an ox, and you’ve got a big dick! Why would you hide a face like yours?"
Silas cleared his throat loudly, a sudden uncomfortable cough escaping his chest as his cheeks warmed slightly in the freezing wind.

"Let’s stay on topic," Silas muttered, shaking his head. "You know that our Territory is becoming quite famous back in my original world. The World Council and the local Government are paying close attention to everything happening and they’re increasing how much they’re offering. Well... I want to make a public appearance to our Government soon, but I don’t want to do it in my regular body or reveal my true identity to them yet."
Silas wanted to get top tier resources for the sake of his territory...
Thora’s eyes lit up with sudden, intense interest. She slapped her hand against her knee.
"Ah! You want to have a secret identity!" Thora exclaimed, nodding her head vigorously. "I think that’s bloody brilliant, My Lord! It’s way better that way! Keep those government bastards guessing!"
She leaned down further, wrapping both of her thick, muscular arms around Silas’s head, pulling his face tightly against her chest in a fierce, affectionate hug.

"Usually, you’re always running back and forth between Earth and here," Thora spoke softly against his spiky dark hair with her voice genuinely tender. "You barely have any time to just sit down and spend time with us without worrying about some external crisis... I’d be honored to make sure you don’t get found out by those high-and-mighty bureaucrats."
Silas felt a rare swell of warm appreciation in his chest. He cleared his throat again, speaking through her tight grip.
"Thanks, Thora. This is actually one of the very first times that you’re being genuinely respectfu—"

"Haahn~!" Thora suddenly let out a sharp breathless moan right into his ear with her body trembling slightly atop his shoulders. "Yes... let me squeeze you just like that~! Mmm, your spiky hair is touching my panties through my trousers, My Lord... ahh, it’s making me so hot!"
Silas froze instantly.
He closed his eyes, a vein throbbing prominently on his temple. He immediately regretted every single warm, appreciative thought that had just passed through his mind a fraction of a second prior.
"We’re here..." Silas said deadpan, striding forward and arriving at the massive double iron doors of the territory’s main forge.
Thora giggled wildly, hopping down from his shoulders and landing lightly on her feet.
She pushed open the heavy reinforced doors, allowing a wave of intense roaring heat to instantly blast out into the freezing night air.
"Welcome to the Foundry, My Lord!" Thora announced with a cheeky grin, gesturing inside.
Silas stepped through the threshold, feeling the sudden wall of heat melt the snow on his coat instantly.

The interior of the Foundry was a magnificent sight... furnaces roared with intense elemental fire, racks of high-tier weapons lined the stone walls, and the deep scent of heated iron and melted ore hung thick in the air.
Thora closed the heavy iron doors behind him, shutting out the storm, and immediately scurried deeper into the workshop.
She ran over to the main anvil in the center of the forge room, where a large glowing ingot of silver metal was sitting inside a containment brazier.

"Look at this!" Thora called out excitedly, pointing her tongs at the metal. "I’ve had this block of Sil-Grave metal sitting in draconic flames summoned from Talira for three full days straight to discover its melting point! And even after all that heat... it hasn’t lost a single fraction of its structural density! It’s incredible! I haven’t even found its melting limit yet!"

sentences.text: Silas stepped inside, closing the heavy wooden door behind him to block out the swirling winter wind.
The air inside the room was thick and warm, smelling heavily of fermented star-apples, sweet floral nectar, and a sharp bite that made his nose sting.
"Care to explain what happened here?" Silas asked, gesturing toward the bodies scattered across the furniture and floorboards.
"It looks like a battle took place."
Thora hopped down from the main oak table with a heavy thud of her iron-soled boots, though she stumbled slightly before catching her balance against the edge of a bench.
She grabbed a small glass vessel sitting atop a brass tray and held it up proudly into the ambient light.
Inside the glass was a thick, luminescent liquid that swirled with dark crimson and gold threads.
"We’ve just finished producing a brand-new, ultra-concentrated variant of alcohol!" Thora declared proudly with her chest puffing out.
"It’s a completely original blend!

We gathered the golden star-apples and divine floral nectar harvested from Eluned’s personal trees, combined them with the raw energy of the Sovereign Realm’s atmosphere, and refined it all through three cycles of heat distillation!"
She raised the small glass vial higher, tapping her finger against the crystal rim.
"And for the final catalyst, we introduced a drop of purified, high-tier monster blood extracted from the core beasts in the eastern forest!"
Silas blinked, his eyebrows drawing together as he stared at the glowing crimson fluid in her hands.
"Isn’t that just poisoning yourselves?" Silas asked drily.
"You’re literally drinking monster blood and raw divine nectar."
"Nonsense!" Thora barked with a dismissive wave of her calloused hand.
"The monster blood was completely purified through my forge filters!
All the toxic impurities were burnt away by Talira’s fire before we added it to the batch!
It doesn’t poison the body... it just delivers a massive instantaneous rush of elemental energy directly to the bloodstream!
It’s completely safe!"
Silas looked past the dwarf forge-mistress, eyeing the four women strewn across the room in various states of unconsciousness.
Right beside the copper distillation stills, Morwenna was sprawled out face-first on the wooden floor with her gray eyes entirely glossed over while her arms dangled limp at her sides.
At the central table, Eluned lay face-down against the oak planks, her long silver-green hair spread out like a fan over scattered parchment sheets.
Over by the pantry sacks, Kaelia was curled up on her side, fast asleep with a peaceful, foolish smile on her face, completely oblivious to her surroundings.
And in the far corner of the room sat Talira still sat there playing with her wings.
Silas let out a slow, long sigh, rubbing the bridge of his nose.

The fact that a primordial dragon from what Aeli had told him about her strength and an SSS-Rank nature deity were both completely incapacitated proved that Thora’s concoction worked, but managing the aftermath was going to be a headache.
"Right," Silas muttered, looking over the room once more.
"If only Aeli was her—"
ZIP!
A sudden sharp ripple of spatial energy tore through the air right beside his left arm.
In a flash of pale silver light, Aeliana materialized out of thin air, standing perfectly composed beside him with her hands folded neatly over her robes.
"You called me, My Lord?" Aeli asked softly, her silver eyes looking up at him with instant, crisp readiness.
Silas flinched slightly, taking a half-step back in surprise.
"Whoa.
I wasn’t expecting you to appear that fast."
Aeli’s long elven ears twitched, a delicate pink blush creeping up her cheeks as she lowered her head slightly.
"Ah..." Aeli stammered softly, her eyes flickering with sudden nervousness.
"Did... did you not want me here, My Lord?
I can return to the library if I am intruding..."
"No, no, that’s not it at all," Silas interrupted smoothly, holding up a hand to reassure her.
"I actually really need your help right now.
Look at this mess.
I need you to carry these four back to where they belong so they don’t freeze on the floor."
He pointed toward the table where the nature deity and the pirate queen were slumped over.
"Take both Eluned and Morwenna up to my private quarters in the Keep and put them on the bed," Silas instructed.
"As for Talira and Kaelia, take them over to the Barracks quarters so they can sleep it off."
"Understood, My Lord," Aeli replied without a moment’s hesitation.
The elven arcanist walked briskly across the room, stepping past the discarded cups and copper tubing.
She reached the table and effortlessly scooped Eluned into her left arm, then reached down and pulled Morwenna up over her right shoulder.
With a brief surge of silver spatial mana coiling around her boots, Aeli vanished from the room in a silent blur.
Thora crossed her arms over her chest, letting out a loud disappointed pestering sound.
"Tch!
The fun was just getting started!
You’re no fun, Captain!"
Silas ignored her complaint and walked straight up to the dwarf forge-mistress.
He stopped directly in front of her, looking down into her wide brown eyes with a serious expression.
"Get on," Silas said calmly.
"I have a favor to ask of you."
Thora paused, her eyes widening in genuine surprise.
She stared up at him, her mouth opening slightly.
Her Lord was usually a man of few words when it came to physical actions... he usually just grabbed her collar or hauled her up by her belt whenever he needed her on his shoulders.
He had never used his actual mouth to explicitly ask her to climb onto him like that before.
’Or has he...?
I don’t actually remember however...
Is this situation that serious?’ Thora thought, her heart giving a strange fluttery beat inside her chest.
Without arguing or throwing out her usual cheeky remarks, Thora set the vial of purified monster blood carefully down on the table.
She reached up with both hands, gripping Silas’s broad shoulders, and pulled herself up with ease, swinging her legs around to settle comfortably atop his neck and shoulders.
Silas turned around and began walking toward the exit.
Just as his hand touched the iron latch of the door, another silver flash erupted in the corner of the room.
Aeli reappeared beside the fallen forms of Talira and Kaelia.
She gathered the sleeping dragon and the unconscious chef into her arms, preparing to teleport away once more.
Silas glanced over his shoulder, catching Aeli’s eye.
"Thank you, Aeli," Silas told her warmly.
Aeli’s face lit up with a breathtaking, radiant smile.
"It is my pleasure, Lord Silas," she whispered, and with another soft shimmer of silver light, she vanished from the Culinary Haven completely.
Silas pushed open the timber door and stepped out into the crisp, cold air, pulling the door shut behind them.
The winter storm was sweeping through the Keep’s courtyard in full force now.
Gentle powdery white snowflakes drifted down from the pitch-black night sky, coating the stone walkways, roof tiles, and wooden fences in a pristine, untouched layer of white.
The cold wind bit against Silas’s face, instantly clearing away the lingering fumes of fermented alcohol and magic herbs from his senses.
Thora rested her hands on top of Silas’s head, leaning forward slightly as she looked up at the sky.
"By the Ancestors..." Thora murmured, her voice dropping into a rare quiet awe.
"It really is beautiful out here tonight, isn’t it?
Back in the underground mountain holds where I grew up, we had stone caverns and lava flows, but we never had sky-fall like this.
I’ve barely seen real snow in my entire life before coming to your territory."
Silas walked at a steady pace with his heavy boots crunching through the fresh layer of snow covering the cobblestones.
"Yeah," Silas agreed softly, gazing out across the quiet glowing courtyard.
"It’s beautiful."
Thora let out a playful chuckle from above his head, her mood shifting back to her usual boisterous self.
She patted his forehead twice with her thick palm.
"Well, My Lord, I know I’m beautiful," Thora boasted smugly, tilting her chin up.
"But why did you call me out here like this?
What’s this favor you need?"
Silas adjusted his footing, keeping his balance as he carried her across the open square.
"I need your help," Silas said plainly.
"I need a disguise."
Thora blinked, leaning over his forehead to stare down at his face in total confusion.
"A disguise?" Thora asked, her nose scrunching up.
"Why the hell would you need a disguise?
You’re handsome, you’re built like an ox, and you’ve got a big dick!
Why would you hide a face like yours?"
Silas cleared his throat loudly, a sudden uncomfortable cough escaping his chest as his cheeks warmed slightly in the freezing wind.
"Let’s stay on topic," Silas muttered, shaking his head.
"You know that our Territory is becoming quite famous back in my original world.
The World Council and the local Government are paying close attention to everything happening and they’re increasing how much they’re offering.
Well...
I want to make a public appearance to our Government soon, but I don’t want to do it in my regular body or reveal my true identity to them yet."
Silas wanted to get top tier resources for the sake of his territory...
Thora’s eyes lit up with sudden, intense interest.
She slapped her hand against her knee.
"Ah!
You want to have a secret identity!" Thora exclaimed, nodding her head vigorously.
"I think that’s bloody brilliant, My Lord!
It’s way better that way!
Keep those government bastards guessing!"
She leaned down further, wrapping both of her thick, muscular arms around Silas’s head, pulling his face tightly against her chest in a fierce, affectionate hug.
"Usually, you’re always running back and forth between Earth and here," Thora spoke softly against his spiky dark hair with her voice genuinely tender.
"You barely have any time to just sit down and spend time with us without worrying about some external crisis...
I’d be honored to make sure you don’t get found out by those high-and-mighty bureaucrats."
Silas felt a rare swell of warm appreciation in his chest.
He cleared his throat again, speaking through her tight grip.
"Thanks, Thora.
This is actually one of the very first times that you’re being genuinely respectfu—"
"Haahn~!" Thora suddenly let out a sharp breathless moan right into his ear with her body trembling slightly atop his shoulders.
"Yes... let me squeeze you just like that~!
Mmm, your spiky hair is touching my panties through my trousers, My Lord... ahh, it’s making me so hot!"
Silas froze instantly.
He closed his eyes, a vein throbbing prominently on his temple.
He immediately regretted every single warm, appreciative thought that had just passed through his mind a fraction of a second prior.
"We’re here..." Silas said deadpan, striding forward and arriving at the massive double iron doors of the territory’s main forge.
Thora giggled wildly, hopping down from his shoulders and landing lightly on her feet.
She pushed open the heavy reinforced doors, allowing a wave of intense roaring heat to instantly blast out into the freezing night air.
"Welcome to the Foundry, My Lord!" Thora announced with a cheeky grin, gesturing inside.
Silas stepped through the threshold, feeling the sudden wall of heat melt the snow on his coat instantly.

The interior of the Foundry was a magnificent sight... furnaces roared with intense elemental fire, racks of high-tier weapons lined the stone walls, and the deep scent of heated iron and melted ore hung thick in the air.
Thora closed the heavy iron doors behind him, shutting out the storm, and immediately scurried deeper into the workshop.
She ran over to the main anvil in the center of the forge room, where a large glowing ingot of silver metal was sitting inside a containment brazier.
"Look at this!" Thora called out excitedly, pointing her tongs at the metal.
"I’ve had this block of Sil-Grave metal sitting in draconic flames summoned from Talira for three full days straight to discover its melting point!
And even after all that heat... it hasn’t lost a single fraction of its structural density!
It’s incredible!
I haven’t even found its melting limit yet!"

chapters.title: Chapter 231: A Disguise [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas walked over, looking at the glowing block of unique metal that carried his own forged name.
"That’s impressive, Thora, but what about the disguise?"
"Right, right!" Thora said, snapping back to attention and tossing her tongs onto a wooden table.

She crossed her arms, tapping her chin thoughtfully. "Look, My Lord... crafting a proper magical disguise item from scratch takes a hell of a long time. It isn’t just a matter of slapping a fake wig and some face paint on you. If you want to fool high-tier government sensors and spiritual detection wards, you need something that restructures your entire presence but if I were to forge a proper disguise artifact from baseline materials right now, it would take weeks to months if not years of work—"
She stopped dead mid-sentence, her brown eyes going wide as saucers.
"Aha!" Thora shouted, slapping her forehead. "I have exactly what you need, My Lord!"
Silas blinked, watching in confusion as the dwarf forge-mistress turned on her heel and ran frantically toward a dusty towering wooden shelf tucked away in the far back corner of the Foundry.
She began rummaging through stacks of old iron boxes, discarded blueprints, and dusty leather pouches, throwing random metal scraps over her shoulder with wild abandon.
"Where the hell is this thing...?" Thora muttered angrily, her voice muffled as her head was buried inside a bottom cupboard. "Fucking hell... I know I put it right here..."
"What are you looking for, Thora?" Silas asked, walking over and leaning against the shelf.

"It’s a Disguise Ring!" Thora explained loudly from inside the cupboard, tossing out an old copper hammer. "I got it from my dad years and years ago back in the mountain holds! It’s an experimental prototype he built before he passed! He ended up losing the original runic scroll where he kept the design schematic, so I’ve been keeping it tucked away, trying to reverse-engineer the conduit paths in my free time!"
She pulled her head out of the cabinet, holding up a small dark object between her thumb and forefinger with a triumphant grin.
"Found it!" Thora cheered. "Look at this beauty!"
Silas leaned in closer to inspect the item.
It was a simple unadorned black metal ring. It didn’t possess any glowing runes, ornate gems, or visible magical auras.
It looked entirely ordinary, almost like a piece of tarnished iron scrap.
"This plain black ring?" Silas asked skeptically.

"Don’t judge an item by its casing, My Lord!" Thora scolded him, holding the ring out toward his hand. "Once you wear it, your physical appearance, your body structure, and even your spiritual presence will completely shift! It overwrites your outward persona on a foundational level! Go ahead, put it on!"
Silas took the cool black band from her palm. He looked at it for a brief second, then slid it smoothly onto his left ring finger.
... Nothing happened.
The air remained still. Silas looked down at his hand, then looked up at Thora with an unamused eyebrow raised.
"Nothing’s happening, Thora." Silas said flatly.
"Eh?" Thora grunted, leaning in close and staring at the ring on his finger. "Hold on, that’s impossible..."
She reached out and gave the black band a hard energetic tap with her fingernail. "Maybe the internal mana conduit is defective after sitting in a dusty drawer for so long...?"
The instant her fingernail made contact with the metal—
BOOM.
A violent surge of deep purple mana suddenly erupted from the black ring!
The purple light swirled outward like a roaring vortex, completely enveloping Silas’s entire six-foot-two frame in a glowing opaque pillar of magic!

The spatial pressure inside the Foundry spiked as the ring forcefully re-wrote his physical parameters from the ground up, compressing his skeletal structure, altering his conduits, and shifting his spiritual frequency.
Thora shielded her eyes with her forearm, taking two steps back as the purple light pulsed violently three times before slowly dissolving into the warm air.
When the light finally cleared, Silas Graves was completely gone.
Standing in his place was a woman.
The woman was noticeably shorter than Silas’s original height, standing at roughly five-foot-seven.
Her body was clad in a simple black button-down shirt and fitted black trousers.
However, her left sleeve dangled empty from her shoulder, rolling loosely in the warm draft of the forge... she only possessed a single right arm!
Her hair was a sleek pitch-black shade that fell loosely to her shoulders, framing a sharp strikingly beautiful face.
And as she slowly opened her eyelids, her eyes shone with a deep radiant mysterious purple color that possessed no trace of Silas’s original golden rings.
Thora stood frozen, her mouth hanging wide open in pure awe as she gawked at the figure standing before her.
Silas looked down at her hands or rather, her single right hand and flexed her fingers.
She brought her right hand up, looking at her smooth, pale skin and her narrower wrist.
"This is weird..." Silas spoke out loud.
Her voice had changed completely.
It was no longer a deep gravelly baritone... it was a smooth and slightly raspy but very womanly voice.
Silas took two steps forward, feeling the shift in her center of gravity.
She was shorter, her frame was far lighter, and the complete absence of a left arm felt strangely natural, as if her body had been born that way.
Stranger still, there was zero pain or phantom ache coming from her empty left shoulder.
Before Silas could fully analyze her new center of balance, Thora snapped out of her trance.
The dwarf forge-mistress darted forward like a striking predator, reaching out with both hands and firmly grabbing a massive handful of Silas’s newly shaped, perky rear end!
SLAP!
"Hey!" Silas snapped, reflexively twisting her torso away and glaring down at the dwarf. "What the hell are you doing?!"
Thora pulled her hands back, holding them up in a mock gesture of surrender, though a dirty, ecstatic grin was spread across her face.

"I apologize, My Lord!" Thora giggled uncontrollably, her eyes sparkling with wild delight. "I couldn’t help myself! No matter whether you’re a rugged man or a gorgeous woman, you’re still absolutely breathtaking! Look at that firm waist and that tight ass! Is the body feeling okay for you?"
Silas let out a long breath through her nose, smoothing down the fabric of her black trousers.

"Physically, yes, the body feels completely fine," Silas admitted, examining her right arm. "It’s surprisingly responsive and light. But what about combat? My primary weapons like my Greatsword and my other swords, or even the Sylvan Spear are strictly designed for two-handed combat. I don’t think I have any formal training or muscle memory for a single-handed sword style..."
She looked at her empty left sleeve, which fluttered gently as she turned.
Silas wanted to get used to this new physical vessel as soon as humanly possible so she wouldn’t fumble during her public debut.

’Maybe I’ll take this body out on a border patrol tomorrow morning or something...’ Silas thought, examining her reflection in a polished steel shield hanging on the wall. ’Who knows? Maybe this is a practical way I can walk around the territory and hang out with the girls without them constantly walking on eggshells around their Lord...’
However, that hopeful thought completely vanished into thin air the very next second.
CREAK!
The heavy double doors of the Foundry swung open, letting in a gust of cold winter wind and swirling snow.
Tasmin stepped through the doorway, her newly evolved S-Rank silver-streaked hair catching the orange glow of the forge fires.
She carried her twin chained shortswords at her waist, looking around the workshop.
"Thora," Tasmin called out. "Is the scout gear reinforcement ready yet? I came to pick up the—"
Tasmin froze.
Her dark eyes locked instantly onto the black-haired, purple-eyed, one-armed woman standing in the center of the forge beside the anvil.
She didn’t pause for more than a single heartbeat.
She didn’t look confused, nor did she raise her weapons in defense against an intruder.
Instead, Tasmin simply tilted her head, her sharp face softening into a flat unimpressed look.
"My Lord," Tasmin said plainly, walking inside and closing the door behind her. "What are you doing in a disguise?"
Silas blinked her purple eyes in total, utter shock. She stood there, dumbfounded, staring at the scout.
"How do you even know...?" Silas asked, her female voice carrying a mix of disbelief and annoyance. "I don’t look like myself at all! I don’t even have the same voice or physical gender!"
Tasmin stopped a few paces away, looking Silas up and down with a quiet, knowing smirk.

"You might not look like our Lord," Tasmin explained smoothly, gesturing toward her own chest where her core hummed. "But you feel like him. You can’t hide it from us, Lord Silas. Every single combatant in this territory that is bound and linked to your banner can see it clearly... that massive brilliant golden aura radiating from your soul. You could turn into a bird or a rock, and we would still recognize your presence instantly."
Silas’s shoulders slumped, her female frame deflating completely as she let out a defeated sigh.
"Oh... alright," Silas grumbled, crossing her single right arm over her chest. "Well, setting that aside... how do you like the disguise visually?"
Tasmin stepped closer, circling around Silas’s new body with an analytical eye. She inspected the empty left sleeve, the sharp jawline, and the glowing purple eyes.

"Visually? I like it a lot," Tasmin admitted honestly with her lips curving upward. "You make a remarkably striking woman, My Lord. But if I’m being completely honest... I definitely prefer when you’re a man."
"It’s just temporary," Silas clarified, flexing her right hand. "I just need to get used to handling myself in combat while using this single-arm structure."
Thora, who had been watching the entire exchange with a mischievous grin, suddenly clapped her hands together loudly.
"Hey!" Thora suggested eagerly. "Why don’t you help out, Tasmin? Give our Lord a proper test drive in his new body right now!"
Silas looked over at Tasmin, thinking it over for a second. "That’s actually not a bad idea. Tasmin, give me a light spar. Let’s see how fast my reaction speed is in this form."
Tasmin’s dark eyes flashed with dangerous excitement. "As you wish, My Lord."
SWOOSH.
Without giving a single word of warning, Tasmin’s body completely dissolved into the floor!
She activated [Shadow-Submersion Drift], vanishing into the dark shadows cast by the forge equipment in a fraction of a millisecond!
The atmosphere in the Foundry dropped five degrees in an instant.
Silas stood perfectly still beside the anvil, her purple eyes narrowing as she centered her breathing. Even without her original eyes, her sensory perception was fully operational.
’Behind me...’ Silas registered instantly.
A sharp, jet-black dagger formed entirely from solid shadow energy materialized out of the floorboards directly behind Silas’s back, thrusting silently toward her right shoulder!
"Heh," Silas smirked confidently.

Having anticipated the strike, Silas gathered a burst of Gold Core mana into her boots and pushed off the ground, intending to execute a simple light backward leap to clear the blade’s range and reposition herself.
However... Silas had drastically miscalculated two critical factors.
Her new body was significantly lighter than her original heavy male frame, and her S-Rank Gold Core was pushing full power into muscles that were now half their original density!
BOOM!
The instantaneous kinetic output was astronomical!
Instead of a light two-foot defensive hop, Silas shot upward into the air like a high-velocity surface-to-air missile!
"WHOA...!" Silas yelped in her new female voice as the floorboards beneath her feet literally shattered from the launching force.
CRASH! SHATTER! BANG!
Silas’s head, shoulders, and upper torso smashed violently through the thick timber crossbeams and reinforced slate tiles of the Foundry’s roof.
Wood splinters, iron dust, and broken roof slate exploded outward into the snowy night sky!
Silence descended over the Foundry once more.
Down on the floorboards, Tasmin materialized out of the shadows, sheathing her shadow blade as she slowly raised her head, looking straight up at the ceiling.

Dangling from the gaping, smoking hole in the roof was a pair of slender legs clad in black trousers, twitching helplessly in the open air while the top half of their Lord remained stuck outside in the snowstorm.
Tasmin let out a slow, long sigh, resting her hands on her hips as she shook her head.
"My Lord really needs more training with this body."
