She carried her twin chained shortswords at her waist, looking around the workshop.
"Thora," Tasmin called out.
"Is the scout gear reinforcement ready yet?
I came to pick up the—"
Tasmin froze.
Her dark eyes locked instantly onto the black-haired, purple-eyed, one-armed woman standing in the center of the forge beside the anvil.
She didn’t pause for more than a single heartbeat.
She didn’t look confused, nor did she raise her weapons in defense against an intruder.
Instead, Tasmin simply tilted her head, her sharp face softening into a flat unimpressed look.
"My Lord," Tasmin said plainly, walking inside and closing the door behind her.
"What are you doing in a disguise?"
Silas blinked her purple eyes in total, utter shock.
She stood there, dumbfounded, staring at the scout.
"How do you even know...?" Silas asked, her female voice carrying a mix of disbelief and annoyance.
"I don’t look like myself at all!
I don’t even have the same voice or physical gender!"
Tasmin stopped a few paces away, looking Silas up and down with a quiet, knowing smirk.
"You might not look like our Lord," Tasmin explained smoothly, gesturing toward her own chest where her core hummed.
"But you feel like him.
You can’t hide it from us, Lord Silas.
Every single combatant in this territory that is bound and linked to your banner can see it clearly... that massive brilliant golden aura radiating from your soul.
You could turn into a bird or a rock, and we would still recognize your presence instantly."
Silas’s shoulders slumped, her female frame deflating completely as she let out a defeated sigh.
"Oh... alright," Silas grumbled, crossing her single right arm over her chest.
"Well, setting that aside... how do you like the disguise visually?"
Tasmin stepped closer, circling around Silas’s new body with an analytical eye.
She inspected the empty left sleeve, the sharp jawline, and the glowing purple eyes.
"Visually?
I like it a lot," Tasmin admitted honestly with her lips curving upward.
"You make a remarkably striking woman, My Lord.
But if I’m being completely honest...
I definitely prefer when you’re a man."
"It’s just temporary," Silas clarified, flexing her right hand.
"I just need to get used to handling myself in combat while using this single-arm structure."
Thora, who had been watching the entire exchange with a mischievous grin, suddenly clapped her hands together loudly.
"Hey!" Thora suggested eagerly.
"Why don’t you help out, Tasmin?
Give our Lord a proper test drive in his new body right now!"
Silas looked over at Tasmin, thinking it over for a second.
"That’s actually not a bad idea.
Tasmin, give me a light spar.
Let’s see how fast my reaction speed is in this form."
Tasmin’s dark eyes flashed with dangerous excitement.
"As you wish, My Lord."
SWOOSH.
Without giving a single word of warning, Tasmin’s body completely dissolved into the floor!
She activated [Shadow-Submersion Drift], vanishing into the dark shadows cast by the forge equipment in a fraction of a millisecond!
The atmosphere in the Foundry dropped five degrees in an instant.
Silas stood perfectly still beside the anvil, her purple eyes narrowing as she centered her breathing.
Even without her original eyes, her sensory perception was fully operational.
’Behind me...’ Silas registered instantly.
A sharp, jet-black dagger formed entirely from solid shadow energy materialized out of the floorboards directly behind Silas’s back, thrusting silently toward her right shoulder!
"Heh," Silas smirked confidently.

Having anticipated the strike, Silas gathered a burst of Gold Core mana into her boots and pushed off the ground, intending to execute a simple light backward leap to clear the blade’s range and reposition herself.
However...
Silas had drastically miscalculated two critical factors.
Her new body was significantly lighter than her original heavy male frame, and her S-Rank Gold Core was pushing full power into muscles that were now half their original density!
BOOM!
The instantaneous kinetic output was astronomical!
Instead of a light two-foot defensive hop, Silas shot upward into the air like a high-velocity surface-to-air missile!
"WHOA...!" Silas yelped in her new female voice as the floorboards beneath her feet literally shattered from the launching force.
CRASH!
SHATTER!
BANG!
Silas’s head, shoulders, and upper torso smashed violently through the thick timber crossbeams and reinforced slate tiles of the Foundry’s roof.
Wood splinters, iron dust, and broken roof slate exploded outward into the snowy night sky!
Silence descended over the Foundry once more.
Down on the floorboards, Tasmin materialized out of the shadows, sheathing her shadow blade as she slowly raised her head, looking straight up at the ceiling.

Dangling from the gaping, smoking hole in the roof was a pair of slender legs clad in black trousers, twitching helplessly in the open air while the top half of their Lord remained stuck outside in the snowstorm.
Tasmin let out a slow, long sigh, resting her hands on her hips as she shook her head.
"My Lord really needs more training with this body."

chapters.title: Chapter 232: Vesper [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas sat on the cold floor of the Foundry with her single right hand reaching up to massage the back of her neck where the heavy impact against the wooden roof beams still throbbed.
Even with the dull headache settling behind her eyes, she couldn’t help but let out a short self-deprecating laugh.
The difference between his original male body and this female vessel was staggering.
He was used to wielding hundreds of pounds of solid muscle and heavy steel armor, anchoring herself to the earth like a boulder.
In this form, she felt light... almost weightless in fact.
It was a strange and completely alien sensation, but if she was being completely honest with herself, she actually enjoyed the fluid effortless agility that came with it.
Tasmin walked over, her dark eyes scanning his altered physical structure as she crossed her arms over her chest armor.

"Do you have a name for this body, My Lord?" Tasmin asked calmly. "If you are going to be making public appearances in front of people, you can’t exactly go around introducing yourself as Silas Graves."
Silas paused, sitting cross-legged on the floorboards as she rubbed her chin thoughtfully with his single hand.

"I haven’t really thought that far ahead," Silas admitted, her smooth and slightly raspy female voice echoing softly through the heat of the room. "I was just focused on finding something that could hide my presence from their magical wards."
Thora hopped down from the anvil, wiping soot off her nose with the back of her forearm as a wide grin spread across her face.
"How about Vesper?" Thora suggested eagerly, her eyes sparkling. "It sounds sleek, mysterious, and sharp! Like a shadow cutting through the night!"
Tasmin hummed softly, nodding her head in slow deliberate agreement.
"Vesper... I actually like that name, My Lord. It suits the single-armed, black-haired look you have right now."
Silas tested the name on her tongue, nodding slowly. "Vesper... Yeah, I like it too. Let’s go with that."
From that moment on, both women naturally began addressing her as Vesper whenever she was wrapped in the magical disguise.
Vesper pushed herself off the floor with her right hand, dusting off her fitted black trousers as she turned her head toward the dwarf forge-mistress.

"Thora, do I really need to get used to this exact body?" Vesper asked, raising her empty left sleeve and letting it roll loosely in the warm draft of the forge fires. "Can’t you tweak the ring’s internal conduits or something to fix it? Having only one arm makes handling heavy weapons almost impossible."
Thora scratched her messy braided hair, letting out a heavy sigh that blew a stray puff of smoke into the air.

"I can try to fiddle with the rune circuits, My Lord... or Vesper," Thora replied, rubbing the back of her neck sheepishly. "But like I said, my dad lost the original scroll years ago, and I’m basically working backward from raw mana flow. If I try to forcibly alter the structure right now, I might end up breaking the disguise ring completely. Just in case I can’t fix it, you might have to master fighting with this body yourself."
Vesper sighed, looking down at her lone right hand and flexing her slender fingers.
"Alright then," Vesper grumbled softly. "Do you have a one-handed sword around here right now? I need something to practice with."
Thora immediately perked up, jumping in place like an excited puppy.
"Do I?!" Thora shouted proudly, beating her chest. "I’m the Master Blacksmith of the Sovereign Realm! Of course I do!"
She turned and sprinted toward a heavy wooden rack near the back wall, rummaging through a bundle of newly forged, high-tier blades.
She picked out a sleek, beautifully balanced longsword with a silver crossguard and a dark leather grip, running back over and presenting the Tier 2 weapon with both hands.
"Here you go!" Thora beamed. "Forged it fresh yesterday! Lightweight, perfectly balanced, and sharp enough to slice cleanly through iron plate!"
Vesper reached out, wrapping her right fingers around the leather grip.
She lifted the blade, performing a series of fast experimental slashes through the air.
SWISH!
SWISH!
The blade moved effortlessly, cutting through the warm air with a crisp whistling sound.
Yet, despite the smoothness of the steel, Vesper’s internal muscle memory kept fighting her.
Every time she executed a slash, her left shoulder twitched instinctively, reaching out to grip a non-existent pommel to stabilize the blow.
’I’m definitely going to need to find a dedicated one-handed sword art... or ask Morwenna to teach me her single-blade fencing techniques tomorrow.’ Vesper thought, eyeing the sharp tip of the blade.
Tasmin stepped forward, interrupting her thoughts as her chained weapons clinked against her waist.

"Since you want to get used to the disguise, My Lord," Tasmin proposed, a sharp eager glint shining in her dark eyes, "why don’t we have a practice spar right now? I just evolved into an S-Rank Shadow Commander, thanks to you, and I need to get used to my own new powers as well."
Vesper looked at the slender woman with a confident smile spreading across her face.
She reached out with her right hand, gently patting Tasmin’s head.
It felt slightly awkward and strange, considering that in her shorter female body, Tasmin was actually a few inches taller than her right now.
"Alright then," Vesper agreed smoothly. "Let’s have a little spar outside my place."
A short while later, Vesper, Tasmin, and Thora were standing in the snowy, wide-open training grounds located right beside the Keep.
The winter storm had slowed to a gentle steady snowfall, casting a soft white blanket over the cobblestones and dirt tracks.
A few of the territory’s Shieldmaidens and girls who were currently running late-night perimeter patrols had stopped nearby, leaning against the wooden fences to watch curiously.
Muffled whispers instantly broke out among the patrolling guards, their eyes wide as they stared at the scene.
"Hey... who is that woman standing with Commander Tasmin?"
"Wait, is that... is that Lord Silas?!"
"Why is our Lord in the body of a beautiful one-armed woman?!"
"I don’t know, but she looks incredibly sharp..."
Thora sat atop a wooden barrel near the edge of the snowy ring, swinging her boots back and forth as she raised her fists into the air, cheering loudly at the top of her lungs.
"GO GET ’EM, VESPER! SHOW HER WHO’S BOSS!"
In the center of the snowy field, Tasmin stood in a relaxed combat stance with her hands resting lightly on the pommels of her twin daggers.
The black-and-silver strands of her hair fluttered in the cold wind.
’I’ll use the daggers since I don’t want to go all out....’
"Are you prepared, My Lord?" Tasmin asked and Vesper lifted the one-handed steel sword, holding the blade vertically before her eyes in a classic duelist stance.
"I’m as prepared as I’ll ever be..." Vesper replied, her purple eyes glowing softly in the dim moonlight.
Tasmin let out a soft chuckle, her daggers sliding out from their sheaths with a sharp metallic ring.
"Remember, it’s just a practice spar," Tasmin reminded her with a playful smirk. "You don’t have to try and kill me, My Lord."
Vesper laughed warmly with her boots shifting in the snow. "Kill you? What for? Don’t hold back on me, Tasmin!"
The second the words left her mouth—
ZIP!
Tasmin vanished from sight!
With her newly evolved S-Rank physical stats and her refined neural pathways, her movement speed was insanity.
She completely blitzed across the fifteen-meter gap like a dark lightning bolt with her boots leaving trailing tracks in the snow before her body even appeared to move.
Inside her mind, Tasmin’s heart pounded with overwhelming fierce devotion as her eyes locked onto Vesper’s form.

’All of this strength... all of this power... it’s all because of my Lord! He saved me, he gave me purpose, and he elevated my potential past its limits! I want to get even stronger so I can protect him forever!’
WHOOSH!
Tasmin materialized right in Vesper’s blind spot with her right dagger sweeping forward in a horizontal arc aimed straight at Vesper’s ribs.
Vesper’s perception picked up the movement instantly.
Her mind registered the incoming attack, and she reflexively reached down with her left hand to draw a secondary parrying blade to lock the strike—
Only to grasp complete, empty air!
"Fuck!" Vesper blurted out, her brain suddenly remembering that she didn’t have a second hand.
CLANG!
At the last second, Vesper forcibly twisted her torso, snapping her single right arm across her body to block the blow with her one-handed longsword!
Sparks exploded into the freezing air as Tasmin’s shortsword collided against the flat of Vesper’s blade.
The force drove Vesper’s boots an inch deep into the snow with the shockwave blasting fresh powder away in a neat circle.
Tasmin’s eyes sparkled with playful excitement. "Get ready, My Lord!"
SWOOSH!
Tasmin violently yanked her left arm back, her Eclipse-Thread chains rattling loudly.

Pitch-black writhing shadow energy suddenly coiled around her left fist like a living serpent and without a single moment of hesitation, she thrust her shadow-infused palm forward at terrifying speed...
Vesper’s purple eyes widened as the dark strike surged toward her chest!
CLACK!
Vesper executed a clumsy hasty backstep, tilting her blade at an awkward angle to parry the thrust.
The first block was uncoordinated with the steel sliding roughly against the dark energy and almost slipping from her single hand.
CLANG!
Tasmin followed up instantly with a vicious, spinning left-hook slash.
Vesper pivoted on her left heel, bringing her sword around in a second, much smoother defensive arc.
The second block was significantly better with the steel ringing out clearly as she absorbed the impact.
CLANG!
CLANG!
CLANG!
The sounds of clashing steel echoed loudly across the quiet snow-covered training grounds!
Tasmin unleashed a relentless, storm-like flurry of dagger strikes and shadow thrusts with her blades turning into continuous blurs of motion.
But with every passing second, Vesper’s battle-hardened adaptation was taking full effect.
Her body began naturally adjusting to the lighter center of gravity with her single right arm moving with increasing fluidity and precision.
CLANG!
Tasmin executed a fierce downward chop aimed directly at Vesper’s head but Vesper’s purple eyes flashed with brilliant golden-purple light.
THWACK!
Instead of simply blocking, Vesper angled her longsword perfectly, executing a high-tier parry that directed the force of Tasmin’s dagger upward into the open air.
"Oh?!" Tasmin gasped out in genuine surprise as her guard was violently broken open.
Before Tasmin could recover her balance, Vesper drove her boot straight forward, delivering a hard, clean kick right into Tasmin’s stomach.
BANG!

The strike connected solidly and Tasmin let out a soft gasp of air as she skidded backward across the frozen dirt with her boots carving two deep grooves in the snow for ten full meters before she snapped her body upright, drawing her secondary dagger with a grin.
However, before Tasmin could even set her stance—
WHOOSH!
Vesper had already moved.
’Fucking hell... not again...’
She had originally planned to execute a straightforward lightning-fast blitz directly into Tasmin’s front guard.
But once again, her new female vessel was far too light, and her Gold Core mana output was far too high.
Instead of stopping in front of her, Vesper completely overshot the trajectory with her body hurtling through the air in a blur and landing right behind Tasmin’s back!
’Let’s capitalize on this mistake!’ Vesper thought instantly, twisting her hips on the snow.
SWOOSH!
Vesper whipped her longsword forward in a wide vicious horizontal slash aimed straight at Tasmin’s waist.
CLANG!
Tasmin didn’t even turn around.
Exercising her S-Rank reflexes, she crossed her twin daggers behind her back, catching Vesper’s heavy steel blade cleanly between her crossed irons.
"Not so fast, My Lord!" Tasmin laughed with her body spinning on a dime.
SWOOSH!
Tasmin executed a blinding high-spinning reverse kick aimed straight at Vesper’s head.
Vesper ducked low to the snow, avoiding the spinning heel by millimeters, and thrust her face forward to deliver a counter-strike...
THWIP!
Suddenly, a thick writhing tendril of pure shadow materialized directly out of the ground.
The dark shadow cable wrapped tightly around the mid-blade of Vesper’s longsword, forcibly yanking the steel back and locking her single arm in place.
"What—?!" Vesper blurted out.
Before Vesper could pull her weapon free, Tasmin brought her boot straight up, landing a clean solid kick right against Vesper’s face.
BANG!

The kick connected flush against her cheek and the physical force sent Vesper tumbling backward across the training grounds with her body rolling three times through the deep snow before she slammed her right boot into the frozen dirt to halt her momentum!
"Cough! Cough!" Vesper coughed, wiping a line of dirt and snow from her lip as she pushed herself up with her single hand. "The hell... that was slick!"

Vesper charged forward through the falling snow with her right hand shooting out like a striking cobra and catching the leather hilt of her sword cleanly out of the air.
"That won’t be enough to stop me..."
Without breaking stride, Vesper poured a massive roaring tide of her Gold Core mana directly into the steel blade.
The silver sword instantly ignited with a radiant, blinding golden aura that melted the falling snow within a five-meter radius.
"Oho~ That’s how you want it then, I will deliver!"

Tasmin’s eyes went wide with thrill as she stomped her boot into the ground, unleashing the full extent of her S-Rank shadow mana, coating her twin shortswords in a dense crackling layer of pitch-black void energy!
BOOM!
Both combatants surged toward each other across the snowy field with their boots kicking up massive clouds of white powder.
’Master sure is talented... If I was in such a situation, I wouldn’t be moving like this.’ Tasmin thought.
CRASH!
Their blades collided in the dead center of the training grounds with a deafening thunderous impact.
BOOM!
A massive shockwave of pure energy erupted outward in all directions, blowing away the surrounding snow cover and exposing the dark frozen dirt beneath!
Golden light and pitch-black shadow energy roared and swirled violently around their locked weapons, crackling like lightning in the winter night.
Tasmin gritted her teeth, pushing forward with every ounce of physical strength in her S-Rank body with her Eclipse-Thread chains burning crimson as she tried to force her Lord back.
’Should I even shout? Does that fit a woman like me?’
Vesper dug her boots deep into the dirt, channeling her dominance through her single right arm and the golden Gold Core aura flared twice as bright, completely overpowering Tasmin’s shadow energy!
CRACK!
SWOOSH!

With a massive surge of force, Vesper completely shattered Tasmin’s guard, sending her shortswords flying out of her grip and spinning wildly through the air before embedding themselves deep into a nearby wooden fence post.
FLICK!
Before Tasmin could even take a breath, the cold tip of Vesper’s silver longsword was resting gently against the front of her throat.
The wind died down and the swirling energy dissipated into fine dust.
Tasmin stood completely still, staring up into Vesper’s glowing purple eyes.
A soft breathless smile slowly spread across the Commander’s face as she raised both of her hands in complete surrender.
"I admit defeat, My Lord," Tasmin whispered, her voice filled with deep pride. "Even in a completely unfamiliar body with only one arm... you are truly absolute."
Off to the side, Thora jumped off her wooden barrel, clapping her hands together wildly and roaring at the top of her lungs.
"WOOOOOOOH! THAT WAS BLOODY AMAZING! GREAT FIGHT, VESPER!"
The patrolling girls who had gathered around the fence let out a collective gasp, instantly bursting into loud cheers and applause for their Lord’s display of combat mastery.
Vesper lowered the longsword, taking a long breath as she let the golden mana fade from her veins.
She smiled warmly at Tasmin, offering her a nod of respect.
"You’ve gotten insanely fast, Tasmin," Vesper praised her genuinely. "Those shadow tendrils completely caught me off guard. You’re going to be a nightmare for our enemies on the battlefield."
Tasmin bowed her head deeply, her heart overflowing with joy. "Thank you, My Lord!"
Vesper turned to Thora, walking over to the edge of the ring.
She reached up with her single hand, grasping the black metal ring on her left ring finger, and pulled it off.
FLASH!
A bright blinding burst of golden light erupted around her frame.
In a fraction of a second, the female vessel of Vesper vanished completely.
Standing in her place was Silas Graves... restored to his full six-foot-two height, his broad shoulders, his dark hair, his golden-ringed eyes, and both of his calloused muscular arms.
Silas stretched his left arm out wide, cracking his knuckles as he tossed the black disguise ring back to the dwarf forge-mistress.
"Here you go, Thora," Silas said, his deep, gravelly male voice returning. "Thanks for letting me test it out."
Thora caught the ring easily, tossing it into her pocket with a confident nod.

"Don’t worry, My Lord! I’ll take this back to the anvil and see if I can tweak the conduit paths! If I can figure out how to add a second arm to the transformation without breaking the illusion, I’ll let you know immediately!"
"I appreciate it, Thora," Silas smiled, turning to look at Tasmin as she retrieved her weapons from the fence post. "Great spar, Tasmin. Get some rest."
"Goodnight, Lord Silas!" both women called out in unison, bowing respectfully.
"Goodnight," Silas waved them off with a smile.
He turned and walked away from the training grounds with his heavy boots crunching through the fresh snow as he approached the grand entrance of the Keep.
He pushed open the heavy timber doors, stepping inside the quiet warm main hall, and pulled the doors shut to lock out the cold night wind.
Exhaustion was finally starting to catch up with him after a long day of class upgrades, library visits, tavern chaos, and disguise sparring.
’Not to mention the Secret Realm stuff... I wonder how Seraphina is doing, hopefully I don’t get attacked or something.’
He walked across the polished stone floor and began ascending the grand wooden staircase, heading up toward his private quarters on the upper floor.
As he walked down the quiet, torch-lit hallway of the second floor, he passed by Aeliana’s room.

The door was slightly ajar, and a quick glance inside revealed that her bed was empty... she was likely still down in the grand Library, passionately rewriting her novel Chapter based on his feedback.
Silas chuckled softly to himself, shaking his head as he reached the heavy oak door of his own private master bedroom.
He reached out, pushing the door open, expecting a quiet empty room where he could finally collapse onto his bed and sleep until morning.
Instead, the moment the door swung open, Silas froze.
Sprawled out across the massive, plush king-sized bed in the center of the room were the two SSS-Rank divine beings that Aeli had dropped off earlier.
Eluned and Morwenna were completely, utterly out cold from Thora’s hyper-concentrated "Blessed Drink."
They were tangled up in the silk sheets, occupying every single inch of space on the mattress.
Eluned’s long, silver-green hair was spread out like a wild forest vine across the pillows, while Morwenna’s leather-clad legs were kicked out sideways across the blankets.
Silas stared at the occupied bed, letting out a long, weary sigh as he rubbed his temple with two fingers.
’Great...’ Silas thought bitterly. ’They took over the whole bed. Maybe I should just go find another empty room down the hall...’
He turned on his heel, preparing to step back out into the corridor...
THWIP!
Before his foot could even touch the hallway floorboards, a thick glowing green plant root suddenly whipped out from under the bedsheets like a striking viper.
The root wrapped tightly around Silas’s waist, yanked him backward into the bedroom with terrifying SSS-Rank strength, and slammed the heavy oak door shut.
THUD!
Silas was forcefully yanked through the air and stuffed right into the middle of the plush mattress, sandwiched directly between the two unconscious women.
Eluned, still fast asleep and completely out cold, immediately wrapped both of her arms and legs around Silas’s torso like a territorial python.
She buried her face deeply into his chest with her soft lips puckering up as she repeatedly kissed the air while sleep-mumbling softly into his coat.
"Mmm... my Lord’s chest... mine... no pirate allowed... mmph..."
On his other side, Morwenna let out a rough sleep-drunken grumble.
The Pirate Queen threw her entire heavy, leather-clad leg over Silas’s thighs, pinning him down, and reached up to blindly bite down right on his left earlobe.
"Ouch! Hey!" Silas winced, turning his head as Morwenna mumbled incoherently into his ear before snoring softly against his neck.
Silas lay flat on his back, completely trapped between a territorial Nature Goddess kissing his shirt and a feral Pirate Queen using his ear as a chew toy.
He looked up at the dark wooden rafters of his ceiling, letting out a long defeated sigh.
"Alright, alright..." Silas muttered softly, a fond smirk touching his lips despite the chaos. "Have it your way."
He relaxed his body into the soft mattress, closing his eyes as the warm divine scents of forest flowers and ocean sea-salt wrapped around him.
And with that, the Lord of the Blessed Land fell fast asleep.
The next morning, Silas sat down behind the heavy mahogany desk in his second-floor office, resting his chin in his hand as he looked out through the tall arched windows.
The heavy winter storm that had battered the Keep for days had finally broken.
The snow was no longer falling. Instead, a brilliant, almost oppressive sunlight was blazing down from above, blindingly bright against the white expanse of the Blessed Land.

Rays of intense warmth beat against the glass, and outside on the roof tiles and stone ledges, thick icicles were already melting rapidly, sending steady streams of water dripping down onto the courtyard cobblestones.
Silas squinted at the sudden shift in climate, letting out a long, incredulous sigh as he shook his head.

"Can’t Asgard fucking control their weather?" Silas grumbled aloud to the empty room, rubbing his eye. "What kind of wars can you even be having up there in the higher realms to be causing all these sudden, ridiculous changes in season?"
CLICK!
The heavy oak door of his office swung open smoothly.
Aeliana stepped inside, carrying a crystal chalice filled with freshly pressed, ice-cold fruit juice on a silver tray.
The elven arcanist wore a soft radiant smile with her green eyes gleaming as she set the drink down right on the edge of his mahogany desk.
"Good morning, Lord Silas," Aeli greeted him warmly. "All of the women in the Territory are currently gathered outside in the central courtyard waiting for you."
Silas picked up the crystal chalice, taking a long refreshing gulp of the sweet juice as he stood up from his leather chair.
"Everyone’s already out there?" Silas asked, setting the empty glass down.
"Yes, My Lord," Aeli confirmed, stepping aside to clear his path. "Every single one."
Silas descended the grand wooden staircase, stepping out through the heavy timber doors of the Keep into the bright, sunlit courtyard.
The scene outside was bustling with life.

Gathered in front of the Keep’s wide stone steps was the entire population of the domain... all 74 women currently bound to his territory were present. From the elite, high-tier combatants like Morwenna, Eluned, and Talira, to the frontline commanders like Brida and Tasmin, all the way down to the newer soldiers, Rangers, and support mages.
Even the Blessed Wolves were present, with the three pups nuzzling against Reina’s legs while the adult Alpha wolves stood calmly at the perimeter.
Seeing their Lord step out onto the porch, a sudden energy swept across the crowd.
Silas looked over the sea of loyal faces, a genuine, warm smile touching his lips. He raised his hand in a casual greeting.
"Good morning, everyone," Silas called out with his deep voice carrying clearly across the wide courtyard.
"GOOD MORNING, MY LORD!"
All the women echoed back in a loud roar of absolute devotion that rattled the wooden eaves of the surrounding buildings.
Silas chuckled, waving his hand to ease their formal posture.

"As you all know," Silas began, leaning his arm casually against the carved stone railing of the porch, "I recently ventured into a Secret Realm... And as with any high-tier realm clearance, we brought back spoils. I have brought back rewards that will most certainly boost our territory’s assets."
He paused, a dry smirk appearing on his face as he added.
"Though to be completely honest, most of the divine artifacts inside were a total joke, considering the god who built the place was a joke himself."
A few chuckles broke out among the crowd, particularly from Aeliana who knew firsthand how cheap the ancient deity Ititius had been.
Silas still couldn’t understand how a literal god could be so remarkably stingy with his tomb rewards.
"However," Silas continued, reaching into his spatial storage Inventory, "there was one very good thing that came out of the expedition."
Silas pulled his hand back, opening his palm to reveal the Realm Seed.
FLASH!

chapters.title: Chapter 234: Mage Royale [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The golden crystalline seed flashed brilliantly under the harsh sunlight, radiating a thick swirling aura of elemental mana and power that immediately caught the attention of every single combatant in the courtyard.
Standing near the front rank beside Rowena, Aeli instantly recognized the artifact.

She remembered the moments inside the Secret Realm when Silas had snatched the golden seed right out of the air before Valerius, could even lay a finger on it, right before she had used her spatial magic to warp him away to safety.
’That was fun.... I hope we can go again someday.’

"This Realm Seed was originally advertised by the god to expand our territory by a full five miles in all directions," Silas explained clearly, holding the golden crystal up so everyone could see it. "Right now, due to some reason, it can only expand our physical boundaries by one mile... But that minor limitation doesn’t matter at all compared to its second, far more important property."
The entire crowd leaned forward, their eyes locked onto the glowing item in his hand.

"This seed carries a permanent high-density elemental blessing," Silas announced. "Whoever absorbs it will instantly gain the ability to command Sand Magic, along with a massive permanent elemental affinity boost for earth too."
The moment those words left his mouth, an electric wave of intense anticipation surged through the ranks.
Every single Mage standing in the front and middle rows perked up instantly.
Their eyes sparkled with fierce competitive desire, even their chests were heaving with excitement.
In a territory where combat utility and strength determined how useful they could be to their Lord, gaining a rare high-tier elemental affinity like Sand Magic was a goldmine!
It was their ticket to becoming deeply relevant and useful in Silas’s eyes!
Silas looked over the eager faces of his spellcasters, letting out a quiet internal sigh.
At first glance, the most logical choice was to simply hand the Realm Seed directly to Rowena or Aeli.
Rowena was one of his primary offensive casters, and giving her Sand Magic would expand her utility immensely. But Silas immediately shot that idea down in his own mind.

’Rowena already has her World Weaver staff, her gravity magic, and her high-tier runes,’ Silas reasoned quietly. ’And Aeli is already my go-to with starlight and even spatial magic. If I just hand every single game-changing treasure to the highest-ranked women every single time, I won’t be able to beat the inevitable feeling of favoritism among the lower ranks.’
Silas looked at the lower-ranked C-Rank and B-Rank Mages standing near the back... girls who worked tirelessly on daily patrols, camp defense, and basic territorial maintenance without complaint.

’If I were a regular soldier in this territory and saw the Lord constantly dumping all the best loot onto the same top-tier women, I’d naturally feel left out...’ Silas thought with his golden-ringed eyes softening. ’I’d feel like my hard work didn’t matter, like I was just background filler who wasn’t loved or valued by the Lord. That’s not what I want. That’s not how I run this place.’
He had summoned these girls right from their original places, tearing them away from everything they knew.
He wanted every single one of them to feel valued, to feel like this Keep was truly their home, and that every girl had a genuine path to rise up and stand beside him.
Silas closed his palm, slipping the Realm Seed safely back into his Inventory.
He clapped his hands together with a sharp sound that cut through the whispering crowd.
"Rowena. Aeliana," Silas called out.
"Yes, My Lord?!" both women answered in unison, stepping forward while practically buzzing to face each other in a duel for the seed.
"Stand down," Silas ordered calmly, waving his hand. "Neither of you is taking this seed. In fact, none of the top-tier commanders are participating."
Aeli and Rowena blinked, pausing in surprise, but they immediately bowed their heads in respectful obedience without a single word of complaint.
Silas looked past them, his eyes locking onto the lower-ranked spellcasters in the back ranks.
"Lower Mages, step forward," Silas commanded, a confident grin spreading across his face. "If you are a Mage class... raise your hand right now."
Apart from Aeli, Rowena, and Kaelia, about ten women scattered throughout the formation raised their hands into the air, looking up at him with wide, uncertain eyes.
Silas smiled warmly at them.

"Today is your time to shine," Silas announced, his voice booming across the sunlit courtyard. "I hereby announce the Mage Royale! All ten of you will enter a battle royale tournament. The winner will not only receive the Realm Seed and its Sand Magic affinity... but you will also earn the official title and position as my Second Secretary!"
The ten lower Mages froze in absolute shock.
For two seconds, silence hung over the courtyard as the weight of his words sank into their minds.
Then, the entire group of ten women threw their hands into the air, bursting into wild ecstatic cheering and screaming.
"AAAAAHHH! MY LORD! THANK YOU!"
"A SECOND SECRETARY POSITION?!"
"I’M GOING TO WIN THIS IF IT KILLS ME!"
They shouted with unbridled joy.
Why wouldn’t they? Silas was offering them a direct path to rise from common ranks to an official executive position right beside him.
An hour later, the entire population of the territory had gathered at the far southern edge of the Keep’s walls.
Using the unused, open space between the inner boundary and the outer perimeter, Eluned had used her SSS-Rank nature manipulation to construct a temporary combat arena.
Vines, thick earth pillars, and woven wooden bleachers had grown directly out of the dirt, forming a compact circular stadium that sat neatly beneath the towering stone walls.
Up in the elevated Lord’s viewing box, Silas sat in a plush carved wooden chair overlooking the sunken dirt arena below.
Sitting directly on his right, leaning her entire body against his shoulder and clinging tightly to his arm, was Eluned.
The ancient Nature Goddess pouted heavily with her silver-green hair brushing against his neck.
"I don’t like this, My Lord..." Eluned whined softly, squeezing his arm against her chest. "Why do we need a Second Secretary? I’m already here to take care of you!"
Morwenna, sitting directly on Silas’s left in her black leather coat with her boots kicked up on the stone ledge, turned her head and glared at the nature deity.
"Stop acting like a damn baby, plant-girl," Morwenna scolded her drily, taking a sip from a wooden cup. "Another woman handling paperwork in the Keep isn’t going to hurt anybody."
"What if the Lord gets horny?!" Eluned countered dramatically, puffing out her cheeks as she looked up at Silas with wounded eyes. "He didn’t even dual cultivate with me yesterday!"
Morwenna let out a sharp, incredulous snort, rolling her gray eyes. "That’s because you were completely passed out drunk on his floor, you brainless weed!"
"I was not drunk! I was absorbing environmental spirit energy!" Eluned huffed angrily, and within seconds, the two divine beings were bickering back and forth right over Silas’s lap yet again.
Silas simply sighed, long accustomed to their daily squabbling, and looked back toward the entrance of the viewing box.
Rowena stepped up to the table, carrying a small leather ledger.
The elegant mage bowed respectfully to Silas with a warm genuine smile gracing her face.

"Thank you for giving the lower girls such a wonderful opportunity, Lord Silas," Rowena said softly, her blue eyes shining with admiration. "It really means the world to them. Though... I must admit, a small part of me wishes I could have competed for that secretary spot as well."
Silas chuckled warmly, reaching out and gently patting Rowena’s head, stroking her smooth hair.
"Don’t worry, Rowena," Silas told her, a playful glint in his golden eyes. "I have something special prepared for you too."
Rowena blinked, her cheeks flushing a delicate pink as her heart skipped a beat.
"R-Really, My Lord?"
"Really," Silas nodded. "Just wait until after this royale is over."
"Understood!" Rowena beamed, bowing deeply before stepping back.
Meanwhile, standing right behind Silas’s plush chair, Aeliana leaned down, her long, slender fingers gently massaging his shoulders, working out the tension in his neck with practiced, soothing care.
"The arena is secured, My Lord," Aeli whispered softly into his ear. "The contestants are ready."
Silas looked down into the wide dirt-filled arena below.
Standing in a wide circle in the center of the ring were the ten lower-ranked Mages, dressed in various robes, leathers, and casting tunics.
Among them were a mix of distinct personalities and elemental classes.
There was Valeria... A fierce, short-fused Pyromancer with fiery red hair tied in a messy ponytail.
The second was Lia... she was a calm Wind Mage holding a sleek wooden focus staff and the third was Thalia... who was a quiet Earth Shaper who kept her eyes fixed on the dirt beneath her boots.

The fourth mage there was Seraina... a boisterous cheerful Lightning Caster stretching her arms near the barrier and the fifth Calia who was soft-spoken Water Specialist fidgeting nervously with her sleeves.
Morrigan was the sixth... She was a sharp-eyed Shadow Weaver standing quietly in the corner shadows.
’I wasn’t even aware we had shadow mages until I looked at their classes again, she could learn a thing or two from Tasmin.’
Seventh was Eliora who was a stern Ice Sculptor clutching a crystal orb, Eight was Venma... A confident Arcane Blaster twirling a bronze catalyst ring on her thumb.

Finally, the last two women that were here were Kadi... she was a cheerful, sweet-natured Mage with sandy-brown hair who was currently chatting nicely with the others and Aurelia who was a tall and elegant Light Weaver stretching her fingers.
Before the start signal, the ten women were chatting and bickering amongst themselves about who was going to take the win.
"I’m taking that secretary desk!" Valeria declared with sparks popping from her knuckles. "Fire reigns supreme!"
"In your dreams, hothead," Lia countered smoothly while adjusting her staff. "Speed and precision win battles."
Ka, the sweet sandy-haired Mage, smiled warmly at her competitors, waving her hands gently.

"Now, now, girls," Kadi said in a sweet, comforting voice. "Whoever wins today, it really doesn’t matter! As long as we all get this amazing opportunity to show our Lord what we can do, we should all be happy for each other!"
The surrounding Mages nodded, touched by her kind wholesome words.
Up in the viewing box, Silas stood up from his chair, walking to the stone railing.
He raised his hand with his voice echoing across the entire stadium like a thunderclap.
"COMBATANTS! READY YOUR MANA!" Silas announced loudly. "LET THE MAGE ROYALE... BEGIN!"
The second the word "BEGIN" left his lips...
BOOM!
The sweet wholesome and kind-hearted smile on Kadi’s face instantly vanished, replaced by a crazy grin.
STOMP!
Kadi slammed her right boot violently down into the dirt arena with explosive force.
CRACK! CRACK! CRACK!
A massive, jagged fissure tore through the solid earth at supersonic speed, racing straight toward Calia, the soft-spoken Water Specialist standing nearby.
The fissure reached Caelia’s boots in a fraction of a second and—
BOOM!
The ground beneath Calia exploded violently upward in a roaring fountain of shattered rock and pressurized dirt.
The explosive force knocked Caelia completely out cold on impact, launching her unconscious body through the air to land heavily outside the ring parameters.
FWOOSH!
A fierce howling gale of wind and pulverized dust blasted across the arena, blinding the remaining contestants.
Dense, glowing brown earth mana erupted frantically out of Kadi’s eyes, swirling around her body like a miniature dust storm as her messy sandy hair flew wild in the wind.
She threw her head back, letting out a loud crazy laugh that echoed off the stadium walls.

"HEHEHEHEHEHE! HAHAHAHA!" Kadi cackled crazily, her eyes glowing with pure, unbridled combat madness as she locked her gaze onto the remaining eight terrified Mages. "I WILL BE THE ONE TO BECOME MY LORD’S MOST PRIZED MAGE!"
The remaining contestants gasped, instantly scrambling back into defensive stances as the sweet-faced girl transformed into a demon of earth magic!
"Attack her first!" Valeria screamed, her palms igniting with superheated crimson fireballs!
FWOOSH! FWOOSH!
Valeria unleashed two massive roaring pillars of fire straight toward Kadi.
At the same time, Lia raised her staff, firing three razor-sharp wind-blade arcs.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
They were aimed at Kadi’s flanks.
"TOO SLOW!" Kadi shrieked with a wild wide-eyed grin.
STOMP!
She slammed both hands flat against the dirt.
RUMBLE!
A massive ten-foot-thick wall of solid bedrock erupted out of the earth in front of her.
BOOM!
The fireballs slammed directly into the stone barrier exploding in a towering mushroom cloud of black smoke and roaring flames.
The wind blades sliced deep grooves into the rock, but failed to break through.
ZIP!
Morrigan materialized out of the smoke directly behind Kadi’s back, her hands coated in sharp dark shadow needles.
"Got you," Morrigan whispered sharply.
THWIP!
Kadi didn’t even turn around!
CRACK!
Two thick spikes of compressed earth erupted directly out of the ground beneath Morrigan’s feet, thrusting upward like spears!
BANG!
Morrigan barely managed to cross her arms in a shadow-shield block but the raw force blasted her off her feet, sending her crashing hard against the arena’s wooden boundary fence.

Up in the viewing box, Silas watched the explosive battle unfolding below with his mouth slightly open in utter shock as he stared at the sandy-haired Mage who had been acting like a sweet angel thirty seconds ago.
"Well," Silas muttered, rubbing his chin as he listened to Kadi’s wild cackling echoing through the arena. "She certainly has enthusiasm."

sentences.text: The golden crystalline seed flashed brilliantly under the harsh sunlight, radiating a thick swirling aura of elemental mana and power that immediately caught the attention of every single combatant in the courtyard.

I hope we can go again someday.’
"This Realm Seed was originally advertised by the god to expand our territory by a full five miles in all directions," Silas explained clearly, holding the golden crystal up so everyone could see it.
"Right now, due to some reason, it can only expand our physical boundaries by one mile...

Their eyes sparkled with fierce competitive desire, even their chests were heaving with excitement.
In a territory where combat utility and strength determined how useful they could be to their Lord, gaining a rare high-tier elemental affinity like Sand Magic was a goldmine!
It was their ticket to becoming deeply relevant and useful in Silas’s eyes!
Silas looked over the eager faces of his spellcasters, letting out a quiet internal sigh.
At first glance, the most logical choice was to simply hand the Realm Seed directly to Rowena or Aeli.
Rowena was one of his primary offensive casters, and giving her Sand Magic would expand her utility immensely.
But Silas immediately shot that idea down in his own mind.
’Rowena already has her World Weaver staff, her gravity magic, and her high-tier runes,’ Silas reasoned quietly. ’And Aeli is already my go-to with starlight and even spatial magic.
If I just hand every single game-changing treasure to the highest-ranked women every single time, I won’t be able to beat the inevitable feeling of favoritism among the lower ranks.’
Silas looked at the lower-ranked C-Rank and B-Rank Mages standing near the back... girls who worked tirelessly on daily patrols, camp defense, and basic territorial maintenance without complaint.

’If I were a regular soldier in this territory and saw the Lord constantly dumping all the best loot onto the same top-tier women, I’d naturally feel left out...’ Silas thought with his golden-ringed eyes softening. ’I’d feel like my hard work didn’t matter, like I was just background filler who wasn’t loved or valued by the Lord.
That’s not what I want.
That’s not how I run this place.’
He had summoned these girls right from their original places, tearing them away from everything they knew.
He wanted every single one of them to feel valued, to feel like this Keep was truly their home, and that every girl had a genuine path to rise up and stand beside him.
Silas closed his palm, slipping the Realm Seed safely back into his Inventory.
He clapped his hands together with a sharp sound that cut through the whispering crowd.
"Rowena.
Aeliana," Silas called out.
"Yes, My Lord?!" both women answered in unison, stepping forward while practically buzzing to face each other in a duel for the seed.
"Stand down," Silas ordered calmly, waving his hand.
"Neither of you is taking this seed.
In fact, none of the top-tier commanders are participating."
Aeli and Rowena blinked, pausing in surprise, but they immediately bowed their heads in respectful obedience without a single word of complaint.
Silas looked past them, his eyes locking onto the lower-ranked spellcasters in the back ranks.
"Lower Mages, step forward," Silas commanded, a confident grin spreading across his face.
"If you are a Mage class... raise your hand right now."
Apart from Aeli, Rowena, and Kaelia, about ten women scattered throughout the formation raised their hands into the air, looking up at him with wide, uncertain eyes.
Silas smiled warmly at them.
"Today is your time to shine," Silas announced, his voice booming across the sunlit courtyard.
"I hereby announce the Mage Royale!
All ten of you will enter a battle royale tournament.
The winner will not only receive the Realm Seed and its Sand Magic affinity... but you will also earn the official title and position as my Second Secretary!"
The ten lower Mages froze in absolute shock.
For two seconds, silence hung over the courtyard as the weight of his words sank into their minds.
Then, the entire group of ten women threw their hands into the air, bursting into wild ecstatic cheering and screaming.
"AAAAAHHH!
MY LORD!
THANK YOU!"
"A SECOND SECRETARY POSITION?!"
"I’M GOING TO WIN THIS IF IT KILLS ME!"
They shouted with unbridled joy.
Why wouldn’t they?
Silas was offering them a direct path to rise from common ranks to an official executive position right beside him.
An hour later, the entire population of the territory had gathered at the far southern edge of the Keep’s walls.
Using the unused, open space between the inner boundary and the outer perimeter, Eluned had used her SSS-Rank nature manipulation to construct a temporary combat arena.
Vines, thick earth pillars, and woven wooden bleachers had grown directly out of the dirt, forming a compact circular stadium that sat neatly beneath the towering stone walls.
Up in the elevated Lord’s viewing box, Silas sat in a plush carved wooden chair overlooking the sunken dirt arena below.
Sitting directly on his right, leaning her entire body against his shoulder and clinging tightly to his arm, was Eluned.
The ancient Nature Goddess pouted heavily with her silver-green hair brushing against his neck.
"I don’t like this, My Lord..." Eluned whined softly, squeezing his arm against her chest.
"Why do we need a Second Secretary?
I’m already here to take care of you!"
Morwenna, sitting directly on Silas’s left in her black leather coat with her boots kicked up on the stone ledge, turned her head and glared at the nature deity.
"Stop acting like a damn baby, plant-girl," Morwenna scolded her drily, taking a sip from a wooden cup.
"Another woman handling paperwork in the Keep isn’t going to hurt anybody."
"What if the Lord gets horny?!" Eluned countered dramatically, puffing out her cheeks as she looked up at Silas with wounded eyes.
"He didn’t even dual cultivate with me yesterday!"
Morwenna let out a sharp, incredulous snort, rolling her gray eyes.
"That’s because you were completely passed out drunk on his floor, you brainless weed!"
"I was not drunk!
I was absorbing environmental spirit energy!" Eluned huffed angrily, and within seconds, the two divine beings were bickering back and forth right over Silas’s lap yet again.
Silas simply sighed, long accustomed to their daily squabbling, and looked back toward the entrance of the viewing box.
Rowena stepped up to the table, carrying a small leather ledger.
The elegant mage bowed respectfully to Silas with a warm genuine smile gracing her face.
"Thank you for giving the lower girls such a wonderful opportunity, Lord Silas," Rowena said softly, her blue eyes shining with admiration.
"It really means the world to them.
Though...
I must admit, a small part of me wishes I could have competed for that secretary spot as well."
