"I have the ability to upgrade your classes directly," Silas declared, his golden-ringed eyes glowing as he said so.
"Every single woman in this territory will eventually be elevated to high-tier forms."
The crowd stood completely stunned, paralyzed by the impossibility of what he was saying.
Class upgrades were legendary in the Sovereign Realm... things that required ancient, unobtainable shrines, divine trials, or legendary elixirs.
Tasmin stepped forward from the front line, taking the floor to stand right beside her Lord.
Her dark eyes burned with intense fierce pride as she looked at her comrades.
"Our Lord speaks the absolute truth," Tasmin announced firmly with her voice ringing across the clearing.
She held up her hands, and deep writhing shadow mana flared violently around her arms.
The black-and-silver strands of her hair fluttered in the wind as dark shadow cables coiled like living serpents around her boots.
"I was once a simple C-Rank, stuck at a hopeless plateau with zero chance of advancement," Tasmin explained clearly.
"My Lord unlocked my core, elevated my potential, and made me vastly stronger.
And even now...
I command the shadows themselves."
Beside her, Brida folded her massive, armored arms over her broad chest.
She didn’t deliver a long speech as she simply flexed her titan muscles.
BOOM!
A shockwave of physical pressure erupted from Brida’s boots, instantly shattering the solid earth beneath her feet into a crater of cracked stone.
"Me too," Brida grunted with a confident fierce smirk.
"Lord Silas raised my core directly to Grand Titan Bastion status...
He can do it for every single one of you."
The lower-ranked women in the crowd stared in utter awe, their hearts pounding against their ribs with wild hope and devotion.
"As long as we gather enough Upgrade Points through combat," Silas explained clearly to the crowd, "every single girl in Blessed Land will grow.
But to gather UP, we need to hunt.
We need to go out into the Umbral Basin and slay the beast packs roaming outside our gates."
"YEAHHHHH!"
"LET’S HUNT!"
"FOR THE UPGRADE POINTS!"
"LEAD US TO WAR, MY LORD!"
The entire assembly cheered in a loud bloodthirsty roar of pure martial excitement!
Silas immediately began organizing them into specialized field deployment teams for major hunting operations outside the walls.
"Fenna," Silas commanded, looking over at the sharp ranger chief.
"You and two archers, including Elara, are scheduled to stay atop the Keep’s main Watchtower.
Keep the heavy mana cannons manned and oversee perimeter defense at all times."
"Understood, My Lord!" Fenna answered with a crisp, precise salute.
"Next, Team Alpha," Silas ordered.
"Tasmin, you take point...
Take Elara and a squad of girls for high-speed scouting, quick-strike ambushes, and tracking."
"As you command, Lord Silas," Tasmin bowed deeply with her shadow weapons clinking at her waist.
"Team Bravo will be led by Brida," Silas continued.
"Focus on heavy armor defense, frontline tanking, and clearing large dense beast nests."
"Leave it to me, Captain!" Brida grinned broadly, slapping her heavy metal gauntlets together with a loud sound.
Before Silas could announce the leadership for the third team, Morwenna stepped forward from his side with her cutlass clinking against her dark leather belt.
"Let me lead Team 3, Captain," Morwenna volunteered, a sharp eager glint in her stormy gray eyes.
"It’ll be a perfect opportunity to educate the newer girls on how to properly weave Tidal-Blade Arts in actual field combat."
Silas smiled, nodding in instant agreement.
"Alright.
Morwenna, you lead Team 3... we’ll call it The Abyss Corsairs."
Morwenna smirked broadly, resting her hand on her hip.
"I like the sound of that name, Captain."
Just as the three field teams were finalizing their squad rosters, a rhythmic thumping echoed from the forest path behind them.
Reina, the territory’s Beast Tamer, walked up leading the domain’s tamed mounts... the Blessed Wolves!
The majestic massive direwolves stepped forward into the clearing, their thick lustrous fur gleaming under the bright sunlight.
The large Alpha male Blessed Wolf known as Titan strode up to the front rank.
The scarred, imposing wolf looked over at Morwenna and lowered his massive, muscular shoulders, allowing the Pirate Queen to easily swing her leg over and mount his back with natural grace.
"Oh, Titan!
You’re such a good boy...
Yes you..."
Beside Titan stood his brother, Scout.
The sleek extraordinarily fast direwolf looked over at Reina, who patted his head affectionately before guiding him over to Brida.
It seemed they had bonded since the time Silas was not around.
"Alright, big guy!" Brida cheered happily, slapping Scout’s broad furry flank with a loud laugh.
"Thanks for the lift!"
She mounted Scout with the massive wolf easily supporting her heavy S-Rank Titan weight without flinching.
The remaining female wolves...
Luna, Nova, and Ember approached the other teams.
Luna bonded directly with Tasmin’s squad, Ember trotted over to one of the leaders in Team Bravo, and Nova stepped up beside Reina to serve as her personal combat mount in Team Abyss Corsairs.
With all three field teams fully mounted, armed, and ready for war, Silas turned toward the massive iron mechanisms of the outer perimeter.
"OPEN THE GATES!" Silas commanded, his deep voice ringing out.
HEAVE!
RUMBLE!
The massive Steel Weave Gates slowly ground open, revealing the dark, untamed wilderness of the Umbral Basin stretching out beyond the territory borders.
"MOVE OUT!" Morwenna roared, drawing her silver Corsair and pointing it toward the wild trees!
The three field teams surged forward through the opening.
The Blessed Wolves sprinted across the threshold in broad, powerful leaps with their heavy paws kicking up dirt as the girls cheered and waved back at Silas.
"See you later, My Lord!"
"We’ll bring back mountain loads of UP!"
"Watch over the territory, Lord Silas!"
Morwenna turned back on Titan’s shoulders, blowing Silas a playful lingering kiss over her shoulder with a wink as her squad disappeared into the dense forest depth.
Silas stood at the open gate, waving them off with a proud, satisfied smile.
Remaining behind with him at the gate were Eluned and Aeli, who immediately attached themselves to his left and right arms like affectionate anchors.
Standing beside his right leg was Valkyrie, the Alpha’s mate, who gently nudged her large, soft head against his thigh.
Silas smiled, reaching down with his broad hand and gently patting Valkyrie behind her ears.
"You’re a really good girl..." The female wolf let out a satisfied huff, leaning into his warm touch.
Silas looked out at the peaceful, sunlit forest surrounding the Keep, turning his head toward Aeli and Eluned with a relaxed, cheerful grin.
"Well," Silas chuckled softly, "Who wants to explore the trees some mo—"
PING!
Before he could even finish his sentence, an urgent blood-red notification violently materialized right in front of his eyes.
The crimson screen flashed.
[A Rival Lord of the Territory known as ’The Unmovable Wall’ has entered your area of the Umbral Basin!]
Silas froze.
His relaxed smile completely vanished, his golden-ringed eyes narrowing into sharp slits as he stared at the warning text.
’Fuck.’

chapters.title: Chapter 238: The Unmovable Wall [I]
paragraphs: Silas gulped with a sudden dry lump forming in his throat as his eyes remained glued to the glowing crimson window suspended in the air before him.
He knew that name.
He knew exactly what territory the Unmovable Wall was, and without a single shadow of a doubt, it was one of the last territories on the entire continent that he ever wanted to run into.
The guy behind it was practically a global celebrity back on Earth and across the entire awakened network.
He was famous everywhere for his constant live streaming, turning survival and territorial warfare in the Sovereign Realm into a massive multi-million-credit entertainment business.
But what truly set him apart... what made him a living legend among Lords was the fact that he was one of the very first people to ever successfully create a Mobile Territory.
Usually, a Lord’s territory was anchored to a single fixed patch of ground.
You built your Keep, raised your walls, cultivated your soil, and defended that stationary boundary with your life.
But Lord Sky, the master of the Unmovable Wall, had bypassed that restriction entirely.
He had placed his Territory Core onto a colossal treads-and-iron moving fortress!

He roamed the boundless sectors of the Sovereign Realm on wheels and tracks, driving his mobile kingdom wherever he pleased, actively hunting down and challenging every Lord he happened to cross paths with.
And based on the fact that the system had just broadcasted his entry into the Umbral Basin... that meant the next target in his path was Silas himself and the Blessed Land.
’Fucking hell...’
Silas felt a genuine knot of apprehension tightening in his gut.
A small cold spike of fear darted through his chest.
Lord Sky was a Classic Lord... a veteran who had awakened early, built his force from the ground up, and possessed years of battle experience.
And so far, in every single official Lord War he had ever broadcasted to his global audience, he had never lost a single time.
His record was a flawless, unbroken streak of victories.
The only saving grace in this whole situation was Sky’s reputation and income model.
Because he had tens of millions of fanatical fans tuning into his streams every day, he made a fortune off subscriptions, corporate sponsorships, and broadcast donations.
Because he was already filthy rich from the streams, he didn’t actually bother to pillage, raze, or strip away the land and resources of the territories he defeated.
He fought strictly for the content, the entertainment, and the system ranking points and sometimes people but he only did so when the Lord considered them useless.
However, that didn’t mean a Lord War with him would be a walk in the park.
Facing a Classic Lord on live television with millions of people watching was a terrifying prospect.

’If I just got this system notification,’ Silas thought rapidly with his mind racing as he analyzed the situation, ’then Sky definitely received the exact same prompt the second his mobile fortress rolled into the Umbral Basin.’
He couldn’t afford to meet a famous livestreamer in his true form.

If Silas Graves appeared on a global broadcast leading an army of SSS-Rank goddesses and elite combatants, the World Council, the government, and every major megacorporation back on Earth would lock their eyes on him instantly.
His peaceful hidden development would be blown wide open. It was a good thing he had Vespera...
Silas turned his head toward Thora.
"Thora! Give me the ring! Quickly!"
Thora blinked her wide brown eyes, then a dirty cheeky grin spread across her face.

Without a single trace of shyness or hesitation, the dwarf forge-mistress reached both of her thick, calloused hands straight down between her heavy chest, rummaging around inside her leather top before pulling out the simple black disguise ring.
She held it out to him, the metal still carrying the warm heat of her skin.
On any normal quiet occasion, Silas would have groaned, complained about her bizarre personal storage habits, or called her out for being a shameless pervert.
But right now, with a legendary Classic Lord rolling into his sector, there was no time for banter.
Silas snatched the black band from her palm and slid it smoothly onto his right ring finger.
BOOM!
A violent surge of deep purple mana erupted from the black ring, expanding outward like a swirling, opaque tornado that completely enveloped Silas’s broad six-foot-two frame.
The spatial atmosphere around the gate warped and twisted as the artifact re-wrote his physical parameters from the bone up.

His height compressed down to five-foot-seven, his broad shoulders narrowed, his heavy muscular frame shifted into slender fluid curves, and his left arm dissolved entirely, leaving an empty black sleeve fluttering in the wind.

His short dark hair lengthened into sleek black locks falling to her shoulders, and when her eyelids opened, her golden-ringed eyes had been completely replaced by a luminous, captivating shade of deep violet.
When the purple light finally dissolved into the cold air, Silas Graves was completely gone.
Standing in his place on the stone ridge was Vespera... the single-armed, black-haired, purple-eyed female Lord.
Eluned, who was standing nearby, gasped loudly with her hands flying to her mouth as her silver-green eyes went wide as saucers.
"My Lord?! What... what happened to you?! Where did your body go?! Where is your left arm?!"
Vespera flexed her single right hand, her smooth female voice echoing through the quiet forest clearing.

"It’s a long story, Eluned. I’ll explain the mechanics of the ring to you later. Right now, we have a mobile fortress approaching our borders, and I need to go meet the guy to discuss terms for a Lord War before he rolls up to our front gates."
BUZZ... BUZZ... BUZZ...
Suddenly, a metallic vibration resonated from Thora’s leather utility belt.
A small polished brass crystal hanging from a metal chain began to flash and pulse with an erratic bright blue light.
Thora slapped her hand against her thigh, her eyes widening. "Ah! My Lord! It’s the communication crystal! The one I gave to Tasmin before she rode out with Team Alpha!"
Thora reached down, unclipping the brass device and tapping the central rune to open the long-distance mana conduit.
CRACKLE...
A soft static hum echoed from the crystal, followed immediately by Tasmin’s calm, crisp, and analytical voice:

"Thora? Can you hear me? Report to Lord Silas immediately. Team Alpha has reached the far western border of the newly annexed forest sector and I’ve temporarily broken off because something strange happened... My shadow perception has picked up several high-density spiritual signatures in the clearing ahead... and they do not belong to wild beasts or basin monsters. They belong to fellow humans."
Thora immediately stepped forward, holding the pulsing brass crystal up toward Vespera.
Vespera leaned down slightly, bringing her face close to the artifact.

"Tasmin, it’s me... Vespera," she instructed clearly. "Listen to me carefully. Engage them yourself, but do not attack blindly. State clearly that you are a patrol scout from the Blessed Land, and demand to speak directly with their Lord."
There was a brief, two-second pause on the other end of the communication line before Tasmin’s voice returned.
"Understood, My Lord... though your voice sounds remarkably confident. Am I permitted to execute hostiles if they prove aggressive? Should I kill them?"
Vespera winced slightly with her purple eyes flickering.

"Avoid killing anyone if you can help it! We don’t want to start an unsanctioned, bloody vendetta before formal terms are drawn up. However... if they strike first or try to subdue you by force, attack back with full power. Defend yourself without holding back."
"Roger that," Tasmin replied coolly. "Initiating contact now."
CLICK.
The blue light fading from the brass crystal as the conduit disconnected.
Vespera let out a slow long exhale, bringing her single right hand up to pinch the bridge of her nose.

’Well, damn,’ Vespera thought to herself, her mind flashing to Tasmin’s newly evolved S-Rank Shadow Commander stats and her lethal shortswords. ’I really hope Tasmin doesn’t overdo it and accidentally decapitate one of his primary stream Heroes on live television...’
She looked up at the two women standing beside her at the open steel gate.
"I’m riding out there right now to handle this personally."
Eluned immediately stepped forward, her long silver-green hair swaying as her face filled with intense protective devotion.
"I’m going with you, My Lord! I won’t let some random wandering Lord disrespect you!"
Vespera turned her head, stepping close to the ancient Nature Goddess.
She reached out with her single right hand, gently cupping Eluned’s delicate cheek, and leaned in to plant a warm, firm kiss directly onto her smooth forehead.
Eluned went completely stiff, her eyes wide as a bright radiant pink blush exploded across her cheeks and spread all the way down to the tips of her slender ears.
Her breath caught in her throat, her lips trembling softly.

"No, Eluned," Vespera told her gently, her glowing purple eyes looking into hers. "Showing an SSS-Rank Nature Deity on an open global livestream right off the bat would be a massive mistake... It would reveal our strongest hand to the entire world before the war even starts. You are my secret weapon. I need you to stay behind, go up to the Watchtower with Fenna, and keep an eye on the perimeter from above."
Eluned’s heart swelled with such overwhelming, ecstatic joy at being called his "secret weapon" that her previous reluctance vanished into thin air.
She nodded vigorously, her silver-green hair bouncing.
"Yes! I understand, My Lord!" Eluned beamed happily, clutching her hands against where his kiss had landed. "I will guard the Keep from the Watchtower and wait for your command!"
Vespera turned her gaze toward the dwarf forge-mistress. "Thora, you’re coming with me."
"Hell yes!" Thora cheered, grinning wildly as she unclasped her heavy smithing hammer from her back. "Let’s go see this rolling fortress!"
Vespera walked over to Valkyrie, the massive Alpha wolf mate who was waiting patiently beside the gate.
Vespera swung her body up onto the wolf’s broad, soft back, using her single right hand on the leather harness to balance her lighter female frame.
Thora scrambled up right behind her, settling onto the wolf’s hindquarters and wrapping her thick arms tightly around Vespera’s waist.
"Take us out, Valkyrie!" Vespera commanded softly.
GRRRR... ROAR!
Valkyrie let out a deep reverberating growl, her massive muscular legs springing off the stone ground like coiled steel springs.
She burst forward through the open Steel Weave Gates, her golden fur blurring as she sprinted into the dense dark woods at amazing speed.
A few miles away, at the far western boundary gave way to a vast desolate mud clearing of the Umbral Basin... as well as dark trees.

Standing on the high forward observation deck of a colossal three-story mobile war-rig constructed from heavy iron plates and treaded steel rollers, a man stood quietly, looking out across the landscape through a pair of enchanted brass spyglasses.
This was Lord Sky... the legendary Lord of the Unmovable Wall.
’This is truly a strange place...’ Sky thought to himself, adjusting the delicate focus wheel of his brass spyglass.
In the far distance, beyond the misty, dark tree line, he could barely make out the faint towering silhouettes of stone walls and massive iron gates rising into the sky.
They were miles away, but according to the flashing system HUD floating in his field of vision, there was zero mistake.
That was the official domain center of the Blessed Land...

’Blessed Land sitting right in the middle of a region that is literally called the Umbral Basin...’ Sky chuckled softly under his breath, shaking his head beneath his headgear. ’What an amazing ironic play of words. Whoever the Lord of that territory is, they definitely possess a sense of humor.’
Physically, Sky did not look like an arrogant top-tier noble or a pompous academy heir.
He was an average-built man standing at roughly five-foot-eleven, wearing practical tactical leather gear reinforced with dark mythril plates.

To protect his real-world identity from government stalkers, rival guilds, and corporate headhunters back on Earth, his entire face was concealed behind a sleek featureless silver-and-black alloy mask that covered him from forehead to chin.
Floating in a neat, hovering orbit around his head were five orb-shaped glowing brass camera drones.

They were capturing every angle of his movement, broadcasting high-definition video feeds directly to the global network servers on Earth, streaming his progress live to millions of concurrent viewers.
Sky turned his masked face toward one of the floating camera drones, raising two fingers in a relaxed casual salute to his massive online audience.

"Alright, chat," Sky spoke into his mask’s built-in microphone, his relaxed, confident voice broadcasting clearly to the stream. "As you can see on the regional HUD overlay, we have officially crossed into the regional jurisdiction of the Blessed Land. We’re pulling the rig to a full stop right here at the outer clearing to establish our forward camp."

"Alright, chat," Sky spoke into his mask’s built-in microphone, his relaxed, confident voice broadcasting clearly to the stream.
"As you can see on the regional HUD overlay, we have officially crossed into the regional jurisdiction of the Blessed Land.
We’re pulling the rig to a full stop right here at the outer clearing to establish our forward camp."

HEAVE... RUMBLE... CLANG!
With a massive ground-shaking metallic groan, the colossal mobile fortress pulled to a complete halt at the edge of the wild clearing.
The massive iron treads dug deep, two-foot trenches into the dark mud, steam venting from the side exhaust pipes with a loud roaring hiss that echoed through the trees.
Stepping down the wide iron ramp at the rear of the rig was a heavy detachment of Sky’s standing army.
Gathering in the open clearing was a force of roughly two hundred troops... a formidable trained mix of heavily armored infantry, sharp-eyed archers, element-casters, and summoned Heroes.
Sky had accumulated this massive two-hundred-strong force over months of victorious Lord Wars.

Whenever he defeated a rival domain, instead of slaughtering their population or burning their homes, he often offered the strongest displaced soldiers and Heroes a choice to join his wandering mobile empire, building an elite, diverse military force.
A few of his frontline officers and Heroes grumbled as they stepped out onto the damp murky soil of the Umbral Basin, looking around at the dark, oppressive atmosphere with visible discomfort.

"Ugh, what an annoying, dreary place," a female fire-caster complained, fanning her flushed face with her sleeve. "It’s so humid, damp, and dark out here. Lord Sky, why are we stopping in the middle of a swamp forest?"
Sky laughed warmly, stepping down the iron ramp to join his troops on the mud floor.
"Relax, everyone," Sky chuckled through his alloy mask. "We’re just deploying a standard scout sweep to announce our presence politely. Don’t go burning down the local flora just yet."
He looked over his two-hundred-strong army, feeling a quiet sense of pride.

’Honestly...’ Sky reflected silently, watching his officers form up their lines, ’I wouldn’t mind taking several warriors from the Blessed Land territory if I win this war. Their domain has been making massive waves on the regional leaderboards lately... However, that is only if the Lord him or herself explicitly consents to terms after the match is over. I don’t force people into my ranks.’
He raised his right hand, giving a hand-signal to his scout commander.
"Deploy the forward reconnaissance team. Standard twenty-man spread. Let’s see if Blessed Land has anyone patrolling these outer trees."
"Understood, My Lord!" the scout commander bowed, turning to wave his hand. "Forward scouts, move out!"
However... before the twenty light scouts could even take ten steps into the wild clearing—
THUD! THUD! THUD!
A heavy pounding echoed through the thick purple canopy ahead!
The dark purple leaves rustled violently, and out of the dense forest emerged a single, breathtaking figure.
Riding atop an oversized majestic direwolf with glowing golden fur and a broad scarred frame was a single woman.
She wore sleek dark armor that hugged her slender, athletic body, and her black hair was streaked with striking strands of pure silver that fluttered wildly in the wind.
Prominently engraved on her chest plate, her shoulder guards, and the pommels of her twin daggers was a sharp glowing crest... it was the official crest of the Blessed Land.
As for who these people were, It was Tasmin, riding atop Luna.
Sky’s eyes narrowed behind his silver mask as he locked his gaze onto her.
’Since this is Blessed Land and that crest is there...’ Sky recognized instantly with his posture straightening. ’That is the official crest of Blessed Land and she’s one of their main officers.’
Even though she was riding completely alone against an army of two hundred, her presence was intense and utterly devoid of fear.

The Blessed Land territory had become immensely famous over the past few weeks due to their rapid rise on the global domain charts, and seeing one of their high-tier champions up close sent a visible ripple of intense curiosity through Sky’s entire army.
Even if this woman was just a messenger sent to deliver a response, as a champion from Blessed Land, she was popular too, and Sky wanted to test her out to gauge her baseline capabilities.
He glanced at his floating camera drones.
The stream chat was exploding with tens of thousands of messages a second as viewers talked about her.
[@SovereignWatcher: HOLY SHIT LOOK AT THAT DIRE WOLF MOUNT!]
[@GamerGod99: IS THAT A HERO?! LOOK AT THAT SILVER HAIR!]
[@PVP_Legend: SHE’S RIDING ALONE AGAINST AN ARMY?! SHE’S CRAZY!]
[@NoobMaster69: ATTACK HER! TEST HER STATS SKY!]
[@ValoriaFan: LORD SKY TEST HER! SEND THE SCOUTS!]
[@DarkKnight_00: She looks dangerous as hell... look at her eyes.]
[@StreamLover: BATTLE TIME! BATTLE TIME!]
[@GuildRecruiter_X: That wolf mount is insane quality.]
[@TacticalNuke: Is she going to fight all 200 of them?!]
[@ProGamer_22: Test her guard!]
Sky smirked beneath his alloy mask.
His audience wanted a show, and he was more than willing to deliver.
"Scouts! Subdue the intruder!" Sky ordered, gesturing forward with his hand. "Don’t kill her... just test her guard and hold her in place!"
"YES, MY LORD!"
The twenty light scouts immediately drew their curved steel sabers, releasing their mana as they charged forward across the open dirt clearing.
At the exact same second, standing right beside Sky’s war-rig, one of his primary silver-ranked Heroes moved.
BOOM!
It was a striking, silver-haired Demi-Human female with sharp wolf ears and lethal, three-inch steel claws mounted over her gauntlets.

She launched off the iron ramp like a pressurized steel spring, shooting straight through the air at amazing speeds, she bypassed the twenty scouts entirely with her steel claws extended as she aimed a blinding dive-attack straight at Tasmin’s throat.
"TAKE THIS, INTRUDER!" the silver-haired Demi-Human roared mid-air with her claws gleaming in the sunlight.
Tasmin didn’t flinch, she didn’t draw her twin daggers and she didn’t even order Luna to take a defensive step back.
Instead, Tasmin simply sat atop the golden direwolf’s saddle with a cold unimpressed, and bored look in her dark eyes.
The second before the silver-haired Demi-Human’s lethal claws could slice into her skin—
ZIP!
Tasmin executed a combat dodge so ridiculously disrespectful that it left the entire two-hundred-man army and Lord Sky utterly speechless.

Without using her hands or shifting her feet in the stirrups, Tasmin simply leaned her upper body straight backward at a casual forty-five-degree angle on Luna’s saddle, allowing the Demi-Human’s lethal steel claws to pass through empty air millimeters above her nose.
As the silver-haired Demi-Human overshot her target from the unstoppable momentum of her mid-air dive, Tasmin’s dark eyes flashed with cold contempt.
THWACK!

While still leaning completely backward on her mount, Tasmin casually whipped her left leg straight upward in a lightning-fast brutal reverse heel-kick, connecting flush against the Demi-Human’s exposed jaw.
BANG!
A sickening bone-crunching crack echoed across the silent clearing.

The silver-haired Demi-Human didn’t even get a single chance to scream as the physical force of the kick shut her brain down instantly, sending her unconscious body flying sideways through the air like a discarded ragdoll before crashing face-first into the dark mud, where she lay completely motionless.
THUD!
The twenty charging scouts froze dead in their tracks with their boots skidding in the mud as their sabers trembled in their hands and their eyes going wide as saucers in utter horror.
Tasmin casually sat back upright in her saddle.
With a slow and terrifyingly calm motion, she reached down to her waist, drawing her right shortsword from its sheath with a ringing metallic sound.
SLIDE... CLANG!
Tasmin jumped smoothly off Luna’s back, landing lightly on her boots in the center of the mud clearing.

She raised the gleaming steel blade of her shortsword, holding it vertically before her face as her dark silver-streaked eyes swept over the entire two-hundred-man army, the floating stream drones, and Lord Sky himself.
Her voice echoed across the quiet clearing.
"If you all wish to attack me... then I’m here."
Tasmin shifted her weight with her pitch-black shadow mana beginning to writhe around her boots like living serpents as her lips curved into a cold-blooded smirk.
"Come at me."

The remaining nineteen scouts stood frozen in the mud, staring back and forth between their silver-haired Demi-Human hero lying unconscious in the dirt and the slender silver-streaked woman standing before them.

Her single shortsword was raised vertically before her face, her dark eyes completely lacking any sort of fear, and her pitch-black shadow mana was already creeping across the ground like living serpents.
Uncertainty flashed through the scouts’ eyes.
They looked over their shoulders toward the high iron ramp of the mobile fortress, waiting for a signal.
Up on the observation deck, Lord Sky adjusted his silver-and-black alloy mask, a sharp excited glint shining in his eyes.
He raised his right hand and gestured forward without a second of hesitation.
"Go!" Sky commanded, his voice broadcasting clearly through his mask’s microphone to the clearing and his stream drones. "Subdue her! Don’t let a single scout hold back!"
"AAAAAHHHH!"
"TAKE HER DOWN!"
"FOR THE UNMOVABLE WALL!"
The nineteen scouts snapped out of their trance, letting out fierce battle-hungry roars as they unleashed their various elemental manas.
Swords, spears, curved sabers, and iron axes were drawn simultaneously as the group surged forward across the mud clearing like a tidal wave.
Tasmin didn’t move an inch from her stance as she simply reached down to her left hip with her free hand, drawing her second shortsword from its leather sheath.
SLIDE... CLANG!

Instead of gripping the leather hilt directly, Tasmin caught the thick silver links of the Eclipse-Thread Chain attached to the pommel and she spun the secondary shortsword around her wrist with the heavy steel blade blurring through the air in a whistling circle.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
"You wish to test the Blessed Land?" Tasmin spoke softly, her voice chilling the warm air. "Then come."
STOMP!
Tasmin drove her right boot violently into the dark soil.
BOOM!
A massive wave-like explosion of thick, jet-black shadow mana erupted out of the earth beneath her feet.
The dark shadow energy spread across the entire mud clearing in a fraction of a millisecond, completely engulfing all nineteen advancing scouts in a dense, blinding dome of pitch-black darkness.

Inside the shadow dome, vision was reduced to absolute zero and the scouts panicked instantly with their battle cries turning into startled shrieks as their elemental lights were smothered by her shadow authority.
"WHAT THE—?!"
"I CAN’T SEE ANYTHING!"
"WHERE IS SHE?!"
"WATCH YOUR BACKS!"
Up above the shadow dome, Lord Sky’s floating camera drones hovered in mid-air, capturing the terrifying sight of a giant writhing sphere of pure darkness pulsating in the middle of the clearing.
His stream HUD flared red with thousands of comments pouring in at light speed.
[@ShadowFanatic: HOLY SHIT SHADOW DOMAIN EXPANSION?!]
[@GamerGod99: IS SHE A HIGH-TIER SHADOW WEAVER?!]
[@PVP_Legend: THOSE SCOUTS ARE GETTING COOKED!]
[@NoobMaster69: SKY YOUR SCOUTS ARE DONE FOR!]
[@SovereignWatcher: That might be S-Rank shadow control! Look at the density!]
[@ValoriaFan: She wrapped 19 people in 1 second?!]
[@TacticalNuke: RIP scouts lmao]
Inside the black dome, the slaughter began... not of lives, but of pure combat spirit.
Tasmin moved through the darkness like a ghost.
She activated [Shadow-Submersion Drift] with her physical body merging completely into the floor before re-emerging directly behind the first two scouts.
WHOOSH!
THWACK! THWACK!
Using the flat side of her heavy shortsword blades, Tasmin struck both scouts cleanly across the back of their necks with terrifying force.
CRACK! CRACK!
Both men went limp instantly with their eyes rolling up into their heads as they collapsed face-first into the mud without ever knowing where the blow came from.
"BEHIND US!" a spearman screamed, thrusting his iron spear blindly into the shadows.
CLANG!
Tasmin caught the steel spearhead cleanly between her bare fingers with her strength locking the weapon in place.
She yanked the spear forward, pulling the scout off balance, and drove her elbow straight into his sternum.
BANG!
THUD!
The scout let out a strangled gasp of air as his armor cracked, his body flying backward into three of his comrades, knocking them all down into a tangled heap in the dirt.
Tasmin didn’t stop for a single breath as she whirled her chained shortsword through the dark air.
"Come on, don’t be a bitch!"

chapters.title: Chapter 240: The Unmovable Wall [III]
paragraphs: SWISH!
THWACK! BANG! CRASH!

The heavy steel blade attached to the rattling chain flew like a striking serpent, cracking against shoulder guards, sweeping legs out from under heavy armor, and delivering precise knock-out strikes to jawlines.
She intentionally avoided lethal pressure points, calculating her output to wound and incapacitate without taking a single life, strictly following her Lord’s orders.
Suddenly, a massive armored warrior wielding a two-handed battleaxe managed to pinpoint her location using an earth-detection spell.
He materialized out of the dark mist right behind her blind spot, throwing his entire body weight into a stealth ambush strike.
"DIE, INTRUDER!" the warrior roared, swinging his giant axe in a horizontal arc aimed straight for her spine.
Tasmin didn’t even turn around.
Her sensory perception picked up the displacement of air micro-seconds before the steel could touch her leather tunic!
"Heh!"
ZIP!
Tasmin executed a lightning-fast forward duck, letting the massive battleaxe whistle harmlessly over her head.
Before the warrior could recover his balance from the heavy swing, Tasmin pivoted on her right heel, driving her body straight into his chest guard.
STOMP!
She planted her left boot into his knee, breaking his stance, and unleashed a combination directly into his exposed stomach!
BANG!
The first hit was a heavy mana-infused fist straight to his solar plexus.
BANG!
The second hit was a brutal palm strike to his ribs.
BANG!
The third hit was a rising knee strike that shattered his iron belt buckle.
"Augh!"
BANG!
The fourth hit was a point-blank shadow-wave palm that made his entire stomach rattle inside his armor and finally the fifth hit was a devastating spinning high kick straight to his jaw!
BOOM!
The massive armored warrior let out a pathetic muffled groan as his eyes rolled back, his body launched five feet into the air before crashing heavily into the mud, completely unconscious.
THUD!

Within three minutes of continuous clashing, screaming, and heavy impacts, the last two scouts were hurled out of the dark dome, tumbling across the mud clearing to land directly at the base of Lord Sky’s iron war-rig.
FWOOSH!
Tasmin released her spell.
The giant dome of black shadow mana dissolved into fine black particles, floating away into the warm afternoon air.
The mud clearing was revealed once more.
All nineteen scouts, along with the silver-haired Demi-Human Hero, were lying scattered across the dirt in various states of unconsciousness.
Some were groaning softly with bruised ribs, others were completely out cold, but not a single one was dead.
Standing in the very center of the cleared field, holding both of her shortswords casually at her sides, was Tasmin.
Her silver-streaked hair fluttered in the gentle breeze, her breath perfectly steady as if she hadn’t even broken a sweat.
She slowly raised her dark eyes, locking her gaze directly onto Lord Sky standing up on the observation deck.
STEP!
Lord Sky took a subtle half-step back, his boots grinding against the iron deck. A cold drop of sweat trickled down the inside of his silver mask.

’She... she took down an entire twenty-man elite scout detachment and an A-Rank Demi-Human Hero in less than three minutes...’ Sky thought with his mind racing. ’And she didn’t even use lethal techniques! She calculated every single strike to knock them out cold without killing them!’
Beside Sky, a tall, imposing man stepped forward.
He wore a dark blindfold wrapped tightly over his eyes, carrying a massive double-edged broadsword strapped across his broad back.
This was Sky’s Main Hero... Toronto, the blind swordsman.
The blindfolded Hero reached back with his calloused hand gripping the pommel of his broadsword as his aura flared with dense steel mana.
"Let me handle this, Master," the blindfolded Hero spoke, his voice deep and raspy. "Her shadow flow is sharp, but my blade can cut through her dark domain."
Sky looked at his main Hero, then looked down at Tasmin standing alone in the clearing.
He raised his left hand, placing it firmly on his Hero’s broad shoulder.
"Stand down," Sky instructed quietly. "We’re not here to start a senseless war of attrition."
The blindfolded Hero paused, then released his grip on his weapon, bowing his head respectfully. "As you wish, My Lord."
Sky ran a hand over his short black hair, taking a deep breath before stepping down the iron ramp of his mobile fortress into the mud clearing.
He walked forward until he was twenty paces away from Tasmin, holding his hands out in a open non-threatening gesture.
"Congratulations on a flawless victory," Sky called out, his voice echoing across the quiet field. "You possess remarkable skill. May I ask for your name and title?"
Tasmin didn’t lower her weapons immediately.

She glanced around the clearing, noticing that the remaining hundred and eighty troops standing around the mobile fortress still had their bows notched, their spears leveled, and their elemental spells primed, looking at her with terrified hostile eyes.
Sky noticed her sharp gaze and immediately turned toward his army, waving his arm aggressively.
"Lower your weapons! All of you!" Sky commanded loudly. "Drop your guards! We are guests at their border!"

The two hundred troops hesitated for a second, then lowered their bows, sheathed their swords, and dispelled their glowing elemental circles, though they continued to stare at Tasmin with wide nervous eyes.
THUD! THUD! THUD!
Out of the dark purple tree line, Luna... the massive female Blessed Wolf with glowing silver-white fur trotted smoothly into the clearing, pulling up right beside Tasmin.
Tasmin reached out with her single hand, gently patting Luna’s soft fur behind her ears.
The giant wolf let out a low, content huff, resting her large head beside Tasmin’s shoulder.
’I should remain formal and dignified as a representative of Blessed Land, right?’ Tasmin thought silently, centering her breathing as her Lord had taught her.
She sheathed both of her shortswords with a crisp metallic CLANG and crossed her arms over her leather chest guard.

"I am Tasmin," she announced clearly, her voice carrying an unshakeable authority. "I am one of the primary Commanders of the Blessed Land. You and your mobile fortress are currently intruding upon our domain’s outer jurisdiction. Therefore... you cannot proceed any further."
Sky stopped ten paces away, nodding his masked head in slow understanding.
"I understand completely, Commander Tasmin," Sky replied politely. "We will halt our forward march right here at this clearing. We have no intention of breaching your borders unannounced."

He looked around at the dark, misty forest surrounding them, tilting his head. "If you don’t mind me asking... what kind of monster ecosystem resides in this region? The atmosphere feels unusually heavy."
Tasmin looked at him neutrally, her silver-streaked hair swaying in the wind.

"The Umbral Basin is populated mainly by wild beast packs however in this area," Tasmin reported plainly. "There are corrupted dire-bears and wolves as well as other monsters like Umbral Bats that sit consistently around Tier 2, and occasionally... high-tier Tier 3 Alpha beasts roaming alongside them. As long as you don’t wander into any strange caverns or provoke the deep forest zones, you probably won’t get yourself and your territory killed."
Sky let out a slow, long sigh behind his alloy mask, shaking his head.
The casual nonchalant way she described Tier 2 and Tier 3 monsters roaming around like regular street stray dogs was mind-boggling!
What kind of absolute hellhole grid did Blessed Land establish its Territory in?!
In standard starter sectors, a single Tier 2 monster was a raid-boss threat that required fifty men to clear, yet here they were just regular border fauna?
"Right... Tier 3 beasts just wandering around," Sky chuckled dryly, rubbing the back of his neck. "Good to know."
Sky turned toward his logistics officers near the iron ramp. "Set up the meeting table! Bring out the luxury spread and prepare fresh tea!"
"Yes, My Lord!" the logistics staff answered immediately.
Within minutes, several soldiers carried out a grand carved mahogany meeting table and set it up right in the center of the mud clearing.
They laid down a fine white tablecloth, set up padded leather chairs, and brought out polished silver trays filled with steaming hot herbal tea, delicate pastries, and iced fruits.
At the same time, a group of terrified scouts scurried out into the field, picking up the twenty unconscious scouts and the silver-haired Demi-Human Hero from the dirt.

’Monsters... she’s a complete monster...’ one scout thought frantically, his hands trembling as he hauled his comrade’s heavy armor out of the mud. ’She knocked out twenty of us without even trying! Don’t look her in the eyes! Just pick them up and run!’
’She didn’t even use lethal strikes...’ another scout gulped, stealing a terrified glance at Tasmin’s shadow weapons. ’If she wanted to, she could have decapitated all of us in the dark...’
Sky walked over to the mahogany table, pulling out a chair and gesturing toward Tasmin with a polite smile.
"Commander Tasmin, please, come forward and sit," Sky offered warmly. "Have a drink and enjoy some refreshments before you relay my message back to your Lord."
Tasmin stood perfectly still beside Luna with her arms crossed, her dark eyes looking at the steaming cup of tea with cold suspicion.

"I don’t eat or drink food offered by strangers," Tasmin refused flatly, her voice as sharp as a razor. "I only eat what my Lord feeds me directly. Who knows? You could have laced that tea with paralyzing poison."
Sky blinked behind his mask, holding his hands up defensively. "I assure you, it’s just regular herbal tea—"
"And regardless," Tasmin interrupted smoothly, a proud smile touching her lips, "my Lord will arrive shortly."
The second those words left her mouth—
THUD! THUD! THUD!
A heavy thunderous pounding echoed through the canopy of the western woods.
Sky snapped his head toward the tree line.
Emerging from the forest at blinding speed was another massive majestic Blessed Wolf... Valkyrie, the gold Alpha mate.
Riding atop Valkyrie’s broad back was a striking, incredibly beautiful woman with long, sleek black hair falling to her shoulders and glowing mysterious purple eyes.
She wore a simple, fitted black button-down shirt and black trousers, though her left sleeve dangled empty from her shoulder, rolling loosely in the wind.
Sitting right behind her on the wolf’s hindquarters was a short, muscular dwarf woman holding a massive blacksmith hammer.
THUD!
Valkyrie came to a smooth halt right beside Tasmin and Luna.
Sky stared at the black-haired, single-armed woman in stunned silence.
Vespera looked down from Valkyrie’s back, her purple eyes scanning the twenty unconscious scouts being carried away before settling on Tasmin.
"Tasmin," Vespera spoke, her smooth, raspy female voice echoing through the clearing. "Did you kill anyone?"
Tasmin’s entire demeanor instantly transformed.
The cold ruthless and terrifying Commander who had just single-handedly butchered twenty men in a dark dome completely vanished.
Instead, Tasmin turned toward Vespera, her dark eyes widening with pure devotion as her cheeks flushed a bright delicate pink.
"No, I didn’t, My Lord!" Tasmin answered softly. "I strictly followed your orders and only knocked them out!"
Vespera smiled warmly, reaching down with her single right hand and gently patting Tasmin’s silver-streaked hair, stroking her head affectionately.
"Good girl," Vespera praised her gently. "You did a fantastic job."
Tasmin let out a soft breathless gasp with her face turning bright crimson as she leaned her head deeply into Vespera’s hand, purring like a spoiled kitten!
"Yes, My Lord..." Tasmin stammered adorably, her hands clutching her chest. "I’m... I’m your good girl..."
"PUFFT—!"
Lord Sky almost spat out his own saliva behind his alloy mask.
He stood there, staring at Tasmin in total mind-boggling shock.

’WHAT THE HELL?!’ Sky screamed internally, his eyes bulging behind his mask. ’WHERE DID THAT BRUTISH, TERRIFYING SHADOW DEMON GO?! WHY IS THIS WOMAN WHO LOOKS LIKE SHE LOVES CAVING SKULLS IN ACTING THIS ADORABLE ALL OF A SUDDEN?!’
Vespera withdrew her hand, patting Valkyrie’s neck as she swung her leg over and dismounted the wolf with fluid grace.
"Come along to the meeting table, Tasmin," Vespera instructed smoothly, turning to Thora as the dwarf forge-mistress hopped down beside her. "You too, Thora."
"Right behind you, Lord!" Thora grinned.
Vespera stepped forward across the mud clearing, walking directly up to the mahogany meeting table until she stood face-to-face with Lord Sky.
She offered him a breathtaking, smooth, and alluring smile, her deep purple eyes gleaming under the afternoon sun.
FLASH!

The six hovering camera drones surrounding Sky’s head captured her gorgeous face in crystal-clear high-definition, broadcasting her image instantly to over fifteen million active viewers across the world.
Sky’s stream HUD went into catastrophic overload.
The comment chat exploded so fast the text turned into an unreadable white blur as ten specific comments flashed prominently on his overlay.
[@GamerGod99: HOLY SHIT WHO IS THIS GODDESS?!]
[@SovereignWatcher: ONE ARM?! BLACK HAIR?! PURPLE EYES?! MY QUEEN!]
[@ValoriaFan: IS SHE THE LORD OF BLESSED LAND?!]
[@NoobMaster69: SHE IS 10/10 BEAUTY BRO!]
[@PVP_Legend: LOOK AT THOSE EYES! SHE’S MAJESTIC!]
[@DarkKnight_00: Blessed Land has the highest tier women in the game hands down.]
[@AnimeFanatic: I’M SIMPING SO HARD RIGHT NOW!]
[@TacticalNuke: WIFE MATERIAL! WIFE MATERIAL!]
[@Degenerate_99: Yo Sky ask her to breed with you on stream lmao!]
[@Coomer_X: BREED THIS WOMAN LORD SKY!]
Sky’s eyes caught the last two perverted comments scrolling across his vision, and a vein popped on his temple beneath his mask.

"Moderator! Ban [@Degenerate_99] and [@Coomer_X] permanently from the feed immediately!" Sky barked into his internal channel, clearing his throat awkwardly as he looked back at the stunning woman standing before him.
Sky cleared his throat, bowing his head politely. "May I ask for an official introduction?"
Vespera smiled smoothly, placing her single right hand over her chest as she delivered an elegant bow.
"I am Lord Vespera of the Blessed Land," Vespera introduced herself with her voice captivating the entire stream. "I am the one you requested to see."
She tilted her head slightly, her purple eyes twinkling with a sly warmth as she added.
"To have a legendary Classic Lord like you personally travel all the way to my territory... Lord Sky, it makes me quite happy. I must admit... I’m a big fan of yours."
Inside her mind, Silas Graves was grinning like a scheming mastermind.

’Butter him up,’ Silas thought slyly behind his female disguise. ’Flatter his ego, praise his reputation, and play the polite fan... so that when we sit down to draw up the formal Lord War terms and I ask what I get when I win... I can list off a massive pile of high-tier loot!’
That was the true art of Lord-to-Lord diplomacy before an official war... one Lord maneuvering to extract maximum profit from the other before the first blade was even drawn.

chapters.title: Chapter 241: The One Who Orchestrated Everything...
paragraphs: The yellow taxicab pulled to a smooth quiet stop right outside the towering steel-and-glass gates of the LAB Syndicate Building.
Outside, a heavy gloomy downpour was lashing against the pavement, turning the sleek city asphalt into a dark reflective mirror.
The streetlights flickered softly in the storm, casting long eerie shadows across the high-security entrance of the corporate skyscraper.
Inside the cab, Harper sat quietly in the backseat.
She wore Silas’s oversized, dark leather trench coat wrapped tightly around her body, the familiar scent lingering deep within the fabric lining.
"Here we are, miss. That’ll be forty-two Spirit credits," the cab driver said, glancing back at her through his rearview mirror.
He took the digital payment transfer from her phone card with a soft chime.
As she pushed the door open, he offered a warm professional smile. "Thank you for riding with us. Have a good evening!"
Harper didn’t respond to him. She didn’t offer a nod, a polite phrase, or even a glance.
She simply stepped out into the pouring rain and let the car door slam shut behind her.
The taxi pulled away immediately with its red taillights cutting through the sheet of falling water before disappearing down the city avenue.
Harper stood alone on the wet sidewalk.
She let out a long sigh with her breath fogging up in the freezing night air.
Raindrops beat steadily against her vibrant purple hair, plastering wet strands against her forehead and cheeks.
She reached down, pulling out her phone from the trench coat’s deep inner pocket as she tapped the screen awake.
The display lit up, showing a single text message she had sent nearly two hours ago:
[Harper]: I’m coming up to the office... We need to talk about the recent mission allocations.
There was no reply. Not a single word, a single notification badge, or even a read receipt.
Harper’s jaw tightened.
ZZZZT... CRACKLE!
A small violent spark of royal purple lightning suddenly coiled around her teeth as she gritted them in silent rising rage.
The tiny electric arc hissed against her tongue before vanishing into her throat.
She shoved her phone back into the trench coat and began walking toward the high-security entrance.
Her father was currently inside that building.
Harper knew, with clarity, that her father was not an innocent man. In fact, calling him "innocent" or even "morally grey" was a complete joke.

The volume of wealth, influence, and corporate standing Collin had built up over the last two decades had been carved out through illegal black-market deals, political blackmail, backroom assassinations, and shady syndicate operations.
Yet, for the longest time, Harper had tried to compartmentalize it.

She had tried to tell herself that in the ruthless dog-eat-dog world of awakened Lords and corporate syndicates, everybody had dirty hands. She had tried to justify his actions as the harsh necessity of a father protecting his bloodline.
Throughout her entire life, Harper had never once seen her mother.
She had grown up entirely under Collin’s roof, surrounded by cold stone, armed guards, and stack after stack of files.
The story her father had always fed her was simple: her mother had been a weak foolish woman who tried to betray the family by taking Collin to court over illegal asset seizures.
And almost immediately after launching that legal battle, her mother had suddenly "lost her life" in a tragic unexplained incident.
Shortly after her mother vanished from existence, Penelope had come to live with them.

Penelope had been brought in under the guise of an orphaned relative but was her sister, and from that very moment, Collin had transformed both of their lives into an endless pipeline of dangerous corporate missions.
Harper had never really stopped to think about her mother before. Well... not until this exact pouring moment.
Harper pushed open the heavy glass doors of the LAB Building, stepping into the warm pristine white marble lobby.
Several junior Lords, corporate executives, and well-dressed receptionists standing behind the front desk looked up as she walked past.
They instantly recognized her... the sharp purple-haired prodigy of the appraisal department.
"Good evening, Miss Harper," a young receptionist greeted politely with a bow.
"Welcome back, Lady Harper," a passing junior Lord chimed in.
Harper didn’t smile.
She didn’t acknowledge a single one of them.

She kept her head down with her hands tucked deep into the pockets of Silas’s heavy trench coat, pulling the broad collar up around her neck as she walked straight past the front desk toward the executive elevator bank.
’I feel like I want to explode...’
She pressed the call button.

The polished steel doors slid open with a soft bell tone and Harper stepped inside, turned around to face the lobby, and slammed her finger against the top-floor button... Collin’s private executive suite.
The elevator doors closed, and the elevator began its smooth silent ascent up the sixty-story skyscraper.
As the floor numbers ticked rapidly upward on the digital display, Harper stared at her reflection in the mirrored walls of the elevator car.
Her thoughts drifted backward, unspooling the painful ribbon of her childhood.
From the moment she had awakened her lightning and blood magic attributes, Collin had started sending her on missions. After all, she had become a Lord early too.
Sneak into this rival territory’s vault...
Retrieve that classified skill scroll...
Infiltrate that corporate gala and secure leverage on that director...
Put your body on the line... use your looks if you have to...
Harper had always drawn a strict ironclad line at that last command.
She had fought, bled, and used every ounce of her combat prowess to complete those infiltration missions without ever allowing a single man to lay a hand on her.
Who knew whether she would even still be a virgin right now if she hadn’t been strong enough to cut her way out of those sleazy traps?
’Though for this one... I was ready to put my body on the line...’
And yet, despite being forced into the shadows for years, she had been okay with it.
She had been completely okay with entrusting her life to that man. She had accepted being enslaved by her own father, doing his dirty illegal bidding without complaint. And for what?
A modest luxury apartment in the city sector?
Even that apartment was something she paid for herself!

Every single credit that went into buying food, paying utilities, purchasing gear, and funding Penelope’s living expenses came directly out of Harper’s own hard-earned mission rewards and appraisal commissions.
Collin hadn’t provided a single dime of real support. He didn’t care about her... He didn’t care about Penelope. He didn’t care about either of them... not even for a fraction of a second.
’Why... Why am I such an idiot...’
And the only reason Harper had finally and fully realized this heartbreaking truth... was because of Silas Graves.
Harper’s fingers tightened against the leather fabric of the trench coat, clutching it tightly across her chest.
’Silas actually cares about me...’ Harper thought with her chest swelling with a strange aching warmth that made her throat feel tight.
The contrast was staggering.
What Silas had given her in a matter of days was completely, fundamentally different from anything her father had ever offered her since the day she was born.
Silas had pulled her back right from the very brink of death when death was devouring her core.
He had healed her with his own resources.
He had helped her stand up when her legs were failing.
He had treated her like a human being... a valuable cherished person rather than a disposable pawn to be deployed and forgotten.
Harper didn’t even know if what she felt for Silas was "love" in the way people in romantic novels talked about it.
She was too broken, too battle-scarred, and too inexperienced to fully understand those complex emotions.
But one thing she knew with terrifying certainty: she wanted to keep receiving that care.
She wanted to stand by his side, she wanted to feel his warm hands on her shoulders, and above all else, she refused to let anyone hurt him.
Why was it so different?
Harper stared at her reflection in the elevator glass with a tear mixing with the rainwater on her cheek.

’Why did a complete stranger in the Sovereign Realm treat me with more love than my own father ever did?’ Harper wondered bitterly in her mind. ’Did I not deserve that same kind of care from the man who gave me life? If my mother were still alive today... would she have loved me like Silas does?’
DING!
The high-pitched ping of the elevator shattered her train of thought.
The doors slid open, revealing the top-floor executive hallway.
The air up here was cold, scented with expensive cologne and polished mahogany, lit by dim ambient LED strips embedded along the floorboards.
Harper staggered slightly as she stepped out of the elevator car.
ZZZZZZT! KRA-THOOM!
Thick, violent coils of royal purple lightning suddenly erupted across her entire figure. The air pressure inside the hallway plummeted instantly.
Her mana was spiking completely out of control, reacting to her overflowing emotional turmoil.

She felt a burning agonizing soreness settling deep inside her throat... a physical sensation that always occurred whenever her lightning affinity reached a critical overload, demanding to be unleashed in a destructive blast.
At the far end of the hallway stood a heavy, reinforced oak door... Collin’s private office.
Standing guard right outside the entrance were two elite armored mercenaries holding submachine guns.
Hearing the crackling electric hum, both guards snapped their heads toward the elevator, raising their weapons.
"Miss Harper?!" the left guard called out, surprised. "Wait, you can’t go in there right now! Director Collin is on an important—"
WHOOSH!
Harper didn’t even speak as she blurred across the twenty-meter hallway like a purple bolt of lightning.
BANG! BANG!
Before either guard could pull his trigger, Harper delivered two lightning-infused palm strikes flush into their stomachs.
The heavy force smashed through their mythril armor plates, instantly driving the wind out of their lungs and shutting down their nervous systems.
Both guards collapsed sideways onto the carpet, completely knocked out cold before their bodies even hit the floor.
Harper stopped in front of the heavy oak door.

She didn’t kick it down immediately. Instead, she reached out with her trembling right hand, turning the polished brass handle just a fraction of an inch, opening a tiny silent crack in the doorway so she could listen to what was happening inside.
Inside the luxurious, dimly lit office, Collin was standing near the floor-to-ceiling glass windows overlooking the rainy city skyline.
He was holding a glass of aged whiskey in one hand and a encrypted satellite phone to his ear with the other, chuckling softly into the receiver.

"...Yeah, I hear you, brother," Collin’s voice echoed arrogantly through the room, completely unaware of the girl standing outside his door. "Don’t worry about the timeline. I’ll need her dead in a few years anyway."
On the other end of the line, a muffled male voice asked a brief distorted question.
"Are you talking about that purple-haired girl? Your daughter?"
Collin let out a loud mocking laugh, taking a sip of his whiskey.

"Yes! The daughter of that stupid naive woman!" Collin scoffed with utter disdain. "God, every single time I look at that Bitch’s face, it’s so bloody annoying. She looks just like her mother. It makes my skin crawl."
Outside the crack in the door, Harper went completely still as the blood in her veins ran ice-cold.
Collin leaned back against his mahogany desk, swirling the liquor in his glass as he continued talking into the phone with a sickening grin.

"The only reason I’ve even kept her and that useless sister of hers alive this long is because they do the dirty work for my infiltration missions," Collin bragged casually into the receiver. "They get me the black-market skill scrolls, they clear out rival assets, and they don’t ask questions. But once their utility runs dry... I need them both to die traceless, just like that woman did."
The voice on the phone laughed heartily back at him. "Ha! Cheers to that, brother! Clean work."

"Cheers," Collin chuckled smoothly. "Once those two girls are completely out of the picture, I’ll be able to claim full inheritance rights over the entire family estate and her mother’s hidden Mana Core vaults. Honestly, those two useless brats should have died from the poison years ago..."
Outside the door, Harper’s eyes went wide as saucers.
Poison...
The word echoed in her mind like a thunderclap.

Her mind flashed back to years ago... to the mysterious agonizing illness that had suddenly struck her out of nowhere, eating away at her core, leaving her bedridden and dying until her blood had overpowered it.

’It was him...?’ Harper realized, her mind fracturing under the weight of the betrayal. ’The poison that almost destroyed my core... the pain I suffered for months... it wasn’t a rival syndicate attack... It was him! He tried to murder me!’
