chapters.title: Chapter 242: Negotiation Between Lords [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Inside the office, Collin tapped his desk, completely oblivious to his impending doom as he added one last detail to his phone call.
"Oh, by the way... she just came back from the Secret Realm. I think I’ve finally uncovered a probable identity for that mysterious Lord of Blessed Lan—"
Harper stopped listening.
She didn’t care about his intelligence and she didn’t care about his asset reports.
Harper didn’t care about anything coming out of his disgusting, lying mouth anymore!
BOOM!
The purple lightning coiling around Harper’s body reached an all-time apocalyptic high.
Her emotional anguish, her rage, her sorrow, and her fiercely protective devotion to Silas fused together into a volcanic explosion of raw power.
CRASH! SHATTER! BANG!
The heavy reinforced oak door was violently blown completely off its steel hinges, exploding inward into a shower of splinters and iron shrapnel!
Collin gasped, violently flinching as the heavy door smashed into his mahogany desk, shattering his whiskey glass onto the carpet.
He spun around, his eyes going wide with utter terror as he stared at the doorway.
Standing in the smoking threshold was Harper.
Her vibrant purple hair was floating in mid-air, suspended by an anti-gravitational field of pure electricity.

Her eyes were no longer human... they were burning orbs of blinding, incandescent lightning as thick arcs of royal purple energy spider-webbed across the floorboards, melting the carpet and scorching the drywall.

"H-Harper?!" Collin stammered with his face turning ghostly pale as his satellite phone slipped from his trembling fingers, hitting the floor. "What... what are you doing here?! How dare you break into my—"
Harper didn’t let him finish his sentence.
She slowly raised her right arm, pointing her open palm directly at his chest.
Her voice echoed through the destroyed office... not with her usual soft reserved tone, but with a cold fury that shook the very foundations of the building:
"Go fuck yourself."
KRA-THOOM!
Harper unleashed her power.
A massive roaring beam of royal purple lightning erupted from her palm but in that exact second of hatred, her intense emotional agony violently triggered her secondary blood magic attribute.
FLASH!
Her blood mana fused with her lightning output at an astronomical density as the roaring purple beam instantly turned into a blinding pure white column of apocalyptic energy.
BOOOOOM!
The white lightning beam struck Collin flush in the chest.

The catastrophic output completely vaporized his body’s defensive shields instantly as the blast hurled his body straight backward, crashing through his mahogany desk, destroying his leather chairs, and smashing through the massive, floor-to-ceiling reinforced glass windows at the top of the skyscraper.
SHATTER! CRASH!

The entire glass wall facing the city exploded outward into millions of sparkling crystal shards as the white lightning beam shot out into the stormy night sky, illuminating the entire downtown district of the city in a blinding flash that could be seen for a long distance.
A howling gale of wind and rain instantly rushed into the destroyed executive office through the gaping hole where the glass wall used to be, swirling dark smoke and papers across the ruined room.
The blinding light slowly faded and the crackling thunder died down into quiet static.
Harper stood alone in the center of the ruined office with her arm slowly dropping to her side.
The white-and-purple lightning around her body flickered three times before completely dissolving into fine dust.
Her chest heaved with heavy gasps.

’All of my troubles...’ Harper thought, her vision blurring with hot streaming tears as she stared at the empty, shattered window frame overlooking the rain-slicked city below. ’All the pain... all the cold nights... all the missions... they were all because of you... You... you...’
Her knees buckled under the weight of emotional exhaustion.
PLOP!
Harper fell forward onto her hands and knees on the wet scorched carpet.
She wrapped Silas’s heavy leather trench coat tightly around her trembling frame, burying her face into the broad collar as sobs began to wrack her body.
Suddenly, a strange acrid smell hit her nose.
Harper froze mid-sob.
She sniffed the air with her eyes widening as she noticed a trail of grey smoke rising from the sleeve of the coat.
The overwhelming heat from her white lightning blast had accidentally scorched the left cuff of Silas’s trench coat, leaving a small, blackened burn mark on the fine leather.
"Fuck...!" Harper gasped out, her tears stopping instantly as pure panic washed over her face.
She frantically pulled the leather sleeve up to her eyes, blowing on the tiny ember to put it out, gently rubbing the scorched leather with her trembling fingers.

"I burned it...!" Harper cried out in a soft panicked voice, hugging the coat against her cheek. "Oh no... don’t burn... please don’t burn! This is Silas’s coat! If it burns... will Silas give me another one?! What if he gets mad at me?!"

She sat there on her knees in the middle of a destroyed corporate skyscraper, completely ignoring her dead father and the ruined office, frantically cuddling the slightly singed coat and praying to whatever gods were listening that Silas wouldn’t scold her for damaging his clothes.
[Meanwhile In the Sovereign Realm...]
At the luxurious mahogany meeting table set up in the mud clearing of the Umbral Basin...
Silas, currently wrapped in his single-armed, purple-eyed female disguise was sitting comfortably across from Lord Sky sighed.
"Achoo!"
Vespera suddenly let out a soft delicate sneeze with her shoulder twitching slightly.
Lord Sky blinked behind his silver-and-black alloy mask, instinctively waving his hand.
"Bless you, Lord Vespera."
Vespera pulled out a small silk handkerchief with her single right hand, dabbing her nose softly.
"Thank you, Lord Sky," she replied smoothly.
Inside her mind, Silas was utterly bewildered.

’Who the hell is thinking about me right now?’ Silas thought to himself, tilting his female disguise’s head. ’Is someone back at the Keep talking shit about me, or did Eluned start talking with a pillow again?’
Across the table, Lord Sky leaned forward slightly, resting his elbows on the white tablecloth.
His masked face looked at her with genuine curiosity.
"So..." Sky spoke up, breaking the brief silence. "Are you really a fan of my channel, Lord Vespera? Or were you just using polite words to ease the tension before we talk business?"
Vespera offered him a warm confident smile, setting her teacup down onto the silver saucer with a soft sound.

"I’m truly a fan, Lord Sky," Vespera answered effortlessly, her purple eyes sparkling under the afternoon sun. "In fact... I distinctly remember watching your stream coverage during the Vigborough Territory campaign."
The second those words left her lips—
Sky’s posture completely froze. Behind his silver alloy mask, his eyes went wide as saucers in genuine utter shock.
’The Vigborough campaign?!’ Sky thought, his heart skipping a beat.
That was a massive detail!

If Vespera had simply come straight out and mentioned his most popular, multi-million-view stream... like his legendary victory at the Red Iron Canyon, it would have been common knowledge that any casual viewer could look up on the global trending tab.
But the Vigborough Territory stream was a fairly recent, niche campaign that had taken place just weeks ago... right before Vespera herself had awakened as a Lord.
It wasn’t a viral sensation, but it was one of Sky’s personal favorite displays and Silas himself wasn’t lying at all.
’I’m not the biggest fan but I’ve seen his streams...’
Back before Silas had awakened his system and received his [Divine Sanctum] trait, he had spent countless late nights back on Earth studying Sky’s livestreams.
He had watched them meticulously, analyzing Lord Sky’s mobile fortress mechanics and command structure just in case he awakened as a regular Lord and was forced to stream 24/7 to make a living.

Who knew back then that Sky would eventually become a world-famous sensation, or that Silas would end up sitting face-to-face with him in a female disguise, preparing to negotiate terms for a Lord War?
Seeing that she truly knew his work, a bright genuine smile spread across Sky’s face beneath his mask.
"Well, I’ll be damned," Sky laughed, his voice instantly becoming remarkably warmer and far more relaxed. "You really are a viewer! That Vigborough run was one of my tightest tactical matches!"
Sky sat back in his padded leather chair, gesturing warmly toward the table. "Please, Lord Vespera, make yourself comfortable!"
He turned his head toward his logistics officers standing near the iron ramp of his mobile fortress, shouting out a merry command.
"Hey! Bring out the luxury cookie spread! The fresh butter biscuits!"
Hearing that command, Vespera smiled slyly inside her mind.
’Jackpot...’ Silas thought triumphantly behind her purple-eyed smile.
Through his extensive late-night research of Sky’s stream archives, Silas knew every single one of Sky’s personal quirks.
Lord Sky only brought out his private, high-tier butter cookie spread when he genuinely liked and respected the Lord he was meeting.
Bringing out the cookies meant that diplomacy was going swimmingly, and that Sky was viewing her as an equal rather than a random target to be steamrolled.
A logistics officer hurried over, placing a silver platter filled with warm, golden-brown butter biscuits and fruit preserves in the center of the table.
Vespera reached out with her single right hand, picking up a delicate cookie and taking a light, elegant bite.
"Mmm. Delicious," Vespera praised softly, setting the biscuit down and looking into Sky’s masked eyes with a sharp glint in her violet gaze.
Now that the ice was broken, the real game was about to begin.
Silas knew how Lord War pre-negotiations worked.

Before two Lords clashed on stream, they sat down to set the stakes. It was a subtle high-stakes game of verbal sparring and with Sky already thoroughly charmed and thoroughly buttered up, Silas was fully prepared to list off a massive, astronomical demands sheet for what Blessed Land would claim when they won.
Vespera picked up another one of the warm, golden-brown butter biscuits between her slender fingers, turning the delicate pastry over in her hand.
The rich aroma of baked vanilla, sweet churned butter, and refined sugar drifted up from the biscuit, filling her senses.
She looked across the white tablecloth at Lord Sky, nervously scratching her cheek with her single right hand as a slight embarrassed blush touched her smooth pale face.
’To act like a woman... I must be a woman!’

"Um... Lord Sky?" Vespera began, her smooth voice dropping into a soft hesitant one. "If... if it isn’t too much trouble... do you think you could distribute some of these cookies to my people as well?"
Sky tilted his silver-and-black alloy mask slightly, taken aback by the request. "To your troops?"
Vespera let out a soft bashful sigh, looking down at the silver platter with a sheepish expression.

"To be completely honest with you," Vespera admitted quietly, rubbing the back of her neck in a cute gesture, "it has been a very long time since I last crossed over into the real world back on Earth. Things have been so hectic in our territory that I really haven’t had much time to go shopping or bring sweet treats like these back through the portal. Seeing my girls look at these pastries with such curious eyes... I feel a little guilty."
Inside her mind, Silas was silently praising his own acting skills.
’Flawless,’ Silas thought smugly behind the female disguise. ’Play the caring, gentle leader who feels bad for her hardworking troops. It completely shatters the image of a bloodthirsty Lord.’
Sky smiled behind his mask, charmed by her endearing concern for her subordinates.
He turned toward his logistics officers standing near the iron ramp of his mobile fortress, waving his hand generously.
"You heard the lady!" Sky called out. "Go into the primary mess hall vault and bring out a full crate of fresh butter biscuit packages for Lord Vespera’s girls!"
"Right away, My Lord!" the logistics staff responded immediately.
A few moments later, a uniformed officer hurried back down the iron ramp, carrying a heavy sealed wooden crate packed to the brim with individually wrapped luxury cookie boxes.
The officer stepped up to Tasmin, offering the package to her with a respectful slightly nervous bow.
Tasmin didn’t touch the crate at first. Her dark, silver-streaked eyes flickered over to Vespera, silently waiting for confirmation.
Vespera nodded gently at her.
"Go ahead, Tasmin. It’s okay."
Only then did Tasmin step forward. She took one of the cookie packages from the crate, bowing her head slightly toward the logistics officer and Lord Sky.
"Thank you," Tasmin spoke formally.
Having seen her Lord take an elegant bite of the biscuit just moments prior, Tasmin carefully opened the paper wrapping.
She picked up a golden biscuit, opened her mouth, and took a small crisp bite, chewing thoughtfully.

sentences.text: Inside the office, Collin tapped his desk, completely oblivious to his impending doom as he added one last detail to his phone call.
"Oh, by the way... she just came back from the Secret Realm.
I think I’ve finally uncovered a probable identity for that mysterious Lord of Blessed Lan—"
Harper stopped listening.
She didn’t care about his intelligence and she didn’t care about his asset reports.
Harper didn’t care about anything coming out of his disgusting, lying mouth anymore!
BOOM!
The purple lightning coiling around Harper’s body reached an all-time apocalyptic high.
Her emotional anguish, her rage, her sorrow, and her fiercely protective devotion to Silas fused together into a volcanic explosion of raw power.
CRASH!
SHATTER!
BANG!
The heavy reinforced oak door was violently blown completely off its steel hinges, exploding inward into a shower of splinters and iron shrapnel!
Collin gasped, violently flinching as the heavy door smashed into his mahogany desk, shattering his whiskey glass onto the carpet.
He spun around, his eyes going wide with utter terror as he stared at the doorway.
Standing in the smoking threshold was Harper.
Her vibrant purple hair was floating in mid-air, suspended by an anti-gravitational field of pure electricity.

Her eyes were no longer human... they were burning orbs of blinding, incandescent lightning as thick arcs of royal purple energy spider-webbed across the floorboards, melting the carpet and scorching the drywall.
"H-Harper?!" Collin stammered with his face turning ghostly pale as his satellite phone slipped from his trembling fingers, hitting the floor.
"What... what are you doing here?!
How dare you break into my—"
Harper didn’t let him finish his sentence.
She slowly raised her right arm, pointing her open palm directly at his chest.
Her voice echoed through the destroyed office... not with her usual soft reserved tone, but with a cold fury that shook the very foundations of the building:
"Go fuck yourself."
KRA-THOOM!
Harper unleashed her power.
A massive roaring beam of royal purple lightning erupted from her palm but in that exact second of hatred, her intense emotional agony violently triggered her secondary blood magic attribute.
FLASH!
Her blood mana fused with her lightning output at an astronomical density as the roaring purple beam instantly turned into a blinding pure white column of apocalyptic energy.
BOOOOOM!
The white lightning beam struck Collin flush in the chest.

The catastrophic output completely vaporized his body’s defensive shields instantly as the blast hurled his body straight backward, crashing through his mahogany desk, destroying his leather chairs, and smashing through the massive, floor-to-ceiling reinforced glass windows at the top of the skyscraper.
SHATTER!
CRASH!

The entire glass wall facing the city exploded outward into millions of sparkling crystal shards as the white lightning beam shot out into the stormy night sky, illuminating the entire downtown district of the city in a blinding flash that could be seen for a long distance.
A howling gale of wind and rain instantly rushed into the destroyed executive office through the gaping hole where the glass wall used to be, swirling dark smoke and papers across the ruined room.
The blinding light slowly faded and the crackling thunder died down into quiet static.
Harper stood alone in the center of the ruined office with her arm slowly dropping to her side.
The white-and-purple lightning around her body flickered three times before completely dissolving into fine dust.
Her chest heaved with heavy gasps.

’All of my troubles...’ Harper thought, her vision blurring with hot streaming tears as she stared at the empty, shattered window frame overlooking the rain-slicked city below. ’All the pain... all the cold nights... all the missions... they were all because of you...
You... you...’
Her knees buckled under the weight of emotional exhaustion.
PLOP!
Harper fell forward onto her hands and knees on the wet scorched carpet.
She wrapped Silas’s heavy leather trench coat tightly around her trembling frame, burying her face into the broad collar as sobs began to wrack her body.
Suddenly, a strange acrid smell hit her nose.
Harper froze mid-sob.
She sniffed the air with her eyes widening as she noticed a trail of grey smoke rising from the sleeve of the coat.
The overwhelming heat from her white lightning blast had accidentally scorched the left cuff of Silas’s trench coat, leaving a small, blackened burn mark on the fine leather.
"Fuck...!" Harper gasped out, her tears stopping instantly as pure panic washed over her face.
She frantically pulled the leather sleeve up to her eyes, blowing on the tiny ember to put it out, gently rubbing the scorched leather with her trembling fingers.
"I burned it...!" Harper cried out in a soft panicked voice, hugging the coat against her cheek.
"Oh no... don’t burn... please don’t burn!
This is Silas’s coat!
If it burns... will Silas give me another one?!
What if he gets mad at me?!"

She sat there on her knees in the middle of a destroyed corporate skyscraper, completely ignoring her dead father and the ruined office, frantically cuddling the slightly singed coat and praying to whatever gods were listening that Silas wouldn’t scold her for damaging his clothes.
[Meanwhile In the Sovereign Realm...]
At the luxurious mahogany meeting table set up in the mud clearing of the Umbral Basin...
Silas, currently wrapped in his single-armed, purple-eyed female disguise was sitting comfortably across from Lord Sky sighed.
"Achoo!"
Vespera suddenly let out a soft delicate sneeze with her shoulder twitching slightly.
Lord Sky blinked behind his silver-and-black alloy mask, instinctively waving his hand.
"Bless you, Lord Vespera."
Vespera pulled out a small silk handkerchief with her single right hand, dabbing her nose softly.
"Thank you, Lord Sky," she replied smoothly.
Inside her mind, Silas was utterly bewildered.

’Who the hell is thinking about me right now?’ Silas thought to himself, tilting his female disguise’s head. ’Is someone back at the Keep talking shit about me, or did Eluned start talking with a pillow again?’
Across the table, Lord Sky leaned forward slightly, resting his elbows on the white tablecloth.
His masked face looked at her with genuine curiosity.
"So..." Sky spoke up, breaking the brief silence.
"Are you really a fan of my channel, Lord Vespera?
Or were you just using polite words to ease the tension before we talk business?"
Vespera offered him a warm confident smile, setting her teacup down onto the silver saucer with a soft sound.
"I’m truly a fan, Lord Sky," Vespera answered effortlessly, her purple eyes sparkling under the afternoon sun.
"In fact...
I distinctly remember watching your stream coverage during the Vigborough Territory campaign."
The second those words left her lips—
Sky’s posture completely froze.
Behind his silver alloy mask, his eyes went wide as saucers in genuine utter shock.
’The Vigborough campaign?!’ Sky thought, his heart skipping a beat.
That was a massive detail!

If Vespera had simply come straight out and mentioned his most popular, multi-million-view stream... like his legendary victory at the Red Iron Canyon, it would have been common knowledge that any casual viewer could look up on the global trending tab.
But the Vigborough Territory stream was a fairly recent, niche campaign that had taken place just weeks ago... right before Vespera herself had awakened as a Lord.
It wasn’t a viral sensation, but it was one of Sky’s personal favorite displays and Silas himself wasn’t lying at all.
’I’m not the biggest fan but I’ve seen his streams...’
Back before Silas had awakened his system and received his [Divine Sanctum] trait, he had spent countless late nights back on Earth studying Sky’s livestreams.
He had watched them meticulously, analyzing Lord Sky’s mobile fortress mechanics and command structure just in case he awakened as a regular Lord and was forced to stream 24/7 to make a living.

Who knew back then that Sky would eventually become a world-famous sensation, or that Silas would end up sitting face-to-face with him in a female disguise, preparing to negotiate terms for a Lord War?
Seeing that she truly knew his work, a bright genuine smile spread across Sky’s face beneath his mask.
"Well, I’ll be damned," Sky laughed, his voice instantly becoming remarkably warmer and far more relaxed.
"You really are a viewer!
That Vigborough run was one of my tightest tactical matches!"
Sky sat back in his padded leather chair, gesturing warmly toward the table.
"Please, Lord Vespera, make yourself comfortable!"
He turned his head toward his logistics officers standing near the iron ramp of his mobile fortress, shouting out a merry command.
"Hey!
Bring out the luxury cookie spread!
The fresh butter biscuits!"
Hearing that command, Vespera smiled slyly inside her mind.
’Jackpot...’ Silas thought triumphantly behind her purple-eyed smile.
Through his extensive late-night research of Sky’s stream archives, Silas knew every single one of Sky’s personal quirks.
Lord Sky only brought out his private, high-tier butter cookie spread when he genuinely liked and respected the Lord he was meeting.
Bringing out the cookies meant that diplomacy was going swimmingly, and that Sky was viewing her as an equal rather than a random target to be steamrolled.
A logistics officer hurried over, placing a silver platter filled with warm, golden-brown butter biscuits and fruit preserves in the center of the table.
Vespera reached out with her single right hand, picking up a delicate cookie and taking a light, elegant bite.
"Mmm.
Delicious," Vespera praised softly, setting the biscuit down and looking into Sky’s masked eyes with a sharp glint in her violet gaze.
Now that the ice was broken, the real game was about to begin.
Silas knew how Lord War pre-negotiations worked.
Before two Lords clashed on stream, they sat down to set the stakes.

It was a subtle high-stakes game of verbal sparring and with Sky already thoroughly charmed and thoroughly buttered up, Silas was fully prepared to list off a massive, astronomical demands sheet for what Blessed Land would claim when they won.
Vespera picked up another one of the warm, golden-brown butter biscuits between her slender fingers, turning the delicate pastry over in her hand.
The rich aroma of baked vanilla, sweet churned butter, and refined sugar drifted up from the biscuit, filling her senses.
She looked across the white tablecloth at Lord Sky, nervously scratching her cheek with her single right hand as a slight embarrassed blush touched her smooth pale face.
’To act like a woman...
I must be a woman!’
Lord Sky?" Vespera began, her smooth voice dropping into a soft hesitant one.
"If... if it isn’t too much trouble... do you think you could distribute some of these cookies to my people as well?"
Sky tilted his silver-and-black alloy mask slightly, taken aback by the request.
"To your troops?"
Vespera let out a soft bashful sigh, looking down at the silver platter with a sheepish expression.

"To be completely honest with you," Vespera admitted quietly, rubbing the back of her neck in a cute gesture, "it has been a very long time since I last crossed over into the real world back on Earth.
Things have been so hectic in our territory that I really haven’t had much time to go shopping or bring sweet treats like these back through the portal.
Seeing my girls look at these pastries with such curious eyes...
I feel a little guilty."
Inside her mind, Silas was silently praising his own acting skills.
’Flawless,’ Silas thought smugly behind the female disguise. ’Play the caring, gentle leader who feels bad for her hardworking troops.
It completely shatters the image of a bloodthirsty Lord.’
Sky smiled behind his mask, charmed by her endearing concern for her subordinates.
He turned toward his logistics officers standing near the iron ramp of his mobile fortress, waving his hand generously.
"You heard the lady!" Sky called out.
"Go into the primary mess hall vault and bring out a full crate of fresh butter biscuit packages for Lord Vespera’s girls!"
"Right away, My Lord!" the logistics staff responded immediately.
A few moments later, a uniformed officer hurried back down the iron ramp, carrying a heavy sealed wooden crate packed to the brim with individually wrapped luxury cookie boxes.
The officer stepped up to Tasmin, offering the package to her with a respectful slightly nervous bow.
Tasmin didn’t touch the crate at first.
Her dark, silver-streaked eyes flickered over to Vespera, silently waiting for confirmation.
Vespera nodded gently at her.
"Go ahead, Tasmin.
It’s okay."
Only then did Tasmin step forward.
She took one of the cookie packages from the crate, bowing her head slightly toward the logistics officer and Lord Sky.
"Thank you," Tasmin spoke formally.
Having seen her Lord take an elegant bite of the biscuit just moments prior, Tasmin carefully opened the paper wrapping.
She picked up a golden biscuit, opened her mouth, and took a small crisp bite, chewing thoughtfully.

chapters.title: Chapter 243: Negotiation Between Lords [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: A momentary spark of pleasant surprise flashed in her dark eyes.
"Mmm," Tasmin murmured softly.
She looked at Sky and his surrounding troops, delivering a deadpan, backhanded compliment without dropping her dignified posture.
"Even if your soldiers do not know how to fight properly... your chefs certainly know how to cook."
"PUFFT—!"
Several of Sky’s surrounding infantrymen choked on their own spit, while a few archers glared at her with twitching eyebrows.
Vespera went bright red in an instant, waving her single hand frantically at her Shadow Commander in adorable panic.
"Tasmin~!" Vespera squeaked out. "Be polite!"
Seeing her Lord react with such cute flustered embarrassment, Tasmin’s cool composure instantly shattered.
A bright rosy flush erupted across Tasmin’s cheeks, spreading rapidly all the way to the tips of her ears.
’It doesn’t matter if Lord Graves is a man or woman... he’s cute either way.’
"A-Ah! Forgive me, My Lord!" Tasmin stammered hastily, bowing her head in flustered panic. "I did not mean to cause offense!"
Trying to make amends, Tasmin hurriedly unwrapped another biscuit, turning to Thora, who was sitting nearby resting her thick arms on her blacksmith hammer.
Tasmin offered the biscuit to the dwarf forge-mistress’s mouth.
"Here, Thora. Taste this," Tasmin offered quickly.
Thora didn’t hesitate for a single second. She leaned her heavy head forward and snapped her jaws down on the biscuit, taking half of it in a loud, crunchy bite.
CRUNCH!
Thora chewed rapidly, her broad soot-stained face lighting up with wild boisterous delight as she slapped her knee.
"BY THE ANCESTORS!" Thora boomed loudly with her hearty laugh echoing across the mud clearing. "That’s bloody fantastic! Buttery as hell! Hey, big girls, try some of this!"
Thora unwrapped two more biscuits from the package and held them out to the two massive direwolves resting beside them.
Valkyrie and Luna sniffed the golden pastries for a brief second before gently taking them from Thora’s palm, crunching down on the butter cookies with satisfied rumbling huffs.
Hovering right above the meeting table, Sky’s five floating camera drones captured every single second of the interaction in crystal-clear, high-definition resolution.
The live-stream broadcast which was currently sitting at over twenty million active concurrent viewers globally went into a frenzy.
The comment overlay on Sky’s HUD exploded into a blinding white wall of light speed text.
[@GamerGod99: AHHHHHH SHE’S SO CUTE!]
[@SovereignWatcher: LORD VESPERA SCOLDING HER HERO IS THE GREATEST THING I’VE EVER SEEN!]
[@NoobMaster69: "Tasmin~" BRO MY HEART CANNOT TAKE THIS!]
[@PVP_Legend: She’s an absolute angel! Look at how she cares for her troops!]
[@ValoriaFan: Feed the direwolves! Look at them crunching the cookies!]
[@StreamLover: The brutal shadow commander getting embarrassed is peak content!]
[@DarkKnight_00: Blessed Land isn’t a dark domain, it’s a paradise!]
[@AnimeFanatic: PROTECT THAT SMILE AT ALL COSTS!]
[@TacticalNuke: Sky, if you hurt her in the Lord War, we are unsubscribing!]
[@ProGamer_22: She’s so shy and gentle... how is she running a high-tier territory?!]
Lord Sky himself stood frozen behind his alloy mask, staring at Vespera in complete speechless bewilderment.
He had met dozens of territory leaders during his travels across the Sovereign Realm.
Most Lords were arrogant, power-hungry, stern, or cold-blooded tyrants who treated their subordinates like disposable pawns and spoke with inflated self-important hubris.
He had fully expected the mysterious Lord of Blessed Land... a domain currently skyrocketing up the regional rankings to be a ruthless iron-fisted ice queen.
Sky cleared his throat awkwardly behind his silver mask, running a hand through his short dark hair as he looked at her with genuine amazement.
"Are you... are you truly the Lord of Blessed Land?" Sky asked, his voice filled with gentle disbelief. "I have to admit... I expected someone far more strict and intimidating."
Vespera pulled her single hand back, resting her elbow on the table and slumping her shoulders slightly with a casual, indifferent shrug.

"I really am the Lord of Blessed Land," Vespera replied plainly, her glowing purple eyes looking into his mask. "And honestly... this is just how I am. I don’t really see the point in putting on a fake, arrogant act."
She took another small, graceful sip of her herbal tea, setting the delicate cup down before continuing.

"Before I awakened my Core and anchored myself to the Sovereign Realm," Vespera explained with a quiet nostalgic smile, "I was a complete, hopeless introvert back on Earth. I barely talked to people, I stayed indoors, and I preferred my own quiet space... Just because I became a Lord doesn’t mean my personality is suddenly going to change overnight."
Hearing her soft, honest confession, Sky felt an unexpected sudden warmth rising into his cheeks beneath his silver alloy mask.
His heart gave a subtle strange flutter in his chest.
’An introverted, gentle woman who was forced into leadership, yet cares deeply for her people...’ Sky thought, his eyes softening behind his eye-slots. ’She’s remarkably charming...’
Sky adjusted his posture, looking down at her empty left sleeve, which was rolling gently in the afternoon breeze.
His curiosity finally got the better of him.
"If you don’t mind me asking, Lord Vespera..." Sky began hesitantly, gesturing toward her empty shoulder. "Your left arm... what happened to it? Was it a permanent territorial sacrifice?"
Inside her mind, Silas Graves let out a heavy, impatient internal groan.

’For fuck’s sake,’ Silas complained bitterly behind his female disguise. ’Why are you asking about my missing hand?! Can we please get to the main part already?! Is this supposed to be an official Lord War pre-negotiation, or are you trying to take me out on a fucking date?!’
Despite his internal annoyance, Vespera maintained her soft delicate demeanor on the outside.
She looked down at her rolling black sleeve, letting out a small, self-deprecating chuckle.

"Ah, this?" Vespera replied smoothly, waving her single hand dismissively. "It’s nothing noble or heroic, I’m afraid... During the very first battle I ever fought after awakening... I was so wildly excited and inexperienced that I charged straight out of the Novice Barrier without checking my surroundings. A high-tier beast ambushed me from the tree line, ripped my left arm clean off, and devoured it right in front of me before I managed to slay it."
Sky gasped, then burst into a warm, booming laugh.

"Hahaha!" Sky laughed heartily, slapping his hand against the mahogany table. "Oh, man! Don’t feel bad about that at all! On my very first day out of the Novice Barrier, I got so overly excited that I sprinted right into a giant spider nest and spent four hours hanging upside down in a web screaming for help until my first summoned hero saved me!"
Vespera let out a melodic laugh, nodding in sympathetic agreement.
"We all make foolish mistakes when we first start out," Vespera chuckled softly.
Sky leaned back in his chair, taking a sip of his tea as he looked at her with growing rapport.
"Where are you from back home on Earth, if you don’t mind my asking? Which city sector do you reside in?"
Vespera paused, her violet eyes narrowing slightly with subtle caution.
She didn’t want to give away her exact location or reveal that she was a student living in a modest apartment.
She kept her answer deliberately vague and ambiguous.
"I live in one of the central metropolitan districts," Vespera answered smoothly, tilting her cup. "It’s a fairly quiet area. What about you, Lord Sky?"
Sky didn’t notice her subtle vagueness, assuming she was simply being shy about her personal privacy in front of millions of stream viewers.
"I’m stationed out in Valoria City," Sky shared freely, tapping his chest plate. "Born and raised near the central commercial hub of Silverleaf."
He set his teacup down, his tone shifting into a slightly more serious, intriguing rhythm.
"By the way, Lord Vespera... have you checked the global news feeds back on Earth recently? Do you know about the massive bounty the government and the World Council have placed on your head?"
Vespera blinked her purple eyes in genuine surprise, tilting her head. "A bounty? Seriously?"

"Oh, absolutely," Sky nodded firmly, leaning forward. "The World Council officially raised the reward for your confirmed real-world identity to Ten Billion Spirit Credits! They’ve dubbed you the ’Hero of Humanity,’ and the top government officials are practically breaking down doors trying to secure an immediate, high-priority meeting with you."
Vespera’s eyes went wide as saucers, her mouth opening slightly in dramatic shock.

"Ten Billion?!" Vespera gasped out, pressing her hand against her chest. "I... I don’t even know the first thing about corporate or government meetings! High-society politics sounds utterly terrifying!"
’Lord Silas is being too natural as a woman... Has he had experience in this too?’ Thora looked at him suspiciously, why was he so good at acting all of a sudden?
Sky laughed warmly at her flustered reaction.
"If you ever need advice on how to handle government bureaucrats or corporate headhunters, just let me know! I’ve been dealing with those suits for years."
Sky’s masked face leaned in a fraction closer, his eyes gleaming with intense curiosity.

"The main reason the World Council is going so insane over you," Sky revealed in a low, quiet voice, "is because of the rumors surrounding your Core class. The global media and the higher academies are convinced that you are a Gold Core Lord... seeing as humanity’s very last recorded Gold Core Lord was born centuries ago."
Sky looked straight into her deep violet eyes, probing for a reaction. "So... tell me, Lord Vespera. Are the rumors true? Are you truly a Gold Core?"
Vespera didn’t flinch.
A sly captivating and mysterious smile slowly curved her lips. She rested her chin on her single palm, her purple eyes twinkling with playful arrogance.
"Well..." Vespera purred softly, her raspy voice dripping with tantalizing tease. "I’ll tell you... if you win the war."
Sky’s lips quirked violently upward behind his silver-and-black alloy mask.
’A challenge?!’ Sky thought, an electric surge of competitive adrenaline shooting straight through his veins.
Meanwhile, inside her mind, Silas Graves let out a massive triumphant sigh of relief!

’FINALLY!’ Silas cheered internally, pumping his metaphorical fists. ’Finally! I can finally turn this absurd conversation toward the actual Lord War! I was getting so damn tired of this small talk... is this supposed to be a date or a Lord negotiation?!’
Sky straightened his spine, sitting up tall in his padded chair as his demeanor shifted from a friendly, relaxed chat partner into a serious veteran Warlord.

"A tempting prize," Sky admitted smoothly, his eyes burning with battle-hungry excitement. "Alright then. Let’s talk about the Lord War. After all... that is the primary reason my mobile fortress entered the Umbral Basin."
Vespera sat up straight as well, setting her teacup aside. "I’m listening, Lord Sky."
Sky looked at her, then looked over at Tasmin and Thora standing nearby.
"Before we set the parameters," Sky began thoughtfully, "I need to gauge your military scale. How large is the standing army of Blessed Land currently?"
Vespera didn’t see any reason to lie about her numbers. She looked Sky dead in his mask and answered plainly:
"I currently have less than one hundred total troops in my territory."
The second those words left her lips—
Sky’s entire body went completely rigid.
His jaw dropped open behind his alloy mask, his eyes bulging in shock.
"Less... less than a hundred?!" Sky gasped out loud, completely failing to hide his utter disbelief! "Are you serious?!"
His mind raced at light speed, calculating the impossibility of what she had just said.
Blessed Land was currently sitting in the Top one on the Newbie Charts and a Top 100 All time territory too, and Asgard as well as other mythical places were in top hundred too.
Their territory points were astronomical... For a territory to achieve that level of global ranking with a total population of fewer than one hundred people meant one terrifying mind-boggling thing:
Every single individual living inside the Blessed Land was an superhuman monster.

If every single one of her seventy-plus troops possessed physical stats, speed, and combat capabilities comparable to Tasmin... who had just single-handedly butchered twenty armed scouts in three minutes without breaking a sweat, then this wasn’t going to be an easy skirmish.
’Fuck...’
Sky realized with chilling clarity that if he didn’t take this Lord War seriously and unleash his full military power, his undefeated streak was going to be brutally shattered live on stream.
Vespera took a calm sip of her tea, looking at his shocked expression with a faint, humble smile.
"We really train very hard," Vespera explained casually. "That’s all there is to it."
Sky took a slow, deep breath, forcing himself to calm down and regain his tactical composure.
He rested his hands flat on the white tablecloth, looking at her with absolute seriousness.
"Alright," Sky spoke, his voice deep and focused. "When would you be available to execute the official Lord War? You know that is why I’m here."
Vespera tilted her head, entering deep thought.
Inside her mind, Silas was rapidly weighing his options.

’I still haven’t gathered enough experience to trigger the Second Stage of Core Ascension for myself,’ Silas analyzed. ’And gaining that massive 30,000-point mana boost before fighting an undefeated Classic Lord would be extremely helpful... I need a bit of time.’
Before Vespera could state a timeframe, Sky raised his hand, offering his own proposal first.
"If it suits you, Lord Vespera," Sky proposed smoothly, "I would prefer to wait one full week before launching the war."

I barely talked to people, I stayed indoors, and I preferred my own quiet space...
Just because I became a Lord doesn’t mean my personality is suddenly going to change overnight."
Hearing her soft, honest confession, Sky felt an unexpected sudden warmth rising into his cheeks beneath his silver alloy mask.
His heart gave a subtle strange flutter in his chest.
’An introverted, gentle woman who was forced into leadership, yet cares deeply for her people...’ Sky thought, his eyes softening behind his eye-slots. ’She’s remarkably charming...’
Sky adjusted his posture, looking down at her empty left sleeve, which was rolling gently in the afternoon breeze.
His curiosity finally got the better of him.
"If you don’t mind me asking, Lord Vespera..." Sky began hesitantly, gesturing toward her empty shoulder.
"Your left arm... what happened to it?
Was it a permanent territorial sacrifice?"
Inside her mind, Silas Graves let out a heavy, impatient internal groan.
’For fuck’s sake,’ Silas complained bitterly behind his female disguise. ’Why are you asking about my missing hand?!
Can we please get to the main part already?!
Is this supposed to be an official Lord War pre-negotiation, or are you trying to take me out on a fucking date?!’
Despite his internal annoyance, Vespera maintained her soft delicate demeanor on the outside.
She looked down at her rolling black sleeve, letting out a small, self-deprecating chuckle.
"Ah, this?" Vespera replied smoothly, waving her single hand dismissively.
"It’s nothing noble or heroic, I’m afraid...
During the very first battle I ever fought after awakening...
I was so wildly excited and inexperienced that I charged straight out of the Novice Barrier without checking my surroundings.
A high-tier beast ambushed me from the tree line, ripped my left arm clean off, and devoured it right in front of me before I managed to slay it."
Sky gasped, then burst into a warm, booming laugh.
"Hahaha!" Sky laughed heartily, slapping his hand against the mahogany table.
"Oh, man!
Don’t feel bad about that at all!

On my very first day out of the Novice Barrier, I got so overly excited that I sprinted right into a giant spider nest and spent four hours hanging upside down in a web screaming for help until my first summoned hero saved me!"
Vespera let out a melodic laugh, nodding in sympathetic agreement.
"We all make foolish mistakes when we first start out," Vespera chuckled softly.
Sky leaned back in his chair, taking a sip of his tea as he looked at her with growing rapport.
"Where are you from back home on Earth, if you don’t mind my asking?
Which city sector do you reside in?"
Vespera paused, her violet eyes narrowing slightly with subtle caution.
She didn’t want to give away her exact location or reveal that she was a student living in a modest apartment.
She kept her answer deliberately vague and ambiguous.
"I live in one of the central metropolitan districts," Vespera answered smoothly, tilting her cup.
"It’s a fairly quiet area.
What about you, Lord Sky?"
Sky didn’t notice her subtle vagueness, assuming she was simply being shy about her personal privacy in front of millions of stream viewers.
"I’m stationed out in Valoria City," Sky shared freely, tapping his chest plate.
"Born and raised near the central commercial hub of Silverleaf."
He set his teacup down, his tone shifting into a slightly more serious, intriguing rhythm.
"By the way, Lord Vespera... have you checked the global news feeds back on Earth recently?
Do you know about the massive bounty the government and the World Council have placed on your head?"
Vespera blinked her purple eyes in genuine surprise, tilting her head.
"A bounty?
Seriously?"
"Oh, absolutely," Sky nodded firmly, leaning forward.
"The World Council officially raised the reward for your confirmed real-world identity to Ten Billion Spirit Credits!
They’ve dubbed you the ’Hero of Humanity,’ and the top government officials are practically breaking down doors trying to secure an immediate, high-priority meeting with you."
Vespera’s eyes went wide as saucers, her mouth opening slightly in dramatic shock.
"Ten Billion?!" Vespera gasped out, pressing her hand against her chest.
I don’t even know the first thing about corporate or government meetings!
High-society politics sounds utterly terrifying!"
’Lord Silas is being too natural as a woman...
Has he had experience in this too?’ Thora looked at him suspiciously, why was he so good at acting all of a sudden?
Sky laughed warmly at her flustered reaction.
"If you ever need advice on how to handle government bureaucrats or corporate headhunters, just let me know!
I’ve been dealing with those suits for years."
Sky’s masked face leaned in a fraction closer, his eyes gleaming with intense curiosity.
"The main reason the World Council is going so insane over you," Sky revealed in a low, quiet voice, "is because of the rumors surrounding your Core class.
The global media and the higher academies are convinced that you are a Gold Core Lord... seeing as humanity’s very last recorded Gold Core Lord was born centuries ago."
Sky looked straight into her deep violet eyes, probing for a reaction.
"So... tell me, Lord Vespera.
Are the rumors true?
Are you truly a Gold Core?"
Vespera didn’t flinch.
A sly captivating and mysterious smile slowly curved her lips.
She rested her chin on her single palm, her purple eyes twinkling with playful arrogance.
"Well..." Vespera purred softly, her raspy voice dripping with tantalizing tease.
"I’ll tell you... if you win the war."
Sky’s lips quirked violently upward behind his silver-and-black alloy mask.
’A challenge?!’ Sky thought, an electric surge of competitive adrenaline shooting straight through his veins.
Meanwhile, inside her mind, Silas Graves let out a massive triumphant sigh of relief!
’FINALLY!’ Silas cheered internally, pumping his metaphorical fists. ’Finally!
I can finally turn this absurd conversation toward the actual Lord War!
I was getting so damn tired of this small talk... is this supposed to be a date or a Lord negotiation?!’
Sky straightened his spine, sitting up tall in his padded chair as his demeanor shifted from a friendly, relaxed chat partner into a serious veteran Warlord.
"A tempting prize," Sky admitted smoothly, his eyes burning with battle-hungry excitement.
"Alright then.
Let’s talk about the Lord War.
After all... that is the primary reason my mobile fortress entered the Umbral Basin."
Vespera sat up straight as well, setting her teacup aside.
"I’m listening, Lord Sky."
Sky looked at her, then looked over at Tasmin and Thora standing nearby.
"Before we set the parameters," Sky began thoughtfully, "I need to gauge your military scale.
How large is the standing army of Blessed Land currently?"
Vespera didn’t see any reason to lie about her numbers.
She looked Sky dead in his mask and answered plainly:
"I currently have less than one hundred total troops in my territory."
The second those words left her lips—
Sky’s entire body went completely rigid.
His jaw dropped open behind his alloy mask, his eyes bulging in shock.
"Less... less than a hundred?!" Sky gasped out loud, completely failing to hide his utter disbelief!
"Are you serious?!"
His mind raced at light speed, calculating the impossibility of what she had just said.
Blessed Land was currently sitting in the Top one on the Newbie Charts and a Top 100 All time territory too, and Asgard as well as other mythical places were in top hundred too.
Their territory points were astronomical...
For a territory to achieve that level of global ranking with a total population of fewer than one hundred people meant one terrifying mind-boggling thing:
Every single individual living inside the Blessed Land was an superhuman monster.

If every single one of her seventy-plus troops possessed physical stats, speed, and combat capabilities comparable to Tasmin... who had just single-handedly butchered twenty armed scouts in three minutes without breaking a sweat, then this wasn’t going to be an easy skirmish.
’Fuck...’
Sky realized with chilling clarity that if he didn’t take this Lord War seriously and unleash his full military power, his undefeated streak was going to be brutally shattered live on stream.
Vespera took a calm sip of her tea, looking at his shocked expression with a faint, humble smile.
"We really train very hard," Vespera explained casually.
"That’s all there is to it."
Sky took a slow, deep breath, forcing himself to calm down and regain his tactical composure.
He rested his hands flat on the white tablecloth, looking at her with absolute seriousness.
"Alright," Sky spoke, his voice deep and focused.
"When would you be available to execute the official Lord War?
You know that is why I’m here."
Vespera tilted her head, entering deep thought.
Inside her mind, Silas was rapidly weighing his options.

’I still haven’t gathered enough experience to trigger the Second Stage of Core Ascension for myself,’ Silas analyzed. ’And gaining that massive 30,000-point mana boost before fighting an undefeated Classic Lord would be extremely helpful...
I need a bit of time.’
Before Vespera could state a timeframe, Sky raised his hand, offering his own proposal first.
"If it suits you, Lord Vespera," Sky proposed smoothly, "I would prefer to wait one full week before launching the war."

chapters.title: Chapter 244: Negotiation Between Lords [III / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Vespera raised an eyebrow. "One week? Why the delay?"

"It will give my engineers enough time to properly clear out a designated battle sector," Sky explained, gesturing toward the surrounding wilderness. "We can clear a massive, wide-open dirt field located right within your territory’s viewing distance... a neutral battleground where both of our full armies can line up and face each other directly, right in front of your Keep’s front gates."
Vespera thought it over for two seconds, then smiled softly. "A wide clearing in front of my gates? That sounds perfectly acceptable to me. One week it is."
"Excellent," Sky nodded, pleased with her quick agreement. "Now... let’s set the official victory stakes."
Sky leaned forward, looking into her violet eyes. "If I win the Lord War... what do I claim as my reward?"
Vespera tilted her head. "What do you want, Lord Sky?"
Sky chuckled softly, waving his hand in a relaxed gesture.

"Nothing crazy," Sky answered casually. "As you know, I don’t strip defeated Lords of their land or destroy their cores. If I win... all I ask for is a guided, personal tour of the Blessed Land itself, along with the full rights to stream the entire walkthrough live on my channel."
Hearing his condition, Vespera blinked her purple eyes, a strange bewildered thought passing through Silas’s mind.

’Maybe this guy doesn’t actually like me that much after all...’ Silas thought drily behind his disguise. ’What kind of insane Lord proposes to another Lord that their victory reward is just looking around every inch of their private territory and broadcasting it to millions of people?! Is he an inspector or a Lord?!’
Still, setting aside the weirdness of the request, allowing a stream tour was an incredibly cheap harmless price to pay compared to losing land or resources.
"I agree to your condition," Vespera accepted smoothly.
She then leaned forward, her deep purple eyes locking onto his mask with a sharp intensity. "Now... as for my reward when I defeat you..."
Sky smiled behind his mask. "Name your terms, Lord Vespera."
Vespera rested her single palm against the table, delivering her terms in a calm, matter-of-fact tone that shattered the quiet clearing:
"When I win... I want every single one of your Female Heroes... as well as every single female troop member in your entire army."
The second those words left Vespera’s mouth—
The entire mud clearing went completely dead silent!
Sky’s main blindfolded Hero stiffened and the surrounding two hundred soldiers gasped in collective shock.
Sky himself froze mid-motion, his hand pausing inches away from his teacup as he stared at her in total disbelief.
Even the live stream chat overlaying Sky’s HUD completely froze for two full seconds before violently exploding into a hysterical tsunami of comments:
[@GamerGod99: WHAT THE ACTUAL FUCK?!]
[@SovereignWatcher: SHE WANTS ALL HIS FEMALE HEROES AND TROOPS?!]
[@NoobMaster69: BRO SHE IS TRYING TO ROB HIS ENTIRE FEMALE POPULATION!]
[@PVP_Legend: THAT IS THE CRAZIEST LORD WAR DEMAND IN HISTORY!]
[@ValoriaFan: IS SHE BUILDING A HAREM OR AN ARMY?!]
[@DarkKnight_00: She didn’t ask for gold or gear, she asked for WOMEN!]
[@TacticalNuke: ABSOLUTE CHAD MOVE!]
[@StreamLover: SKY DON’T DO IT LMAO!]
[@ProGamer_22: Why does she only want female troops?!]
Sky slowly lowered his hand, his masked face filled with genuine mind-boggling confusion as he looked at Vespera.
"Why...?" Sky asked with his voice completely bewildered. "Why specifically female troops and Heroes?"
Vespera offered him a calm, elegant, and completely shameless explanation, smoothing down her black trousers with her single hand.

"Because my territory operates under a very strict, foundational rule," Vespera explained smoothly. "Men are strictly prohibited from entering or living within the Blessed Land. Therefore, if I am to expand my population and bolster my military ranks through this war... I can only accept female combatants. I hope you can consider my request."
It was madness! Who in their right mind demands an entire gender category of an opponent’s army as war loot?!
Vespera obviously knew how utterly insane and outrageous her demand sounded.
Inside her mind, Silas was chuckling slyly.

’I know it sounds crazy,’ Silas reasoned behind his disguise. ’Which is why I’m setting the anchor outrageously high on purpose! That way, we have plenty of room to negotiate down to a realistic number.’
Silas didn’t actually expect Sky to hand over every single female Hero he owned.
He didn’t care that much about acquiring a massive stockpile of high-tier Heroes... maybe one or two interesting ones would suffice.
What Silas truly wanted... were the troops!
Behind legendary Heroes, it was the standing disciplined troop population that formed the true foundation and daily output of any great territory.
Acquiring decades-trained, experienced female soldiers, archers, and casters to populate his expanding Blessed Land was a goldmine that he couldn’t bear to lose.
Sky stared at Vespera for a long five seconds, then suddenly threw his head back and burst into a loud, hearty laugh.
"Hahaha! Well, I’ll be damned!" Sky chuckled merrily, shaking his head. "It sounds to me like your territory just really hates men!"
Vespera let out a small, delicate sigh, offering a playful helpless smile.
"I can’t help it. Rules are rules."
Up on the floating camera drones, the live-stream chat captured her response, and a specific demographic of viewers back on Earth went completely wild.
The comment section was suddenly flooded with posts from modern online movements.
[@FeministIcon_99: QUEEN BEHAVIOR! WE LOVE VESPERA!]
[@GirlPower_X: A TERRITORY WITH NO MEN?! SIGN ME UP RIGHT NOW!]
[@SovereignQueen: WE HATE MEN TOO! LORD VESPERA IS OUR NEW IDOL!]
[@AlphaGirl_00: BLESSED LAND IS A FEMALE UTOPIA!]
[@Empowerment_22: BAN ALL MEN! VESPERA FOR PRESIDENT!]
[@EqualityNow: Best Lord on the continent hands down!]
[@LadyVanguard: I’m transferring my application to Blessed Land!]
[@ShieldMaiden_99: MEN ARE CANCELLED! LONG LIVE QUEEN VESPERA!]
Sitting across the table, Vespera happened to catch a brief glimpse of those specific comments scrolling across Sky’s stream HUD.
Silas’s eyelid twitched violently beneath his female disguise.

’I wonder how these insane modern feminists would react if they found out that the Lord of Blessed Land is actually a six-foot-two guy with a giant dick...’ Silas thought dryly with a wave of dark amusement washing over his mind. ’They’d probably label me an international perverted criminal and try to nuke my Keep from orbit...’
Silas took a quiet sip of his tea, internally nodding to himself.
’Perhaps this female disguise... is far more practical and useful than I originally thought.’
Sky wiped an imaginary tear of laughter from his mask, leaning back over the table as he began the actual counter-negotiation.

"Look, Lord Vespera," Sky spoke reasonably, holding up his hands. "I obviously cannot hand over every single female in my army. That would completely cripple my mobile war-band’s operational balance."
"I understand," Vespera replied politely, nodding her black-haired head. "What is your counter-offer?"
Sky thought it over carefully, calculating his roster numbers before speaking firmly:

"If you defeat me in the Lord War... I will hand over seventy female troops from my standing army, along with two of my female Heroes... including the silver-haired beast-kin girl Tasmin just knocked out earlier."
Vespera’s purple eyes brightened.
Seventy highly trained, battle-hardened female soldiers, plus two high-tier female Heroes?
That was an astronomical haul! It would instantly double the population of Blessed Land, providing dozens of elite guards for perimeter patrols and field hunting!
Vespera placed her single hand over her chest, offering Sky a deep and breathtakingly gorgeous bow.
"Thank you, Lord Sky," Vespera expressed warmly, her voice filled with genuine appreciation. "Your generosity honors me."
Sky smiled warmly behind his silver mask, waving his hand dismissively.

"Don’t mention it," Sky replied kindly. "To be completely honest with you... I acquired most of those female troops and those two Heroes from the last Lord I fought. That bastard was mistreating them terribly, using them as disposable meat-shields and denying them proper rations. I took them into my ranks to save them, but my mobile rig is primarily built for swift travel, not long-term population housing. I genuinely hope you treat them much better than their previous master did."
Vespera looked into Sky’s eyes with her voice becoming remarkably sincere.
"I give you my word as a Lord," Vespera promised softly. "Every woman who enters the Blessed Land is treated with respect, dignity, and care. They will have a true home."
"Good," Sky nodded, visibly relieved. "I trust your word."
Sky reached out, picking up his teacup to take a slow sip.
He paused for a brief second, setting the cup back down as a slight embarrassed scratch of his neck betrayed his next thought.
He looked at Vespera, clearing his throat awkwardly as he transitioned the topic to his final pressing concern.
"So... about the food...?"
Sky gestured vaguely back toward his massive, three-story mobile fortress resting at the edge of the clearing.

"You see..." Sky admitted sheepishly, a slight awkward laugh escaping his mask. "our onboard food rations are thinning down quite a bit, and we desperately need to restock our pantries... especially to feed two hundred hungry soldiers for the entire week leading up to our Lord War..."
Vespera smiled warmly across the white tablecloth, her deep purple eyes shining with a calm accommodating light as she looked at Lord Sky.
She raised her single right hand, offering a gracious gesture toward his mobile fortress.

"You really don’t have to worry about that at all, Lord Sky," Vespera said smoothly, her voice projecting effortless hospitality. "I would be more than happy to handle your army’s feeding arrangements... I can have my kitchen staff and my master chef cook up a massive feast using our own stored supplies, and I’ll personally assign a detachment of my soldiers to transport the rations directly out here to your camp every day leading up to the war."
As Vespera spoke those polite words, inside her mind, Silas was ruthlessly dissecting the situation.

’I’m trying to see just how stupid this guy actually is,’ Silas thought with his internal voice stripped of all feminine softness, replaced by the sharp edge of a Lord. ’Will he actually agree blindly to that whole proposal?’
Silas didn’t necessarily consider Sky to be a complete idiot.

The man hadn’t survived for years as an undefeated Classic Lord by being a total fool but if Silas were in Sky’s position... standing on foreign soil, preparing to fight a high-stakes Lord War... he wouldn’t adhere to any kind of polite buttering up, no matter how beautiful or charming the opposing Lord appeared on stream.
More importantly, Silas would never put his own people on the line without their explicit permission just to seal a trade deal or look good for an online audience.
These soldiers weren’t just AI NPCs or disposable background meat-shields; they were living breathing human beings who had entrusted their lives to his banner.

’At the end of the day,’ Silas reflected silently behind his violet-eyed disguise, ’Sky is a good Lord. He cares about his troops, and he doesn’t slaughter the weak but he is not the kind of Lord I aspire to be. His priorities are split between his survival and his entertainment broadcast.’
Sky paused, sitting back in his padded leather chair.
He raised his gauntleted hand, offering a respectful, polite nod of his masked head as he firmly declined the offer.

"I appreciate the extraordinary generosity, Lord Vespera, but I must politely reject that request," Sky explained with his voice broadcasting clearly through his alloy mask. "In the past, during my early travels across the outer sectors, rival guilds and hostile Lords tried poisoning my war-band using disguised ’gift rations’ and laced hospitality feasts. Now... while I know with certainty that a Lord of your standing wouldn’t attempt something so dishonorable, as the leader of this mobile fortress, I still have to be completely sure. My troops’ safety comes first."
Vespera’s smile softened, her posture exuding understanding as she nodded.

"It is completely right for you to worry about your people, Lord Sky," Vespera reassured him smoothly. "If prepared meals are a security risk then it isn’t an issue at all. Instead of cooked food, I can have my hunters go out into the basin, harvest fresh, untouched game, and bring the raw unbutchered carcasses right over to your camp so your own chefs can inspect and prepare the meat themselves."
Sky shook his head again, waving his hand in a relaxed gesture.

"Even with raw game, I would prefer to keep our supply chain entirely internal," Sky rejected politely once more. "It would be much better for us if we got more of an authentic feel for this local territory by hunting the regional monsters ourselves. In fact... since you know the terrain, I would like to ask you to act as our personal guide for today’s hunt, Lord Vespera. Take us to a viable hunting ground where we can harvest enough meat to feed my two-hundred-man army."
Inside her mind, Silas felt a sudden spike of irritation.
’Fucking hell...’ Silas thought bitterly.
